# Code-Generated User Load Combinations for {Design Type} {Code} Form

Additional form:  Design Load Type

Use the Code-Generated User Load Combinations for {Type} Frame Design - {Code} form to review and as necessary specify the limit state and the load cases to be included in the generation of load combination based on the code and user input. Limit states are code-specified types of combinations to be generated.

Note:  The code selected using the Design menu > {Type} Design > View/Revise Preferences command determines the options available on this form.

- Limit States for which User Defined Load Combinations are to be Generated and associated check boxes. Specify the limit state(s) for which the combinations are to be generated. When a limit state check box is checked, the program will generate combinations for that limit state.

- Choose Load Cases to Use for Limit State
- - Limit State drop-down list. Limit states are code-specified types of combinations. Choose the Limit State for which combinations will be generated using the load cases specified in the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations  list. The list of load combinations must be specified for each Limit State. Note that the  Copy to button (see below) can be used to speed this process.
  - List of Load Cases and Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations.  All load cases are listed in the List of Load Cases display lists (i.e., Load Case Name, Load Case Type, Design Load Type). The cases to be used in generating the automatic load combination are listed in the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists. To specify that a load case be included in or excluded from a combination, select a load case by clicking on it and then use the arrow keys to move the selected load case into or out of the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists.
- Note:  Each load case has a Design Type that can be set by the user or be program determined. The Design Type of a load case determines if it can be included in a given limit state, how it is to be included (e.g., additive, envelope), and the scale factor to be used, all in accordance with the design code. Only load cases with the appropriate Design Type can be included in a given limit state. For this reason, load cases can not be added arbitrarily to a limit state.
- 1. 1. - Show Only Load Cases with Valid Design Load Type check box. When this check box is checked, only those load cases with a valid design type for the applied code are listed in the List of Load Cases display lists.
        - Copy to button. Use this button to copy the specified load combination definition to the limit state selected in the drop-down list.
  1. - Show Load Case Definition button.
     - 1. Highlight a load case in the List of Load Cases or Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display list to enable this button.
       2. Click the button to access the [Load Case Data - {Load Case} definition form](../Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) for the load case selected in Step 1.
       3. The form is provided for review purposes only. Any changes made will be ignored. Use the Define menu > Load Cases command to make permanent changes to the load case definition.
     - Set Design Load Type button.
     - 1. Highlight a load case in the List of Load Cases or Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists to enable this button.
       2. Click the button to access the Design Load type form.
       3. Choose an option to set the Design Load Type of the load case selected in Step 1 to Program Determined  or User Defined. If the User Defined option is selected, choose a load type from the drop-down list to update the load case definition.
- Note:  If the Design Type is program determined, the Design Type is inherent in the Load Case type or it is based on the Design Type of the load patterns that have been applied in the load case. The [Define menu > Load Patterns command](../Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) accesses the form needed to specify the Design Type for individual load patterns.

# Load Combinations

Form:  Define Load Combinations, Load Combination Data

Program design is based on a set of loading combinations. In SAP2000, load combinations, or combos, are generated automatically by SAP2000 or user defined. If the automatically generated load combinations are acceptable (note that these combos are created/recreated after each design run), no definition of additional load combinations is required.

Use the  Design menu > {[Steel](../../Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Select_Design_Combos.md), [Concrete](../../Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Select_Design_Combos.md), [Aluminum](../../Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Select_Design_Combos.md), [Cold Formed Steel](../../Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Select_Design_Combos.md)} > Select Design Combos command to work with automatic load combinations.

Use the Define menu > Load Combinations command to specify your own user combinations. The user-defined combinations can be created manually or based on a selected code, as described in this topic. This command can be used to convert automatic load combinations to user-defined combinations that can then be modified to meet specific needs.

Note:   The Design menu command must be used to select the user-defined combinations to be used in design, regardless of whether the combos were created manually or if the combination(s) is based on code using the Define menu.  The program automatically selects the automatic code-generated combos (generated after each design run).

Automatic and user-defined combination may be used simultaneously for design. Note that each time a design is run, the automatic combos are regenerated, thereby replacing any previous automatic combos. User-defined combinations (manual or based on code) are not changed during design. The Define menu > Load Combinations command can be used to convert automatic code-generated combos to user-defined combos.

Note: Notional loads are not included in code-generated or automatic combinations. Thus, to consider the combination of notional and lateral loads, appropriate User Load Combinations should be generated.

Manually Create User-Defined Load Combination

1. Click the Define menu > Load Combinations command to access the Define Load Combinations form.
2. Use the following buttons on that form to complete the appropriate action.

   - Add New Combo button. Click this button to display the Load Combination Data form and manually create a user-defined load combination for the model.
   - 1. Use the default or type another name in the Load Combination Name edit box. Note that each load combination and [load case](../Load_Cases/Define_Load_Cases.md) must have a unique name. Also, the word Mode is reserved and can not be used for either a load case name or a load combination name.
     2. Select the Load Combination Type:

1. 1. 1. - Linear Add.  All load case results are multiplied by their scale factor and added together. This Combo Type can be used for static loads. Multiple steps can be reported for a load combination with a **Linear Add** Type if any of the following multi-stepped load case/combo types are included in the *Define Combination of Load Case Results* section of the form:

           - Multi-step load cases
           - Time history load cases
           - Staged construction load cases
           - Other load combinations that have multiple steps

         The Combo maximum (or minimum) for each step is an algebraic linear combination of the values for each of the included multi-stepped load case/combo types at the specific step and the maximum (or minimum) values of all other included analysis cases. The results for each step as well as for the envelope over all the steps can be viewed in the display and table output.

         - Envelope.  A max/min Envelope of the defined load cases is evaluated for each frame output segment and object joint. The load cases that give the maximum and minimum components are used for this combo. Therefore the load Combo holds two values for each output segment and joint. The Combo Type can be used for moving loads and any load case where the load producing the maximum or minimum force/stress is required.
         - Absolute Add. The absolute of the individual load case results are summed and positive and negative values are automatically produced for each output segment and joint. Use this Combo Type for lateral loads.
         - SRSS. The Square Root Sum of the Squares calculation is performed on the load cases and positive and negative values are automatically produced for each output segment and joint. Use this Combo Type for lateral loads.
         - Range Add. The combined maximum is the sum of the positive maximum values from each of the contributing cases (a case with a negative maximum does not contribute), and the combined minimum is the sum of the negative minimum values from each of the contributing cases (a case with a positive minimum does not contribute). This Combo Type is useful for pattern or skip-type loading where all permutations of the contributing load case must be considered.
      3. Select the appropriate action:

         - Add button. Add a load combination.
         1. 1. Select a load case name from the Load Case Name drop-down list and type in the multiplier in the Scale Factor edit box. The Load Case Type display box shows the load case type for the specified load case.
            2. Click the Add button to add the load case and multiplier to the Load Case Name/Scale Factor display areas.
            3. Repeat as necessary.
         - Modify button. Modify a load combination.
         - 1. Select the load case/multiplier to be modified in the Load Case Name/Scale Factor display areas.
           2. Type the revisions into the Load Case Name/Scale Factor edit boxes.
           3. Click the Modify button.
         - Delete button. Delete a load combination.
         - 1. Select the load case/multiplier to be deleted in the Load Case Name/Scale Factor display areas.
           2. Click the Delete button.
         - Convert to User Load Combo button. Use this button to convert a [Code-Generated Automatic Load Combination](../../Design/Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.md) to a User Load Combination that can then be modified using the options described herein.
         - 1. Select a Code-Generated Automatic Load Combination. Note that, as explained previously, this type of load combination is generated automatically by the program during the design process. Therefore, this button will not be available until at least one iteration of analysis and design has been completed.
           2. Click this button to convert the selected load combination to a user-defined load combination. This action occurs immediately; no form displays.
         - Create Nonlinear Load Case from Load Combo button. Use this button to create a new nonlinear load case based on this load combination.
   1. 1. Select a user defined load combination that has a Load Combination Type of Linear Add and has at least one linear static load case in the combination.
      2. Click this button to combine all linear static load cases in the combination into a new nonlinear static load case. This action occurs immediately; no form displays.

- Modify/Show Combo button. Click this button to display the Load Combination Data form and manually create a user-defined load combination for the model.

1. Select the load combination to be modified in the Load Combinations display area.
2. Click the Modify/Show Combo button to access the Define Response Combinations form.
3. Make the necessary adjustments using the options on the form (see above).
4. Click the OK button to return to the Define Load Combinations form. Then click the OK button on that form to close it.

- Delete Combo button. Use this button to delete a combo.

  1. Select the load combination to be  deleted in the Load Combinations display area.
  2. Click the Delete Combo button.
- **Convert Combos to Nonlinear Cases button**. Use this button to open a form that allows selecting one or more load combinations from which nonlinear p-delta load cases should be generated. If the checkbox 'Include Large Displacements' is checked, the load cases will be generated as nonlinear p-delta plus large displacements.

User-Defined Load Combinations Based on Code

1. Click the Define menu > Load Combinations command to access the Define Load Combinations form.
2. Click the Add Default Design Combos button to access the [Add Code-Generated User Load Combinations form](Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md).
3. Select the design type (e.g., steel frame, concrete frame, aluminum frame, cold-formed steel frame).
4. If necessary, click the Set Load Combination Data button to access the [Code-Generated User Load Combinations for {Code} form](Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_for_{Code}_Form.md) and refine the definition of the code-generated combination.

Converting Automatic Code-Generated Combos to User-Defined Combos

1. Click the Design menu > {Steel, Concrete, Aluminum, Cold Formed Steel} > Select Design Combos command to access the Define Load Combinations Selection form.
2. Check the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box.
3. Run an analysis and design.
4. Click the Define menu > Load Combinations command to access the Define Load Combinations form.
5. Highlight the automatic load combination to be converted into a user-defined load combination.
6. Click the Modify/Show Combo button to display the Load Combination Data form.
7. Click the Convert Combos  to User Load Combo button.
8. A query will be displayed asking that the conversion be verified and advising that the conversion can not be undone.
9. Click the Yes button and SAP2000 will convert the automatic code-generated load combinations into a user-defined load combination. Click the No button and the conversion will not take place.

As indicated above, each time a design is run, the automatic code-generated combos are regenerated, thereby replacing any previous automatic code-generated combos. However, any automatic code-generated combo that has been converted to a user-defined combinations will not be changed during design.

Example:  Definition of combinations is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md), [Problem B](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md), [Problem I](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_I.md) and [Problem U](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

## See Also

[Aluminum Frame Design - Select Design Combos](../../Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Select_Design_Combos.md)

[Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design - Select Design Combos](../../Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Select_Design_Combos.md)

[Concrete Frame Design - Select Design Combos](../../Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Select_Design_Combos.md)

[Steel Frame Design - Select Design Combos](../../Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Select_Design_Combos.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.htm | Define Load Patterns -->

# Define Load Patterns

Form: Define Load Patterns

Use the Define menu > Load Patterns command to access the Define Load Patterns form and add, modify, or delete load patterns. [Click there for more information about load patterns.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

Loads represent actions upon the structures,
such as force, pressure, support settlement, thermal effects, ground
acceleration, and others. A spatial distribution of loads upon the
structure is called a load pattern. An unlimited number of load patterns
can be defined in SAP2000. Typically, separate load patterns would
be defined for dead load, live load, wind load, snow load, thermal
loads, and so on. Loads that need to vary independently, for design
purposes or because of how they are applied to the structure, should
be defined as a separate load pattern. SAP2000 uses the type of load
to create design load combinations automatically.

Load patterns can include automated loads, such
as self weight or code-specified wind or earthquake lateral force
distributions. For all other loads on the structure, specific load
values must be assigned to objects as part of a load pattern (see
the topics in the Menus/Assign - Joint Loads, Frame Loads, Cable Loads,
Tendon Loads, Area Loads, Solid Loads and Link/Support Loads books
of this Help for more information about assigning loads). The load
values assigned to an object specify the type of load (e.g., force,
displacement, temperature, and so forth), its magnitude, and its direction
(if applicable). Different loads can be assigned to different objects
as part of a single load pattern. Each object can be subjected to
multiple load patterns.

The Define Load Patterns form also displays when the + (plus symbol) is clicked on any of the forms used to assign loads; see the topics in the Assign -  Area Loads, Frame Loads, Cable Loads, Tendon Loads, Joint Loads, Link/Support Loads and Solids Loads books of this Help.

Note: To calculate any response of the structure resulting from the load patterns, you must define and run [load cases](../Load_Cases/Define_Load_Cases.md) that specify how the load patterns are to be applied (e.g., statically, dynamically) and how the structure is to be analyzed (e.g., linearly, nonlinearly). The same load pattern can be applied differently in different load cases.

Tip: Every time a new load pattern is defined, the program automatically creates a corresponding linear static analysis case of the same name that applies the load. For a new model, the program creates a default load case called DEAD that applies the self weight of the structure. The corresponding linear static analysis case is also called DEAD.

1. Click the Define menu > Load Patterns command to access the Define Load Patterns form. The form has the following edit boxes and drop-down lists.

1. - Load Pattern Name edit box. Type a unique name for the load pattern in this edit box. The previously assigned load  pattern names will appear in the display list below this edit box.  Note that each load pattern and [load combination](../Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) must have a unique name. Also, the word Mode is reserved and can not be used for either a load pattern name or a load combination name.
   - Type drop-down list. Choose the type of the load pattern for design. The program uses these values when [automatically creating design load combinations](../Load_Combination/Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md) for the design postprocessor. The factors used in the design load combinations are different for the various types of loads. The choices for load pattern types are extensive and are assumed to be basically self explanatory with the following brief explanations.
   - - Use the OTHER option if the design load is not to be included in the design load combination automatically created by the program..
     - The SUPER DEAD option is superimposed dead load.
     - The REDUCE LIVE option is Reducible Live Load; a live load that is specified as reducible will be affected by the LLRF design overwrite value, if assigned, when running the design.
   - Self-Weight Multiplier edit box. This is a scale factor that multiplies the weight of the structure and applies it as a force in the gravity direction (negative global Z direction). The self-weight of the structure is determined by multiplying the weight per unit volume of each object that has structural properties times the volume of the object. The weight per unit volume is specified in the [material properties](../Material/Define_Materials.md). Use the Self-Weight Multiplier edit box to specify what portion of the self-weight is to be applied to any load pattern. A self-weight multiplier of 1 means to include the full self-weight of the structure in the load pattern. A self-weight multiplier of 0.5 means to include half of the self-weight of the structure in the load pattern. Normally a self-weight multiplier of 1 should be specified in one load pattern only, usually the dead load pattern, with all other load patterns having a self-weight multipliers of zero. Note that if a self-weight multiplier of 1 is included in two different load patterns, and then those two load patterns are combined in the same load combination, the results for the load combination are based on an analysis where double the self-weight of the building has been applied as a load.
   - Auto Lateral Load Pattern drop-down list. The Auto Lateral Load Pattern drop-down list becomes active when the load pattern type is specified as Quake, Wave or Wind.
   - - Choose None from the drop-down list to not use the automatic loads and instead assign loads using the commands available on the Assign menu.
     - Choose one of the codes from the drop-down list to specify that code-compliant loads be created automatically for the load pattern. Another form will appear that can be used to review and as necessary specify the appropriate parameters for the automatic pattern. (See the Modify Lateral Pattern bullet below for hyperlinks to topics addressing those forms.)

Use the buttons in the Click To area of the form to complete the actions described below:

- Add New Load Pattern button.

- 1. Type the name of the load pattern in the Load Pattern Name edit box.
  2. Select a load pattern type from the Type drop-down list.
  3. If appropriate, type a self-weight multiplier in the Self-Weight Multiplier edit box. (See the Self-Weight Multiplier text above for cautions related to applying self weight.)
  4. If the load Type specified is Quake, Wave  or Wind, select an option from the Auto Lateral Pattern drop-down list.
  5. Click the Add New Load Pattern button. If the load pattern type specified is Quake, Wave  or Wind, note the text for the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button.
- Modify Load Pattern button.

1. 1. Highlight the existing load pattern in the Load Patterns area. Note that the data associated with that load pattern appears in the edit boxes and drop-down lists at the top of the Load Patterns area.
   2. Modify any of the data in the Load Patterns area for the load pattern.
   3. Click the Modify Load Pattern button.

Note:  If nothing happens when the  Modify Load Pattern button is clicked, the load pattern is an automatic load pattern. As described in the Note below, highlight the load pattern and the click the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button.

- Modify Lateral Load Pattern button.

If a new pattern is being defined with a load Type of Quake, Wave  or Wind and a code (i.e., automatic pattern) has been selected in the Auto Lateral Load Pattern drop-down list, first click the Add New Load Pattern button, then click the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button to access a form specific to [wave,](Wave_Load/Wave_Load_Pattern_Form.md)  [wind](Wind_Load_Pattern_Form.md) or [seismic](Seismic_Loading_Form.md) loading. Use the form to specify parameters consistent with the code selected  in the Auto Lateral Load Pattern drop-down list. For example, if the load type is Quake and NEHRP 97 is selected in the Auto Lateral Load Pattern drop-down list, the form that appears is the NEHRP 97 Seismic Loading form. The options available on that form relate to code requirements. Thus, fill in parameters on the form as appropriate. Then click the OK button to complete the operation and return to the Define Load Patterns form.

Note: After a code specific pattern has been defined as described here, highlight it in the list of patterns and click the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button to redisplay the form if any additional changes are needed.

If a new pattern is being defined with a Type of Moving Live, first click the Add New Load Pattern button to specify the load pattern, then highlight that pattern and click the Modify Moving Live Load button to access the [Multi Step Live Load Pattern Generation](Multi_Step_Moving_Live_Load_Pattern_Generation_Form.md) form. Use that form to refine the path loading for a [moving load analysis](../Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md). Note that  a [path](../Moving_Loads/Path_Data_Form.md) and a [vehicle(s](../Moving_Loads/Define_Vehicles.md)) must be defined before the live load can be defined.

- Delete Load Pattern button.

Note that when a static load pattern is deleted, all of the loads that have been assigned to the model as a part of that static load pattern also are deleted.

- 1. Highlight the existing load pattern in the Load Patterns area. Note that the data associated with that load pattern appears in the edit boxes and drop-down lists at the top of the Load Patterns area.
  2. Click the Delete Load Pattern button.
- Show Load Pattern Notes button. Click this button to access the [Load Pattern Notes](../Material/Notes_Form.md) form. Use that form to add load pattern notes to the model file. Type the notes directly into the form. Any previously entered Notes will be displayed when the form is accessed.

After a load pattern has been defined, assign loads to the objects as part of that load pattern by selecting the objects to be loaded and using the appropriate command from the Assign menu.

Example:  Definition of load patterns is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md) (Quake), [Problem B](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md) (Quake), [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md) (Live), [Problem E](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_E.md) (Quake), [Problem H](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_H.md) (Live), [Problem I](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_I.md) (Live), [Problem J](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_J.md) (Live), [Problem K](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_K.md) (Live, Quake), [Problem O](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_O.md) (Live),  [Problem P](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_P.md) (Other-Axial), [Problem U](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md) (Live), [Problem V](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_V.md) (Dead with 0 Self Weight), and [Problem W](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_W.md) (Dead with 0 Self Weight).

# Multi Step Moving Live Load Pattern Generation Form

Use the Multi Step Moving Live Load Pattern Generation form to refine the path loading for a [moving load analysis](../Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md).

- Vehicle drop-down list. Choose the type of vehicle for which the load is being defined from this list of previously defined [vehicle(s).](../Moving_Loads/Define_Vehicles.md)

Note:  Vehicles that are defined using a uniform load will not be included in the program generated multi-step load case. Click this note on the form to view a list of vehicles defined using uniform loads.

- Path drop-down list. Choose the path to which the vehicle load is being applied.
- Start Dist. Enter a value for the starting distance for the specified vehicle, measuring from the start of the path as specified when the [path](../Moving_Loads/Path_Data_Form.md) was defined.
- Start Time. Enter a value for the starting time for the specified vehicle.
- Direction drop-down list. Choose to have the vehicle move Forward or Backward, relative to the start of the path as specified when the [path](../Moving_Loads/Path_Data_Form.md) was defined.
- Speed edit box. Specify the speed of the specified vehicle.
- - Add button. With selections made and values entered in the above drop-down list and edit boxes, click the Add button to add the vehicle to the definition.
  - Modify button. Highlight a previously defined vehicle definition by clicking on it. Modify the selection or values in the appropriate drop-down list or edit box, and then click the Modify button to change the selected vehicle definition.
  - Delete button. Highlight a previously defined vehicle definition by clicking on it. Then click the Delete button to delete the vehicle definition.

- Load Discretization Information. Use the options in this area of the form to specify how the load is discretized.
- - Duration of Loading is edit box. Specify the total duration of the multi step moving load pattern in seconds.
  - Discretize Load every edit box. Specify the frequency in seconds between each step in the multi step moving load pattern.
- Units drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select new units from this drop-down list for use with this form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Multi Step Live Load Pattern Generation form as follows:   1. Define a [path](../Moving_Loads/Define_Paths.md) and a [vehicle(s](../Moving_Loads/Define_Vehicles.md)). 2. Click the Define menu > Load Patterns command to display the Define Load Patterns form. 3. Define a moving load by selecting MOVING LIVE in the Type drop-down box. 4. Click the Add New Load Pattern button. 5. Highlight the newly defined load and click the Modify Moving  Live Load button to display the Multi Step Moving Live Load Pattern Generation form. |

# Override Diaphragm Eccentricities Form

When defining automatic seismic lateral loads as part of a [load pattern definition](Define_Load_Patterns.md), an option exists to specify that the load is eccentric to the center of mass of the diaphragms. An eccentricity ratio may be specified that applies to all diaphragms. In addition, the eccentricity may be overwritten individually for one or more diaphragms.

Eccentric loading is applied to diaphragm constraints only; it is applied as a torsional moment. The non-eccentric portion of the load is applied to the whole model based on mass, and does not require diaphragm constraints.

Use the following buttons on the Override Diaphragm Eccentricities form to override the eccentricity ratio for one or more diaphragms.

- Add button
- 1. From the Diaphragm drop-down list, select the diaphragm name for which eccentricity values are to be specified.
  2. Enter a value in the Eccentricity, X-Dir (Eccen Y) or Y-Dir (Eccen X) edit box
  3. Click the Add button.

Note:  Eccentricities are specified as lengths, not ratios. If you are defining a load in the X direction, the eccentricity is measured in the Y direction, and vice-versa.

- Modify button
- 1. In the Diaphragm/Eccentricities display areas, select the diaphragm name for which eccentricity values are to be modified.
  2. Enter a revised value in the Eccentricity, X-Dir (Eccen Y) or Y-Dir (Eccen X) edit box.
  3. Click the Modify button.
- Delete button
- 1. In the Diaphragm/Eccentricities display areas, select the definition to be deleted.
  2. Click the Delete button.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Override Diaphragm Eccentricities form as follows:    [Diaphragm constraints](../Joint_Constraints/Diaphragm_Constraints_Form.md) must be [assigned to joint objects](../../Assign/Joint/Joint_Constraints.md) in the model for the auto lateral load to apply eccentric loads.  Note:  Eccentricity overrides apply to diaphragm constraints whose associated coordinate system is Global, and whose associated axis is Z. Thus, this type of diaphragm must be included in the model for this feature to be available.  Method 1   1. Click the Define menu > Load Patterns command to display the Define Load Patterns form. 2. Select a Quake Load Type. 3. Specify an Auto Lateral Load Pattern other than None and click the Add New Load Pattern button. 4. Highlight the newly defined load case and click the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button to display the {Code} Seismic Loading form. 5. Click the Override button to display the Override Diaphragm Eccentricities form.   Method 2   1. Click the Define menu > Load Cases command to access the Define Load Cases form. 2. Click the Add New Load Case button, or highlight a previously defined case and click the Add Copy of Load Case or Modify/Show Load Case button, to display the Load Cases Data form. 3. Select Response Spectrum from the Load Case Type drop-down list to display the Load Case Data - Response Spectrum form. 4. Click the Overrides button in the Diaphragm Eccentricity area of the form to display the Override Diaphragm Eccentricities form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Load_Pattern/Seastate_Load_Pattern_Form.htm | Seastate Load Pattern Form -->

# Seastate Load Pattern Form

Use the this form to specify the various parameters
for a seastate load. Those parameters include the following:

- Load Method and
  Direction
- - Rotations/Translations
    option. Choose this option
    to define the inertia load parameters in terms of rotations and/or
    translations, using amplitudes, periods, and phase angles.
  - Accelerations/Velocities
    option. Choose this option
    to define the inertia load parameters in terms of accelerations
    and velocities.
  - Coord System drop down. Select the coordinate
    system to use for defining the center of rotation and the inertia
    load parameters. The center of rotation is also defined with respect
    to the origin of the selected coordinate system.
  - Include Lateral Gravity Correction
    check box. When checked, the generated lateral loads will include
    the effects of the rotated structure. This correction is the sin(q)\*g
    term, where q
    is the rotation about X or Y. This option is only available when
    the Rotations/Translations load method is selected.
  - - Scale Factor edit box.  Specify
      a scale factor to apply to the lateral gravity correction.
  - Include Vertical Gravity Correction
    check box. When checked, the generated vertical loads will include
    the effects of the rotated structure. This correction is the[1
    - sqrt(1 - sin2q - sin2y)]\*g term, where q and y
    are the rotations about  X and Y. This option is only available
    when the Rotations / Translations load method is selected.
  - - Scale Factor edit box. Specify
      a scale factor to apply to the vertical gravity correction.

Note: The self-weight
vertical load is not automatically included in this load pattern. To include
self-weight either specify a self-weight multiplier on the load pattern,
or define a separate load pattern for self-weight and combine the load
patterns using a load combination. If using other load patterns to simulate
the mass of items not modeled via a mass source definition, it is necessary
to also include these load patterns in a load combination if their self-weight
should be included in the final results.

- Center of Rotation
- - X-coordinate
    edit box. Specify the x-coordinate,
    relative to the origin of the selected coordinate system, about
    which the rotations shall occur.
  - Y-coordinate
    edit box. Specify the y-coordinate,
    relative to the origin of the selected coordinate system, about
    which the rotations shall occur.
  - Z-coordinate
    edit box. Specify the z-coordinate,
    relative to the origin of the selected coordinate system, about
    which the rotations shall occur.
- Units drop
  down, The units used for input on this form.
- Inertia Load Parameters
  - Rotations/Translations. When
  the load method is rotation/translations, the following inertia load
  parameters are input.
- - Vertical Input or Full
    Input option. Choose whether to input only three degrees
    of freedom to simulate vertical motion or input all six degrees
    of freedom.
  - Amplitude edit boxes. UX, UY, and UZ translational
    degrees of freedom take an amplitude in the currently selected
    length units. Rx, Ry, and RZ rotational degrees of freedom take
    a rotation angle, in degrees.
  - Period edit boxes. The period of the motion
    in the respective degree of freedom.
  - Phase edit boxes. The phase angle of the
    degree of freedom with respect to the other degrees of freedom.
    The phase angle is in degrees.
  - All
    Same check boxes. Use
    these check boxes to make all inputs in a column the same as the
    uppermost input field in the column.
  - IgnorePhase check
    box. When checked, the input phases for the rotations and translations
    are ignored. This will result in all accelerations and velocities
    occurring simultaneously.

Note: It generally
makes sense that all periods are the same, bt
this is not required. It generally makes sense that UZ is ++ 90 degrees
out-of-phase with respect to RZ and RY, but this is not required.

- Inertia Load Parameters
  - Accelerations/Velocities. When
  the load method is accelerations/velocities, the following inertia
  load parameters are input.
- - Acceleration UX,
    UY, UZ edit boxes. The translational acceleration in the
    currently selected units.
  - Acceleration RX,
    RY, RZ edit boxes. The rotational acceleration in rad/sec2.
  - Velocity RX, RY,
    RZ edit boxes. The rotational velocity in rad/sec.

Note: Centrifugal
forces generated by rotational velocities, whether using the Rotations/Translations
option or the Accelerations/Velocities option, are nonlinear in the sense
that they are proportional to the square of the velocity. The forces are
always generated away from the center of rotation regardless of the sign
of the velocity. For this reason the true velocity (or period and amplitude)
should be specified and the load pattern should not be further scaled
in a load case or load combination. If scale factors are later applied,
they will scale the centrifugal force, not the velocity. Seastate load
patterns applied in a steady-state or PSD load case will omit the centrifugal
forces, since these do not vary sinusoidally. 

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Seastate Load Pattern form as follows:   1. Click    the Define    menu > Load Patterns command to display the Define Load Patterns form. 2. Specify    a Seastate Load Type    and an Auto Lateral Load of Auto and click the Add New Load    Pattern. 3. Highlight    the name of the newly defined load pattern and click the Modify    Lateral Load Pattern button to display the Seastate Load Pattern    form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Load_Pattern/Seismic_Loading_Form.htm | Seismic Loading Form -->

# Seismic Loading Form

Form:  {Code-Specific} Seismic Loading

Use the Seismic Loading form to the input the parameters and coefficients for the specified seismic load, including load direction and diaphragm eccentricity, seismic coefficients, time period, lateral load elevation range, near source factors, and additional code-specific factors. Code-specific program defaults are provided.

Note: Options to specify your own factors are available when the User Coefficients or User Load option is selected in the Auto Lateral Load drop-down list on the Define Load Patterns form.

The diaphragm eccentricity options have meaning only if the model has [diaphragms](../Joint_Constraints/Define_Joint_Constraints.md). SAP2000 ignores eccentricities where diaphragms are not present.

Where diaphragms are present, SAP2000 calculates a maximum width of the diaphragm perpendicular to the direction of the seismic loading. This width is calculated by finding the maximum and minimum X or Y coordinates (depending on direction of load considered) of the points that are part of the diaphragm constraint and determining the distance between these maximum and minimum values.

After the appropriate diaphragm width has been determined, SAP2000 applies a moment that is equal to the specified percent eccentricity times the maximum width of the diaphragm perpendicular to the direction of the seismic loading times the total lateral force applied to the diaphragm. This moment is applied about the diaphragm center of mass to account for the eccentricity.

Click the [Override button](Override_Diaphragm_Eccentricities_Form.md) to modify eccentricities on a diaphragm-by-diaphragm basis.

## See Also

[Define Load Patterns](Define_Load_Patterns.md)

|  |
| --- |
| Access the {Code-Specific} Seismic Loading form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Load Patterns command to display the Define Load Patterns form. 2. Type a unique name for the load pattern in the Load edit box. 3. Select a Quake load type and an Auto Lateral Load other than None. 4. Click the Add New Load Pattern button. 5. Highlight the Quake load definition and click the Modify Lateral Load Pattern button. |

# Current Profile Data Form

A Current Profile defines the velocity and direction of the current as a function of depth (from storm water level to the mud line elevation). By default, a wave load is specified to have no current profile.

- Current Profile Name. Use the default or specify a new name in this edit box.
- Current Blockage Factor edit box. Use the default or specify another value. The current blockage factor accounts for the reduction in current speed at the offshore platform that occurs because the platform causes the current flow to diverge. Typical current blockage factors range from 0.7 to 1.
- Current Profile Stretching Option drop-down list. Two methods are provided to stretch (or compress) the current to the wave surface level at a given horizontal location. These methods are Linear and Nonlinear.
- Number of Elevations edit box. Input the number of vertical elevations at which the current profile data is specified.
- Current Profile Data spreadsheet. After a value has been specified in the Number of Elevations check box and the Enter key on the keyboard has been pressed or another text box on the form is clicked, the number of rows in the  Current Profile Data spreadsheet will change to match the value specified in the Number of Elevations edit box.

Input the vertical elevation (measured from the datum), the current velocity and the current direction at each data point. The current direction is input as an angle in degrees measured counterclockwise from the positive global X axis. Enter the data in descending vertical elevation order. If necessary, click the Order Rows button to reorder the data in correct manner. Also note that the program will automatically order the data in descending vertical elevation order when you click the OK button to close the form.

If the top specified elevation is below the storm water level, the program assumes that the current profile data at the storm water level is the same as the data specified at the top specified elevation. Similarly, if the bottom specified elevation is above the mud line, the program assumes that the current profile data at the mud line is the same as the data specified at the bottom specified elevation.

# Drag and Inertia Coefficients Form

Use the Drag and Inertia Coefficients form to define drag and inertia coefficients for a specified number of vertical elevations. The data can then be used to calculate the wave forces acting on a structure.

- Drag and Inertia Coefficient Name edit box. Use the default or enter a new name in this edit box.
- Number of Elevations edit box. Input the number of vertical elevations at which the drag and inertia coefficient data are specified.
- Drag and Inertia Coefficient Data spreadsheet. After a value has been entered in the Number of Elevations edit box and the Enter key on your keyboard has been depressed or another text box on the form has been clicked, the number of rows in the Drag and Inertia Coefficient Data spreadsheet will change to match the value specified in the Number of Elevations edit box.

Input the vertical elevation (measured from the datum) and drag and inertia coefficients at each data point in descending vertical elevation order. Clicking the Order Rows button will reorder the data. Note, however, that the program will automatically reorder the data in descending vertical elevation order when you click the OK button to close the form.

The drag and inertia coefficient values used at a particular vertical elevation are linearly interpolated from the specified data.

The drag and inertia coefficients are used in Morison’s equation when calculating the wave forces acting on the structure. By default, a wave load is specified to have API Default drag and inertia coefficients. The values for the API Default drag and inertia coefficients depend on whether the location considered is above or below the specified high tide elevation, as shown in the following table.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Location | Drag Coefficient | Inertia Coefficient |
| Above High Tide Elevation (Smooth) | 0.65 | 1.6 |
| Below or At High Tide Elevation (Smooth) | 1.05 | 1.2 |

# Marine Growth Data Form

The marine growth thickness on the structure is specified as a function of depth. By default a wave load is specified to have no marine growth.

- Marine Growth Name edit box. Use the default or specify a new name in this edit box.
- Number of Elevations edit box. Input the number of vertical elevations at which the marine growth data is specified.
- Marine Growth Data spreadsheet. After a value has been entered in the Number of Elevations edit box and the Enter key on your keyboard has been depressed or another text box on the form has been clicked, the number of rows in the Marine Growth Data spreadsheet will change to match the specified Number of Elevations.

Input the vertical elevation (measured from the datum) and marine growth thickness at each data point in descending vertical elevation order. If necessary, click the Order Rows button to reorder them in the correct manner. Note that the program will automatically reorder the data when you click the OK button to close the form.

The marine growth value used at a particular vertical elevation is linearly interpolated from the specified data. For a typical pipe member, two times the marine growth thickness is added to the diameter of the pipe when calculating the force exerted on the pipe by the wave.

# Wave Characteristics Form

Additional form:  Wave Data Table, User Wave Data

Use the Wave Characteristics form to define the characteristics of a wave. The appearance of the form changes depending on the Wave Type selected. The form has the following input options.

- Wave Characteristic Name edit box.  Use the default or specify a new name in this edit box for the wave characteristics definition
- Wave Factors.
- - Wave Kinematics Factor edit box. The wave kinematics factor accounts for wave directional spreading and irregularity in the wave profile shape that is not typically accounted for in two-dimensional wave kinematics. Typical wave kinematics factors range from 0.85 to 1.
  - Storm Water Depth edit box. Storm depth is the depth measured from the storm water level to the mud line. The specified storm water depth is added to the specified mud line elevation to obtain the storm water level.
- Wave Type. Choose to define the wave according to a published theory or define the wave yourself.
- - From Selected Wave Theory option. When this option is selected for wave type, also specify any one of the following Wave Theory types to calculate the wave water particle velocities and accelerations:
  - - Airy Wave Theory (Linear)
    - Stokes Wave Theory. Also specify the Order.
    - Cnoidal Wave Theory. Also specify the Order.
    - Wave Data options. This area of the form displays when From Selected Wave Theory is the Wave Type.
    - - Wave Height edit box. The wave height is distance from the wave trough to the top of the wave. The distance from the storm water level to the top of the wave is equal to half the wave height.
      - Wave Period edit box. The wave period is the period of the wave as seen by a stationary observer.

1. - User Defined option.  When this option is selected for wave type, the wave is specified by defining a rectangular grid of points in a horizontal cut through the wave and then inputting the water particle velocity and acceleration at each point in the grid. The following areas appear on the form for a user defined wave type:
   - - Number of Horiz. Points and Number of Vert Points edit boxes. Use these edit boxes to specify the number of horizontal and vertical points in the grid used to define the wave. After values have been entered in these edit boxes, fill in the horizontal grid line locations and the wave surface elevation (measured from the vertical reference datum; see Global Z Coordinate of Vertical Datum item on the [Wave Load form](Wave_Load_Pattern_Form.md)) at each horizontal grid line in the Horizontal Coordinates and Surface Elevation spreadsheet. The horizontal grid locations should start at zero and proceed in ascending order to define a full wave length cycle. The horizontal grid lines typically are, but are not necessarily, equally spaced.

Similarly, fill in the vertical grid line locations (relative to the vertical reference datum; see Global Z Coordinate of Vertical Datum item on the [Wave Load form](Wave_Load_Pattern_Form.md)) in the Vertical Coordinates spreadsheet. The vertical grid locations should start at the top of the wave and proceed in descending order to the mud line elevation. The vertical grid lines are typically more closely spaced near the top of the wave.

1. 1. 1. - Modify/Show Wave button. Click the Modify/Show Wave button to display the User Wave Data form. The number of horizontal and vertical points that display in the grid area of this form correspond to the Number of Horiz. Points and Number of Vert Points specified on the Wave Characteristics form.

Note:  The User Wave Data form and the Wave Data Table form are essentially the same. The Wave Data Table form is accessed by clicking the Show Wave Table button on this form or on the [Wave Plot form](Wave_Load_Pattern_Form.md).

Choose a Display Option:  All, At Horizontal Coordinate, or At Vertical Coordinate. Use the At Horizontal Coordinate and At Vertical Coordinate drop-down boxes to select the appropriate point. The grid area will update depending on the selection made.

In the grid, the Horiz Loc (Horizontal Location) and Vert from Datum (Vertical from Datum) columns are automatically filled. Fill in the Horiz Wave Vel (Horizontal Wave Velocity), Horiz Wave Acc (Horizontal Wave Acceleration), Vert Wave Vel (Vertical Wave Velocity) and Vert Wave Acc (Vertical Wave Acceleration) columns.

When entering data in the grid, enter zero if the considered point lies above the wave surface. The one exception to this rule is when the wave surface does not lie exactly at a specified grid vertical elevation. In that case, the velocities and accelerations at the wave surface are input at the point that lies immediately above the wave surface. It is understood by the program that these values apply at the wave surface, not at the grid location immediately above the wave surface.

Tip:  When user waves are defined, it may be convenient to first define a wave from theory and then modify the resulting velocities and accelerations as desired. To do this, define the data for the wave from selected theory. Then, click the Show Wave Plot button or Show Wave Table button on the Wave Load form. This will cause the velocities and acceleration to be calculated based on the selected wave theory. Return to the Wave Load form and click the Modify button associated with the wave characteristics to redisplay the Wave Characteristics form. Then change the wave type to user defined and update the data as necessary.

# Wave Load Pattern Form

Additional form:  Wave Plot

Use this form to specify the various parameters for a wave load. Those parameters include the following:

- Wave Characteristics. Use the default, or click the Add or Modify/Show button to access the [Wave Characteristics form](Wave_Characteristics_Form.md).
- Current Profile. Use the default or click the Add or Modify/Show button to access the [Current Profile Data form](Current_Profile_Data_Form.md).
- Marine Growth. Use the default or click the Add or Modify/Show button to access the [Marine Growth Data form](Marine_Growth_Data_Form.md).
- Drag and Inertia Coefficients. Use the default or click the Add or Modify/Show button to access the [Drag and Inertia Coefficients  form](Drag_and_Inertia_Coefficients_Form.md).
- Wind Load. Use the default or click the Add or Modify/Show button to access the [Wave Wind Load  form](Wave_Wind_Load_Pattern_Form.md).
- Include Buoyant Loads check box. When this check box is checked, buoyant loads will be included as part of the wave load pattern. Uncheck the check box to exclude buoyant loads from the wave load pattern.
- Maximum Discretization Segment Size edit box. The wave load discretization is the maximum discretization length for distributed wave loads that are applied to objects in the model. For example, consider a distributed wave load acting along a frame object. A value is calculated for the wave load at points along the frame object that are no further apart than the specified wave load discretization length. The magnitude of the distributed wave load is assumed to vary linearly between these calculated locations.
- Wave Crest Position

1. - Global X Coord of Pt on Initial Crest Position and Global Y Coord of Pt on Initial Crest Position edit boxes. Specify global X and Y coordinates of a point on the initial wave crest position.

1. - Number of Wave Crest Positions Considered edit box. Specify the number of wave crest positions to be considered. The meaning of the number of wave crest positions to be considered is explained by the example shown in the figure, which shows a case of four wave crest positions. The location of the initial wave crest position is uniquely identified by the specified global X and Y coordinates on the initial wave crest and the specified wave approach angle (wave direction).

![](../../../../assets/images/Images/Wave%20Crest%20Positions.jpg)

- Wave Approach Angle in Degrees edit box. Specify the wave approach angle in degrees. The wave direction angle is input as an angle in degrees measured counterclockwise from the positive global X axis.
- Global Z Coordinate of Vertical Datum edit box. Specify the Global Z Coordinate of Vertical Datum to locate the vertical reference datum. All other vertical elevations in the wave load definition, including those used in defining currents, marine growth and drag and inertia coefficients, are specified with reference to this datum. The location of the vertical reference datum is arbitrary. Any convenient location can be selected. One convenient location for the datum is at the storm water level.
- Other Vertical Elevations Relative to Datum
- - Mudline from Datum edit box. Specify the Mudline from Datum to locate the mud line with respect to the vertical reference datum. No wave loads are applied below the mud line.
  - High Tide from Datum edit box. Specify the High Tide from Datum to locate the high tide with respect to the vertical reference datum. The high tide elevation is used when determining the [default drag and inertia coefficients](Drag_and_Inertia_Coefficients_Form.md).
- Water Weight Density edit box. This is the unit weight of the water in Force/Length3 units.
- Show Wave Table button. Click this button to display the Wave Data Table form. This form provides a summary of all input parameters entered using the options on this form and the associated forms for Wave Characteristics, Current Profile, Marine Growth, Drag and Inertia Coefficients, and Wind Load.
- Show Wave Plot button. Click this button to display the Wave Plot form. The form has various options to specify the type of display (values, contours, using arrows, or vertical or horizontal cuts), the item to be displayed (horizontal wave velocity, horizontal current velocity, horizontal total velocity, horizontal wave velocity, vertical wave velocity, vertical wave acceleration) and the Z/X scaling ratio for displaying the plot. The form also has the following commands, check boxes, and buttons:

- Use the File menu > Capture Picture commands on the Wave Plot form to generate a .jpg format file of the Entire Form, the Form without the Title Bar or the Plot Only.
- When the Show Wave Discretization check box is checked, the plot will include the specified wave load discretization length as part of the display.
- With the Show Values at Pointer check box checked, run the cursor over the plot to display the values at the location of the cursor.
- Modify/Show Wave button. Click this button to display the [Wave Characteristics form](Wave_Characteristics_Form.md), which can be used to modify or update the wave definition.
- Refresh View button. Click this button to update the display of the wave.
- Show Wave Table button. Click this button to display the Wave Data Table form (see description above).

For additional clarification of wave loading, click the Help menu > Documentation command and double click on Waves in the SAP2000 Documentation display area. This will display a list of technical notes related to the waves feature in SAP2000. Highlight a document name in the list and click the Display Selected Document button to access the document in .pdf file format.

## See Also

# Wave Wind Load Pattern Form

Wave wind loads act on the portion of the structure that is not submerged. By default a wave load is specified to have no wind load.

- Wave Wind Name edit box. Use the default or specify a new name in this edit box.
- Wind Direction Angle edit box. Specify the wind direction angle. The wind direction angle is input as an angle in degrees measured counterclockwise from the positive global X axis.
- 1-Hour Mean Wind Speed at 32.8 Ft edit box. Specify the one-hour mean wind speed at 32.8 feet (10 meters).
- Averaging Time Period edit box. Specify the averaging time period. The averaging time period, t, is in the range 0 < t ≤ 3600 seconds.
- Mass Density of Air edit box. Specify the mass density of air.
- Typical Shape Coefficient edit box. Specify the typical shape coefficient. The typical shape coefficient applies to all objects in the model unless the wind load shape coefficient for that object has been overwritten in the [wave overwrites](../../../Assign/Fame_Loads/Frame_Loads_Auto_Wave_Loading_Parameters.md).

# Wind Load Pattern Form

Form:  {Code-Specific} Wind Load Pattern

Additional form:  Wind Exposure Width Data

The input required on the form depends on the code, or in the case of a "User Defined" wind load, provide values for Fx, Fy and Mz directly into the spreadsheet cells.

The code-specific forms share the following areas, although the specific parameters in a given area may vary from form to form:

- Exposure and Pressure Coefficients. Choose to define these coefficients by checking the appropriate check box:
- - Exposure from Extents of Rigid Diaphragms option.  If this option is selected, the Wind Exposure Parameters area becomes active. This option allows the same wind load to be applied each time the load pattern is assigned. [Diaphragm constraints](../Joint_Constraints/Diaphragm_Constraints_Form.md) must be [assigned to joint objects](../../Assign/Joint/Joint_Constraints.md) in the model for the auto lateral load pattern to apply wind loads using this option.
  - - Wind Exposure Parameters. Use the available edit boxes to specify the wind direction angle and the windward and leeward coefficients.
    - Modify/Show Exposure Widths button. Click this button to display the Wind Exposure Width Data form. The Exposure Width spreadsheet is inactive when the Calculate from Diaphragm Extents check box is checked. Check the User Defined check box to edit values in the spreadsheet, including Trib (Tributary) Height and Width. If the form is blank, no diaphragms have been assigned to joints in the model.
  - Exposure from Frame and Area Objects option. If this option is selected, the Wind Exposure Parameters area becomes inactive. The windward and leeward coefficients can then be assigned when the wind load is applied to an area object (see [Wind Pressure Coefficients](../../Assign/Area_Loads/Area_Loads_Wind_Pressure_Coefficients.md)). Using this option allows application of wind load coefficients and wind direction on an area-object-by-area-object basis.

If ASCE 7-02 code was selected in the Auto Lateral Load drop-down box on the Define Loads form (the form that precedes use of this form) and the Exposure from Area Objects option is selected, two check boxes will be added in this area of the form:  Include Area Objects check box and Include Frame Objects (Open Structure) check box. Choose the appropriate option for your load definition.

- Exposure Height options. Choose to have the program calculate the exposure height (i.e., use the Program Calculated option), or specify the Maximum and Minimum Global Z values to define a User-Specified exposure height.
- Wind Coefficients options. Specify the wind speed, select the exposure type from the drop-down list, provide an importance factor for the structure, specify a topographical factor, a gust factor, a directionality factor, and when available, a solid/gross area ratio factor.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Mass_Source.htm | Mass Source -->

# Mass Source

Forms:  Mass Source, Mass
Source Data

Use the Define menu > Mass Source command
to access the Mass Source form to specify
how SAP2000 should calculate mass for the model. In SAP2000, mass and
weight serve different functions. Mass is used for the inertia in dynamic
analyses, and for calculating the built-in [acceleration
loads](Load_Cases/Applying_Acceleration_Loads.md). Weight is a [load
that you define](Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) and assign in one or more load patterns (see the topics
in the Assign - Area Loads, Frame Loads, Cable Loads, Tendon Loads, Joint
Loads, Link Loads, and Solid Loads books of this Help), which can then
be applied in one or more static or dynamic [load
cases](Load_Cases/Define_Load_Cases.md). Weight can also be used to define mass, which is the purpose
of the mass source.

Mass Source is a named definition. Most models have a single mass source
that applies to all load cases, and this is the default. Additional mass
sources can be created to handle special situations, such as the dynamics
of a structure supporting different configurations of heavy equipment,
or to explicitly consider the effect of different eccentricities of story
mass on the mode shapes.

On the Mass Source form:

- Use the Add New Mass
  Source, Add Copy of Mass Source,
  Modify/Show Mass Source, and Delete
  Mass Source buttons to create/modify/delete mass source definitions.
- Use the Default Mass Source option to select
  one mass source as the default to be used for all load cases unless
  specified otherwise in the load case definition.
- The default Mass Source cannot be deleted.

Again, for most models, only a single Mass Source is needed.

Using the Add New, Add
Copy, or Modify/Show buttons on the
Mass Source form opens the Mass
Source Data form for a given mass source definition. Use this form
to specify how mass is to be computed for all load cases use this mass
source:

- **Mass
  Source Name**: Used for reference when defining load cases
- **Mass Source**. Choose
  how to define the mass of the structure using either or both of the
  following options:
- - Element Self Mass and Additional Mass option.
    This is the default. With this option, mass is calculated from
    the following specifications:
  - - Mass density specified
      for [materials](Material/Define_Materials.md).
    - Mass specified
      for [link
      properties](../Assign/Link_Support/Link_Support_Properties.md).
    - Additional mass
      assigned directly to the [joints](../Assign/Joint/Joint_Masses.md).
    - Additional line
      mass assigned to [frame](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Line_Mass.md)
      or [cable](../Assign/Cable/Cable_Line_Mass.md)
      objects.
    - Additional
      area mass assigned to [area](../Assign/Area/Area_Mass.md)
      objects.
  - Specified Load Patterns option. With this
    option, mass is calculated from a scaled combination of load patterns
    (see Define Mass Multiplier for Loads, below). The net load acting
    downward (in the negative global Z direction) on each element
    is divided by the acceleration due to gravity, in the current
    units, and is used for the mass in the three translational directions.
    See "Detailed Calculations" below. Load patterns should
    generally represent weight, and should not contain self-equilibrating
    loads, such as temperature and prestress.
  - If
    both options are selected, the total mass is the sum of the mass
    from each option. Be careful not to include load patterns containing
    self-weight when using the Element Self Mass, or the mass may
    be double-counted.

- Mass Multipliers
  for Load Patterns. If the Specified Load
  Patterns option was selected for Mass
  Source, enter a combination of one or more load patterns and
  corresponding multipliers in the table using the Add,
  Modify, and Delete
  buttons. These load patterns will be scaled by the specified factors
  and then added together to determine the mass. Do not include the
  acceleration due to gravity in the multipliers; the load patterns
  should represent weight, and the gravity constant will be applied
  internally.

Detailed Calculations

The mass used by analysis for a given mass source definition is computed
as follows:

1. If the option Specified Load Patterns is
   selected, the loads acting at every joint are computed from the scaled
   combination of the load patterns. Only the component acting in the
   global Z direction at each joint is of interest. This result is then
   divided by the gravitational constant and applied as equal mass to
   the three translational degrees of freedom in the joint. Downward
   loads generate positive mass and upward loads generate negative mass.
2. If the option Element Self Mass and Additional
   Mass is selected, the mass from materials, link properties, joint
   mass, line mass, and area mass are added to the results from step
   1. Except for joint mass, these contributions are always positive
   and equal for the three translational degrees of freedom at each joint.
   Joint mass can be positive or negative and may be different at each
   of the joint's six degrees of freedom.
3. The net result after combining steps 1 and
   2 for any degree of freedom may be positive or negative and will be
   reported as such in the "Assembled Joint Mass" table.
4. During the equation solution, any negative
   mass values that remain after combining mass for constraints are set
   to zero and a warning is issued in the analysis log file.

Using Mass Source

A defined Mass Source can be selected for the following types of load
cases:

- Nonlinear static.
- Nonlinear staged construction
- Nonlinear direct-integration time history

If you do not select a specified Mass Source for these types of load
cases, the Mass Source used will be either the default Mass Source (if
the load case starts from zero initial conditions), or the Mass Source
used in the previous load case (if continuing from another one of these
same three types of load cases).

For all other load cases, a similar rule applies. The default Mass Source
will be used if the load case uses the stiffness from zero load conditions.
Otherwise, the Mass Source used will be the same as for the nonlinear
static, staged-construction, or direct-integration time-history load case
used to calculate the stiffness. Response-spectrum and modal time-history
load cases use the Mass Source of their corresponding modal load case.

# Additional Material Damping Form

Additional form:  Damping Conversion

Use the options on the Additional Material Damping form to specify damping.

- Modal Damping edit box. Enter a value for the damping ratio  (0 <= r < 1) to be used during a [Response Spectrum](../Load_Cases/Response_Spectrum_Form.md) or [Model Time-History](../Load_Cases/Time_History/Nonlinear_Modal_History_Form.md) load case, or a [Direct Integration Time History](../Load_Cases/Time_History/NonLinear_Direct_Integration_History_Form.md) load case where Modal Damping is enabled.
- Viscous Proportional Damping - Mass Coefficient and Stiffness Coefficient edit boxes. Enter values for these parameters that will be used during a [Direct Integration Time History](../Load_Cases/Time_History/NonLinear_Direct_Integration_History_Form.md) load case.
- Hysteretic Proportional Damping - Mass Coefficient and Stiffness Coefficient edit boxes. Enter values for these parameters that will be used during a [Steady State](../Load_Cases/Steady_State_Form.md) or [Power Spectral Density](../Load_Cases/Power_Spectral_Density_Form.md) load case.
- Make Other Damping Similar button. Clicking this button after entering a value for one of the preceding types of damping will cause the program to automatically calculate damping that would be similar for the various types of analysis.  In this way, the "same" damping can be evaluated for different load cases.

After the additional material damping has been specified as part of the material property definition, the additional damping is applied to the model by assigning the material property definition to a selected [area(s)](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md), [frame(s)](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), [cable(s)](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md), [tendon(s)](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) or [solid(s)](../../Assign/Solid/Solid_Properties.md).

|  |

| Access the Additional Material Damping form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to display the Define Materials form. The Define Materials form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). 2. Check the Show Advanced Properties check box. 3. Click the Add Copy of Material button to display the Material Property Options form. 4. Click the Modify/Show Material Properties button to display the Material Property Data form. 5. Click the Material Damping Properties button to access the Additional Material Damping form. |

# Coupled Nonlinear Material Data Form

Use the Coupled Nonlinear Material Data form to specify the coupled nonlinear material property data to be used if property nonlinearity is considered during analysis. Coupled nonlinear material properties are used in coupled layers of nonlinear layered shell properties.

- Material Name display box. The name of the material property to which the nonlinear property data applies appears in this display box.
- Material Type display box: The material type to which the nonlinear property data applies appears in this display box.
- **Coupled Modeling Type Options:** Choose the coupled behavior model and enter the associated parameters as required. The options available depend on the material type.

- None: If this option is chosen, the material property will not have coupled material behavior.
- **Von Mises Plasticity:** This is a three-dimensional plasticity model with the von Mises yield criterion which represents the yielding of a ductile material such as steel. This model considers isotropic and kinematic hardening and does not model strength loss, damage, or fracture. When used in the layered shell, the plane stress condition is assumed. This option is available for all material types except for Concrete.
- **Modified Darwin Pecknold Concrete:** This is a two-dimensional co-axially rotating smeared crack concrete material model. The compression behavior is represented by a multilinear backbone curve, generated based on the uniaxial nonlinear stress-strain behavior of the material (see: *[Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data Form](Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md)*). This model assumes zero tension strength. This option is only available for Concrete materials.
- The behavior of the model is further described in the Technical Note “Modified Darwin-Pecknold 2-D Reinforce Concrete Material Model”. This document can be found in the Manuals subfolder where the software is installed or accessed from inside the software using the menu command Help > Documentation > Technical Notes.

- **Von Mises Plasticity Parameters** area:

For information on the formulation of the model, see the **[Von Mises Plasticity](Von_Mises_Plasticity_Model.md)** topic.

- **Yield Stress:** For material types where the yield stress is specified in the [***Material Property Options*** *form*](Material_Property_Options_Form.md), the display box shows the defined yield stress. For the material type *Other*, specify the yield stress in the edit box.
- **Linear Isotropic Hardening:** Use the checkbox to enable linear isotropic hardening. When enabled, specify the *isotropic hardening modulus* parameter in the edit box.  When applied individually for an effective uniaxial behavior, the post yield stiffness will be equal to (E\*K)/(E + K) where K is the isotropic hardening modulus and E is the elastic modulus.
- **Linear Kinematic Hardening:** Use the checkbox to enable linear kinematic hardening. When enabled, specify the *kinematic hardening modulus* parameter in the edit box.  When applied individually for an effective uniaxial behavior, the post yield stiffness will be equal to (E\*H)/(E + H) where H is the kinematic hardening modulus and E is the elastic modulus.
- **Nonlinear Isotropic Saturation Hardening:** Use the checkbox to enable nonlinear isotropic saturation hardening. When enabled, specify the *ultimate stress as a ratio of the yield stress* and the *hardening rate* parameters in the edit boxes. Saturation hardening produces a nonlinear post-yield hardening curve which approaches the ultimate stress using an exponential decay function. The specified *hardening rate* parameter controls the rate of approaching the ultimate stress. A larger hardening rate means that the post-yield hardening curve is steeper and will approach the ultimate stress faster.

This hardening option can be used to represent the behavior of material which harden to an ultimate stress, such as steel. When applied individually for an effective uniaxial behavior, the stress in the material will not exceed the ultimate stress. Note that the parameter *ultimate stress as a ratio of the yield stress* must be strictly greater than unity.

Note: All selected hardening options will be applied additively.

- **Show Effective Uniaxial Stress-Strain Plot** button: Click this button to display the [***Effective Uniaxial Stress-Strain Plot for Coupled Material*** *form*](Effective_Uniaxial_Stress-Strain_Plot_for_Coupled_Material_Form.md). That form shows an effective uniaxial stress-strain plot for the specified coupled material property data. For Von Mises Plasticity, the effective uniaxial behavior represents the axial behavior of the model where all other components are stress-free, such as a steel coupon test. For Modified Darwin Pecknold Concrete, the effective uniaxial behavior represents the behavior of unreinforced concrete without including biaxial effects.
