# Define Materials

Forms:  Define Materials, Add Material Property, Material Property Data

Code-specified and other pre-defined material properties are defined in the installed files “CSiMaterialLibrary\*.xml” located in the subfolder “Property Libraries” under the SAP2000 installation folder. Additional material property libraries that use the “CSiMaterialLibrary.xsd” schema may also be added by the user to this subfolder and/or to the subfolder “Property Libraries” under the user settings folder where the “SAP2000 v18.ini” file is located.

These files are first read in alphabetical order from the installation subfolder, then from the user settings subfolder. Any duplicated properties will use the values in the definition read last. Within each file, properties are grouped under user-defined Regions (e.g., China, Europe, or USA). Within regions, properties are grouped under user-defined Standards (e.g., ASTM A572). Within Standards, individual materials are defined to be of a certain type (concrete, steel, aluminum, cold-formed, rebar, tendon, or other) and identified by a user-defined label called Grade. The set (Region, Standard, type, Grad) uniquely identifies a material and determines whether or not it is duplicated within a file or in multiple files.

Use the Define menu > Materials command to add, modify, or delete a material property definition. The material property definitions are then used in defining the structural objects ([frame sections](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md), [cable sections](../Section_Properties/Cable_Sections/Cable_Sections.md), [tendon sections](../Section_Properties/Tendon_Sections/Tendon_Sections.md), [area sections](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md), [solid properties](../Section_Properties/Solid_Property/Define_Solid_Property.md)).

TIP:  The forms described in this topic also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md).

1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to access the Define Materials form.
2. Click the appropriate button to complete the required action:

   - Add New Material button. Click this button to access the Add Material Property form. Use this form to select the region,  material type, standard, and grade that are pre-defined in the CSiMaterialLibrary\*.xml mentioned above.
   - 1. Select a Region from the drop-down list.
     2. Select the Material Type from the drop-down list.
     3. Select a Standard from the drop-down list.
     4. Select a Grade from the drop-down list.
     5. Click the OK button to close the Add Material Property form and return to the Define Materials form. The newly defined material property will be highlighted in the Materials list box.
     6. Highlight the newly defined definition and click the Modify/Show Material button to display the Material Property Data form and review, and where appropriate, modify the specifications for the definition.

A built-in Region, Standard, and Grade called "User" are also available for each material type. The corresponding properties can be directly edited by the user and do not make use of the pre-defined materials in the property libraries. The name "User" is reserved and should not be used in the material property file libraries.

Note: The Modify/Show Notes button on the Material Property Data form can be used to access the [Material Notes form](Notes_Form.md). Use the form to add Material Notes to the model file.

1. - Add Copy of Material button. Highlight the name of a previously defined material in the Materials area of the form and click this button to create a copy of the selected material that can be further modified.
   - 1. Click the Add Copy of Material button to access the Material Property Data form with a copy of the previously selected material property. Use the options on the form to modify the material property as desired.
     1. - Material Name and Display Color. The program will suggest a name and display color for the material definition. Use the suggestions, or type a name in the Material Name edit box, or click the Color box to access the Color form and choose a new display color.
        - Material Type. Choose a material type from this drop-down list. The selection made here determines the other parameters to be specified for the definition. This field is often fixed based on the material type selected when adding the initial material property.
        - Modify/Show Notes button. Click this button to access the [Material Notes form](Notes_Form.md).
        - Weight and Mass, Isotropic Property Data and Other Properties for {Steel, Concrete, Aluminum, Cold Formed, Rebar, Tendon} Materials areas. Reviews the parameters specified in these areas of the form, and where necessary, type revised values in the edit boxes. The Units drop-down list can be used to change the units on this form to facilitate data entry for the various parameters.
        - Switch to Advanced Property Display check box. Check this check box to access the [Material Property Options form](Material_Property_Options_Form.md). Use the form to specify advanced materials properties and to access additional forms related to nonlinear material data, damping properties and thermal properties.

1. - 2. Click the OK button to close the Material Property Data form and return to the Define Materials form. The newly named material property will be listed in the Materials list box. After the property has been defined, use the commands on the Assign menu to assign the property to an [area(s)](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md), [frame section(s)](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), [cable(s)](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md), [tendon(s](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md)) or [solid(s)](../../Assign/Solid/Solid_Properties.md).
   - Modify/Show Material button.
   1. 1. Highlight the name of the previously defined material in the Materials area of the form.
      2. Click the Modify/Show Material button to access the Material Property Data form.
      3. Use that form to change the appropriate entries.
      4. Click the OK button to close the form and return to the Define Materials form.
   - Delete Material button.
   - 1. Highlight the name of the previously defined material in the Materials area of the form.
     2. Click the Delete Material button to delete the selected definition.
   - Show Advanced Properties check box. Check this check box and then click the Add New Material button to access the [Material Property Options form](Material_Property_Options_Form.md). Use that form to specify advanced materials properties and to access additional forms related to nonlinear material data, damping properties, time dependent properties (concrete and tendon material properties only), and thermal properties (heat transfer).

Example:  Definition of materials is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md), [Problem B](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md), [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem D](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_D.md) and [others](../../../Example_Problems/Problems_Introduction.md).

## See Also

[Area - Material Property Overwrites](../../Assign/Area/Area_Material_Property_Overwrites.md)

[Frame - Material Property Overwrites](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Material_Property_Overwrites.md)

[Cable - Material Property Overwrites](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Material_Property_Overwrites.md)

# Effective Uniaxial Stress-Strain Plot for Coupled Material Form

Use the Effective Uniaxial Stress-Strain Plot for Coupled Material form to show an effective uniaxial stress-strain plot for the coupled material property defined in the ***Coupled Nonlinear Material Data*** form. The plot shows the effective uniaxial behavior under two cycles of positive and negative strain to demonstrate the cyclic behavior of the material. The maximum strain of each cycle can be specified in the Plot Control Parameters. To view the backbone curve of the material, set the maximum strain of the cycles equal to or greater than the maximum expected strain for the material.

Note: The effective uniaxial behavior represents the behavior of a single axial component in the model with the following assumptions on the behavior of the other components. For Von Mises Plasticity, the effective uniaxial behavior represents the axial behavior of the model where all other components are stress-free, such as a steel coupon test. For Modified Darwin Pecknold Concrete, the effective uniaxial behavior represents the axial behavior of unreinforced concrete without including biaxial effects.

- Material Property Name display box: The material definition to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Coupled Modeling Type display box: The coupled modeling type to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Material Type display box: The material type to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Plot Control Parameters:
- - Background box: This box shows the color that is used for the background. Click this color box or the *Change* button to display the Color form and select a revised display color for the background.
  - **Stress-strain curve** box. This box shows the color that is used to display the curve. Click this color box or the *Change* button to display the Color form and select a revised display color for the stress-strain curve.
  - **Snap Point** box. This box shows the color that is used to display the snap point. Click this color box or the *Change* button to display the Color form and select a revised display color for the snap point.
  - **Show Curve Points** check box. When this check box is checked, the points which form the curve are shown as colored dots.
  - **Disable Snap** check box. When this check box is unchecked and the mouse is moved over the plot, the cursor snaps to the curve and a colored dot shows the location of the cursor. Check this check box to allow the cursor to be move anywhere over the plot.
  - **Maximum Strain** edit boxes. Use these edit boxes to define the maximum strain, in absolute value, for each of the two strain cycles shown on the plot.
  - **Start Cycle in Negative Direction** check box. Check this check box to change the direction of the cyclic behavior so that strain cycles in the negative direction first.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Material/Material_Property_Options_Form.htm | Material Property Options Form -->

# Material Property Options Form

Additional form:  Material Property Data

Use the Material Property Options form to specify advanced materials properties and to access additional forms related to nonlinear material data, damping properties and thermal properties.

- Material Name edit box. Use the suggested name or type a new name in the edit box.
- Material Notes Modify/Show button.  Click this button to access the [Material Notes form](Notes_Form.md). Use the form to add Material Notes to the model file.
- Material Type drop-down list. Choose the material type from the drop-down list.
- Directional Symmetry Type drop-down list. Select a directional symmetry type from the drop-down list.
- - Isotropic - The behavior of an isotropic material is independent of the direction of loading or the orientation of the material. In addition, shearing behavior is uncoupled from extensional behavior and is not affected by temperature change.
  - Orthotopic - The behavior of an orthotropic material can be different in each of the three local coordinate directions. However, shearing behavior is uncoupled from extensional behavior and is not affected by temperature change.
  - Anisotropic - The behavior of an anisotropic material can be different in each of the three local coordinate directions. In addition, shearing behavior can be fully coupled with extensional behavior and can be affected by temperature change.
  - Uniaxial - This type is intended for use with rebar material types.
- Display Color. The color shown will be used to display the objects to which the material property is assigned. Click the color box to access the Color form and select another display color, as necessary.
- Modify/Show Material Properties button.
- - When the Material Properties are Temperature Dependent check box is checked, and the Modify/Show Material Properties button is clicked, the [Temperature Dependent Material Properties form](Temperature_Dependent_Material_Properties.md) will display. Use the form to specify temperatures at which associated specified material property parameters apply.
  - When the Material Properties are Temperature Dependent check box is unchecked, and the Modify/Show Material Properties button is clicked, the Material Property Data form will display with parameters specific to the selection made in the Directional Symmetry Type drop-down list (on the Material Property Options form). Revise the modulus of elasticity, Poisson's ratio, coefficient of thermal expansion, the weight and mass or the steel materials  as needed to achieve the required material property definition. In addition, the form has the following buttons to allow specification of nonlinear properties, damping properties, time dependent properties (for concrete and tendon material properties only), and thermal properties (heat transfer).
  - **Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data** button. Click this button to access the [Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data form](Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md). Use that form to specify the uniaxial stress-strain curve and the hysteresis type to be used in a nonlinear analysis. That form defines the uniaxial material behavior, used in fiber hinges and directional layers of nonlinear layered shell properties.
  - **Coupled Nonlinear Data** button. Click this button to access the *[Coupled Nonlinear Material Data form](Coupled_Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md)*. Use that form to specify the coupled modeling type and parameters to be used in a nonlinear analysis. That form defines the coupled material behavior, used in coupled layers of nonlinear layered shell properties.

**Note**: Coupled nonlinear material data is only available if the *Direction Symmetry Type* of the material property is *Isotropic* .

1. - Time Dependent Properties button. Click this button to access the [Time Dependent Properties for {Concrete or Steel} form](Time_Dependent_Properties_for_Concrete_Tendons_Form.md).
   - Material Damping Properties button. Click this button to access the [Additional Material Damping form](Additional_Material_Damping_Form.md) and add material modal damping for Response Spectrum, Time History, Steady State, and Power Spectral Density load cases.
   - Thermal Properties button. Click this button to access the [Temperature Dependent Properties form](Thermal_Properties_Form.md). Use that form to specify the heat capacity and the thermal conductivity matrix to specify heat transfer parameters as part of the material property definition.
   - Stress-Strain Curve Definitions button. Click this button to access the [Material Stress-Strain Curve Data form](Material_Stress_Strain_Curve_Plot_Form.md).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Material Property Options form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to access the Define Materials form. The Define Materials form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). 2. Check the Show Advanced Properties check box. 3. Click the Add New Material button or highlight a previously defined material property in the Materials display list and click the Add Copy of Material or Modify/Show Material button. |

# Material Property Time Dependent Plot Form

Use the Material Property Time Dependent Plot form to view a plot of the temperature dependent property definition.

- Material Name, Material Type, Symmetry Type and Property Temperature display boxes. These display boxes identify the material name and type, and the directional symmetry and property temperature (if any has been specified) for the material property definition as specified using the Material Property Data form.
- Select Item to Plot drop-down list. Choose the time dependence parameter to be plotted. The options available depend on the selections made on the Time Dependent Properties for {Concrete, Tendons} form.
- Time Range Plotted and From (Days) and To (Days) edit boxes. Use the edit boxes to specify the time range for the plot.
- Plot Scale Type and Log Scale for Horizontal Axis and Log Scale for Vertical Axes options.
- Background drop-down list. Use the Auto selection or choose another background color from this drop-down list for the plot display.
- Curve Color box. This box shows the color that is used to display the curve. Click this color box to display the Color form and select a revised display color for the stress-strain curve.
- Add Let and Right Borders and Add Top and Bottom Borders check boxes. Check these check boxes to add a border area around the plot display.
- Disable Snap check box. When this check box is unchecked and the mouse is moved over the plot, the cursor snaps to the curve and a red dot shows the location of the cursor. Check this check box to allow the cursor to be move anywhere over the plot.
- Slide bar and Days edit box and Vert display box. Use the slide bar beneath the plot to move the mouse cursor along the curve even when the Disable Snap check box is checked. The location of the mouse pointer relative to the Days (horizontal axis) and the specified value (vertical axis) for the Selected Item to Plot is shown in the edit and display boxes. To review a particular day, enter a value in the Days edit box.
- File menu. Use the commands on the file menu to print the plot, display tables and to save the plot in a .bmp file format.
- - Print Setup for Graphics. Use this command to access the Print Setup form and specify the printer, paper size and orientation for printing the plot.
  - Use Color Printer. Use this command to send the plot as a color print, assuming a color printer is available.
  - Print Graphics. Use this command to send the plot to the printer immediately.
  - Display Tables. Use this command to access the Choose Tables For form and select the types of data to be displayed in tabular format.
  - Capture Picture. Use this command to save the plot as a .bmp file. This command has sub commands to save the Entire Screen, the Form Including the Title Bar, the Form Without the Title Bar, and the Plot Only area on the form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Material Property Time Dependent Plot form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to display the Define Materials form. The Define Materials form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). 2. Check the Show Advanced Properties check box. 3. Click the Add New Material button to display the Material Property Options form. 4. Select Concrete or Tendon in the Material Type drop-down list. 5. Click the Modify/Show Material Properties button to access the Material Property Data form.          Note that if the Material Properties are Temperature Dependent check box is checked when the Modify/Show Material Properties button is clicked, the [Temperature Dependent Material Properties form](Temperature_Dependent_Material_Properties.md) will display; specify the required temperature and then click the appropriate button to access the Material Property Data form 6. Click the Time Dependent Properties button to access the Time Dependent Properties for {Concrete, Tendons} form. 7. Click the Show Plot button. |

# Material Stress-Strain Curve Plot Form

Additional form:  Mander concrete Stress-Strain Data

Use the Material Stress-Strain Curve Data form to display the material stress-strain curve plot as defined using the options on the Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data form.

- Material Property Name display box. The material definition to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Material Type display box. The material type to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Symmetry Type display box. The directional symmetry type to which the stress-strain curve applies appears in this display box.
- Property Temperature display box. If the material property has been defined as temperature dependent, this area is added to the form and the display box shows the temperature at which the specified parameters apply.
- Plot Control Parameters
- - Background drop-down list. Use the Auto selection or choose another background color from this drop-down list for the plot display.
  - Curve Color box. This box shows the color that is used to display the curve. Click this color box to display the Color form and select a revised display color for the stress-strain curve.
  - Add Left and Right Borders and Add Top and Bottom Borders check boxes. Check these check boxes to add a border area around the plot display.
  - Reverse Plot Axes Direction check box. Check this check box to change the orientation of the plot by reversing the positive and negative ends of the X and Y axes of the plot.
  - Disable Snap check box. When this check box is unchecked and the mouse is moved over the plot, the cursor snaps to the curve and a red dot shows the location of the cursor. Check this check box to allow the cursor to be move anywhere over the plot.
- Mander Concrete Model:
- - Modify/Show Mander Data button. This button is visible only for Mander Concrete stress-strain curves (Mander was selected from the Stress-Strain Curve Definition Options drop-down list on the Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data form) . Clicking this button accesses the Mander Concrete Stress-Strain Data form. Select a Mander Type and if the Mander Type is Confined, specify a concrete frame section property (use the drop-down list), or specify user-defined reinforcing data. After the frame section or reinforcing data has been specified, click the Update Plot button to review how the section properties affect the stress-strain curve plot. This data is for display purposes in the forms only; the data specified has no effect on the model.
- Slide bar and Mouse Pointer Location Strain and Stress display boxes. Use the slide bar beneath the plot to move the mouse cursor along the curve even when the Disable Snap check box is checked. The coordinates of the mouse pointer are shown in the Strain and Stress display boxes.
- File menu. Use the commands on the file menu to print the plot, display tables and to save the plot in a .bmp file format.
- - Print Setup for Graphics. Use this command to access the Print Setup form and specify the printer, paper size and orientation for printing the plot.
  - Use Color Printer. Use this command to send the plot as a color print, assuming a color printer is available.
  - Print Graphics. Use this command to send the plot to the printer immediately.
  - Display Tables. Use this command to access the Choose Tables For form and select the types of data to be displayed in tabular format.
  - Capture Picture. Use this command to save the plot as a .bmp file. This command has sub commands to save the Entire Screen, the Form Including the Title Bar, the Form Without the Title Bar, and the Plot Only area on the form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Material Stress-Strain Curve Plot form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to display the Define Materials form. The Define Materials form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). 2. Check the Show Advanced Properties check box. Then do one of the following to display the Material Property Data form:     - Click the Add New Material button.    - Highlight an existing material definition in the Materials list and click the Modify/Show Material button. 3. Click the Nonlinear Uniaxial Material Data button to display the Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data form. 4. Click the Show Stress-Strain Plot or Show Plot button, depending on whether the stress-strain curve is parametrically defined or user defined. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Material/Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.htm | Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data Form -->

# Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data Form

Use the Uniaxial Nonlinear Material Data form to specify the uniaxial nonlinear material property data to be used if property nonlinearity is considered during analysis. Nonlinear uniaxial material properties are used in fiber hinges and directional layers of nonlinear layered shell properties.

- Material Name display box. The name of the material property to which the nonlinear property data applies appears in this display box.
- Material Type display box. The material type to which the nonlinear property data applies appears in this display box.
- Property Temperature display box. If the material property has been defined as temperature dependent, this area is added to the form and the display box shows the temperature at which the specified parameters apply.
- Hysteresis Type drop-down list. Select the hysteresis type for the curve and enter the associated parameters as required. See [Hysteresis Types](../../Assign/Hysteresis_Types.md) for more information.
- Drucker-Prager Parameters and the Friction Angle and Dilatational Angle edit boxes. When available, use the defaults or type values in degrees in the edit boxes.
- Stress-Strain Curve Definition Options. Choose to define the stress-strain curve parametrically or by specifying values directly.
- - Parametric option and drop-down list and Convert to User Defined button.
  - - Parametric Strain Data area. Use the suggested default values or enter revised values in the edit boxes in this area to specify the Strain at the Unconfined Compressive Strength and the Ultimate Unconfined Strain Capacity.
    - Show Stress-Strain Plot button. Click this button to display the [Material Stress-Strain Curve Plot form](Material_Stress_Strain_Curve_Plot_Form.md).
  - User Defined option. When this option is selected, specify the number of points to be used to define the plot in the Number of Points in Stress-Strain Curve edit box. The number specified in this edit box determines the number of rows of data required in the  spreadsheet in the User Stress-Strain Curve Data area. Use the default or enter revised values in the cells in the Strain and Stress columns
  - - Order Rows button. After entering data in this spreadsheet, click this button to reorder the rows in ascending order, which is necessary for the data to plot correctly.
    - Show Plot button. Click this button to display the [Material Stress-Strain Curve Plot form](Material_Stress_Strain_Curve_Plot_Form.md).

After the nonlinear data has been specified as part of the material property definition, the definition can be assigned to a selected [area(s)](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md), [frame(s)](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), [cable(s)](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md), [tendon(s)](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) or [solid(s)](../../Assign/Solid/Solid_Properties.md).

# Notes Form

Use the Material Notes,
 Frame Section Property Notes, Tendon Section Notes,
Cable Section Notes,
Area Section Notes,
Solid Property Notes,
Link Notes,  Frequency Dependent Link Notes,
Load Pattern Notes, Load Case Notes and
Load Combination Notes forms to add notes
to the model file. Type the notes directly into the large text box area.

The forms have several toolbar buttons for standard
Windows type operations that can be used to manipulate the information
posted to the notes. Those operations include the following:

- Open an existing notes
  file to add additional information.
- Save the notes file
  to a user specified location in a Word rich text format (.rtf) file.
- Print the notes immediately
  to a printer.
- Cut, Copy, and Paste
  text within the notes file and from other application, such as Word
  or Excel.
- Undo and Redo the last
  action taken in the Notes form.
- Edit the font of selected
  text, including size and typeface.
- Apply boldfaced type
  to selected text.
- Apply Italic type to
  selected text.
- Underline selected text.
- Change the color of
  selected text.
- Align text along the
  left margin, in the center, or along the right margin.
- Apply bullets to selected
  text.
- Increase and decrease
  the indentation of text.

The commands on the File,
Edit, and Format
menus generally duplicate the operations completed using the toolbar buttons.

# Temperature Dependent Material Properties

Use the Temperature Dependent Material Properties form to designate temperature values at which specified parameters apply.

- Material Name, Material Type and Symmetry Type display boxes. These display boxes identify the material name and type, and the directional symmetry for the material property definition as specified using the Material Property Options form.
- Add Properties at New Temperature button.
- 1. Click this button to access the Material Property Data form.
  2. Enter a temperature value in the Degrees F edit box.
  3. Use the default values or type revised values for the other parameters on the form. Use the buttons on the form as needed to specify [uniaxial nonlinear material data](Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [coupled nonlinear material data](Coupled_Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [material damping properties](Additional_Material_Damping_Form.md), [time dependent properties](Time_Dependent_Properties_for_Concrete_Tendons_Form.md), and [thermal properties (heat transfer)](Thermal_Properties_Form.md).
  4. Click the OK button to return to the Temperature Dependent Material Properties form.
  5. Repeat Steps 1 through 4 as needed, then click the OK button to return to the Material Property Options form.
- Add Copy of Properties at Selected Temperature button. Use this button to add another temperature dependent material property.
- 1. Highlight an existing material temperature in the Temperatures display list.
  2. Click the Add Copy of Properties at Selected Temperature button to access the  Material Property Data form. The form will be pre-loaded with the parameters associated with the temperature selected in Step 1.
  3. Use the Degrees F edit box to specify a temperature for the material property definition.
  4. Revise the other parameters on the form as necessary. Use the buttons on the form as needed to specify [uniaxial nonlinear material data](Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [coupled nonlinear material data](Coupled_Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [material damping properties](Additional_Material_Damping_Form.md), [time dependent properties](Time_Dependent_Properties_for_Concrete_Tendons_Form.md), and [thermal properties (heat transfer)](Thermal_Properties_Form.md).
  5. Click the OK button to return to the Temperature Dependent Material Properties form.
  6. Repeat Steps 1 through 5 as needed, then click the OK button to return to the Material Property Options form.
- Modify/Show Properties at Selected Temperature button. Use this button to modify an existing temperature dependent material property without adding another definition.

1. 1. Highlight an existing material temperature in the Temperatures display list.
   2. Click the Add Copy of Properties at Selected Temperature button to access the  Material Property Data form.
   3. Use the Degrees F edit box to specify a temperature for the material property definition.
   4. Revise the other parameters on the form as necessary. Use the buttons on the form as needed to specify [uniaxial nonlinear material data](Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [coupled nonlinear material data](Coupled_Nonlinear_Material_Data_Form.md), [material damping properties](Additional_Material_Damping_Form.md), [time dependent properties](Time_Dependent_Properties_for_Concrete_Tendons_Form.md), and [thermal properties (heat transfer)](Thermal_Properties_Form.md).
   5. Click the OK button to return to the Temperature Dependent Material Properties form.
   6. Repeat Steps 1 through 5 as needed, then click the OK button to return to the Material Property Options form.

- Delete Properties at Selected Temperature button.
- 1. Highlight an existing material temperature in the Temperatures display list.
  2. Click the Delete Properties at Selected Temperature button to delete the selected temperature dependent material property definition.

# Thermal Properties Form

Use the Thermal Properties form to specify a heat capacity value and values for the thermal conductivity matrix to specify parameters for heat transfer as part of the material property definition.

After the temperature dependent properties have been specified as part of the material property definition, the properties are applied to the model by assigning the material property definition to a selected [area(s)](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md), [frame(s)](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), [cable(s)](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md), [tendon(s)](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) or [solid(s)](../../Assign/Solid/Solid_Properties.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Material/Time_Dependent_Properties_for_Concrete_Tendons_Form.htm | Time Dependent Properties for Concrete Tendons Form -->

# Time Dependent Properties for {Concrete, Tendons} Form

Use the Time Dependent Properties for Concrete form to choose CEB-FIP 90, CEB-FIP 2010, ACI 209R-92, or User and then, where needed, specify the Compressive Strength and Stiffness, Creep, and Shrinkage factors for the material definition.

Simple scale factors may be specified to adjust the time-dependent concrete behavior for the purpose of performing sensitivity studies. The scale factor on the modulus of elasticity directly multiplies the Young’s modulus and shear modulus of the material for any staged-construction load case that considers time-dependent behavior, and consequently affects dependent load cases. No other load cases are affected. The scale factors on creep and shrinkage directly multiply the corresponding creep or shrinkage strains computed during any time-dependent staged-construction load case.

Use the Time Dependent Properties for Tendons form to choose CEB-FIP and then specify if time dependence is to be considered for Prestressing Steel Relaxation, the relaxation analysis type, and the CEB-FIP class, where appropriate.

When selecting the User option, full control is given for defining the following data:

- Stiffness versus age, defined as a multiplier of the material modulus of elasticity.
- Creep coefficient versus days since loading, for multiple ages at loading. Interpolation will be used between the different age at loading curves.
- Shrinkage strain versus age.

Use the Time Dependent Properties for Tendons form to choose CEB-FIP and then specify if time dependence is to be considered for Prestressing Steel Relaxation, the relaxation analysis type, and the CEB-FIP class, where appropriate.

A simple scale factor may be specified to adjust the time-dependent tendon behavior for the purpose of performing sensitivity studies. The scale factor directly multiplies the relaxation strain computed during any time-dependent staged-construction load case.

Click the Show Plot button on the forms to display the [Material Property Time Dependence Plot form](Material_Property_Time_Dependent_Plot_Form.md).

- Material Name, Material Type, Symmetry Type and Property Temperature display boxes. These display boxes identify the material name and type, and the directional symmetry and property temperature (if any has been specified) for the material property definition as specified using the Material Property Data form.
- Show Plot button. Click this button to access the Material Property Time Dependent Plot form. Use the form to view a plot of the temperature dependent property definition.

After the time dependent properties have been specified as part of the material property definition, they will be applied to those [area(s)](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md), [frame(s)](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md),and  [tendon(s)](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) whose section properties use these materials. For areas, only homogeneous shell (thin and thick) section properties are considered..

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Time Dependent Properties for {Concrete, Tendons} form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Materials command to display the Define Materials form. The Define Materials form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available materials, such as the Material drop-down list on the [Shell Section Data form](../Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), or the [{Frame Section Type} Data forms](../Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). 2. Check the Show Advanced Properties check box. 3. Click the Add New Material button to display the Material Property Options form. 4. Select Concrete or Tendon in the Material Type drop-down list. 5. Click the Modify/Show Material Properties button to access the Material Property Data form.          Note that if the Material Properties are Temperature Dependent check box is checked when the Modify/Show Material Properties button is clicked, the [Temperature Dependent Material Properties form](Temperature_Dependent_Material_Properties.md) will display; click the appropriate button to access the Material Property Data form 6. Click the Time Dependent Properties button. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Material/Von_Mises_Plasticity_Model.htm | Von Mises Plasticity Model -->

# Von Mises Plasticity Model

**Von
Mises Plasticity Model**

The plasticity model used in this program is based on the von Mises
(J2) yield criterion and an infinitesimal, rate-independent plasticity
formulation using the implicit backward-Euler difference scheme outlined
in “Computational Inelasticity” by J.C. Simo and T.J.R. Hughes. The model
uses the following flow rule and hardening law:

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image002.png)

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image004.png)

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image006.png)

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image008.png)

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image010.png)

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image012.png)

where:

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image014.png) is the stress tensor,

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image016.png) is the plastic-strain tensor,

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image018.png)is the *yield
stress* parameter,

*K* is the *isotropic
hardening modulus* parameter,

*H*
is the *kinematic hardening modulus*
parameter,

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image020.png) is the ultimate stress, equal
to the ![](../../../assets/images/clip_image018.png) multiplied by the parameter
*ultimate stress as a ratio of
the yield stress*,

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image022.png) is the *hardening
rate* parameter, and

![](../../../assets/images/clip_image024.png) is the *plastic
multiplier,* an internal
state variable that indicates plastic flow, computed iteratively. 

## References

J.C. Simo and T.J.R. Hughes, 1998. *Computational
Inelasticity*, Springer-Verlag New York, Inc., New York, N.Y.

# Define  - Moving Load Case Results Saved

Form:  Moving Load Case Results Saved

The options on this form can be used  to selectively control what information is calculated for joints and frame objects in the computationally intensive [moving-load analysis](../Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md).

1. Response Category check boxes. Check each of the response categories to be analyzed (Displacements, Reactions, and so forth).
2. Select Group drop-down list. Choose the [group](../Groups.md) for which responses are to be computed. The default is ALL.

Important: If no groups are selected for response calculation, no results will be produced for moving-load analysis.

3. Correspondence check boxes. Check the Correspondence check box associated with a response category to use the Max/Min Correspondence in design of frame sections when using moving loads. This is a very time-intensive operation so use it only when it is required.
4. Method of Calculation. Select Exact or Refinement Level and enter a value in the edit box. The value entered can be any positive integer. This feature provides a "fast analysis option" for preliminary analysis. The larger the integer the greater the level of refinement.
5. Allow loads to reduce response severity check box. Check this check box to moderate the severity of the response based on the loads specified for the moving load analysis.

## See Also

|  |
| --- |
| Click the [Define menu > Moving Loads > Moving Load Case  Responses command](Define_Moving_Loads.md) to access the  Moving Load Case Response Requests form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Moving_Loads/Define_Moving_Loads.htm | Define Moving Loads -->

# Define - Moving Loads

Use the Define menu > Moving Loads commands to specify paths, vehicle loads and classes, and moving load case results to enable moving-load analysis. Generally, the process requires creating the following definitions:

- Paths are defined and then frame objects are assigned to the defined paths.
- Vehicles loads are defined and then the defined loads are added to one or more vehicle classes.
- The moving load case results to be saved are defined, which specifies what information is calculated for joints and frame objects, thereby controlling the complexity of, and thus the time required to complete, the analysis.
- The defined paths, vehicle loads, vehicle classes, and moving load case results to be saved are then used in defining a [Moving Load analysis](../Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md).

Use the following Define menu > Moving Loads subcommands to prepare for the analysis:

- Paths. Use the Define menu > Moving Loads > Paths command to define paths that describe how vehicles move on the structure. A path can be defined as a chain of frame objects, with an optional centerline offset if the vehicles are located to one side or the other of the frame object. Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Paths command to access the [Define Paths form](Define_Paths.md).

- Vehicles. Use the Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicles command to define Vehicle loads. Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicles command to access the [Define Vehicles form](Define_Vehicles.md). After defining vehicles, they must be added to one or more Vehicle Classes before they can be assigned to paths in a moving-load analysis, even if a Vehicle Class contains only a single vehicle.

- Vehicle Classes. Use the Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicle Classes command to specify sets of one or more vehicles that can be assigned to act on a path(s) in a moving-load analysis. Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicle Classes command to access the [Define Vehicle Classes form](Define_Vehicle_Classes.md). Only one vehicle in a class acts on the path at a time. Results are reported for the vehicle causing the most severe response.

- Moving Load Case Results Saved. Use the Define menu > Moving Loads > Moving Load Case Results Saved command to selectively control what information is calculated for joints and frame objects in the computationally intensive moving-load analysis. This command is useful in modifying the time required to complete the analysis. Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Moving Load Case Results Saved command to access the [Moving Load Case Results Saved form](Define_Moving_Load_Case_Results_Saved.md). Use that form to specify the response categories to be analyzed and the calculation method to be used.

# Define - Paths

Form:  Define Paths

Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Paths command to access the Define Paths form. Use the buttons on that form to define paths for moving loads using  frame objects.

- Add New Path Defined From Frames button. This button is available if at least one [straight frame object has been drawn](../../Draw/Draw_Frame_Cable_Tendon.md) in the model. Click this button to display the [Path Data form](Path_Data_Form.md) and specify a new path definition. After paths have been defined using the  Path Data form, use the [Assign menu > Frame > Paths command](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Path.md) to assign frame objects to the defined path.
- Add Copy of Path button. Highlight the path to be copied in the Paths display area. Then, click the Add Copy of Path button to display the  Path Data form and add another path to the model based on the originally selected path.

- Modify/Show Path button. Highlight a previously defined path definition to display the  Path Data form. Use the form to make the necessary revisions.
- Delete Path button. Highlight a previously defined path definition and click the Delete Path button to delete the selected path definition.

Use the Define menu > Moving Loads  > Vehicle Classes command  to access the Define Vehicle Classes form and add, modify, or delete vehicle classes.

# Define - Vehicles

Form:  Define Vehicles

Use the Define menu > Moving Loads  > Vehicles command access the Define Vehicles form and  add, modify, or delete vehicle definitions that can be used to load paths for moving load  analysis.  Use the buttons on the form to complete the required actions.

- Add Vehicles button. Clicking this button will display the [Vehicle Data form](Vehicle_Data_Form.md). Use that form to specify the vehicle name and load parameters, including elevation, load length type, and other parameters.

2. Click the Modify/Show Vehicle button to access the Vehicle Data form; use the form to modify the Vehicle definition.

2. Click the Delete Vehicle button to delete the vehicle definition.

After vehicles have been defined, use the [Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicle Classes command](Define_Vehicle_Classes.md) to add the defined vehicle to one or more Vehicle Classes.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Moving_Loads/Move_Path_Form.htm | Move Path Form -->

# Move Path Form

Use the options on the Move Path form to change the path offset relative to the frame object, depending on how the form was accessed (see below).

- Change Offset by Specified Amount option. This option changes the offset at each station along the path by the value entered in the Centerline Offset edit box.
- Move Start to Specified Offset option. This option calculates the difference between the current path centerline offset at the first station along the path and the value entered in the Centerline Offset edit box. The offset at each station along the path is then changed by the calculated difference.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Move Path  form as follows:    Method 1   1. Click the Define menu > Moving Loads > Paths command to display the Define Paths form. 2. Click the Add New Path Defined From Frames button or highlight a previously defined path and click the Modify/Show Path button to display the  Path Data form. 3. Click the Move Path  button to display the Move Path  form.   Method 2: This method is used in conjunction with Method 1 to assign frame objects to the defined paths.   1. After a [path(s) has been defined](Define_Paths.md), select a straight frame to be assigned to the previously defined path(s). 2. Click the Assign menu > Frame > Paths command to access the Assign Paths form. 3. Click the Modify/Show Path button to display the  Path Data form. 4. Click the Move Path  button to display the Move Path  form. |

# Path Data Form

A path is a chain of frame objects, with an optional eccentricity if the vehicles are located to one side or the other of the frame objects.

Tip:  Click the Set Display Options button ![](../../../assets/images/Images/Set%20Display%20Options%20button.GIF) to access the Display Options for Active Window form, and in the Frames/Cables/Tendons area, check the Labels check box to display the frame label in the specified window(s). This can be helpful in selecting the frames for the path definition process.

- Path Name edit box/display box. If the Define menu (Method 1 below) was used to access the form, accept the default or enter another name in this edit box. If the Assign menu (Method 2 below) was used to access the form, the name in the display box is the name specified when the path was defined and that name cannot be changed here.
- Display Color.  The color that will be used to display the section on-screen in the model. Click on the "Display Color" text or the small sample square of the color to bring up the Color form. Select the desired new color on the Color form and click the OK button.
- Frame edit box. If the Define menu was used to access the form, enter the label of the frame representing the path. The label will appear in the Frame display area when the Add button is clicked. If the Assign menu was used to access the form, the edit box will display the ID of the frame object selected before the Assign menu command was clicked.

- Centerline Offset edit box. Enter the distance of the path centerline (in the current length units) from the frame representing the path.
- - Add button. After entering values in the Frame, Centerline  and Offset edit boxes, click the Add button to add the definition.

1. - Insert button. Enter a label ID in the Frame edit box and click the Insert button to insert the newly entered ID in sequential order in the Frame display box.

- - Modify button.
  1. 1. Highlight a frame ID in the display area.
     2. Type a new ID or centerline offset  value in the  edit box.
     3. Click the Modify button.
  - Delete button.
  1. 1. Highlight a frame ID in the display area.
     2. Click the Delete button to remove the frame object from the path definition.
- Reverse Order button. Click the Reverse Order button to reorder the data according to frame IDs.

- Reverse Sign button. Click the Reverse Sign button to change positive centerline offset values to negative or negative values to positive. The Reverse Sign button acts on all values, so it is not necessary to select a value before using the button.

- Move Path button. Click this button to display the [Move Path form](Move_Path_Form.md) and move the path a specified distance or to specified coordinates.
- Discretization area.
- Maximum Discretization Length. Use this edit box  to specify the maximum discretization of the load along the length of the path.  The value is  entered in the current length units.
- Discretization Length Not Greater Than 1/{value} of Path Length check box and value. Use this check box to specify that the load be distributed on the path based on a fraction of the path length. Checking this check box ensures proportional load discretization on every path in this definition. This can be helpful, for example, when multiple paths have been defined and the length of a path(s) is less than the length specified in the Maximum  Discretization Length edit box.

Note:  The smallest value specified for path load discretization and discretization based on fractional values of the path lengths is the controlling value for distributing the load on a path.

Note:  After the path has been defined based on frames (i.e., Method 1 below),  the [Assign menu > Frame > Path command](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Path.md) must be used to assign frame objects to the defined path (i.e., Method 2 below).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the  Path Data form using either of the following methods:    Method 1   1. Click the [Define menu > Moving  Loads > Paths  command](Define_Moving_Loads.md) to display the Define Paths form. 2. Click the Add New Path Defined from Frames button or highlight a [previously defined path](Define_Paths.md) and click the Modify/Show Path button to display the  Path Data form.   Method 2   1. Select a frame object. 2. Click the Assign menu > Frame > Paths  command to display the Assign Path form. Note that at least one path must be have been defined as described in Method 1 for this command to be available. 3. Click the Modify/Show Path button to display the  Path Data form. |

# Vehicle Class Data Form

Vehicle classes are sets of one or more vehicles that can be assigned to act on paths in a [moving-load case](../Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md). Only one vehicle in a class acts on the path at a time. Results are reported for the vehicle causing the most severe response.

- Vehicle Class Name edit box. Enter a Vehicle Class Name or accept the default name.
- Vehicle Name drop-down list. Select a Vehicle Name from the drop down list. The names listed were defined using the Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicles command to access the [Define Vehicles form](Define_Vehicles.md).
- Scale Factor edit box. Specify a Scale Factor for the selected vehicle.
- - Add button.
  1. 1. Click the Add button after the Vehicle Class Name, Vehicle Name and Scale Factors have been specified.
     2. Click the OK button to add the new Vehicle Class to the Classes list on the [Define Vehicle Classes form](Define_Vehicle_Classes.md).
  - Modify button.
  1. 1. Highlight the items to be modified in the Vehicle Name/Scale Factor display lists.
     2. As appropriate, select a new Vehicle Name or type revised data in the Scale Factor edit box.
     3. Click the Modify button.
  - Delete button.
  - 1. Highlight the item to be deleted in the Vehicle Name/Scale Factor display lists.
    2. Click the Delete button.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Vehicle Class Data form as follows:   1. Define  vehicles using the [Define menu > Moving Loads > Vehicles](Define_Vehicles.md)  command. 2. Click the [Define menu > Moving  Loads > Vehicle Classes command](Define_Moving_Loads.md) to display the Define Vehicle Classes form. 3. Click the Add New Class button, or highlight a previously defined vehicle class and click the Modify/Show Class button, to display the Vehicle Class Data form. |

# Vehicle Data Form

Use the Vehicle Data form to specify the various loads associated with a named vehicle.

- Vehicle Name edit box. Enter a Vehicle Name or accept the default.
- Load Elevation display area.  Graphically displays the uniform and axle loads defined for the vehicle in the  elevation view.

![](../../../assets/images/Images/BRIDVEHI2.GIF)

- Loads
- - Load Length Type drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select the type of load length (leading or trailing load or fixed or variable length).
  - Minimum and Maximum Distance edit boxes. Enter a minimum and maximum distance between the current and previous axle.

Note: A value of Zero for Maximum Distance indicates an infinite distance. Only one intermediate axle may have a value of Maximum Distance > Minimum Distance. The remaining intermediate axles must have values of Maximum Distance = Minimum Distance.

1. - Uniform Load edit box. Enter uniform load values in load/length units.
   - Axle Load edit box. Enter an axle load in the edit box; this is the total load for the axle.
   - - Add button. After the parameters in the Loads area of the form have been specified, click the Add button to add the parameters to the Vehicle definition.
     - Insert button. After the parameters in the Loads area of the form have been specified, click the Insert button to insert the parameters to the Vehicle definition above any selected parameters in the Loads display area.
     - Modify button. Select parameters in the Loads area of the form to be modified and use the drop-down lists and edit boxes to specify the modifications. Then click the Modify button to make the changes.
     - Delete button. Select the load definition in the Loads area of the form to be deleted. Then click the Delete button to delete the load definition.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Vehicle Data form as follows:    Click the [Define menu > Moving  Loads > Vehicle command](Define_Moving_Loads.md). Then do one of the following:   - Click the Add Vehicle button. - Highlight a  Vehicle definition in the Vehicle display area and  click the Modify/Show Vehicle button. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Named_Property_Sets.htm | Named Property Sets -->

# Named Property Sets

Forms:  Frame Property
Modifiers, Frame Property Modifier Data, Cable Property Modifiers, Cable
Property Modifier Data, Area Stiffness Modifiers, Area Stiffness Modifier
Data, Frame End Releases, Frame End Release Data

Use the Define menu > Named Property Sets
command and the submenu command--Frame Modifiers, Cable
Modifiers, Area Modifiers, and Frame End Releases--to
define modification factors.

Note:  The
modification factors specified using these command apply to [Static
Nonlinear Staged Construction Load Case](Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Staged_Construction_Form.md)s only.

A named set of property modifiers can be applied to a frame or area
object during staged construction to change the property modifiers that
were previously assigned or applied to the object. The effect of property
modifiers in a named set is exactly the same as the effect of those modifiers
that can be assigned directly to frame and area objects using the [Assign menu > Frame > Property Modifiers
command](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Property_Modifiers.md) or the [Assign menu > Area > Area Stiffness Modifiers
command](../Assign/Area/Area_Stiffness_Modifiers.md). By default, all objects use the property modifiers that are
assigned to them unless explicitly changed by applying a named set during
staged construction, in which case they replace the previously assigned
or applied property modifiers for all subsequent loading in the analysis.
Named sets of property modifiers affect only the element values of the
modifiers, not those which are defined as part of the frame/area section
properties.

- Define
  menu > Named Property Sets > Frame Modifiers. Click this
  command to access the Frame Property Modifiers
  form.
- - Click the
    Add New Modifiers button, or highlight
    a previously defined modifier definition and then click the Add Copy of Modifier or Modify/Show
    Modifier buttons,  to access the Frame
    Property Modifier Data form. Use that form to specify the
    modifiers that will be applied to frames in a static nonlinear
    staged construction load case.
  - Highlight a previously
    defined modifier definition and clicking the Delete
    Modifier button will remove the highlighted modifier definition.
- Define
  menu > Named Property Sets > Cable Modifiers. Click this
  command to access the Cable Property Modifiers
  form.
- - Click the Add New Modifiers button, or highlight a
    previously defined modifier definition and then click the Add Copy of Modifier or Modify/Show
    Modifier buttons,  to access the Cable
    Property Modifier Data form. Use that form to specify modifiers
    for the cross-sectional area, mass and weight that will be applied
    to cables in a static nonlinear staged construction load case.
  - Highlight a previously
    defined modifier definition and clicking the Delete
    Modifier button will remove the highlighted modifier definition.
- Define
  menu > Named Property Sets > Area Modifiers. Click this
  command to access the Area Stiffness Modifiers
  form.
- - Click the Add New Modifiers button, or highlight a
    previously defined modifier definition and then click the Add Copy of Modifier or Modify/Show
    Modifier buttons,  to access the Area
    Stiffness Modifier Data form. Use that form to specify
    the modifiers that will be applied to areas in a static nonlinear
    staged construction load case.
  - Highlight a previously
    defined modifier definition and clicking the Delete
    Modifier button will remove the highlighted modifier definition.
- Define
  menu > Named Property Sets > Frame Releases. Click this
  command to access the Frame End Releases
  form. A named set of frame releases can be applied to a frame object
  during staged construction to change the releases that were previously
  assigned or applied to the object. The effect of frame releases in
  a named set is exactly the same as the effect of those releases that
  can be assigned directly to selected frame objects using the [Assign menu > Frame > Releases/Partial Fixity
  command](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Releases_and_Partial_Fixity.md). By default, all frame objects use the releases that are
  assigned to them unless explicitly changed by applying a named set
  during staged construction, in which case they replace the previously
  assigned or applied releases for all subsequent loading in the analysis.
- - Click the Add New Modifiers button, or highlight a
    previously defined modifier definition and then click the Add Copy of Modifier or Modify/Show
    Modifier buttons,  to access the Frame
    End Release Data form. Use that form to specify the modifiers
    that will be applied to frame end releases in a static nonlinear
    staged construction load case.
  - Highlight a previously
    defined modifier definition and clicking the Delete
    Modifier button will remove the highlighted modifier definition.

# Define Named Sets

Forms: Define Database Table Named Sets, Virtual Work Diagram, Define Pushover Named Sets, Pushover Named Set Data, Response Spectrum Named Sets, Plot Function Trace Display Definition

Use the Define menu > Named Sets command to save the options selected on the various forms used to generate output (tables, curves, and the like) as a definition known as a Named Set. The various types of Named Sets that can be defined are generated using the follow options:

- Tables (database)
- 1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Tables command to display the Define Database Table Named Sets form.
  2. Use the various options on that form to define the required output. For more information about the various options and buttons on the form, see the description of the [Choose Tables for form](../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md) because it is similar to the Define Database Table Named Sets form.
  3. When all selections have been made, click the Save Named Set button to display the Database Table Named Sets form.

     1. Type the name of the Named Set in the DB Table Set edit box.
     2. Click the Add New DBT Set button. Alternatively, highlight a previously defined Named Set, type a new name, and then click the Change DBT Set Name button to change the name of the Named Set. Highlight a Named Set and use the Delete DBT Set button to delete the selected Named Set.
- Virtual Work
- 1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Virtual Work command to display the [Virtual Work Diagram form](../Display/Virtual_Work_Diagram_Form.md).

     1. Use the various options on that form to define the required output.
     2. When all selections have been made, click the Save Named Set button to display the Virtual Work Named Sets form.

        1. Type the name of the Named Set in the Virtual Work Set edit box.
        2. Click the Add New VW Set button.  Alternatively, highlight a previously defined Named Set, type a new name, and then click the Change VW Set Name button to change the name of the Named Set. Highlight a Named Set and use the Delete VW Set button to delete the selected Named Set.
- Pushover Named Sets

Note:  A [nonlinear static (pushover) analysis](Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) case must be defined in the model for this command to be available.

1. 1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Pushover Named Sets command to display the Define Pushover Named Sets form.
   2. Choose the appropriate action:

      - Add New Named Set button. Use this button to display the Pushover Named Set Data form and add a Named Set to the model.
      - Add Copy of Named Set button. Highlight a previously defined Named Set in the Named Sets display area and click this button to display the Pushover Named Set Data form and add a copy of an existing Named Set to the model.
      - Modify/Show Named Set button. Highlight a previously defined Named Set in the Named Sets display area and click this button to display the Pushover Named Set Data form and modify the Named Set without adding a Named Set to the model.
      - Delete Named Set button. Highlight a previously defined Named Set in the Named Sets display area and click this button to delete that Named Set from the model.

The Pushover Named Set Data form has the following areas:

- Pushover Named Set Name edit box. Use the suggested default name for the Named Set or type a new one in this edit box.
- Plot Type drop-down list. Choose the type of plot for which the Named Set is being specified from this drop-down list.
- Plot Parameters drop-down list. This drop-down list will include any previously defined parameters that may have been defined using the Define menu > Pushover Parameters Sets command.
- The Add New Parameters, Add Copy of Parameters, and Modify/Show Parameters buttons function as described in the [Pushover Parameters Sets](Pushover_Parameter_Sets.md) topic to add or modify the parameters used to display a pushover curve.
- Static Nonlinear Case drop-down list. This drop-down list shows any nonlinear static (pushover) analysis cases in the model that have been defined as [displacement controlled](Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Load_Application_Control_for_Nonlinear_Static_Analysis_Form.md) and [multi-step](Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Results_Saved_for_Nonlinear_Static_Load_Cases_Form.md). Choose the load case to be included in the Named Set.

- Joint TH Response Spectra

Note:  A [Time History function](Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) must be defined in the model for this command to be available.

1. 1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Joint TH Response Spectra command to display the [Response Spectrum Generation form](../Display/Show_Response_Spectrum_Curves.md).
   2. Use the various tabs and options on that form to define the required output. For more information about the tabs and options on the form, see the [Response Spectrum Curves](../Display/Show_Response_Spectrum_Curves.md) topic.
   3. When all selections have been made, click the Save Named Set button to display the Response Spectrum Named Sets form.

      1. Type the name of the Named Set in the Resp Spec Set edit box.
      2. Click the Add New RS Set button.

The Response Spectrum Named Sets form can also be used to change the name of a Named Set or to delete a named set. To change the name, highlight the Named Set in the display area, type the new name in the Resp Spec Set edit box and click the Change RS Set Name button. To delete a Named Set, highlight the Named Set in the display area and click the Delete RS Set button.

- 4. After a Named Set has been saved, click the Show Named Set button on the Response Spectrum Named Sets form to display the Select Resp Spec Set Named Set form. Select the Named Set and click the OK button to recall the setting applied to the Response Spectrum Generation form when the Named Set was defined. Choose a Time History Case and a Joint and then click the Display button on the Response Spectrum Generation form to view the Response Spectrum Curve diagram.
- Plot Function Traces

Note:  A [Time History function](Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) must be defined in the model for this command to be available.

1. 1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Plot Function Traces command to display the [Plot Function Trace Display Definition form](../Display/Show_Plot_Function/Plot_Functions.md).
   2. Use the various options on that form to define the required output. For more information about the options, display areas, drop-down lists and buttons on the form, see the [Plot Functions](../Display/Show_Plot_Function/Plot_Functions.md) topic.
   3. When all selections have been made, click the Save Named Set button to display the [Plot Function Trace Named Sets form](../Display/Show_Plot_Function/Plot_Function_Trace_Named_Sets_Form.md).

      1. Type the name of the Named Set in the Plot Function Set edit box.
      2. Click the Add New PF Set button.

The Plot Function Trace Named Sets form can also be used to change the name of a Named Set or to delete a named set. To change the name, highlight the Named Set in the display area, type the new name in the Plot Function Set edit box and click the Change PF Set Name button. To delete a Named Set, highlight the Named Set in the display area and click the Delete PF Set button.

# **Pile End Restraint Property**

Use the Pile End Restraint form to define the restraint conditions at the bottom of a pile for the *Pile Group*, *Pile Pier* and *Pile Shaft* foundation properties. For each degree of freedom, the restraint type can be “Free”, “Fixed” or “Partial Fixity”. When the type “Partial Fixity” is selected, the Stiffness textbox will be enabled for tuser to input the stiffness for that particular degree of freedom.

Click the **OK** button to save the restraint data or click the **Cancel** button to ignore the change to the form.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Pile_Group_Foundation_Property.htm | Pile Group Foundation Property -->

# **Pile Group Foundation Property**

Use the Pile Group Foundation form to define the material, dimensions and soil properties for a pile group foundation property. This property can be assigned to a joint using the Draw > Isolated Foundation command.

The pile cap will be modeled as area objects at the mid-surface of the pile cap. The piles will be modeled as line objects.

Each pile will be discretized based on the elevation of the soil layers. The pile line objects within the pile cap thickness will be set as end offsets with rigid zone factor 0.5. All the pile line objects are assigned with line springs in the local 2 and 3 (transverse) directions of the line object to provide the horizontal support, and a line spring in the local 1 (longitudinal) direction of the line object to provide the vertical support (friction between pile and soil). The spring constant of the horizontal line spring is equal to the corresponding soil modulus multiplied by the pile diameter. The spring constant of the vertical friction line spring is equal to the soil modulus Ks multiplied by the shear factor from the corresponding soil layer and the circumference of the pile. If the length of the pile exceeds the depth of the specified soil layers, then the property from the deepest soil layer will be used for the exceeding length of the pile. The point support condition at the end of the pile can be defined under the *End Spring* field .

After this property is assigned to a joint, the top of the pile cap will be located at the same elevation as the joint. The pile cap is centered on the column and oriented according to the frame object's local axis. The top center point of the pile cap is called the insertion point. In the model, the frame line object will be extended to the mid-surface of the pile-cap area objects, and assigned a corresponding end offset with rigid zone factor 0.5.

- **General:**
- - **Name: The name of the foundation property.**
- **Pile Cap:**
- - **Footing Material: Specify a previously defined material for the footing.**
  - **Total Length, Lx: The length of the footing parallel to the pile cap's local X-axis. This value depends on the overhang length, the number of piles, and the pile spacing. This value cannot be directly input. .**
  - **Total Width, Ly: The width of the footing transverse to the pile cap's local Y-axis. The value depends on the overhang length, the number of piles, and the pile spacing. This value cannot be directly input. .**
  - **Thickness, T: The thickness of the pile cap.**
  - **Overhang, Ox: The length of the overhang measured from the center of the outermost pile to the edge of the pile cap along its X-axis.**
  - **Overhang, Oy: The length of the overhang measured from the center of the outermost pile to the edge of the pile cap along its Y-axis.**
  - **Max. Mesh Size: The maximum area-object mesh size for the footing model.**

- **Pile Group:**
- - **Pile Material: The name of the foundation property.**
  - **Number of Piles, Nx:** Number of piles along the pile-cap X-axis.
  - **Number of Piles, Ny:** Number of piles along the pile-cap Y-axis.
  - **Pile Diameter:** **The diameter of each pile.**
  - Pile Vertical Length, H: **The vertical pile length measured from the bottom of the bent column to the tip of the pile.**
  - Pile Spacing, Sx: The pile spacing along the pile-cap X-axis.
  - Pile Spacing, Sy: The pile spacing along the pile-cap Y-axis.
  - Battered Angle Along X, Ax: The battered angle of the outermost piles along the pile-cap X-axis. The rotation is always outward and about the pile-cap X-axis. Zero indicates vertical piles.
  - Battered Eyeing Along Y, Ay: The battered angle of the outermost piles along the pile-cap Y-axis. The rotation is always outward and about the pile-cap Y-axis. Zero indicates vertical piles.
  - **End Spring:** The values of the point restraints or spring constants at the pile tip (bottom) that represent the lateral and vertical subgrade modulus of soil. To edit these values, click the item “End Spring” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Pile End Restraint](Pile_End_Restraint.md)  form.
- **Soil Properties:**
- - **Soil Cover, Sc: The distance above the top surface of the footing to the top of soil, where soil layers start.**
  - **Layer Properties: The values of the modulus of subgrade reaction in the soil layers. To edit these values, click the item “Layer Properties” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Soil Layer Properties](Soil_Layer_Properties.md)  form.**
- **Model 3D:**
- - **Use the controls in this region to control the 3D display of the defined foundation property.**

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Pile Group Foundation Property form as follows:   1. Click the Define > Foundation Properties command to bring up the [Advanced Foundation Properties](Advanced_Foundation_Property_-_For_SAP2000.md) form. 2. Click the Add New Foundation button to display the  Add Foundation Property form. Then click the Advanced Foundation Properties form, select  Pile Group and click OK.  Alternatively, highlight the name of a previously defined foundation in the Foundation area and click the Add Copy of Foundation or Modify/Show Foundation button to display the Pile Group Foundation Property form. |

# **Pile Pier Foundation Property**

Use the Pile Pier Foundation form to define the material, dimensions and soil properties for a pile pier foundation property. This property can be assigned to a joint using the Draw > Isolated Foundation command.

The pile pier will be modeled as line objects. The pile pier will be discretized based on the elevation of the soil layers. All the pile line objects are assigned with line springs in the local 2 and 3 (transverse) directions of the line object to provide the horizontal support, and a line spring in the local 1 (longitudinal) direction of the line object to provide the vertical support (friction between pile and soil).

The spring constant of the horizontal line spring is equal to the corresponding soil modulus multiplied by the pile diameter.

The spring constant of the vertical friction line spring is equal to the soil modulus Ks multiplied by the shear factor from the corresponding soil layer and the circumference of the pile. If the length of the pile exceeds the depth of the specified soil layers, then the property from the deepest soil layer will be used for the exceeding length of the pile. The point support condition at the end of the pile can be defined under the End Spring field.

- **General:**
- - **Name: The name of the foundation property.**
- **Pile Pier:**
- - **Material: Specify a previously defined material for this property.**
  - **Diameter, D: The diameter of the pile.**
  - **Length, H: The vertical pile length measured from the joint to the tip of the pile.**
  - **End Spring:** The values of the point restraints or spring constants at the pile tip (bottom) that represent the lateral and vertical subgrade modulus of soil. To edit these values, click the item “End Spring” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Pile End Restraint](Pile_End_Restraint.md)  form.
- **Soil Properties:**
- - **Soil Cover, Sc: The distance above the top surface of the footing to the top of soil, where soil layers start.**
  - **Layer Properties: The values of the modulus of subgrade reaction in the soil layers. To edit these values, click the item “Layer Properties” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Soil Layer Properties](Soil_Layer_Properties.md)  form.**
- **Model 3D:**
- - **Use the controls in this region to control the 3D display of the defined foundation property.**

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Pile Pier Foundation Property form as follows:   1. Click the Define > Foundation Properties command to bring up the [Advanced Foundation Properties](Advanced_Foundation_Property_-_For_SAP2000.md) form. 2. Click the Add New Foundation button to display the  Add Foundation Property form. Then click the Advanced Foundation Properties form, select  Pile Pier and click OK.
