<!-- source: Menus/Define/Pile_Shaft_Foundation_Property.htm | Pile Shaft Foundation Property -->

# **Pile Shaft Foundation Property**

Use the Pile Shaft Foundation form to define the material, dimensions and soil properties for a pile shaft foundation property. This property can be assigned to a joint using the Draw > Isolated Foundation command.

The pile shaft will be modeled as line objects. The pile shaft can be of hollow or solid circular section and will be discretized based on the elevation of the soil layers. All the pile line objects are assigned with line springs in the local 2 and 3 (transverse) directions of the line object to provide the horizontal support, and a line spring in the local 1 (longitudinal) direction of the line object to provide the vertical support (friction between pile and soil).

The spring constant of the horizontal line spring is equal to the corresponding soil modulus multiplied by the pile diameter.

The spring constant of the vertical friction line spring is equal to the soil modulus Ks multiplied by the shear factor from the corresponding soil layer and the circumference of the pile. If the length of the pile shaft exceeds the depth of the specified soil layers, then the property from the deepest soil layer will be used for the exceeding length of the pile. The point support condition at the end of the pile can be defined under the *End Spring* field.

- **General:**
- - **Name: The name of the foundation property.**

- **Shaft:**
- - Material: Specify a previously defined material for this property.
  - Diameter, D: The diameter of the shaft.
  - Shaft is Hollow: This is to specify whether the shaft is hollow (True) or solid (False).
  - Wall Thickness, T: The thickness of the shaft wall. This value must be smaller than half of the pile diameter. This item is available only when Shaft is Hollow is True.
  - Length, H: The vertical pile length measured from the joint to the tip of the shaft.
  - Base Diameter, Db: The diameter of the shaft base.
  - Base Length, Hb: The height of the shaft base.
  - End Spring: The values of the point restraints or spring constants at the pile tip (bottom) that represent the lateral and vertical subgrade modulus of soil. To edit these values, click the item “End Spring” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Pile End Restraint](Pile_End_Restraint.md) form.

- **Soil Properties:**
- - **Soil Cover, Sc: The distance above the top surface of the footing to the top of soil, where soil layers start.**
  - **Layer Properties: The values of the modulus of subgrade reaction in the soil layers. To edit these values, click the item “Layer Properties” and then click the “…” button. This will display the [Soil Layer Properties](Soil_Layer_Properties.md)  form.**
- **Model 3D:**
- - Use the controls in this region to control the 3D display of the defined foundation property.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Pile Shaft Foundation Property form as follows:   1. Click the Define > Foundation Properties command to bring up the [Advanced Foundation Properties](Advanced_Foundation_Property_-_For_SAP2000.md) form. 2. Click the Add New Foundation button to display the  Add Foundation Property form. Then click the Advanced Foundation Properties form, select  Pile Shaft and click OK.  Alternatively, highlight the name of a previously defined foundation in the Foundation area and click the Add Copy of Foundation or Modify/Show Foundation button to display the Pile Shaft Foundation Property form. |

# Property/Stiffness Modification Factors Form

Use the Property/Stiffness Modification Factors form to modify properties included in a [frame](Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md), [cable](Section_Properties/Cable_Sections/Cable_Sections.md), or [area](Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md) section property definition.

Modification factors can also be [assigned to individual frame, cable, and area objects](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Property_Modifiers.md). If modifications are assigned to an object that has modification factors included in the property definition for the object, the effects are multiplicative.

Note: For objects using non-prismatic section properties, the modifiers on the section properties are ignored. Only the modifiers assigned to the objects are used.

|  |
| --- |
| Specify modification factors as part of the definition as follows:  Access the Frame Property/Stiffness Modification Factors form as follows:   1. 1. Click the Define menu > Frame Sections command, or click on a [line object that has been drawn as a frame](../Draw/Draw_Frame_Cable_Tendon.md) and click the  Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command, to access the Frame Properties form.    2. Select a property type in the Choose Property Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add New Section button, or select a previously defined property in the Properties list and click the Add Copy of Section or  Modify/Show Section button, to display the {Type} Section form.    3. Click the Set Modifiers button.   Access the Cable Property/Stiffness Modification Factors form as follows:   1. 1. Click the Define menu > Cable Sections command, or click on a [line object that has been drawn as a cable](../Draw/Draw_Frame_Cable_Tendon.md) and click the  Assign menu > Cable > Cable Sections command, to access the Cable Sections form.    2. Click the Add New Section or select a previously defined cable section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or  Modify/Show Section button to display the Cable Section Data form.    3. Click the Modify/Show Cable Property Modifiers button.   Access the Property/Stiffness Modification Factors form for area sections as follows:   1. 1. Click the Define menu > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to display the Area Sections form.    2. Click the Add New Section or select a previously define area section and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button to display the Shell Section Data, Plane Section Data or Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data form.    3. Click the Set Modifiers button.     Assign modification factors to frame, cable, or area objects on an object-by-object basis as follows:   1. Select the object(s) to be assigned modification factors. 2. Click the Assign menu > Frame > Property Modifiers,  Assign menu > Cable > Property Modifiers, or  the  Assign menu > Area > Area Stiffness Modifiers (Shells) command, depending on the type of object selected. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Pushover_Parameter_Sets.htm | Pushover Parameter Sets -->

# Pushover Parameter Sets

Use the Define menu > Pushover Parameter Sets
command to specify the parameters for displaying pushover curves. The
parameters are saved as a named definition so they can be recalled and
applied quickly.

1. Select the Define
   menu > Pushover Parameter Sets command. A submenu will appear
   listing the available types of pushover parameters.

2. Select
   one of the parameter types to display the Define
   Pushover Parameters for {Parameter Type} form.

   - Add
     New Parameters button. Use this button to define a new
     parameter set.
   - 1. Click this button to display one of
        the following forms, depending on the selection made in Step
        1:
     1. - [Parameters for Base Shear vs Monitored
          Displ form](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Parameters_for_Base_Shear_vs_Monitored_Displ_Form.md).
        - [Parameters for ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum
          form.](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Parameters_for_ATC_40_Capacity_Spectrum_Form.md)
        - [Parameters for FEMA 356 Coefficient Method
          form](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Parameters_for_FEMA_356_Coefficient_Method_Form.md).
        - [Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization
          form](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Equivalent_Linearization_Form.md).
        - [Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP
          form](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Displacement_Modification_Form.md).
     2. Use the options available on the forms
        to specify how the pushover curve will display.
   - Add
     Copy of Parameters button. Use this button to add a parameter
     set definition based on a previously defined parameter set.
   - 1. Highlight a
        previously defined parameter set in the Pushover
        Parameters area of the form to select it.
     2. Click the Add Copy of Parameters button.
     3. The form that
        appears depends on the type of parameter set selected; the
        form will be "pre-loaded" with the parameters from
        the previously defined set.
     4. Use the options
        on the form to make any adjustments to the definition.
   - Modify/Show
     Parameters button. Use this button to modify an existing
     parameter set definition.
   - 1. Highlight a previously defined parameter
        set in the Pushover Parameters
        area of the form to select it.
     2. Click the Modify/Show
        Parameters button.
     3. The form that appears depends on the
        type of parameter set selected.
     4. Use the options on the form to make
        the necessary adjustments.
   - Delete
     Parameters button.
   - 1. Highlight a
        parameter set in the Pushover
        Parameters area of the form to select it.
     2. Click the Delete Parameters button to delete the
        parameter set definition.

## See Also

[Pushover
Curve](../Display/Show_Static_Pushover_Curve/Pushover_Curve_Form.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Cut_Advanced_Axes_Form.htm | Section Cut Advanced Axes Form -->

# Section Cut Advanced Axes Form

Use the Section Cut Advanced Axes form to specify the axial reference vector and the local plane and its reference vectors for the specified section cut.

- Default option. When the Default option is selected, the other areas of the form are not available and no further input is required.
- Advanced option. When the Advanced option is selected, the input required on the form changes depending on the options selected in the Axial Reference Vector Specified by and Plane Reference Vector Specified by areas of the form.
- - Local Plane and Plane drop-down list. Select the local plane for the section cut from the drop-down list.
  - Axial Reference Vector Specified by - Choose one of the following options to specify how the axial reference vector will be defined.
  - - Coordinate Direction - When this option is selected, the  form will display an Axial Coordinate Direction area, a Coordinate System drop-down list and Direction drop-down list.  Choose the coordinate system for the reference vector and then the coordinate direction for it from the drop-down list.
    - Two Joints - When this option is selected, the lower portion of the form will display a Two Joints for Axial Reference Vector area with Axial Joint 1 and Axial Joint 2 drop-down lists. The lists consist of the joints included in the model and a None selection. Choose the two joints to be used to specify the axial reference vector.
    - User Vector - When this option is selected, the lower portion of the form will display a Coordinate System drop-down list and a User Axial Reference Vector area with edit boxes for Axial Vector X, Axial Vector Y, and Axial Vector Z. Select the coordinate system for the reference vector, and then enter coordinate values in these edit boxes to specify the axial reference vector.
  - Plane Reference Vector Specified by - Choose one of the following options to specify how the plane reference vector will be specified.
  - - Coordinate Direction - When this option is selected, the form will display a Coordinate System drop-down list and a Plane Coordinate Direction area with Primary and Secondary Dir (Direction) drop-down lists. Choose the coordinate system for the reference vector and then choose a coordinate direction from each drop-down list.
    - Two Joints - When this option is selected, the lower portion of the form will display a Two Joints for Plane Reference Vector area with Plane Joint 1 and Plane Joint 2 drop-down lists. The lists consist of the joints included in the model and a None selection. Choose the two joints to be used to specify the plane reference vector.
    - User Vector - When this option is selected, the form will display a Coordinate System drop-down list and a User Plane Reference Vector area with edit boxes for Plane Vector X, Plane Vector Y, and Plane Vector Z. Choose the coordinate system for the reference vector and then enter coordinate values in the edit boxes to specify the plane reference vector.

## See Also

[Section Cut Output Conventions](../../Output/Section_Cut_Output_Conventions.md)

[Section Cut Plot Function](../Display/Show_Plot_Function/Section_Cut_Plot_Function.md)

[Draw Section Cuts](../Draw/Draw_Section_Cuts.md)

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Section Cut Advanced Axes form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Cuts command to display the Section Cut form. 2. Click the Add Section Cut button, or highlight a previously defined section cut and click the Modify/Show Section Cut button, to display the Section Cuts Data form. 3. Check the Advanced Axes check box and click the Advanced button to display the Section Cut Advanced Axes form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Cuts.htm | Section Cuts -->

# Section Cuts

Form:  Section Cuts, Section Cut Data

Use the Define menu > Section Cuts command
to obtain resultant forces acting at section cuts through a model.  Section
cuts can be defined before or after an analysis has been run; however,
it is safest to wait until after the analysis has been run. Typically
do not define section cuts, and more importantly, the groups used in the
section cut definition, until all manual meshing of the model (if any)
has been completed (see [Frame
- Automatic Frame Mesh](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Automatic_Frame_Mesh.md),  [Area
- Automatic Area Mesh](../Assign/Area/Area_Automatic_Area_Mesh.md) or [Solid
- Automatic Solid Mesh](../Assign/Solid/Solid_Automatic_Solid_Mesh.md) for more information about meshing). If the
groups are defined before manual meshing, some of the point objects that
should be in the group may not yet be created.

Define section cuts as follows:

1. Define the group that
   is used to specify the extent of the section cut as follows.

   1. Select the objects
      that are to be part of the section cut.
   2. Select the Assign menu > Assign to Group command
      to access the Assign/Define Group Names
      form.
   3. Click the Add New Group button to access the Group Definition form.
   4. Enter a name in
      the Group Name edit box.
      If it is not already checked, check the Section
      Cut Definition check box, and click the OK
      button.
   5. Select the Add to Group option in the
      lower left-hand corner of the Assign/Define
      Group Names form and click the OK
      button.
2. Click the Define
   menu > Section Cuts command to access the Section
   Cuts form. Use the buttons on this form to add, modify, or
   delete section cuts.

   - Add
     Section Cut button. Click the Add
     Section Cut button to access the Section
     Cuts Data form, which has the following areas, options,
     and buttons:
   - - Section Cut Name edit box.
       Use the default or type in a new name.
     - Coordinate System drop-down
       list. Choose the coordinate system in which the section cut
       will be defined.
     - Units drop-down list. Use
       the specified units or select new units from the drop-down
       list for the various values on the form.
     - Section Cut Defined By area.
       Choose an option for defining the section cut.
     - - Group
         option. When this option is selected, section cut results
         are reported for all elements included in the Group specified
         using the Group
         drop-down list in the Section
         Cut Group area of the form.
       - Quadrilateral
         Cutting Planes option. When this option is selected,
         the Quadrilateral Cutting
         Planes spreadsheet area is added to the form, along
         with the Results Reported
         Are on This Side of Elements area.
       - - Quadrilateral Cutting Planes
           spreadsheet area. Use the cells of the spreadsheet
           to specify the coordinates for the four points that
           define the quadrilateral. Click the Check
           For Legal Quadrilateral button to verify that
           the points are valid. SAP2000 will display a message
           confirming or denying the validity of the coordinates.

         Section
         cut results are reported for all elements that are fully
         cut by the quadrilateral and that have their associated
         objects included in the Group selected in the Group
         drop-down list in the Section
         Cut Group area of the form (see below).
       - Results
         Reported Are on This Side of Elements area. Use
         the options in the area of the form to specify that the
         results are reported for the Positive 3 Axis Side of the
         Quadrilateral, or the Negative 3 Axis Side of the Quadrilateral.
         The positive 3 axis of quadrilateral elements follows
         the same convention as that for shell objects, where the
         axis orientation is normal to the quadrilateral area and
         points toward the user when the four corners of the quadrilateral
         appear in counter-clockwise order. When viewing the negative
         face, the corners appear in clockwise order.

1. 1. - Section Cut Group area.
        Select the name of the group that defines the section cut
        from the Group drop-down
        list.
      - Section Cut Result Type
        area. Choose the type of results to be reported, Analysis
        or Design. The options in the Section
        Cut Local Axes Orientation area at the bottom of the
        form vary depending on the type of results selected.
      - - Section
          Cut Axes Orientation - Analysis.  By default
          the positive local 1, 2 and 3 axes of the section cut
          correspond to the global X, Y and Z axis, respectively.
           Type in a value for rotation angles about the Z,
          Y’ and X” axes, in degrees (Y’ and X” are used as axes
          names instead of Y and X to emphasize that after an angle
          about Z has been specified, the local X and Y will change
          as a result).

1. 1. - - - Advanced Axes check
            box and Advanced button.
            Check this check box and click this button to access
            the [Section Cut Advanced Axes
            form](Section_Cut_Advanced_Axes_Form.md). Use the form to specify the axial reference
            vector and the local plane and its reference vectors
            for the specified section cut.
        - Section Cut Axes Orientation
          - Design.  Choose
          to specify the orientation using the Wall, Spandrel, or
          Slab option.
        - - Wall option. In
            this case, the Local 1 axis is parallel to the Global
            Z axis. The 2 and 3 axes lie in the global XY plane.
          - Spandrel
            or Slab
            option. In these
            cases, the Local 2 axis is parallel to the Global
            Z axis. The 1 and 3 axes lie in the global XY Plane.
          - Angle from Global X to
            Local 2 or Local 1 edit box. Use this edit
            box to specify the angle between the Global X and
            the Local 2 (Wall option) or Local 1 (Spandrel and
            Slab options) axis. A positive angle appears counterclockwise
            when viewed from above.
          - Results Reported Are on
            This Side of Elements area.
            Use the options in this area of the form to specify
            that the results are reported on the Top or Bottom
            side of the section cut for a Wall-type cut, or on
            the Left or Right side for a Spandrel- or Slab-type
            cut. Top and Right are on the positive 1-axis side
            of the cut. Bottom and Left are on the negative 1
            axis side of the cut.
      - Results Reported at this Location
        options. Define the location (point) about which section cut
        forces are summed. Choose from the following two options:

Note:
 A point object does not need to be defined at the point about which
the section cut forces are being summed.

1. 1. 1. - Default
           option.  By default the section cut forces are reported
           at a location (point) that has coordinates equal to the
           average of the coordinates of all of the point objects
           included in the group that defines the section cut.
         - User-Defined
           option.  Any arbitrary point can be specified about
           which section cut forces are to be summed by entering
           the global X, Y and Z coordinates of that point. Note
           it is not necessary that a point object be defined at
           the point about which the section cut forces are to be
           summed.

1. - Modify/Show
     Section Cut button.

1. 1. 1. Highlight
         the name of the section cut to be modified in the Section
         Cuts area of the Section Cuts
         form.
      2. Click
         the Modify/Show Section Cut button
         to access the Section Cuts Data
         form.
      3. Use
         the drop-down lists and edit boxes on the Section
         Cuts Data form to modify the section cut as necessary.
         The various areas on the Section Cuts
         Data form are described under the "Add
         Section Cut Button" portion of this topic.
   - Delete
     Section Cut button.

1. 1. 1. Highlight
         the name of the section cut to be deleted in the Section
         Cuts area of the Section Cuts
         form.
      2. Click
         the Delete Section Cut button
         to access the Section Cuts Data
         form.

After running an analysis, use the Display menu
> Show Tables command to display the Choose
Tables for Display form; click the Structure
Output item and click the OK button
to view the section cut forces.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated
in [Problem N](../../Example_Problems/Problem_N.md) and [Problem S](../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md).

## See Also

[Section
Cut Output Conventions](../../Output/Section_Cut_Output_Conventions.md)

[Section
Cut Plot Function](../Display/Show_Plot_Function/Section_Cut_Plot_Function.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Axisymmetric_Solid_Asolid_Section_Data_Form.htm | Axisymmetric Solid Asolid Section Data Form -->

# Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data Form

Use the Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data form to specify the parameters for an asolid definition.

- Section Name edit box. Use the suggested default or type a name in the edit box.
- Section Notes Modify/Show button. Click this button to access the [Area Section Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md). Use that form to add Area Section notes to the model file.
- Display Color box. The Display Color box shows the color that will be used to display the area section being defined. Click the Display Color box to display the Color form; click on a new color to change the display color.
- Incompatible Modes check box. When this check box is checked, incompatible bending modes are included in the stiffness formulation. In general, incompatible modes significantly improve the bending behavior of the object. Uncheck the check box to exclude incompatible bending modes from the stiffness formulation.
- Material Name drop-down list. Select the [Material definition](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) from the drop-down list.
- Material Angle edit box. Use this edit box to specify an angle to modify the local axis of the area objects to which this area section definition is assigned.
- Coordinate System drop-down list. Select the coordinate system for the definition. The area object will be symmetric about the Z axis in the specified coordinate system.
- Arc (Degrees) edit box. Type a value for the arc of the object; that is, the number of degrees through which the object's planar shape is rotated to define the solid-type object.  Inputting 0 for this item means that the arc will be taken as 1 radian.
- Set Modifiers button. Click the Set Modifiers button to access the [Property Stiffness Modification Factors form](../../Property_Stiffness_Modification_Factors_Form.md).
- Thermal Properties button. This feature is under development.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the  Area Sections form. 2. Choose Asolid from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list. 3. Click the Add New Property button to display the Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data form. Alternatively, highlight a previously defined asolid section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button to display the Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section Data form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Concrete_Shell_Section_Design_Parameters_Form.htm | Concrete Shell Section Design Parameters Form -->

# Concrete Shell Section Design Parameters Form

Use the Concrete Shell Section Design Parameters form to specify the rebar layout for the concrete shell definition.

- Section Names display box. This is the label given to the area section property on the Shell Section Data form.
- Rebar Layout Options. Choose the appropriate option for the rebar used in the section
- - Default option. When this option is selected, the program uses two layers and the cover is 0.1 times the thickness of the section as specified on the Shell Section Data form.
  - One Layer option. When this option is selected, one layer of rebar is used. Placement of the layer is measured from the top of the section. Use the Top Bar - Direction 1 and Top Bar Direction 2 edit boxes to specify placement of the rebar.
  - Two Layers option. When this option is selected, two layers of rebar are used. Placement of the layers is measured from the top and the bottom of the section. Use the Top Bar - Direction 1, Top Bar Direction 2, Bottom Bar - Direction 1, and Bottom Bar Direction 2 edit boxes to specify placement of the rebar.

Directions 1 and 2 are the local axes directions of the area object.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Concrete Shell Section Design Parameters form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the Area Sections form. 2. Choose Shell from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list. 3. Click the Add New Property button to display the Shell Section Data form. Alternatively, highlight a previously defined shell section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button to display the Shell Section Data form. 4. Select CONC (concrete) from the Material Name drop-down list. 5. Click the Modify/Show Shell Design Parameters button to display the Concrete Shell Section Design Parameters form. |


---
<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Concrete_Shell_Section_Quick_Start_Parameters_Form.htm | Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters Form -->

# Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters Form

Use the Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters form to specify the rebar material and size for a single layer or the top and bottom of a two-layer concrete shell object.

- Section Name display box. This is the name given to the section on the Shell Section Layer Definition form.
- Rebar Layers. Choose to specify one layer of rebar in the shell object or a shell object with a two layers (a top and a bottom layer of rebar).
- - One Layer option. When this option is selected, one layer of rebar will be modeled in the shell section.
  - - Bars - Direction 1 and Bars - Direction 2 drop-down lists and edit boxes and Cover edit boxes. When the One Layer option is selected, these drop-down lists and edit boxes will appear on the form. Select the rebar size from the drop-down list and specify the spacing using the associated edit boxes. Specify the concrete cover in the current units.
  - Two Layer option. When this option is selected, a top and bottom layer of rebar will be modeled in the shell section.
  - - Top Bars - Direction 1, Top Bars - Direction 2, Bottom Bars - Direction 1, Bottom Bars - Direction 2 drop-down lists and edit boxes and Cover edit boxes. When the Two Layer option is selected, these drop-down lists and edit boxes will appear on the form. Select the rebar size from the drop-down lists and specify the spacing using the associated edit boxes. Specify the concrete cover in the current units.
  - Size and Spacing is the Same for All Rebar check box. Check this check box to quickly specify that the sizes and spacing of all rebar be the same.
- Units drop-down list. Use the displayed units for specifying the parameters on the form, or select different units from the drop-down list.
- Concrete Material drop-down list and Allow Nonlinear check box. Use the drop-down list to select a previously defined [material definition](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) for the concrete material. Check the Allow Nonlinear check box to allow the concrete to have nonlinear behavior during analysis.
- Rebar Material drop-down list and Allow Nonlinear check box. Use the drop-down list to select a previously defined [material definition](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) for the rebar material. Check the Allow Nonlinear check box to allow the rebar to have nonlinear behavior during analysis.
- Concrete Thickness edit box. Use this edit box to specify the thickness of the concrete section.
- In-Plane Element Component Behavior check boxes. Use these check boxes to specify which material components will be nonlinear.
- Out-of-Plane Element Component Behavior options. Choose to specify if the out-of-plane behavior is the same as in-plane or if it is linear.
- Shell Section Elevation View display area. Use this area of the form to display a 1-3, or 2-3 Elevation View of the rebar layout in the concrete shell object.
- Shell Section Plan View display area. Choose to display the Top or Bottom plan view of the rebar layout in the concrete shell object.

When the OK button is clicked, the data entered on this form will automatically transfer to the spreadsheet area of the Shell Section Layer Definition form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the  Area Sections form. 2. Choose Shell from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list. 3. Click the Add New Property button, or highlight a previously defined shell section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button, to display the Shell Section Data form. 4. Select the Shell-Layered/Nonlinear option. 5. Click the Modify/Show Layer Definition button to display the Shell Section Layer Definition form. 6. Click the Quick Start button to display the Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.htm | Define Area Sections -->

# Define - Area Sections

Form:  Area Sections, Area Section Data

Use the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command or the Assign menu > Area > Sections command to access the  Area Sections form and add, modify, or delete an area property definition. The area property definition consists of geometrical and material properties.

TIP:  The forms described in this topic also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available sections on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates) that are used to start a new model or to add objects from a template (Edit menu).

1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the Area Sections form. The Area Sections form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to an Area drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates).
2. Choose the type of section to add from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list:  Shell, Plane, or Asolid.
3. Click the appropriate button:

1. - Add New Section button.
   - 1. Depending on the type of section selected in Step 2, the [Shell Section Data](Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), [Plane Section Data](Plane_Section_Data_Form.md), or [Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section](Axisymmetric_Solid_Asolid_Section_Data_Form.md) data form will appear.
     2. Use the options on that form to add a new area section definition to the model file.
   - Add Copy of Section button.
   - 1. Select the property definition to be copied from the list of property definitions in the Sections area of the Area Sections form.
     2. Click the Add Copy of Section button. Depending on the type of section selected in Step a, the [Shell Section Data](Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), [Plane Section Data](Plane_Section_Data_Form.md), or [Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section](Axisymmetric_Solid_Asolid_Section_Data_Form.md) data form will appear "pre-loaded" with the parameters of the selected property definition.
     3. Use the form to review or modify the definition and add a section definition to the model file.
   - Modify/Show Section button.
   - 1. Select the property definition to be modified from the list of property definitions in the Sections area of the Area Sections form.
     2. Click the Modify/Show Section button. Depending on the type of section selected in Step a, the [Shell Section Data](Shell_Section_Data_Form.md), [Plane Section Data](Plane_Section_Data_Form.md), or [Axisymmetric Solid (Asolid) Section](Axisymmetric_Solid_Asolid_Section_Data_Form.md) data form will appear.
     3. Use the form to modify the existing definition without adding a new definition to the file.
   - Delete Section button
   - 1. Select the property definition to be deleted from the list of property definitions in the Sections area of the Area Sections form.
     2. Click the Delete Section button to delete the definition.

Example:  Definition of area sections is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md), [Problem B](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md), [Problem C](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem M](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_M.md), ,[Problem N](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_N.md), [Problem O](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_O.md), [Problem S](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md),  and [Problem Z](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Z.md).

# Plane Section Data Form

Use the Plane Section Data form to specify the parameters for a plane section definition.

- Section Name edit box. Use the suggested default or type a name in the edit box.
- Section Notes Modify/Show button. Click this button to access the [Area Section Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md). Use that form to add Area Section notes to the model file.
- Display Color box. The Display Color box shows the color that will be used to display the area section being defined. Click the Display Color box to display the Color form; click a new color to change the display color.
- Type area. Choose the Plane-Stress or Plane-Strain option to indicate the type of plane element.
- Incompatible Modes check box. When this check box is checked,  incompatible bending modes are included in the stiffness formulation. In general, incompatible modes significantly improve the bending behavior of the object. Uncheck the check box to exclude incompatible bending modes from the stiffness formulation.
- Material Name drop-down list. Select the [Material definition](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) from the drop-down list.
- Material Angle edit box. Use this edit box to specify an angle to modify the local axis of the area objects to which this plane section definition is assigned.
- Thickness edit box. Type a value for the membrane thickness in this edit box, if appropriate.
- Set Modifiers button. Click the Set Modifiers button to access the [Property Stiffness Modification Factors form](../../Property_Stiffness_Modification_Factors_Form.md).
- Thermal Properties button. This feature is under development.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Plane Section Data form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties  > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the  Area Sections form. 2. Choose Plane from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list. 3. Click the Add New Property button to display the Plane Section Data form. Alternatively, highlight a previously defined plane section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button to display the Plane Section Data form. |

# Shell Section Data Form

This button becomes available when the Shell-Layered/Nonlinear option is selected; note also that other areas of the form become unavailable when this option is selected. - Thickness
- - Membrane edit box. Use the default or type a revised value for the membrane thickness in this edit box.

- Set Modifiers button. Click this button to access the [Property Stiffness Modification Factors form](../../Property_Stiffness_Modification_Factors_Form.md).
- Display Color box. The Display Color box shows the color that will be used to display the area section being defined. Click the Display Color box to display the Color form; click on a new color to change the display color.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.htm | Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form -->

# Shell Section Layer Hinge Layer Definition

Use the Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition form to define the linear and nonlinear behavior of the hinge layered shell layer. When a layer has a Concrete type base material, the hinge layer can be used to model flexural reinforced concrete shear walls and the program can automatically generate nonlinear P-M3 Fiber hinges with uniform rebar. For specific rebar layouts, you can create a user-defined P-M3 Fiber hinge and assign it to the hinge layer.

**Note**: The *Hinge* layer type will only be applied to 4-joint area objects that do not have auto-meshing enabled. If a layered shell section property with a hinge layer is assigned to a triangular area object or an area object which is auto meshed, the hinge layer will be converted to a linear *Directional* layer with the specified layer thickness and material.

- Section Name display box: This is the label given to the area section property on the **Shell Section Data** form.
- Layer Name display box: This is the name of the selected layer.
- **Base Material** display box: This is the name of the material assigned to the layer.
- **Nonlinear Properties** drop-down lists:

For the S11 and S22 P-M3 directions, the following options are available:

- ***None***: This option will set the direction to inactive and no stiffness or force will be provided for the direction.
- ***Linear*:** This option will set the direction to be linear elastic with the stiffness calculated using the Base Material, Layer Thickness, and size of the Area object.
- ***Auto P-M3***: This option will create an auto P-M3 Fiber hinge based on the Base Material, Layer Thickness, size of the Area object, and parameters set in the **Auto Hinge Options** section of this form. This option is only available when the **Base Material** is Concrete.
- Any previously defined ***User Fiber P-M3*** hinge property: The **Nonlinear Properties** dropdown list will include all user Fiber P-M3 hinge properties defined in the model. This option will use the user P-M3 Fiber hinge exactly as it is defined for the P-M3 behavior in the specified direction, even if the hinge cross-section does not match the thickness of the layer or size of the Area object.

For the Shear Material direction, the following options are available:

- ***None***: This option will set the shear behavior to inactive and no stiffness or force will be provided for shear.
- ***Linear*:** This option will set the shear behavior to be linear elastic.
- Any previously existing material property of the same type as the *****Base Material*****: The **Nonlinear Properties** dropdown list will include all material properties with the same type as the **Base Material**. Selecting one of the material properties will set the shear behavior to nonlinear using the nonlinear shear stress-strain behavior of the selected material. The ability to select a different material property for the shear direction is useful for modeling reinforced concrete shear walls where the shear direction can be specified with reduced stiffness compared to the axial direction.

- Auto Hinge Options: This set of parameters is used for defining the program-generated Auto M3 Fiber Hinge and are only available when the **Base Material** is Concrete and *Auto P-M3* is selected for the **Nonlinear Properties** for the specific direction.

- ***Rebar Ratio*** edit box: Enter a value for the rebar ratio for the generated Auto Hinge. This is the rebar cross-sectional area as a ratio of the total layer cross-sectional area in the specific direction.
- ***Rebar Material*** drop down list:  Select a previously defined rebar material to be used for the rebar fibers in the auto P-M3 Fiber hinge.
- ***Rebar Fibers***radio button and edit box: Use the radio button to select whether the number of rebar fibers in the Auto Fiber P-M3 hinge is *Auto* or *User*. If *User* is selected, use the edit box to specify the number of rebar fibers to be used in the auto hinge.
- **Concrete Fibers**radio button and edit box: Use the radio button to select whether the number of concrete fibers in the Auto Fiber P-M3 hinge is *Auto* or *User*. If *User* is selected, use the edit box to specify the number of concrete fibers to be used in the auto hinge.

- Save Individual Fiber Response for Fiber Hinges check box: Use this parameter to set whether the responses of individual fibers in a Fiber hinge are saved for each step. Setting this option to No can be used in models with many fiber P-M2-M3 hinges where the user may not be interested in viewing detailed fiber results for all hinges to reduce the size of the analysis results data files.

**Note**: If the **Save Individual Fiber Response for Fiber Hinges** option is not checked, the individual fiber results (stress, strain, state, and status) will not be available after analysis has been completed. Hinge response (hinge state and status) will be available.

# Shell Section Layer Definition Form

Note:  The [area section thickness and joint offset overwrite assignments](../../../Assign/Area/Area_Thickness_Overwrites.md) do not apply to layered shells.

Use the Shell Section Layer Definition form to define a layered shell object.

- Quick Start button. Click this button to display the [Concrete Shell Section Quick Start Parameters form](Concrete_Shell_Section_Quick_Start_Parameters_Form.md). Use the form to specify rebar material and size for a single layer or the top and bottom of a two-layer concrete shell object. After the parameters have been specified on that form, the data will transfer automatically to the spreadsheet area on this form (i.e., the cells for the Layer Name, Distance, Thickness, Material, and so forth on the Shell Section Layer Definition form will be filled automatically). Modification to the parameters can be made by direct entry into the appropriate cell, as described below.
- Layer Name edit box. Use the default or type a revised label for the name of the layer (e.g., 1, 2, 3 or Top, Middle, Bottom).
- Distance edit box. Enter a value for the distance from the shell reference surface (shell object joint location plus offsets) to the mid-height of the layer.  Positive distances are in the positive shell object local 3 axis direction
- Thickness edit box. Use this edit box to specify the thickness of the layer. Note that the thickness of the section depends on the thickness specified for each layer (i.e., this value) and any overlaps or gaps between the layers. Thus, the section thickness is the value calculated by the program using all of the entries made in this column for each layer of the section.
- Type drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select the behavior for each layer. Select Membrane to model only in-plane behavior, Plate to model only out-of-plane bending behavior, and Shell to model full shell behavior.
- Num Int. Points edit box. Use the default or specify a revised number of integration points in the thickness direction for the layer. The locations are determined by the program using standard Gauss-quadrature rules.
- Material drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select the [material type](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) for each layer. Each material type will be given a unique color in the display area in the lower left corner of the form.
- Material Angle edit box. If appropriate, specify the material angle for the layer definition.  The angle is measured counterclockwise from the local 1 axis of the shell object to the local 1 axis of the material.
- Material Component Behavior:

- Type drop-down list: Use the drop-down list to select the material component behavior type: *Directional* may be chosen for any material property, *Coupled* is available if coupled nonlinear data is available for the specified material property (see: *[Material Property Options Form](../../Material/Material_Property_Options_Form.md)*), and *Hinge* may be chosen for any material property but Auto-hinge options will only be available for Concrete material properties. When *Directional* is selected, the behavior of the nonlinear components is determined from the material’s uniaxial nonlinear data and each component is independent from the others. When *Coupled* is selected, all three membrane stress components (S11, S22, and S12) will be nonlinear and their behavior is determined from the material’s coupled nonlinear data. When *Hinge* is selected, the behavior of the membrane components is selected in the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md).

Note: The *Hinge* layer type will only be applied to 4-joint area objects that do not have auto-meshing enabled. If a layered shell section property with a hinge layer is assigned to a triangular area object or an area object which is auto meshed, the hinge layer will be converted to a linear *Directional* layer with the specified layer thickness and material

- S11, S22, and S12 drop-down lists: When *Directional* is chosen in the Type drop-down list, choose *Linear*, *Nonlinear*, or *Inactive* from the drop-down list for each component. When any of the components is set to be Linear, the layer will behave linearly in that direction in a nonlinear load case. When any of the components is set to be Nonlinear, the layer will behave nonlinearly in that direction in a nonlinear load case. When any of the components is set to Inactive, the layer will not contribute to the stiffness in that direction in a nonlinear load case. When *Coupled* is chosen in the Type drop-down list, all components will be set to *Nonlinear*. When *Hinge* is chosen in the Type drop-down list, the components cannot be changed directly in the Layer Definition Data table. The S11 and S22 components will be displayed as *Linear*, *User NL Hinge*, *Auto NL Hinge*, or *Inactive* based on the Nonlinear Properties set for the S11 P-M3 and S22 P-M3 directions in the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) form. The S12 component will be displayed as *Linear*, *Nonlinear*, or *Inactive* based on the Nonlinear Property set for the Shear Material direction in the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md).

Note:  When *Hinge* is chosen in the *Type* drop-down list, the *Num Int. Points* is set to 1 and cannot be changed. The membrane behavior of a Hinge type layer is determined by the Nonlinear Properties and Auto Hinge Options selected in the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) and the Material Component Behavior will be automatically filled based on that selection. The plate behavior of a Hinge type layer is linear elastic and will use the material property and thickness specified for this layer.

When Directional is chosen in the Type drop-down list,  the Poisson's ratio will be taken as zero in a nonlinear load case, regardless of the value defined in the material property, unless all three material components are linear.

Note:  Regardless of the selected behavior, all three material components will behave linearly in a linear load case.

- Up and Down buttons. When multiple rows of data have been specified, use these buttons to move quickly through the spreadsheet area of the form.
- Add, Insert, Modify, and Delete buttons. Use these buttons to manage the rows of data in the spreadsheet area.
- - Enter text or numbers in the Layer Name edit box, values in the Distance, Thickness, Material Angle or Num Intg Points edit boxes or make a selection in the  Material or Nonlinear drop-down lists and then click the Add button to add that row of data to the definition. When *Hinge* is chosen in the Type drop-down list, clicking the **Add** button will cause the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) to pop-up. This is where the nonlinear hinge and shear material behavior can be defined for the layer.
  - Enter text or numbers in the Layer Name edit box, values in the Distance, Thickness, Material Angle or Num Intg Points edit boxes or make a selection in the  Material or Nonlinear drop-down lists and then click the Insert button to insert that row of data between two existing rows of data in the definition. When *Hinge* is chosen in the Type drop-down list, clicking the **Insert** button will cause the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) to pop-up. This is where the nonlinear hinge and shear material behavior can be defined for the layer.
  - Make a change in the Layer Name, Distance, Thickness, Material Angle or Num Intg Points edit boxes or the  Material or Nonlinear drop-down list and then click the Modify button to change that row of data. For a  *Hinge* type layer where the *Material* selection is changed such that the previous and current material are different types, the nonlinear hinge and shear material behavior of the layer will be reset upon clicking the **Modify** button - click the Modify/Show Hinge Layer Data button to view the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) form and set the nonlinear hinge and shear material behavior for the new material.
  - Highlight a row of data and click the Delete button to remove it from the definition.
- **Modify/Show Hinge Layer Data** button. This button is enabled when a Hinge type layer is selected. Use this button to open the [Shell Section Hinge Layer Definition Form](Shell_Section_Hinge_Layer_Definition_Form.md) where the membrane behavior of the layer, the nonlinear hinges and shear material, can be specified.

- Highlight Selected Layer check box. When this check box is checked, the layer selected/highlighted in the spreadsheet area will be shown in the display area with an outline in a darker hue of the Material display color.
- Transparency Control slide bar. The slide bar can be used to increase or decrease the transparency of the layers shown in the Display area. This slide bar is inactive when the Highlight Selected Layer check box is checked.
- Display area. A simple drawing of the orientation of the layer(s) relative to the shell reference surface (i.e., the red line shown in the display area) is displayed here.
- Section Name display box. This is the label given to the area section property on the Shell Section Data form.
- Order Ascending button and Order Descending button. Click these buttons to reorder the rows of data in the spreadsheet area according to the values in the Distance column.
- Calculated Layer Information area. The Number of Layers, Total Section Thickness, Sum of Layer Overlaps and Sum of Gaps Between Layers display boxes in this area of the form are informational and cannot be edited directly. The program displays information in these display boxes using the entries in other portions of the form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Shell Section Layer Definition form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Area Sections command, or select an area object(s) and click the Assign menu > Area > Sections command, to access the  Area Sections form. 2. Choose Shell from the Select Section Type To Add drop-down list. 3. Click the Add New Property button to display the Shell Section Data form. Alternatively, highlight a previously defined shell section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or the Modify/Show Section button to display the Shell Section Data form. 4. Select the Shell-Layered/Nonlinear option. 5. Click the Modify/Show Layer Definition button. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Time_Dependent_Properties_Form.htm | Time Dependent Properties Form -->

# Time Dependent Properties Form

Use the Time Dependent Properties form to display or specify the notional size parameters for the frame section or area section. Notional size is used for creep and shrinkage time-dependent analysis to determine the rate moisture can move through a section. Notional size is defined by the equation *h = 2A/P*, where *h* is the notional size, *A* is the cross-sectional area, and *P* is the cross-sectional perimeter. For a thin-walled frame section, *h* is on the order of the section thickness. For a circular section, *h* is equal to the radius. For a shell section, *h* is usually the thickness of the section.

Choose one of the following options:

- None: Creep and shrinkage are not computed for this section
- Auto: Notional size is computed automatically for the section. You may specify a scale factor to multiply the automatic value if desired.
- User: Specify the notional size you want to use for this section. The automatic value will be ignored.

For frame sections, the automatic value is computed from the area and perimeter of the section as h=2A/P.

For shell sections, the automatic value is taken as the thickness of the section. For the homogeneous shell sections (thin/thick plate/shell/membrane), the membrane thickness is used unless thickness overwrites have been applied to the shell object, in which case the interpolated values of the thickness overwrites are used for the affected objects. For the layered shell section, time-dependent behavior is not currently supported.

The Time Dependent Properties form is currently available for the steel/aluminum sections – I/Wide Flange, Channel, Tee, Angle, Double Angle, Double Channel, Pipe and Tube sections, all the concrete sections – Rectangular, Circular, Pipe, Tube, Precast I and Precast U sections, and the Shell Section Data.

To a*ccess the* Time Dependent Properties *form*, select a specific frame type from the [Add Frame Section Property form](../Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md) or access it via the **[Shell Section Data form](Shell_Section_Data_Form.md)**.

# Cable Section Data Form

Use the Cable Section Data form to define a cable section.

- Cable Section Name edit box. SAP2000 will suggest a default cable section name. Use the default or type a new one in the edit box.
- Section Notes Modify/Show button. Click this button to access the [Cable Section Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md). Use that form to add Cable Section notes to the model file.
- Material Property drop-down list. Select the [Material definition](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) for the cable from the drop-down list. Alternatively, click the + (plus symbol) next to the drop-down list to display the [Define Materials form](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) and define a new material property for use with this tendon.
- Cable Properties
- - Specify Cable Diameter option. Use this option to specify the diameter of the cable. Use the default or enter another value in the current units in the edit box.
  - Specify Cable Area option. Use this option to specify the area of the cable (length2). Use the default or enter another value in the current units in the edit box.
  - Torsional Constant, Moment of Inertia, Shear Area display boxes. These parameters are based on the cable diameter or area. They cannot be edited and are provided for informational purposes only.
- Modify/Show Cable Property Modifiers button. Click the Modify/Show Cable Property Modifiers button to access the [Cable Property Stiffness Modification Factors form](../../Property_Stiffness_Modification_Factors_Form.md). Use the form to modify the stiffness of the cable. Modification factors can also be assigned to individual [cable](../../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md) objects. If modifications are included in the property definition and then also assigned to an object,  the effects are multiplicative.
- Units drop-down list. Use the displayed units or select new units from the drop-down list.
- Display Color. The color in this box will be used to display the cable on screen or in printouts, if a color printer is used. Click on the box to display the Colors form. Click on a color and the OK button to change the display color for the cable.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Cable Section Data form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Cable Sections, or click on a [line object that has been drawn as a cable](../../../Draw/Draw_Frame_Cable_Tendon.md) and click the  Assign menu > Cable > Cable Sections command, to display the Cable Sections form. Then do one of the following:     - Click the Add New Section button    - Highlight a previously defined cable section definition and click the Add Copy of Section or Modify/Show Section button. |

# Cable Sections

Forms:  Cable Sections

Use the Define menu > Section Properties > Cable Sections command to display the Cable Sections form and add, modify, or delete a cable section definition.

- Add New Section button. Click this button to display the [Cable Section Data form](Cable_Section_Data_Form.md); use the options on the form to define a cable section.

- Add Copy of Section button.
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously defined cable section definition.
  2. Click the Add Copy of Section button to display the Cable Section Data form.  The form will be "pre-loaded" with the parameters specified for the definition selected in Step 1.
  3. Make the necessary modification to the form, if any, to complete a new cable section definition.
- Modify/Show Section button.
- 1. Select the property definition to be modified from the list of property definitions in the Sections area of the Cable Sections form.
  2. Click the Modify/Show Section button to access the Cable Section Data form and modify the selected definition.
- Delete Section button.
- 1. Select the property definition to be deleted from the list of section definitions in the Sections area of the Cable Sections form.
  2. Click the Delete Section button to delete the definition.

# Add Frame Section Property Form

Use the Add Frame Section Property form to add frame sections to the model. Adding sections to the model makes those sections available for assignment to selected frame sections. Note that code-specific frame sections also can be [imported](Import_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md) from [database files](Frame_Section_Databases.md) provided with the program.

1. Frame Section Property Type drop-down list. Select a material property for this frame section definition from this drop-down list.
2. {Section Type} buttons. Choose the type of section to be added by clicking on the button that has a graphical representation of the frame section type. The buttons available depend on the type of material property selected from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list. The following types of sections can be added.

1. - Frame Section Property Type:  Aluminum or Steel
   - - [I/Wide Flange Section](I_Wide_Flange_Section.md)
     - [Channel Section](Channel_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type: Steel
   - - [Tee Section](Tee_Section.md)
     - [Angle Section](Angle_Section.md)
     - [Double Angle Section](Double_Angle_Section.md)
     - [Double Channel Section](Double_Channel_Section.md)
     - [Auto Select List](Auto_Select_List.md)
     - [Steel Joist](Joist_Properties_User.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type: Steel or Concrete
   - - [Pipe Section](Pipe_Section.md)
     - [Box/Tube Section](Box_Tube_Section.md)
     - [Rectangular Section](Rectangular_Section.md)
     - [Circular Section](Circle_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type:  Concrete
   - - [Trapezoidal Section](Trapezoidal_Section.md)
     - [Precast I](Precast_I_Girder.md)
     - [Precast U](Precast_U_Girder.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type:  Built-Up Steel
   - - [Built Up Steel Section -- Cover Plate I](Built_Up_I_Section_with_Cover_Plates_.md)
     - Hybrid I
     - Hybrid U
   - Frame Section Property Type:  Cold Formed
   - - [Cold-Formed C](Cold-Formed_C_Section.md)
     - [Cold-Formed Z](Cold-Formed_Z_Section.md)
     - [Cold-Formed Hat](Cold-Formed_Hat_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type:  Other
   - - [General Section](General_Section.md)
     - [Nonprismatic](Nonprismatic.md)
     - [Section Designer](Section_Designer_Section.md)

3. The program will display a {Type} Section form. Use the form to define the section.

Note:  Although the types of sections have been grouped for presentation on the form according to the material most typically associated with that section type, any material property can be used by selecting the material from the Material drop-down list on the {Type} Section form. Note that clicking the + symbol preceding the drop-down list on that form displays the [Define Materials form](../../Material/Define_Materials.md), which can be used to define the material property for the section definition.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Add Frame Section Property form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections command, or select a frame object and click the Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command, to access the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a Section {Beam, Column, Chord, Brace} drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates). 2. Click the Add New Property button. |

# Auto Select List

Form: Auto Selection Sections

Auto select section lists are lists of previously defined steel sections (including cold-formed steel). When an auto select section list is [assigned to a frame member](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), the program can automatically select the most economical, adequate section from the auto select section list when designing the member. Auto Select Section Lists are used in Steel Frame, Aluminum Frame, and Cold-Formed Steel Frame design. At least two steel frame [sections must be defined](Frame_Section.md) before an auto select section list can be defined.

Define an Auto Select Section List as follows:

1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections command to display the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a {Type} Section drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates).
2. Click the Add New Property button to access the Add Frame Section Property form.  
     
   Alternatively, a previously defined Auto Select Section list can be modified by highlighting its name in the List of Sections display area on the Frame Properties form and then clicking the Modify/Show Property button. With the name of an Auto Select Section list highlighted in the List of Sections display area, the Add Copy of Property button can be used to start a new Auto Select Section list based on an existing list, and the Delete Property button can be used to delete an Auto Select Sections list.
3. Select Other from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list on the Add Frame Section Property form.
4. Click the Auto Select List button to access the Auto Selection Sections form.
5. Use the Auto Selection Sections form to name the auto select section list and choose the sections to be added or removed from that list.

   1. Auto Section Name edit box. Type a name for the Auto Select Sections list into the edit box.
   2. Section Notes Modify/Show Notes button. Click this button to access the [Frame Section Property Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md) and add section notes to the model file.
   3. Choose Sections area. Locate the sections to be included in the auto select list in the List of Sections display box. Use standard Windows methods to select the desired sections (i.e., click on a section and hold down the left mouse button as you drag the mouse down the list to select multiple sections; highlight a section and click the left mouse button to select sections one at a time; hold down the Ctrl key and click the left mouse button to make random multiple selections). Click the Add button to add the selected sections to the Auto Selections list on the right side of the form. To remove a section(s), highlight it in the Auto Selections list and click the Remove button. Removing a section from the Auto Selections list does not removed it from the List of Sections.
   4. Starting Section and Overwrites button. As indicated in the first paragraph of this topic, after an auto select sections list has been assigned to a frame member, SAP2000 automatically selects the most economical, adequate section from the auto select section list to use when designing the member. By default, SAP2000 performs the initial analysis using the median section by weight in the assigned auto select section list. If the Overwrites button is clicked, select a section from the list of sections shown in the Auto Selections list and SAP2000 will perform the initial analysis using the selected section. The selected section will display in the Starting Section box.
6. Click the OK button to close the Auto Selection Sections form and return to the Frame Properties form. Click the OK button on that form to complete the addition of the Auto Select Section definition.

Example:  Definition of an auto select section is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).

## See Also

[Aluminum Frame Design - Make Auto Select Section Null](../../../Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Make_Auto_Select_Section_Null.md)

  has been used
  and multiple sections have been selected for import.
- Set Time
  Dependent Properties button. Click this button to access the
   [Time Dependent Properties form](../Area_Sections/Time_Dependent_Properties_Form.md).
- Set Modifiers button.
  Click this button to display the
   Frame Property/Stiffness Modification
  Factors form. Use that form
  to specify the desired modification factors. Note that modification
  factors can be assigned here as well as directly to line objects,
  as explained in [Frame - Property Modifiers](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Property_Modifiers.md).
- Material drop-down list. Displays
  the list of  defined material properties. Use the list to choose
  the property to be included in the section definition. Clicking
  the + (plus) symbol preceding the Materials
  drop-down list will access the
  [Define
  Materials form](../../Material/Define_Materials.md), which can be used to add or modify
  the material definition associated with the selected section type.
- Dimensions area.  Displays
  the default values for outside depth, outside flange width, flange
  thickness, and web thickness. If the Channel
  Section form was accessed using the Add
  drop-down list or the Modify/Show button,
  the dimension values can be changed as necessary. Note that the section
  shown in the grid lined display box on the right side of the form
  updates as changes are made to the dimension values.
- Display Color.  The color that
  will be used to display the section on-screen in the model.

1. 1. Click on the "Display
      Color" text or the small sample square of the color to bring
      up the Color form.
   2. Select the desired
      new color on the Color form and
      click the OK button.

| Access the Channel Section form as follows:  Click the [Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections](Frame_Section.md) command or select a frame object and click the [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md)  command to display the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a {Type} Section drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates).  Then do one of the following:   1. - Click the Import New Property      button to access the      Import Frame Section Property      form or the      Add New      Property button      to access the Add Frame      Section Property form.    1. 1. Select Steel          from the Frame Section          Property Type drop-down list.       2. Click the Channel          button.    - Highlight the name of a previously      defined channel section in the Properties      area/Find      this Section list      on the left side of the  Frame Properties form      and click the Modify/Show      button.   If the Import New Property button is used and a database containing the selected section type has already been accessed, a form listing the sections of that type in that database will appear; choose the sections to be imported from the list by highlighting them. Note that clicking the + (plus) symbol preceding the Materials drop-down list will access the Define Materials form, which can be used to add or modify the material definition associated with the selected section type.    If sections of the specified type are not included in the database, a form to select another database to be imported will appear; choose a database from the list. If the selected type of section is not included in that database, an error message will display. To switch to another database, see the Note below. |

Note:  When
the Import New Property
button is used as described
above, the Channel Section form will include
an Open File button; click that button to
access a form listing the [various
section database files available](Frame_Section_Databases.md). After choosing a database, a form
listing the individual sections within the selected database will appear.
Choose the sections to be imported from the list and click the OK
button to display the Channel Section form.
 If the selected type of section
is not included in that database, an error message will display. Click
the OK button
on the error message to close it, and then click the Open
File button on the Channel Section form
to redisplay the list of possible databases; choose another database.
Repeat this process until a list of available sections of the required
type is displayed.

Click the Double          Channel button.    - Highlight the name of a previously      defined double channel section in the Properties      area/Find      this Section list      on the left side of the  Frame Properties form      and click the Modify/Show      button. <!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.htm | Frame Section -->

# Frame Sections

Form:  Frame
Properties

Defining a frame section makes the section available for assignment
to selected frame objects. The Define menu
> Section
Properties > Frame Sections command
can be used to (a) import sections from predefined databases, (b) define
frame section properties on the basis of their dimensions, (c) review
and modify section properties, and (d) delete section properties.

Note that after a frame section has been defined, it must be assigned
to selected frame objects (see the  [Assign
- Frame - Frame Sections](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) topic for more information).

TIP:  The forms
described in this topic also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus)
symbol that may appear next to a drop-down list of available sections,
such as the Beam and Column
drop-down lists on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates) that are used to start
a new model or to add objects from a template (Edit menu).

1. Click the Define
   menu > Frame Sections command to display the Frame
   Properties form. The Properties
   area of that form lists the names of all of the currently defined
   frame section properties; SAP2000 automatically creates this list.

Note:  The
Frame Properties form also displays when
the + (plus) symbol associated with the Beams, Columns drop-down lists
on the {Template} forms is clicked when
a [New Model](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates) is being
created or a when a {Template} is being
[added to a model](../../../Edit/Add_to_Model_from_Template.md).

2. Use the following buttons
   on that form to import or add sections to the list, modify previously
   defined sections, or delete sections from the list.

   - Import New Property button. Click this button
     to display the [Import Frame Section Property form](Import_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md).
     Use this feature to import code-specific sections from several
     [database files](Frame_Section_Databases.md) included
     with the program. Importing a section makes it available for assignment
     to selected frame objects. The Import
     Frame Section Property topic identifies the types of sections
     that can be imported.

1. - Add New Property button. Click this button to display the
     [Add
     Frame Section Property form](Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md). Use the form
     to select the type of section to be added to the model before
     accessing a form specific to the type of section selected.
     The Add Frame Section Property
     topic identifies the types of sections that can be added.

1. - Add Copy of Property button
   1. 1. Highlight
         the section property to be copied in the list of names in
         the Properties area
         of the form.
      2. Click the Add Copy of Property button.
         SAP2000 then displays a form specific to the type of section
         selected, with the editable parameters "pre-loaded"
         with the data used to define the section property selected
         in Step a.
      3. Use the editable
         options on the form to change the section definition as necessary.
         With the form displayed, use the F1 key to access a topic
         that has hyperlinks to individual Help topic relevant to the
         section types.
   - Modify/Show Property button
   1. 1. Highlight the
         section property to be reviewed/modified in the list of names
         in the Properties
         area of the form.
      2. Click the Modify/Show Property button.
      3. SAP2000 displays
         a form specific to the type of section selected. Use that
         form to modify the desired parameter. With the form displayed,
         use the F1 key to access a topic that has hyperlinks to individual
         Help topic relevant to the section types.
   - Delete Property button
   1. 1. Highlight
         the section property to be deleted in the list of names in
         the Properties area
         of the form.
      2. Click
         the Delete Property button.

Note:
Frame sections that are currently assigned to any line objects in the
model or that are used to define other frame section properties, such
as [nonprismatic sections](Nonprismatic.md) and [auto
select section lists](Auto_Select_List.md), cannot
be deleted.

Example:  Definition of
a frame section is demonstrated in [Problem
C](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem E](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_E.md),
[Problem H](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_H.md), [Problem I](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_I.md), [Problem J](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_J.md), [Problem L](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_L.md), [Problem N](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_N.md), [Problem P](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_P.md), [Problem Q](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Q.md),  and
[Problem Z](../../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Z.md).

## See Also

[Assign
- Frame - Frame Sections](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md)

[Assign
- Cable - Cable Properties](../../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md)

[Assign
- Tendon - Tendon Properties](../../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md)

[Add SD Section](Section_Designer_Section.md)

# Frame Section Databases

SAP2000 ships with the following section databases that can be accessed using the [Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections](Frame_Section.md) command or the [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) command.

- AA6061-T6.xml: AA standard sections for 6061-T6 extruded aluminum
- AISC16.xml: American Institute of Steel Construction shapes V16
- AusNzV8.xml: Australian and New Zealand steel shapes
- BSShapes2006.xml:  British Standards steel shapes
- ChineseGB08.xml: Chinese steel shapes
- CISC10.xml: Canadian Institute of Steel Construction shapes
- Euro.xml: European steel shapes
- Indian.xml:  Steel shapes in accordance with specifications from India
