# Import Frame Section Property Form

Use the Import Frame Section Property form to select code-specific frame sections to be imported into a model. Importing a frame section makes that section available for assignment to a frame section.

1. Frame Section Property Type drop-down list. Select a material property for this frame section definition from this drop-down list.
2. {Section Type} buttons. Choose the type of section to be imported by clicking on the button that has a graphical representation of the frame section type. The buttons available depend on the type of material property selected from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list. The following types of sections can be imported.

1. - Frame Section Property Type: Aluminum or Steel
   - - [I/Wide Flange Section](I_Wide_Flange_Section.md)
     - [Channel Section](Channel_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type: Steel
   - - [Tee Section](Tee_Section.md)
     - [Angle Section](Angle_Section.md)
     - [Double Angle Section](Double_Angle_Section.md)
     - [Double Channel Section](Double_Channel_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type: Steel or Concrete
   - - [Box/Tube Section](Box_Tube_Section.md)
     - [Pipe Section](Pipe_Section.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type: Concrete
   - - [Rectangular Section](Rectangular_Section.md)
     - [Circular Section](Circle_Section.md)
     - [Precast I](Precast_I_Girder.md)
   - Frame Section Property Type:  Other
   - - [General Section](General_Section.md)

3. Depending on the {Section Type} selected in Step 2, the program may display a form that lists the individual sections in the database (see Note). That form will display the Section Type, a Material drop-down list, and a list of the available sections.

Note that clicking on the + (plus) symbol beside the Material drop-down list will display the [Define Materials form](../../Material/Define_Materials.md), which can be used to adjust the material property for the section definition.

Click on one section in the list to select it for import, or [click here to learn about methods for selecting multiple sections](javascript:TextPopup(this)). The program will then display a {Type} Section form for the selected type of section.

1. 1. - Select one section by left clicking on it and then continue to hold down the left mouse button while dragging your mouse up or down to select additional adjacent sections.
      - Select one section by left clicking on it. Then hold down the Shift key on your keyboard and select another section. The second section is added to the selection as well as all sections between the first and second section.
      - Select one section by left clicking on it. Then hold down the Ctrl key on your keyboard and select another adjacent or non-adjacent section. That section is added to the selection. You can continue holding down the Ctrl key and clicking on other sections to add them to the selection.

Note:  If the program displays the Section Property File form, a database from which to import the section must be opened. See [Frame Section Databases](Frame_Section_Databases.md) for a listing of the databases of code-specific section properties that are included with the program (that is, \*.XML files). The Section Property File form most likely will display the first time the program is used to import a section. In that case, selecting the AISC16.XMLfile will open a database containing many standard section types. If the required type of section is not included in the open database(s), an error message will display. In that case, click the OK button on the message form to close the form. The program will display a {Type} Section form for the section type. Click the Open File button on that form to redisplay the Section Property File form; then choose another database until the form described in Step 3 displays.

TIP:  When sections are imported, most of the options on the {Type} Section form will be inactive and available for review purposes only. To change any of the parameters, click the OK button on the {Type} Section form to import the section and return to the  Frame Properties form; then highlight the newly imported section and click the Modify/Show button to redisplay the {Type} Section form with the options in editable format.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Import Frame Section Property form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections command, or select a frame object and click the Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command, to access the Frame Sections form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a Section {Beam, Column, Chord, Brace} drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates). 2. Click the Import New Property button. |

# Joist Properties User

- Design Type options. Choose the Standard (Like the K Series Joists) option or the Envelope (Like the KCS Series Joists) option. The options available on the Joist Properties User form depends on the Design Type selected.

- Material drop-down list. Choose the material property for this joist definition. Clicking the + (plus symbol) preceding this drop-down list displays the Define Materials form; use that form to add a new property or modify an existing one.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Nonprismatic.htm | Nonprismatic -->

# Nonprismatic

Note: At least two frame sections must already be defined for the Add Nonprismatic option to be included in the Add {Section Type} drop-down list box.

Nonprismatic frame sections may be defined with the properties varying along the section length. In addition, the section length may be divided into any number of segments of unequal lengths. Most common situations can be modeled using one to five segments. The variation of the bending stiffnesses may be linear, parabolic, or cubic over each segment of length. The axial, shear, torsional, mass, and weight properties all vary linearly over each segment. Section properties may change discontinuously from one segment to the next. [Click here](javascript:TextPopup(this)) to review figures and example input for nonprismatic frame sections.

Figure "a" shows a steel beam with
cover plates at the ends. Section A is the section without cover plates
and section B is the section with cover plates.

![](../../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-1816286110%202.gif)

Table 1 shows the assignments that would be entered
in the Nonprismatic Section Definition
form for the steel beam with cover plates in figure a. Note that segment
2 has a length type of variable and a segment length of 1. See "Segment
Lengths" for an explanation of this.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Table 1: Input for nonprismatic frame section shown in Figure a | | | | | | |
| Segment | Start  Section | End  Section | Length | Length  Type | EI33  Variation | EI22  Variation |
| 1 | B | B | 24 | Absolute | Not Used | Not Used |
| 2 | A | A | 1 | Variable | Not Used | Not Used |
| 3 | B | B | 30 | Absolute | Not Used | Not Used |

Figure "b" shows a concrete column
with a flare at the top. Section A is the section at the lower portion
of the column and section B is the section at the top of the column.
Table 2 shows the assignments that would be entered in the Nonprismatic
Section Definition form for the concrete column with a flare
at the top shown in Figure b.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Table 2: Input for nonprismatic frame section shown in Figure b | | | | | | |
| Segment | Start  Section | End  Section | Length | Length  Type | EI33  Variation | EI22  Variation |
| 1 | A | A | 1 | Variable | Not Used | Not Used |
| 2 | A | B | 50 | Absolute | Cubic | Linear |

To define a nonprismatic frame section, provide input in the following areas of the Nonprismatic Section Definition form and use the buttons to Add, Insert, Modify or Delete section definitions:

- Nonprismatic Section Name  Use the default or specify another name for the nonprismatic section to be defined. This name will appear in the Properties area of the Frame Properties form after the section has been successfully defined.
- Display Color box. The color that will be used to display the section on-screen in the model.
- 1. Click on the "Display Color" text or the small sample square of the color to access the Color form.
  2. Select the desired new color on the Color form and click the OK button.
- Section Notes Modify/Show Notes button. Click this button to access the [Frame Section Property Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md) and add section notes to the model file.
- Start Section and End Section
- 1. Select the name of a previously defined/default prismatic section from the Start Section drop-down list. This defines the end closest to joint i.
  2. Select the name of a previously defined/default prismatic section from the End Section drop-down list. This defines the end closest to joint j.

The starting and ending sections may use the same named section if the properties are constant over the length of the segment. The material would normally be the same for both the starting and ending sections and only the geometric properties would differ, but this is not required.

- Length edit box and Length Type drop-down list. Enter a value for the length of the section, and specify the length of the  nonprismatic segment as variable or absolute using the Length Type drop-down list. When a nonprismatic frame section is assigned to a line object, the actual lengths of each segment for that object are determined as follows:

- - The clear length of the object, Lc, is first calculated as the total length minus the end offsets: Lc = L - (ioff + joff). In that equation, L is the full length of the frame section and ioff and joff are the lengths of the end offsets along the length of the frame section at the i and j ends of the object, respectively.
  - If the sum of the absolute lengths of the segments exceeds the clear length, the absolute lengths are scaled down proportionately so that the sum equals the clear length. Otherwise the absolute lengths are used as specified.
  - The remaining length (the clear length minus the sum of the absolute lengths) is divided among the segments having variable lengths in the same proportion as the specified lengths. For example, for two segments with variable lengths, vl, specified as vl = 1 and vl =2, one third of the remaining length would go to the first segment, and two thirds to the second segment.
- El22 and EI33 Variation drop-down lists. Nonprismatic column/beam/brace section properties are interpolated along the length of each segment from the values at the two ends. Select linear, parabolic, or cubic from the EI22 and EI33 Variations drop-down lists to specify the variation of bending stiffnesses for the section.

SAP2000 calculates the linear, parabolic or cubic variation for EI33 as follows:

1. - Linear: The value EI33 varies linearly along the length of the segment.
   - Parabolic: The value ![](../../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-1544854799%203.GIF)varies linearly along the length of the segment.
   - Cubic: The value ![](../../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-1935685605%203.GIF) varies linearly along the length of the segment.

This usually corresponds to a linear variation in one of the section dimensions. For example, a linear variation in the width of a rectangular shape yields a linear variation for EI33. A linear variation in the depth of a rectangular shape yields a cubic variation for EI33. Finally, a linear variation in the depth of an I-shape yields a parabolic variation for EI33.

The interpolation of the bending stiffness in the 1-2 plane, EI22, is defined in the same manner to that for the 1-3 plane.

The remaining stiffness properties, other than EI33 and EI22, are always assumed to vary linearly between the ends of each segment. Similarly, the mass and weight densities are always assumed to vary linearly between the ends of each segment.

If a shear area is zero at either end, it is taken to be zero along the full segment, thus eliminating all shear deformation in the corresponding bending plane for that segment.

Effect on End Offsets Along the Length of Frame Sections

Frame section properties vary only along the clear length of the line object. Section properties within the longitudinal end offset at the i-end of the object are constant using the starting section of the first segment. Section properties within the end offset at the j-end of the object are constant using the ending section of the last segment. Note that if a longitudinal end offset rigidity factor is specified, the specified part of the end offset is rigid and the rest has the section property described herein.

- Add button. After parameters have been selected from the various drop-down lists and a value has been entered for the Length, click the Add button to add the definition to the section identified in the Nonprismatic Section Name edit box.
- Insert button. The Insert button is available only after at least one property has been defined. Highlight a previously specified definition and click the Insert button to insert another definition that is a duplicate of the highlighted definition. The option can be used to quickly add definitions when, for example, the length is the only item that requires changing.
- Modify button.
- 1. Highlight the definition to be changed.
  2. Select from the drop-down boxes or enter the revised values in the edit box.
  3. Click the Modify button to complete the change.
- Delete button. Highlight the definition to be deleted and click the Delete button.

Note: More than one pair of frame sections can be added to build the Nonprismatic section. Enter Absolute lengths (defined in the current units) to define sections that are of fixed length. Then the sections defined as Variable Length Type will be extended between the fixed sections. The Variable Length value is the ratio of the length of the section relative to all the variable length sections defining the Nonprismatic member. For example, if there are two Variable Length sections with lengths of 1 and 2, the section with length 1 will be 1/3 of the total variable length, and the section with a length of 2 will be 2/3 of the total variable length.  
  
This method of defining Nonprismatic sections can be used to define sections that have top and bottom fixed length Nonprismatic sections with a prismatic section defined between them, like a bridge pier, where the prismatic part of the section can “telescope” to fit the space between the fixed ends.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Nonprismatic Section Definition form as follows:  Click the [Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections](Frame_Section.md) command or select a frame object and click the [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) command to display the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a {Type} Section drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates).  Then do one of the following:   1. - Click the Add New Property button to access the Add Frame Section Property form.    - 1. Select Other from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list.      2. Click the Nonprismatic button.    - Highlight the name of a previously defined nonprismatic section in the Properties area/Find this Section list on the left side of the  Frame Properties form and click the Modify/Show button. |

# Property Data Form

Use the Property Data form to display, or in the case of a General section specify, the properties of the frame section. The program uses the property data values to calculate the section.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Property Data form as follows:   1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections command, or select a frame object and click the Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command, to display the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a {Type} Section drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates). 2. Then do one of the following:     - Click the Import New Property button to access the Import Frame Section Property form or the Add New Property button to access the Add Frame Section Property form.    - 1. Select {Material Type} from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list.      2. Click a {Section Type} button.   If the Import New Property button is used, a form to locate a database to be imported may appear. If a database containing the selected section type has already been accessed, a form listing the available sections in that database will appear. Choose the sections to be imported from the list. If sections of the specified type are not included in the database, an error message will display. To switch to another database, click the Open File button on the {Section Type} form to display the Section Property File form. Use that form to select another database. If the error message appears again, click the Open File button again to redisplay the Section Property File form and select another database. Continue this process until a list of available sections appears. Select a section(s) to be imported and click the OK button to complete the import.  When the Add New Property button is clicked and Other is selected for the Frame Section Type and the General button is clicked, the Property Data form will display immediately.   1. - Highlight the name of a section in the Properties area/Find this Section list on the left side of the  Frame Properties form and click the Modify/Show button.  3. For all section types except a General section type, a form for the selected type of section will appear with a Section Properties button on it. Click the Section Properties button to display the Property Data form. |

# Reinforcement Data Form

When frame section properties are specified for rectangular or circular concrete members, some of the reinforcing information for that member can also be specified using the Reinforcement Data form.

- Rebar Material
- - Longitudinal Bars and Confinement Bars drop-down lists. Select previously defined rebar materials from these drop-down lists, or click the + (plus) symbol preceding the drop-down lists to access the [Define Materials form](../../Material/Define_Materials.md) and add or modify a material property definition for use in the rebar material definition.
- Design Type. The choice made in the Design Type area of the Reinforcement Data form—Column or Beam—determines the parameters to be provided in the balance of the form.

Column

If the Design Type is Column, provide input for the following:

1. - Reinforcement Configuration  options.
   - - If the Section Type is Circle on the Frame Properties form, the reinforcement can be circular only.
     - If the Section Type is Rectangular on the Frame Properties form, specify rectangular or circular reinforcement.
   - Confinement Bars options.
   - - If the Reinforcement Configuration is Rectangular, the Confinement Bars can be Ties only.
     - If the Reinforcement Configuration is Circular, the Confinement Bars (transverse) can be Ties or Spiral.
   - Rectangular Configuration options.  If the Section Type is Rectangular on the Frame Properties form and the Reinforcement Configuration is "Rectangular," provide input for the following:
   - - Longitudinal Bars

1. 1. 1. - Clear Cover for Confinement Bars edit box. This is  the clear cover from the edge of the column to the confinement bar.
         - Number of Longit. Bars Along  3-dir Face edit box. This is the number of longitudinal reinforcing bars (including corner rebar) on the two faces of the column that are parallel to the local 3-axis of the section.
         - Number of Longit. Bars Along 2-dir Face edit box. This is the number of longitudinal reinforcing bars (including corner rebar) on the two faces of the column that are parallel to the local 2-axis of the section.
         - Longitudinal Bar Size drop-down list. This is the specified size of longitudinal reinforcing steel for the section. Only one longitudinal bar size can be specified for a given concrete frame section property.

TIP:  Click the + (plus) symbol beside the Longitudinal Bar Size or Confinement Bar Size (see below) drop-down list to access the Rebar Sizes form. Use that form to add or modify the rebar size for this definition.

1. - - Confinement Bars
     - - Confinement Bar Size drop-down list. This is the specified size of confinement reinforcing steel for the section. Only one confinement bar size can be specified for a given concrete frame section property.
       - Longitudinal Spacing of Confinement Bars edit box. Use the default or specify another value for the spacing of the confinement bars.
       - Number of Confinement Bars in 3-dir edit box. This is the number of confinement reinforcing bars that run parallel to the local 3-axis of the section.
       - Number of Confinement Bars in the 2-dir edit box. This is the number of confinement reinforcing bars that run parallel to the local 2-axis of the section.
   - Circular Configuration options.  If the Section Type is Rectangular or Circle on the Frame Properties form and the Reinforcement Configuration  is "Circular," provide input for the following:
   - - Longitudinal Bars
     - - Clear Cover for Confinement Bars edit box. This is  the clear cover from the edge of the column to the confinement bar.
       - Number of Longitudinal Bars edit box. This is the number of longitudinal reinforcing bars in the section.
       - Longitudinal Bar Size drop-down list. This is the specified size of reinforcing steel for the section. Only one bar size can be specified for a given concrete frame section property.
     - Confinement Bars
     - - Confinement Bar Size drop-down list. This is the specified size of confinement reinforcing steel for the section. Only one confinement bar size can be specified for a given concrete frame section property.
       - Longitudinal Spacing of Confinement Bars edit box. Use the default or specify another value for the spacing of the confinement bars.

Beam

If the Design Type is Beam, provide input for the following:

- Concrete Cover to Longitudinal Rebar Center options. Rebar cover is specified at the top and bottom of the beam. The Top cover is measured from the top of the beam to the centroid of the top longitudinal reinforcing. The Bottom cover is measured from the bottom of the beam to the centroid of the bottom longitudinal reinforcing.
- Reinforcement Overrides for Ductile Beams options. The reinforcement overrides are specified areas of longitudinal reinforcing steel that occur at the Top and Bottom of the left and right ends of the beam. These overrides are used by SAP2000 as follows:

- 1. - In the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor
     - - When the design shear in a concrete beam is to be based on provided longitudinal reinforcement (that is, the shear design is based on the moment capacity of the beam), SAP2000 compares the calculated required reinforcement with that specified in the reinforcement overrides and uses the larger value to determine the moment capacity on which the shear design is based.
       - When the minimum reinforcing in the middle of a beam is to be based on some percentage of the reinforcing at the ends of the beam, SAP2000 compares the calculated required reinforcement at the ends of the beam with that specified in the reinforcement overrides and uses the larger value to determine the minimum reinforcing in the middle of the beam.
       - When the shear design of columns is to be based on the maximum moment that the beams can deliver to the columns, SAP2000 compares the calculated required reinforcement with that specified in the reinforcement overrides and uses the larger value to determine the moment capacity of the beam.
     - For any degree of freedom in the frame nonlinear hinge properties assigned to a concrete member that is specified as default, SAP2000 calculates the hinge force-deformation properties based on the larger of the calculated required reinforcement at the ends of the beam (assuming that run the design has been run through the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor) and the specified reinforcement overrides.

- Check/Design options.  Specify that a member with this frame section property be checked or designed by SAP2000's Concrete Frame Design postprocessor. If the reinforcement is to be checked, all information in the Reinforcement Data form is used. If the reinforcement is to be designed, all information in the Reinforcement Data form is used except the bar size, which is ignored, and the total required steel area is calculated. The Reinforcement Configuration, Longitudinal Rebar data and Cover to Rebar Center are used.

If reinforcing is specified in a concrete column frame section property that was specified using the [Section Designer utility](Section_Designer_Section.md), the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor checks the column for the specified reinforcing or designs new reinforcing depending on the option that was selected in Section Designer.

[Reinforcement Bar Sizes](../Reinforcement_Bar_Sizes.md)

# Add SD Section

Form:  SD Section Data

Use the Section Designer utility to graphically define unusual sections. SAP2000 then calculates the section properties for that section.

Add frame section properties using Section Designer as follows:

Note:  To specify the rebar to be used in the cross section, click the Define menu > Section Properties > Reinforcement Bar Sizes command to access the [Reinforcing Bar Sizes form](../Reinforcement_Bar_Sizes.md) before opening Section Designer as described herein.

1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frame Sections command to access the Frame Properties form. The Frame Properties form also can be accessed by clicking the + (plus) symbol that may appear next to a {Type} Section drop-down list, such as appears on the [{Template} forms](../../../File/New_Model.md#Templates).
2. Click the Add New Property button to access the Add Frame Section Property form.

Alternatively, a previously defined SD Section can be modified by highlighting its name in the List of Sections display area on the Frame Properties form and then clicking the Modify/Show Property button. With the name of an SD Section highlighted in the List of Sections display area, the Add Copy of Property button can be used to start a new SD Section based on an existing list, and the Delete Property button can be used to delete an SD Section

3. Select Other from the Frame Section Property Type drop-down list.
4. Click the Section Designer button to access the SD Section Data form.
5. Use the SD Section Data form to provide parameters for the following:

   - Section Name. Specify or modify the name of the frame section.
   - Section Notes Modify/Show Notes button. Click this button to access the [Frame Section Property Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md) and add section notes to the model file.
   - Base Material and Design Type. Select a previously defined material property from the Base Material drop-down list or click the + (plus) symbol preceding the list to access the Define Materials form, which can be used to define a new material property or revise an existing one. The material option selected determines which of the Design Type options are available.
   - - When a steel material property has been specified, the No Design/Check option and the General Steel Section option are available for Design Type. If the Design Type is General Steel Section, any frame section assigned this property is designed by the Steel Frame Design postprocessor as a general section.
     - When a concrete material property has been specified, the No Design/Check option and the Concrete Column option are available. If the Design Type is Concrete Column, any frame section assigned this property is designed by the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor.
     - When an Aluminum, Cold Formed Steel, or Other material property has been  specified material, No Design/Check is the only option available. If the section type is Other, any frame section assigned this property is not designed by any postprocessor.

1. - Concrete Column Check/Design: This area is active only if the Concrete Column option has been selected in the Design Type area. Use this option to specify whether the concrete column is to have its specified reinforcing checked or new longitudinal reinforcing designed when it is run through the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor.
   - Section Designer button: After you have appropriately specified items in the rest of the form, click the Section Designer button in this area to go to the Section Designer utility and draw the section. When you exit the Section Designer utility, you return to the SD Section Data form. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the frame section property. Use the Help menu and the F1 key to access help topics when using the Section Designer utility.
   - Properties button. Click this button to display the [Property Data form](Property_Data_Form.md), which shows the frame section properties. When the form is accessed using this button, the values are not editable and are provided for review purposes only.
   - Set Modifiers button. Click this button to display the Frame Property/Stiffness Modification Factors form. When the form is accessed using this button, the values are not editable and are provided for review purposes only. Note that modification factors can be assigned directly to line objects, as explained in [Frame - Property Modifiers](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Property_Modifiers.md).
   - Display Color. The display color box identifies the color that will be used to display the section. Click on the box to access the Color form. Use that form to select a different color. Click the OK button to close the Color form after selecting the new color.

## See Also

[Reinforcement Bar Sizes](../Reinforcement_Bar_Sizes.md)

# Define - Frequency Dep. Link Props

Form:  Define Frequency Dependent Links

Use the Define menu > Section Properties >  Frequency Dep. Link Props command to add, modify or delete the definition of frequency dependent link properties. Frequency dependent link properties are used in [steady state](../../Load_Cases/Steady_State_Form.md) and [power spectral density](../../Load_Cases/Power_Spectral_Density_Form.md) analysis.

Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Frequency Dep. Link Props  command to access the Define Frequency Dependent Links form. Use the following buttons on the form to complete the appropriate action:

- Add New Property button. Click the Add New Property button to access the [Frequency Dependent Link Property Data form](Frequency_Dependent_Link_Property_Data_Form.md) and add a new frequency dependent link property.

- Modify/Show Property button.

- 1. Highlight the name of a previously defined link property in the Properties display area.
  2. Click the Modify/Show Property button to access the [Frequency Dependent Link Property Data form](Frequency_Dependent_Link_Property_Data_Form.md) and make the necessary changes to the selected link property definition.
- Delete Property button.
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously defined link property in the Properties display area.
  2. Click the Delete Property button to delete the selected property.

# Frequency Dependent Link Property Data Form

Frequency dependent link properties are used in [steady state](../../Load_Cases/Steady_State_Form.md) and [power spectral density](../../Load_Cases/Power_Spectral_Density_Form.md) analysis. Use the Frequency Dependent Link Property Data form to specify the frequency, stiffness, and damping for user-selected degrees of freedom.

- Property Name. SAP2000 will suggest a sequential default name. Type a new name in the edit box if required.
- Section Notes Modify/Show button. Click this button to access the [Frequency Dependent Link Notes form](../../Material/Notes_Form.md). Use that form to add Frequency Dependent Link notes to the model file.
- Degrees of Freedom with Nonzero Properties Shown Checked. This area of the form helps keep track of which degrees of freedom have been given non-zero properties, as explained in the balance of the topic.
- Show Properties for this Degree of Freedom. Use this drop-down list to select a degree of freedom to which nonzero values for frequency, stiffness and damping will be specified.
- Properties for Degree of Freedom {Degree ID}. This area requires spreadsheet type input. Enter the necessary values for frequency, stiffness, and damping for the degree of freedom selected in the Show Properties for this Degree of Freedom drop-down list. The grid-lined display area will display a plot of the definition.
- - Click the Insert Row Above Row 1 button to insert a blank row of cells in the spreadsheet area and enter another row of data.
  - Click the Add Row {Number} button to add a blank row of cells at the end of the spreadsheet area.
  - Click the Clear button to reset the grid-lined display area.
- Display Color. The color that will be used to display the property definition on-screen in the model.
- 1. Click on the "Display Color" text or the small sample square of the color to bring up the Color form.
  2. Select the desired new color on the Color form and click the OK button.

Link Props command or select an object that has been [drawn as a link/support](../../../Draw/Draw_2_Joint_Link_Element.md) and click the Assign menu > Link/Support > Frequency Dep. Link Props command to display the Define Frequency Dependent Links form. Then do one of the following:     - Click the Add New Property button.    - Highlight a previously defined frequency dependent link property and click the Modify/Show Property button. |

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Hinge_Properties/Curve_Interaction_Surface_Definition_for_Property_Name_Form.htm | Curve Interaction Surface Definition for Property Name Form -->

# {Curve} Interaction Surface Definition for {Property Name} Form

Use the {Curve} Interaction Surface Definition for {Property Name}  form to define, review and modify the interaction surface (P-M2-M3) or curve (P-M2, P-M3, M-2M3). The options available on the form depend on the type of interactive hinge. The options are common to all hinge types unless noted otherwise.

- Interaction Curve is Symmetric check box - for P-M2, P-M3, M2-M3 type hinges. When this check box is checked, the interaction curve is symmetric.
- User Interaction Surface Options - for P-M2-M3 type hinges only. Choose the symmetry for the interaction surface:  circular symmetry, doubly symmetric about M2 and M3, or with no symmetry. Doubly Symmetric about M2 and M3 is the default.
- - For the Doubly Symmetric About M2 and M3, the interaction surface is input in the (+ M2, +M3) quadrant for all values of P (i.e., both positive and negative). Thus only 90 degrees of the full 360-degree interaction surface is input. Symmetry is then used by the program to define the interaction surface in the (- M2, +M3), (- M2, -M3), and (+ M2, -M3) quadrants.
  - For the Circular option, input is needed for all 360 degrees of the interaction surface.

Note the tips in the Interaction Surface Requirements area in the lower left corner of the form. These tips explain the requirements for the various interaction surface options to assist in understanding the input on this form.

- Number of Curves edit box. Enter the number of curves for the interaction curve. For the P-M2-M3 hinge type, this is the number of equally spaced P-M curves that will be used to define the interaction surface.
- Number of Points on Each Curve edit box. Enter the number of points on each curve of the interaction surface/curve. Eleven is the default.
- Scale Factors (Same for All Curves), P, M2, and M3 edit boxes.

- Enter a scale factor in the P edit box of the Scaling area. The default for this value is 1. This scale factor multiplies all values in the P column in the Spreadsheet on the right side of the form.
- Enter a scale factor in the M edit boxes of the Scaling area. The default for this value is 1. This scale factor multiplies all values in all the M columns in the Spreadsheet on the right side of the form. Typically the interaction surface in the spreadsheet is normalized so that the maximum moment at Angle 90 is 1, and the scale factor is set to the actual value of maximum moment at Angle 90 (+M3). Alternatively, you may set the scale factor to 1 and input actual moment values in the spreadsheet, or use any other scaling.
- Include Scale Factors in Plots check box  - for P-M2-M3 type hinges only. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will modify the plot shown in the lower right corner of the form to reflect the selected scale factors.

- Units drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to change the units on the form.
- First and Last Points (Same for All Curves) area, P, M2 and M3 edit boxes. Specify axial values for the first point and the last point of the interaction surface curve. If the edit boxes are available (depending on the selections made elsewhere on the form), also specify moment values.
- Interaction Curve Data
- - Current Curve drop-down list and scroll buttons. Use the drop-down list to select a curve; the data for that curve will display in the spreadsheet. The scroll (i.e. arrow) buttons to the right of the Current Curve drop-down list also can be used to move from one curve to another.
  - Spreadsheet
  - - Use the defaults or enter values in the spreadsheet to indicate the various P-M interaction curves, which in the case of a P-M2-M3 hinge together define the interaction surface. The spreadsheet will display M column data for each of the curves specified in the Number of Curves edit box. Move through the data using the Current Curve scroll buttons.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Important Notes: | |
|  | For the axial load values, tension should always be input as positive and compression should always be input as negative. This is opposite the design convention for concrete but is consistent with the analysis convention and the steel-design convention. |
|  | The angle associated with each M column is indicated in the Interaction Surface Requirements area in the lower left corner of the form. Angle 0 corresponds to the +M2 axis (usually the minor moment), Angle 90 corresponds to +M3 (usually the major moment), and so on. The moment values in each M column should always be input as positive values. |

When entering values in the P column of the spreadsheet, the plot at the right-hand side of the form shows the P versus M Curve 1 diagram. When entering values in an M column, the plot at the right of the form shows P versus the M Curve associated with the cursor location.

1. 1. - Check Full Curve button. If the hinge type is P-M2, P-M3, or M2-M3, use this button to check the acceptability of the curve after changes have been made in the spreadsheet
      - For P-M2-M3 hinge types only:
      - - 3D Plot, Plan, Elevation, and Aperture arrow buttons and 3D, MM, PM3 and PM2 buttons. Use these buttons to adjust the graphical display of the interaction surface in the lower right corner of the form. Angle values can also be typed directly into the edit boxes.
        - Show All Lines check box. Check this check box to display all lines on the graphical display to the right of the check box.
        - Hide P Direction Lines check box. Check this check box to hide the P Direction Lines on the graphical display to the right of the check box.
        - Hide M2-M3 Lines check box. Check this check box to hide the M2-M3 Lines on the graphical display to the right of the check box.
        - Insert Curve button. Click this button to insert another curve in the plot.
        - Delete Curve button. Click this button to delete a curve.
        - Check Surface button. After making changes to the spreadsheet, click this button to have SAP2000 verify the acceptability of the interaction surface. SAP2000 will display a message box confirming acceptability or identifying the condition that makes the surface unacceptable.
      - Highlight Current Curve check box. Check this check box to display the current curve on the graphical display to the right of the check box. The "current curve" is the curve selected in the Current Curve drop-down list near the top of the form.

<!-- source: Menus/Define/Section_Properties/Hinge_Properties/Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.htm | Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge Form -->

# Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge Form

Use the Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge form to define, review and modify the parameters that affect the cyclic degradation behavior of the hinge.

- Cyclic Degradation Options, These options specify how the parameters will be defined.
- - None option. Choose this option to turn off cyclic degradation. This is the default.
  - Based on BUCDE Points option. Choose this option to use the deformation/SF values already defined in the hinge and specify the corresponding energy degradation factors. This option is only enabled when the hinge is defined with strength loss.
  - User Defined option. Choose this option to use the deformation/SF values for points B and E and input three intermediate user defined points along with the corresponding energy degradation factors .
- Cyclic Degradation Parameters. These parameters define the bending deformation/SF values and the corresponding energy degradation factors for five points. The points are either based on the defined hinge points or user defined points, depending on the option selected above .

## See Also

[Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Force_Deformation_Data_for_Parametric_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge.md) form

[Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 Hinge](Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form

Access the Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge form as follows:

1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties >  Hinge Properties command to display the Define Hinge Properties form. Then do one of the following:

   - Click the Add New Property button. The Default For Added Hinges form, with Steel, Concrete, and User Define options, will display. Choose an option as the basis for defining the new hinge property. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
   - Highlight a previously defined property and click the Add Copy of Property or  Modify/Show Property button. The Hinge Property Data form will display. Note that this button is available only if a hinge property is active; that is, a [hinge property has been assigned to a frame element](../../../Assign/Frame/Hinges/Frame_Hinges.md) in the model.
2. In the Hinge Type area, select the Deformation Controlled option and then select a parametric hinge type. (Concrete P-M2-M3 or Steel P-M2-M3) from the drop-down list.
3. Click the Modify/Show Hinge Property button to access the Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form.
4. Click the Modify/Show Force-Deformation Relationship button to access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 form.
5. Click the Modify/Show Cyclic Degradation Parameters button to access the Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge form.

# Define Fibers for Hinge {Number} Form

Additional Form: Fiber Hinge Properties for Hinge

Use the Define Fibers for Hinge {Number} form to define, review or modify the fiber definition data.

- Number of Fibers edit box. Enter the number of fibers to be used in the definition. Increasing the number in this edit box will add rows to the Fiber Definition Data spreadsheet.
- Overlay Section on Plot check box and Section drop-down list. To generate a graphic of the section showing placement of the fibers as the hinge is defined, check the Overlay Section on Plot check box and then select a section from the Section drop-down list. The selected section will be displayed in the "grid paper" display area in the upper right portion of the form.
- Fiber Definition Data spreadsheet. Use the cells in this area of the form to specify the area and coordinates of the fibers to be used to define the hinge. The graphical display in the upper right of the form updates as changes are made in the cells of the spreadsheet.
- - By Coord3 button. Click this button to reorder the fiber definition data in ascending order by the values in the Coord3 column of the spreadsheet.
  - By Coord2 button. Click this button to reorder the fiber definition data in ascending order by the values in the Coord2 column of the spreadsheet.
  - Clean Fiber Data button. Click this button to delete all data from the spreadsheet.
- Show Properties button. Click this button to display the Fiber Hinge Properties for Hinge form. This form is for display purposes and cannot be edited. Use the form to review the area, centroid, I33 and I22 of the fiber hinge and the section. The Overlay Section on Plot check box on the Define Fibers for Hinge {Number} form must be checked for the section properties to display.

## See Also

[Hinge Property Data Form](Hinge_Property_Data_Form.md)

# Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge Form

Use the Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form to define, review and modify the parameters that define the deformation capacities or acceptance criteria for the hinge.

- Deformation Capacity Options. These options specify how the deformation capacities will be defined.
- - Independent of P and V option. Choose this option to specify the deformation capacities independent of the axial and shear forces.
  - Dependent on P and V option. Choose this option to specify the deformation capacities dependent on the axial and shear forces.

- P and V Values on which Capacity Depends. These parameters define the axial and shear force values when the deformation capacities are specified to be dependent on the axial and shear forces.
- - P upper, PU the upper axial force.
  - P lower, PL the lower axial force.
  - V upper, VU the upper value shear force.
  - V lower, VL the lower value shear force.

- Deformation Capacity/Deformation SF for Bending about Axis 3. These are the ratios of the deformation capacity and deformation scale factor for bending about the 3-3 axis.
- - Number of Deformation Capacity Levels Defined specifies the number of levels to consider.
  - Values are the input ratios for the demand capacity levels IO, LS, and CP. If the deformation capacities are independent of the axial and shear forces, only one set of values is input. If the deformation capacities are dependent on the axial and shear forces, four sets of values are required.

- Capacities for Bending about Axis 2. This defines the deformation capacity for bending about the 2-2 axis.
- - Ratio of Axis 2 Capacity to Axis 3 Capacity (same for all levels) this is a ratio of the bending capacity about the 2-2 axis to the bending capacity about the 3-3 axis. The value must be non-zero.

  ## See Also

  [Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Force_Deformation_Data_for_Parametric_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge.md) form

  Access the Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form as follows:

  1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Hinge Properties command to display the Define Hinge Properties form. Then do one of the following:

     - Click the Add New Property button. The Default For Added Hinges form, with Steel, Concrete, and User Define options, will display. Choose an option as the basis for defining the new hinge property. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
     - Highlight a previously defined property and click the Add Copy of Property or  Modify/Show Property button. The Hinge Property Data form will display. Note that this button is available only if a hinge property is active; that is, a [hinge property has been assigned to a frame element](../../../Assign/Frame/Hinges/Frame_Hinges.md) in the model.
  2. In the Hinge Type area, select the Deformation Controlled option and then select a parametric hinge type. (Concrete P-M2-M3 or Steel P-M2-M3) from the drop-down list.
  3. Click the Modify/Show Hinge Property button to access the Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form.
  4. Click the Modify/Show Force-Deformation Relationship button to access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 form.
  5. Click the Modify/Show Deformation Capacities button to access the Cyclic Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form.

# Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge

Use the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form to define, review and modify the force-deformation data for a parametric P-M2-M3 hinge. The following figure shows the typical shape of the force-deformation curve used for this hinge and the corresponding control points.

![](../../../../assets/images/image2.gif)

- Curve Shape options. Use the following options to control the shape off the force-deformation curve and which inputs are active.
- - Elastic Perfectly Plastic option. Choose this option to force a bilinear curve.
  - Trilinear option. Choose this option to enable a trilinear curve.
  - Include Strength Loss (M2 and M3 only) check box. Toggle this option on to enable strength loss in the hinge. The onset of strength loss is based on bending deformations only. Strength loss in the axial direction will occur simultaneously with the strength loss in the bending directions .

- Force/SF area.
- - Ratio Point U/Point B the ratio of the force between point U and point B. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape .
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Axial the ratio of the axial force between point D and point B. This value is only used when considering strength loss.
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Bending the ratio of the bending moment between point D and point B. This value is only used when considering strength loss.
  - Axial Force at Balance Point/Comp SF this value specifies the position of the balanced point, scaled by the compression scale factor. The value should be less than 1.0 and greater than or equal to 0.

- Deformation/SF area.
- - Point U, Tension the deformation/SF representing point U in axial tension. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Compression the deformation/SF representing point U in axial compression. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point U for bending about the 2-2 axis. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point U for bending about the 3-3 axis. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point C, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 2-2 axis. This value is only used when considering strength loss.
  - Point C, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 3-3 axis. This value is only used when considering strength loss.
  - Point E, Tension the deformation/SF representing point E in axial tension.
  - Point E, Compression the deformation/SF representing point E in axial compression.
  - Point E, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point E for bending about the 2-2 axis.
  - Point E, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point E for bending about the 3-3 axis.
  - Ratio Point D/Point C, Bending the ratio of the deformation/SF between point D and Point C. This value is only used when considering strength loss.

- Force-Deformation Data spreadsheet area. Note, this area is for information only. To adjust the data and the plot, the parameters in the Force/SF and Deformation/SF areas should be modified.
- - Select Curve select the curve for which to display the data and corresponding plot.
  - Show Scaled Data check box. Check this option to show the scaled values when user-defined scale factors have been input for the force and/or deformation scale factors.

- Modify/Show Cyclic Degradation Parameters button. Clicking this button will display the [Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge](Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form. Use the form to define, review, and modify the parameters that affect cyclic degradation within a hinge..
- Modify/Show Deformation Capacities button. Clicking this button will display the [Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Deformation_Capacity_for_Parametric_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form. Use this form to define, review, and modify the parameters that define the deformation capacities or the acceptance criteria  for the hinge.
- ## See Also

  [Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Hinge_Property_Data_for_a_Parametric_Steel_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge.md) form
- [Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge](Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form
- [Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Deformation_Capacity_for_Parametric_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form

  Access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form as follows:

  1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Hinge Properties command to display the Define Hinge Properties form. Then do one of the following:

     - Click the Add New Property button. The Default For Added Hinges form, with Steel, Concrete, and User Define options, will display. Choose an option as the basis for defining the new hinge property. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
     - Highlight a previously defined property and click the Add Copy of Property or  Modify/Show Property button. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
  2. In the Hinge Type area, select the Deformation Controlled option and then select the Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 hinge from the drop-down list.
  3. Click the Modify/Show Hinge Property button to access the Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form.
  4. Click the Modify/Show Force-Deformation Relationship button to access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 form.

# Force Deformation Data for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 Hinge

Use the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 Hinge form to define, review, and modify the force-deformation data for a parametric steel P-M2-M3 hinge. The following figure shows the typical shape of the force-deformation curve used for this hinge and the corresponding control points.

![](../../../../assets/images/image1.gif)

- Curve Shape options. Use the following options to control the shape off the force-deformation curve and which inputs are active.
- - Elastic Perfectly Plastic option. Choose this option to force a bilinear curve.
  - Trilinear option. Choose this option to enable a trilinear curve.

- Strength Loss (M2 and M3 Only) options. Use the following options to control the strength loss in the hinge. The onset of strength loss is based on bending deformations only. Strength loss in the axial direction will occur simultaneously with the strength loss in the bending directions.
- - None option. Choose this option to turn off strength loss effects.
  - Independent of P option. Choose this option to turn on strength loss effects that are independent of the axial force.
  - Dependent on P option. Choose this option to turn off strength loss effects that are dependent on the axial force.
  - P upper (PU)/Comp SF the ratio of the upper value axial force and the compression scale factor. This value is only used when strength loss is specified as dependent on the axial force.
  - P lower (PL)/Comp SF the ratio of the lower value axial force and the compression scale factor. This value is only used when strength loss is specified as dependent on the axial force.

- Force/SF area.
- - Ratio Point U/Point B the ratio of the force between point U and point B. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape .
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Axial at PU the ratio of the axial force between point D and point B. This value is only used when considering strength loss and corresponds to the upper value axial force when strength loss is dependent on the axial force.
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Bending at PU the ratio of the bending moment between point D and point B. This value is only used when considering strength loss and corresponds to the upper value axial force when strength loss is dependent on the axial force.
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Axial at PL the ratio of the axial force between point D and point B, corresponding to the lower value axial force. This value is only used when considering strength loss that is dependent on the axial force.
  - Ratio Point D/Point B, Bending at PL the ratio of the bending moment between point D and point B, corresponding to the lower value axial force. This value is only used when considering strength loss that is dependent on the axial force.

- Deformation/SF area.
- - Point U, Tension the deformation/SF representing point U in axial tension. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Compression the deformation/SF representing point U in axial compression. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point U for bending about the 2-2 axis. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point U, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point U for bending about the 3-3 axis. This value is only used for the trilinear curve shape.
  - Point C at PU, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 2-2 axis. This value is only used when considering strength loss and corresponds to the upper value axial force when the strength loss is dependent on the axial force.
  - Point C at PU, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 3-3 axis. This value is only used when considering strength loss and corresponds to the upper value axial force when the strength loss is dependent on the axial force.
  - Point C at PL, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 2-2 axis, corresponding to the lower value axial force. This value is only used when considering strength loss that is dependent on the axial force.
  - Point C at PL, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point C for bending about the 3-3 axis, corresponding to the lower value axial force. This value is only used when considering strength loss that is dependent on the axial force.
  - Point E, Tension the deformation/SF representing point E in axial tension.
  - Point E, Compression the deformation/SF representing point E in axial compression.
  - Point E, Bending, Axis 2 the deformation/SF representing point E for bending about the 2-2 axis.
  - Point E, Bending, Axis 3 the deformation/SF representing point E for bending about the 3-3 axis.
  - Ratio Point D/Point C, Bending at PU the ratio of the deformation/SF between point D and point C. This value is only used when considering strength loss and corresponds to the upper value axial force when strength loss is dependent on the axial force.
  - Ratio Point D/Point C, Bending at PL the ratio of the deformation/SF between point D and point C, corresponding to the lower value axial force. This value is only used when considering strength loss that is dependent on the axial force.

- Force-Deformation Data spreadsheet area. Note, this area is for information only. To adjust the data and the plot, the parameters in the Force/SF and Deformation/SF areas should be modified.
- - Select Curve select the curve for which to display the data and corresponding plot.
  - Select P Level select the level of axial force to consider for the display of the data and corresponding plot. This option is only available when strength loss dependent on the axial force is enabled.
  - Show Scaled Data check box. Check this option to show the scaled values when user-defined scale factors have been input for the force and/or deformation scale factors.

- Modify/Show Cyclic Degradation Parameters button. Clicking this button will display the [Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge](Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form. Use the form to define, review, and modify the parameters that affect cyclic degradation within a hinge..
- Modify/Show Deformation Capacities button. Clicking this button will display the [Deformation Capacity for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 Hinge](Deformation_Capacity_for_Parametric_Steel_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form. Use this form to define, review, and modify the parameters that define the deformation capacities or the acceptance criteria  for the hinge.
- ## See Also

  [Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Hinge_Property_Data_for_a_Parametric_Steel_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge.md) form
- [Cyclic Degradation Parameters for Parametric P-M2-M3 Hinge](Cyclic_Degradation_Parameters_for_Parametric_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form
- [Deformation Capacity for Parametric Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge](Deformation_Capacity_for_Parametric_Concrete_P-M2-M3_Hinge_Form.md) form

  Access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 Hinge form as follows:

  1. Click the Define menu > Section Properties > Hinge Properties command to display the Define Hinge Properties form. Then do one of the following:

     - Click the Add New Property button. The Default For Added Hinges form, with Steel, Concrete, and User Define options, will display. Choose an option as the basis for defining the new hinge property. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
     - Highlight a previously defined property and click the Add Copy of Property or  Modify/Show Property button. The Hinge Property Data form will display.
  2. In the Hinge Type area, select the Deformation Controlled option and then select the Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 hinge from the drop-down list.
  3. Click the Modify/Show Hinge Property button to access the Hinge Property Data for a Parametric Steel/Concrete P-M2-M3 Hinge form.
  4. Click the Modify/Show Force-Deformation Relationship button to access the Force-Deformation Data for Parametric Steel P-M2-M3 form.

# Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} - Fiber P-M2-M3 Form

Use the Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} - Fiber P-M2-M3 form to define hinge properties based on fibers. The form has the following options:

- Fiber Definition Options
- - Default from Section option. Choose this option to have SAP2000 use fiber definition data based on the [section](../Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md) to which the hinge property definition is assigned.
  - User Defined option. Choose this option to enable the Define/Show Fibers button that can be used to display the [Define Fibers for Hinge {Property Name} form](Define_Fibers_for_Hinge_Number_Form.md), which can be used to define or modify the fiber definition data.
- Hinge Length edit box and Relative Length check box. Use the default or specify a different value for hinge length in the Hinge Length edit box. The hinge length may be input as an absolute length or a relative length. Check the Relative Length check box to input the hinge length as a relative length. Relative length is a fraction from zero to one of the clear length of the element, i.e., the length of the element minus the length of any end offsets.
- Define/Show Fibers button. Click this button to display the [Define Fibers for Hinge {Property Name} form](Define_Fibers_for_Hinge_Number_Form.md). Use that form to define, review, or modify fiber definition data.

## See Also

[Hinge Property Data Form](Hinge_Property_Data_Form.md)

Note that if an Auto hinge property is highlighted, the Hinge Property Data form will appear for display purposes only; the options will not be available for editing. 3. In the Hinge Type area, select the Deformation Controlled option and then select the Fiber P-M2-M3 hinge type from the drop-down list. 4. Click the Modify/Show Hinge Property button to access the Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} - Fiber P-M2-M3 form. |

# Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} Form - Deformation Controlled

Use the Hinge Property Data for {Property Name}  form to define deformation controlled frame or shell hinge properties. The options available on the form depend on the type of hinge being defined. The forms for Axial P, Shear V2, Shear V3, Torsion T, and Moment M2, and Moment M3 are generally the same. The forms for interacting hinges (P-M2, P-M3, M2-M3, and P-M2-M3) and Fiber hinges differs significantly from the others and is described in separate topics (see [Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} - Interacting {Hinge Type}](Frame_Hinge_Property_Data_for_Property_Name_Interacting_Hinge_Type_Form.md) and [Hinge Property Data for {Name} - Fiber](Frame_Hinge_Property_Data_for_Property_Name_Fiber_Form.md)  for more information).

- Type area. This area appears on the right portion of the form. The selection made here affects the other options available on the form.
- If the Hinge Type is Axial P, Shear V2, or Shear V3, the force-displacement criteria and the acceptance criteria may be input as one of the following:
- - Force - Displacement. Use this option to specify force versus displacement.
  - Stress - Strain With the Stress-Strain check box checked, fill in the hinge length in the Hinge Length edit box. The hinge length may be input as an absolute length or a relative length. Check the Relative Length check box to input the hinge length as a relative length. Relative length is a fraction from zero to one of the clear length of the object, i.e., the length of the object minus the length of any end offsets.
  - - When the force-displacement criteria and the acceptance criteria are input as stress versus strain, the program internally converts it to force versus displacement.
    - For an axial hinge, the force is calculated as stress times the cross-sectional area.
    - For shear hinges, the force is calculated as stress times the shear area.
    - For both axial and shear hinges, the displacement is calculated as strain times the hinge length.
- If the Hinge Type is Torsion T, Moment 2 or Moment3, the force-displacement criteria and the acceptance criteria may be input as one of the following:
- - Moment - Rotation. Use this option to specify moment versus rotation.
  - Moment - Curvature. With the Moment-Curvature check box checked, fill in the hinge length in the Hinge Length edit box. The hinge length may be input as an absolute length or a relative length. Check the Relative Length check box to input the hinge length as a relative length. Relative length is a fraction from zero to one of the clear length of the element, i.e., the length of the element minus the length of any end offsets.

- Hysteresis Type and Parameters. Select the hysteresis type for the  curve, and enter the associated parameters as required. See [Hysteresis Types](../../../Assign/Hysteresis_Types.md) for more information.
- Spreadsheet area.  Fill in the A, B, C, D, and E values (see figure) for the load-deformation table.

![](../../../../assets/images/Images/Load-def_wmf.jpg)

Note that the program will multiply the values given in this table by the scale factors specified in the Scaling for {Force and Disp, Moment and Rotation) area. The scale factors usually are chosen to be the yield load (force, stress, or moment) and the yield deformation (displacement, strain, or rotation), although you may use any scaling you wish. For non-symmetric curves, separate scale factors may be given for positive and negative values. In the following, the scale factors are indicated with the subscript SF:

1. 3. For Axial P hinge properties, when the force-displacement input type is chosen, the force is input as P/PSF and the displacement is input as D/DSF. When the stress-strain input type is chosen, the force (stress) is input as s/sSF and the displacement (strain) is input as e/eSF.
   4. For Shear V2 and Shear V3 hinge properties, when the force-displacement input type is chosen, the force is input as V/VSF and the displacement is input as D/DSF. When the stress-strain input type is chosen, the force (stress) is input as t/tSF and the displacement (strain) is input as e/eSF.
   5. For Torsion T hinge properties, the force is input as T/TSF and the displacement is input as q/qSF.
   6. For Moment M2 and Moment M3 hinge properties, the force is input as M/MSF and the displacement is input as q/qSF.
   7. For P-M2-M3 hinge properties, the force is input as M3/M3SF and the displacement is input as q3/q3SF. You cannot actually specify the moment scale factor M3SF; it is created automatically by the program when the hinge yields. Only the ratios of the moments at B, C, D and E are important, so you can assume any arbitrary value of M3SF when specifying the M3/M3SF values. The program internally creates M2 versus q2 and P versus D curves that are work-equivalent to the given M3/M3SF versus q3/q3SF plot at the time of yielding.

For all of the above, only the plastic deformation can be defined. Elastic deformation is determined by the frame or shell element containing the hinge. Therefore, only the positive deformations relative to point B and the negative deformations relative to point B’ are important. The load values at B and B’ are important, but not the deformation values (they may be zero).

3. Load Carrying Capacity Beyond Point E options.
4. Drops to Zero option. When this option is selected, the load carrying capacity drops to zero at point E.
5. Is Extrapolated option. When this option is selected, the load carrying capacity is extrapolated at point E (typically extrapolated parallel to line D-E).
6. Scaling for {Force and Disp, Moment and Rotation) area. Select the scale factors, SF, to be used for the load-deformation curve. Allow the program to compute yield values to be used for this purpose by checking the appropriate Use Yield check box, or uncheck the box and type values in the corresponding SF edit boxes. For non-symmetric curves, separate scale factors may be given for positive and negative values.
7. Acceptance Criteria area. The Acceptance Criteria IO, LS and CP values are deformations (displacements, strains, or rotations) that have been normalized by the same deformation scale factors used to specify the load deformation curve, and are typically located between points B and C and points B’ and C’ on the curve. They are used to indicate the state of the hinge when viewing the results of the analysis, but they do not affect the behavior of the structure.
8. Show Acceptance Criteria on Plot check box. Check this check box and SAP2000 will display the specified acceptance criteria on the model using the colors shown for the individual criterion.

Click the Add New Property button, or highlight a previously defined hinge property in the Defined Hinge Props area of the form and click the Modify/Show Property button, to display the Hinge Property Data form. Note that if an Auto hinge property is highlighted, the Hinge Property Data form will appear for display purposes only; the options will not be available for editing. 3. # Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} Form - Force Controlled

Use the Hinge Property Data for {Property Name}  form to define force controlled hinge properties. The options available on the form depend on the type of hinge being defined. The forms for all force-controlled hinge types, except Fiber, are generally the same. The form for Fiber (P-M2-M3) differs significantly from the others and is described in a separate topic (see [Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} - Fiber](Frame_Hinge_Property_Data_for_Property_Name_Fiber_Form.md)  for more information).

- For Axial P, Shear V2, Shear V3, Torsion T, Moment 2, and Moment 3
- Maximum Allowed {Force, Moment} area.
- - Specified Proportion of Yield {Force, Moment} option and Positive and Negative edit boxes. When this option is selected, use the edit boxes to specify the proportion of the yield force or moment. The value specified will be multiplied by the maximum allowed force or moment. The Negative edit box becomes enabled when the Hinge is Symmetric check box near the bottom of the form is not checked.
  - User Specified {Force, Moment} option and Positive and Negative edit boxes. When this option is selected, use the edit boxes to specify the maximum allowed force or moment. The Negative edit box becomes enabled when the Hinge is Symmetric check box near the bottom of the form is not checked.
  - Hinge Loses All Load Carrying Capacity When Maximum {Force, Moment} Is Reached check box. When this check box is checked, the hinge capacity drops to zero after the maximum force or moment is reached. When the check box is unchecked, the hinge behavior is linear elastic.
- Hinge is Symmetric (Tension Behavior Same as Compression Behavior) check box. When this check box is checked, this hinge definition will be symmetric. Any changes made to the values in the Positive edit boxes (tension) of the form will apply automatically to the Negative values (compression).
- Acceptance Criteria area. The Acceptance Criteria IO (Immediate Occupancy), LS (Life Safety) and CP (Collapse Prevention) values are deformations (displacements, strains, or rotations) that have been normalized by the same deformation scale factors used to specify the load deformation curve, and are typically located between points B and C and points B’ and C’ on the curve. They are used to indicate the state of the hinge when viewing the results of the analysis, but they do not affect the behavior of the structure.

![](../../../../assets/images/Images/Load-def_wmf.jpg)

- For Interacting P-M2, P-M3, M2-M3, and P-M2-M3
- Capacity Factor Defining Lower Bound Strength
- - Capacity Factor edit box. Use this edit box to specify the capacity factor defining the lower bound strength of the hinge. The lower bound strength of the force controlled interacting hinge is determined from an interaction curve (or surface for P-M2-M3 hinge) that is constructed by multiplying the specified capacity factor and the ordinates of the interaction curve (or surface) specified for the hinge.
  - Hinge Loses All Load Carrying Capacity when Lower Bound Strength Is Reached check box. When this check box is checked, the hinge capacity drops to zero after the lower bound strength is reached. When the check box is unchecked, the hinge behavior is linear elastic.
- Acceptance Criteria area. The Acceptance Criteria IO (Immediate Occupancy), LS (Life Safety) and CP (Collapse Prevention) values are deformations (displacements, strains, or rotations) that have been normalized by the same deformation scale factors used to specify the load deformation curve, and are typically located between points B and C and points B’ and C’ on the curve. They are used to indicate the state of the hinge when viewing the results of the analysis, but they do not affect the behavior of the structure.
- Modify/Show {P-M2, P-M3, M2-M3, P-M2-M3} Interaction Surface (Capacity) Data button. Click this button to display the [Hinge Interaction Surface for {Hinge Name - Hinge Type} form.](Hinge_Interaction_Surface_for_Property_Name_Interacting_Hinge_Type.md)
