<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Display_Design_Info.htm | Alum Display Design Info -->

# AL - Display Design Info

Form:  Display Aluminum Design Results

Review some of the results of the Aluminum frame design directly on the SAP2000 model (i.e., on screen) using the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Display Design Info command. This command displays design sections, unbraced lengths, effective length factors, allowable stresses, and stress ratio information.

Display design information on screen as follows:

1. Run an analysis.
2. Perform at least one design using the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command.
3. Select the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Display Design Info command to access the Display Aluminum Design Results form.
4. Select the Input or Output option and choose from the drop-down list the type of information to be displayed on screen. Use the Assign menu > Clear Display of Assigns command to remove the on-screen display of design information.

TIP:  Design results can also be displayed by right clicking on a frame section to display the [Aluminum Stress Check Information form](Alum_Interactive_Aluminum_Frame_Design.md), which also can be displayed using the Interactive Aluminum Frame Design command.

TIP:  When selecting to display design ratios a check box is available giving you the option to specify the minimum ratio for which results will be displayed.  For example, you can specify the only ratios above 0.90 are to be displayed.  In addition, another check box is available giving you the option to select the frame objects for which results are displayed.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Interactive_Aluminum_Frame_Design.htm | Alum Interactive Aluminum Frame Design -->

# AL - Interactive Aluminum Frame Design

Form:  Aluminum
Stress Check Information, Aluminum Details (Database), Aluminum Stress
Check Data

Interactive aluminum frame design allows you to review
the design results for any frame section and to interactively change the
design overwrites and immediately view the results.

Access
Interactive Aluminum Frame Design as follows:

1. Select the Analyze
   menu > [Run
   Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to analyze the model.
2. Select the Design
   menu > Aluminum Frame Design > [Start
   Design / Check of Structure](../Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md) command.
3. Right click on a frame
   section while the design results are displayed on it to access the
   Aluminum Stress Check Information form
   and enter the interactive design mode to interactively design the
   object.

If design results are
not currently displayed, click the Design menu >
Aluminum Frame Design > Interactive Aluminum Frame Design command
and then right click a frame section to enter the interactive design mode
for that section.

4. Use the various areas
   of the Aluminum Stress Check Information
   form to review the design:

   - Frame ID: Numerical identification
     assigned to the object.
   - Design Code: The design code
     selected using the [Aluminum Frame Design Preferences form](Alum_View_Revise_Preferences.md).
   - Analysis Section: The section
     property that was used for this frame object in the last analysis.
     Thus the design forces are based on a frame object  with
     this section property.
   - Design Section: The current
     design section property. If the frame object is assigned an auto
     select list, the section displayed in this form initially defaults
     to the optimal section. If no auto select list has been assigned
     to the frame object, the object design is performed for the section
     property specified in this edit box.  
       
     It is important to note that subsequent analyses use the section
     property specified in this list box for the next analysis section
     for the frame object. Thus the forces and moments obtained in
     the next analysis are based on this section. Change the Design
     section property by clicking the Overwrites
     button and making the changes on the resulting form.

Note:
 For final design iteration, the Analysis Section and the Design
Section property should be the same. Use the [Verify Analysis vs Design Section command](Alum_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.md)
to determine if this is the case. If it is not, repeat steps 1 through
4 until the analysis and design sections match. As appropriate, use the
Overwrites button and the [Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this))
to change the design parameters. Thus, the Analysis Section is changed/updated
by rerunning the analysis. The Design Section is changed by selecting
a new section on the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design
Overwrites form.

Use the [Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites form](Alum_View_Revise_Overwrites.md)
to make revisions to the aluminum frame design parameters, such as
unbraced length ratio, effective length factor, bending coefficient,
buckling constant, tensile strength, major and minor bending stress
and major and minor shear stress, among others. Then use the Details buttons on the Aluminum
Stress Check Information form to immediately see the new design
results.

If you modify some
overwrites in this mode and exit both the Aluminum
Frame Design Overwrites form and the Aluminum
Stress Check Information form by clicking their respective
OK buttons, the changes made to the overwrites
are permanently saved. When you exit
the Aluminum
Frame Design Overwrites form
by clicking the OK
button, the changes are temporarily
saved. If you then exit the Aluminum
Stress Check Information form
by clicking the Cancel
button, the changes made to the steel
frame overwrites are considered temporary only and are not permanently
saved. Permanent saving of the overwrites does not actually occur
until you click the OK
button in the Aluminum Stress Check Information
form.

4. - Table Showing Stress Details:
     This table shows the stress ratios obtained for each design load
     combination at each output station along the frame section. Initially
     the worst stress ratio is highlighted. Following are the headings
     in the table.
   - - Combo
       ID: The name of the design load combination considered.
     - Station
       location: The location of the station considered measured
       from the i-end of the frame object.
     - Ratio:
       The total PMM stress ratio for the object. When stress ratios
       are reported for this item, they are followed by (T) or (C).
       The (T) item indicates that the axial component of the stress
       ratio is tension. The (C) item indicates that the axial component
       of the stress ratio is compression. Note that typically the
       interaction formulas are different depending on whether the
       axial stress is tension or compression.
     - Axl:
       The axial component of the PMM stress ratio.
     - B-Maj: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the major axis.
     - B-Min: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the minor axis.
     - Maj Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio
       for shear acting in the major direction of the frame object.
     - Min
       Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio for shear acting
       in the minor direction of the frame object.
   - Overwrites button. Click the Overwrites
     button to access the [Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites form](Alum_View_Revise_Overwrites.md).
     Use the form to make revisions to the aluminum frame design parameters,
     such as unbraced length ratio, effective length factor, bending
     coefficient, buckling constant, tensile strength, major and minor
     bending stress and major and minor shear stress, among others.
     Then use the Details buttons on the
     Aluminum Stress Check Information
     form to immediately see the new design results.
   - Details button. Clicking the Details
     button displays design details for the selected design combination
     and station location. Print this information by selecting the
     File menu > Print command at the
     top of the window displaying the design details.
   - Tabular Data button. Click the Tabular
     Data button to access the Aluminum
     Details (Database) form. Use the various [menu
     commands](../../../Database_Tables/Database_Table_Form.md) on the form to export, display, and print the data
     table.
   - Table Format File button. Click the Table Format File button to access the Set Database Table Formats File form.
     Use the form to specify the Use
     Program Default Table Formats option or the Use
     Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option. When
     the Use Formats from User Defined
     Table Formats File option is chosen, also click the Select button to locate a previously defined
     format file. Table formats are defined using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).
     The default or selected table format will be applied to output
     of the data (export, display or print).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Make_Auto_Select_Section_Null.htm | Alum Make Auto Select Section Null -->

# AL - Make Auto Select Section Null

This command replaces the [Auto Select section assignments](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) for the selected members with the current design section previously chosen from the auto select group. This is an irreversible action, i.e. once the Auto Select sections are turned off they will no longer be available for optimal design. After using this command, Auto Select sections would need to be reassigned if they were to once again be included in the design selection process.  

Note: This action should be taken only after the final design cycle.

1. Select the frame members for which the Auto Select sections are to be replaced with the current design section.
2. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Make Auto Select Section Null command.
3. SAP2000 will issue a warning message that the Auto-Selected Sections Assignments will be replaced by the current design sections for the selected members. Click OK if acceptable; otherwise, click Cancel.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Reset_All_Aluminum_Overwrites.htm | Alum Reset All Aluminum Overwrites -->

# AL - Reset All Aluminum Overwrites

The Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Reset All Aluminum Overwrites command resets the [overwrites](Alum_View_Revise_Overwrites.md) for all frame sections with the Aluminum Frame design procedure to their default values. It is not necessary to make a selection before using the Reset All Aluminum Overwrites command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with the Aluminum Frame design procedure. The command can be used to reverse changes made using the View/Review Overwrites command.

Resetting your overwrites will reduce the size of your SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Reset_Design_Section_to_Last_Analysis.htm | Alum Reset Design Section to Last Analysis -->

# AL - Reset Design Section to Last Analysis

In some instances design sections may change several times (before the analysis is rerun) and then the design section for one or more frame objects may need to be restored to match the last used analysis section. The Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command is a quick and easy way to reset the design section to match the last analysis section. The anticipated process would be as follows:

1. Run the analysis and use the [Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure](../Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md).
2. Use the [Interactive Aluminum Frame Design](Alum_Interactive_Aluminum_Frame_Design.md) or [Change Design Section](Alum_Change_Design_Section.md) command to change the design sections.
3. Use the Start Design/Check of Structure command to update the design. For this example process, after review, portions of the updated design have been determined to be unnecessary or unacceptable.
4. Select the frame objects whose design sections are to be reset. If no frame objects have been selected, this command will not be available.
5. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command to immediately reset the design section to match the last analysis section.

Note:  Rerunning the analysis updates the Analysis Section to match the Design Section.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Select_Design_Combos.htm | Alum Select Design Combos -->

# AL - Select Design Combinations

Form:  Design Load Combinations Selection

Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Select Design Combo command to open the Design Load Combinations Selection form. It is not necessary to run the analysis or select an object before using the command; however, the program will not generate the code-generated automatic load combinations until at least one analysis and design iteration has been run, and therefore, the automatic load combinations will not be shown until design has been run. Use the form to review and modify the design load combinations used during design.

- Load Combination Type selection box. Select the type of design combination to review or specify (i.e., Strength, Deflection).
- Select Load Combinations area. All of the available design load combinations are listed in the List of Load Combinations list box. The design load combinations actually used in the design are listed in the Design Load Combinations list box. All three of the following buttons act on the highlighted design load combination in those two list boxes.

1. - Use the Add and Remove buttons to move load combinations into and out of the Design Combos list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections in this form for use with the Add and Remove buttons.
   - Use the Show button to review the definition of a design load combination.

Note:   If a user-defined combination(s) is to be used in design, it must be selected as described herein, regardless of whether the combo was created manually ([Define menu options](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)) or if the combination(s) is based on code (Define menu, [Add Default Design Combos button](../../Define/Load_Combination/Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md))  The program automatically selects those combos that are created when the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box is checked (see next bullet). Note also that these automatically generated combos are regenerated (i.e., replaced) after each design run.

- Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box. When this check box is checked, the design load combinations generated based on the selected code (i.e., the code selected using the [Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences command](Alum_View_Revise_Preferences.md)) are added to the List of Load Combinations.
- - Set Automatic Design Load Combination Data button. With the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box checked, click this button to access the [Code Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Code} form](../Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.md). Use that form to make changes to the automatically generated code-based design load combinations to be applied during model design.

The default aluminum frame design load combinations have names such as DALM1, DALM2 and so forth.

## See Also

[Load Combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Select_Design_Groups.htm | Alum Select Design Groups -->

# AL - Select Design Groups

Form: Aluminum Design Group Selection

In SAP2000, frame objects can be grouped for aluminum frame design. When a group is specified for design, all frame objects in the group are given the same section.

1. Define the groups by selecting the frame objects and clicking the Assign menu > Assign to Groups command. Designing with groups only works if you have assigned [auto select sections](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) to the frame. Typically, assign the same auto select section to each frame object to be used in a design group, although this is not absolutely necessary. Any frame object in a design group not assigned an auto select section will be ignored for group design and will be designed individually.
2. After the group has been defined, use the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Select Design Group command to access the Aluminum Frame Design Group Selection form. All of the available groups are listed in the List of Groups list box on the Aluminum Design Group Selection form. The groups actually in use are listed in the Design Groups list box.
3. On the Aluminum Design Group Selection form, use the Add and Remove buttons to move groups into and out of the Design Groups list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections before using the Add and Remove buttons.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Set_Displacement_Targets.htm | Alum Set Displacement Targets -->

# AL - Set Displacement Targets

Form: Lateral Displacement Targets

For displacement optimization, SAP2000 predicts which members should be increased in size to control the displacements based on the energy per unit volume in the members. The members with more energy per unit volume are increased in size a larger percentage than those with smaller energies per unit volume. Some members with small energy per unit volume may be decreased in size if they are still acceptable for strength considerations.

Note: [Auto select lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to the frame objects for the displacement optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the desired displacement target may never be reached no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Specify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form, which can be used to specify displacement targets for various load cases. The intent is that a point is picked, typically at the roof level of the model, and a maximum displacement target (in any direction) is specified for one or more load cases on that point.
2. In the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form, select the load pattern from the drop-down list for which the displacement is to be optimized.
3. Specify the location for the displacement by specifying a Point.
4. Specify the target displacement.
5. Click the Add button.
6. Repeat Steps 1 through 5 as needed.
7. Run the design (Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure) and then rerun the analysis (Analyze menu > Run Analysis) with the new section sizes to view the displacements by right clicking on selected points. Displacement optimization is an iterative process that typically requires rerunning the analysis and design multiple times. There is no guarantee that the displacement target will be reached using this option.

Tip:  To rerun the analysis, it will be necessary to delete the design results (i.e., unlock the model, or use the Delete Results button on the Set Analysis Cases to Run form). This will not adversely affect the specification of displacement targets.

Modify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be modified in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form. Note that the data for the specification appears in the boxes at the top of the Loads area. Modify the data in the boxes as desired.
3. Click the Modify button.
4. Rerun the analysis with the new section sizes to review the displacements.

Delete a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be deleted in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
3. Click the Delete button.

Deactivate Targets check box. Check the Deactivate Targets check box to exclude the displacements from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include displacements in design.

## See Also

[Set Time Period Targets](Alum_Set_Time_Period_Targets.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Set_Time_Period_Targets.htm | Alum Set Time Period Targets -->

# AL - Set Time Period Targets

Form: Time Period Targets

For time period targets, specify a mode and a target period for that mode. Then, during design, SAP2000 automatically optimizes the structure to meet the target period using energy considerations. During the optimization process, members with large energy per unit volume are changed more than those with small energy per unit volume.

Note: [Auto select section lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to frame objects for the time period optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select section list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the displacement target may never be met, no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Use the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Set Time Period Targets command to display the Time Period Targets form.

- Modal Analysis Case. Select the modal analysis case for which time period targets are being set.
- Add a Target.
- 1. Enter a number in the Mode Number edit box.
  2. SAP2000 will suggest a value in the Target Period edit box. Use this target period or type a revised value in the edit box.
  3. Click the Add button. Then run the design for the model with the time period targets set.
- Modify a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be modified in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Type revised value in the Target Period edit box.
  3. Click the Modify button. Then rerun the design for the model with the time period targets modified.
- Delete a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be deleted in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Click the Delete button. Then rerun the design for the model with the time period targets deleted.

Deactivate Time Period Targets check box. Check the Deactivate Time Period Targets check box to exclude the time periods from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include time periods in design.

## See Also

[Set Displacement Targets](Alum_Set_Displacement_Targets.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.htm | Alum Start Design-Check of Structure -->

# AL - Start Design/Check of Structure

The Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command starts the aluminum frame design process.

Run a aluminum frame design as follows:

1. Click the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of the model.
2. Click Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command.

Note: This command is unavailable if no line objects with the Aluminum Frame design procedure have been included in the model. If line objects have been selected when this command is used, only the selected line objects are designed. If no line objects are selected when this command is used, all line objects with the Aluminum Frame design procedure are designed.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Verify_All_Members_Passed.htm | Alum Verify All Members Passed -->

# AL - Verify All Members Passed

When the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command is used, the program reports if structural members passed the stress/capacity check.

Use the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command as follows:

1. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis.
2. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to run the design.
3. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command.

SAP2000 will display a pop-up box indicating the outcome of the verification. If members do not pass the check, the [Change Design Section command](Alum_Change_Design_Section.md) can be used to change the design section before rerunning the design.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.htm | Alum Verify Analysis vs Design Section -->

# AL - Verify Analysis vs Design Section

When the iterative design process is complete, the
last used analysis section property for a frame object and the current
design section property for that frame object should be the same. If this
is not the case, the frame object may not have been designed for the correct
forces. The Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design
> Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is useful for verifying
that the last used analysis section and the current design section are
the same for all aluminum frame objects in the model.

When the Verify Analysis vs
Design Section command is used, SAP2000 identifies how many frame
objects with the Aluminum Frame design procedure have different analysis
and design sections and then selects those frame objects, if you ask it
to. Typically this command would be used after the final design iteration
to verify that the analysis and design properties used are consistent.

It is not necessary to select any frame objects before
using the Verify Analysis vs Design Section
command. This command automatically checks all frame sections with the
Aluminum Frame design procedure.

Note: Update the
Analysis Section by rerunning the analysis, perhaps several times in a
complex model. Update the Design Section using the [Interactive Aluminum Frame Design command](Alum_Interactive_Aluminum_Frame_Design.md)
and the Overwrites button or the [Change Design Section command](Alum_Change_Design_Section.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm | Alum View Revise Overwrites -->

# AL - View/Revise Overwrites

Form:  Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites for {Code}

Aluminum frame design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the frame/cable objects to which they are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all aluminum frame overwrite items. Thus, it is not required that overwrites be specified. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items and change them as necessary to make sure they are acceptable.

Some of the default overwrite values are based on aluminum frame preferences. Thus the preferences should be defined before defining the overwrites (and before designing or checking any aluminum frame members).

When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the objects to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the objects that are selected when the overwrites are changed.

Change an overwrite as follows:

Be sure to check, and as necessary, review, and change if necessary, the [Aluminum Frame Design Preferences](Alum_View_Revise_Preferences.md)  before completing the following steps.

1. Select the frame object(s) for which overwrites are being specified.
2. Click the Design menu > Aluminum Frame Design > View/Revise Overwrites command, which brings up the Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites form. The aluminum frame overwrites are displayed with an Item column and a Value column. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the overwrite item.

Note:  The Overwrites button on the Aluminum Stress Check Information form can also be used to display the Aluminum Frame Design Overwrites form.

3. Left click in the Value column to activate a drop-down box or to highlight the contents of the cell.

- If the drop-down box appears, select a value from the box. Values in the drop-down boxes can not be changed.
- If the cell contents becomes highlighted, type in a revised value(s) as needed.

- Set to Prog Determined Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program defaults. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.

5. Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the items and then click the Selected Items button to restore those items to previously specified values.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Aluminum_Frame_Design/Alum_View_Revise_Preferences.htm | Alumi View Revise Preferences -->

# Alum View/Revise Preferences

Form:  Aluminum Frame Design Preferences for {Code}

Preferences are basic settings that design parameters. Use the Aluminum Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form to access those design parameters, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using this form.

1. Click the Design  menu > Aluminum Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences command to display the Aluminum Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form.

1. - Item/Value. Click in any of the drop-down lists or edit boxes in the Value column to change the default values to your specific choices.
   - Item Description. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the preference item.
   - Explanation of Color Coding for Values area. The items in this area are color-coded blue, black or red. The meaning of each color code is defined in the this area of the form.
   - Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.
   - Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.htm | Code-Generated Automatic Load Combinations for Type Code Form -->

# Code-Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Type} Frame Design {Code} Form

Additional form:  Design Load Type

Program design is based on a set of loading combinations. This topic describes automatically generated load combinations for the specified design code. If the automatically generated load combinations are acceptable, no definition of additional load combinations is required. If additional load combinations are required, user load combinations can be defined using the [Define menu > Load Combinations command](../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md).

Use the Code-Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Type} Frame Design - {Code} form to review, and if necessary specify, the limit state and the load cases for which a load combination will be automatically generated. Combinations will be generated for each specified limit state.  Automatically generated combinations generally are those required by the code selected using the Design menu > {Type} Design > View/Revise Preferences command.

Note: Automatically generated load combinations are created after one iteration of analysis and design has been performed. Automatically generated load combinations update automatically with each analysis/design iteration; [user defined load combinations](../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) do not update automatically.

- Limit States for which Automatic Load Combinations are to be Generated and associated check boxes. Specify the limit state(s) for which the combinations are to be generated. When a limit state check box is checked, the program will generate combinations for that limit state.
- Choose Load Cases to Use for Limit State
- - Limit State drop-down list. Limit states are code-specified types of combinations. Choose the Limit State for which combinations will be generated using the load cases specified in the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations  list. The list of load combinations must be specified for each Limit State. Note that the  Copy to button (see below) can be used to speed this process.
  - List of Load Cases and Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations.  All load cases are listed in the List of Load Cases display lists (i.e., Load Case Name, Load Case Type, Design Load Type). The cases to be used in generating the automatic load combination are listed in the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists. To specify that a load case be included in or excluded from a combination, select a load case by clicking on it and then use the arrow keys to move the selected load case into or out of the Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists.

Note:  Each load case has a Design Type that can be set by the user or be program determined. The Design Type of a load case determines if it can be included in a given limit state, how it is to be included (e.g., additive, envelope), and the scale factor to be used, all in accordance with the design code. Only load cases with the appropriate Design Type can be included in a given limit state. For this reason, load cases can not be added arbitrarily to a limit state.

1. 1. - Show Only Load Cases with Valid Design Load Type check box. When this check box is checked, only those load cases with a valid design type for the applied code are listed in the List of Load Cases display lists.
      - Copy to button. Use this button to copy the specified load combination definition to the limit state selected in the drop-down list.

1. - Show Load Case Definition button.
   - 1. Highlight a load case in the List of Load Cases or Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display list to enable this button.
     2. Click the button to access the [Load Case Data - {Load Case} definition form](../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) for the load case selected in Step 1.
     3. The form is provided for review purposes only. Any changes made will be ignored.
   - Set Design Load Type button.
   - 1. Highlight a load case in the List of Load Cases or Load Cases for Automatic Load Combinations display lists to enable this button.
     2. Click the button to access the Design Load type form.
     3. Choose an option to set the Design Load Type of the load case selected in Step 1 to Program Determined  or User Defined. If the User Defined option is selected, choose a load type from the drop-down list to update the load case definition.

Note:  If the Design Type is program determined, the Design Type is inherent in the Load Case type or it is based on the Design Type of the load patterns that have been applied in the load case. The [Define menu > Load Patterns command](../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) accesses the form needed to specify the Design Type for individual load patterns.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Code-Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Type} Frame Design - {Code} form as follows:   1. Click the Design menu > {Type} Frame Design > Select Design Combos command to access the Design Load Combination Selection form. 2. Check the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box. 3. Click the Set Automatic Design Load Combinations Data button. |


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Change_Design_Section.htm | CFSF Change Design Section -->

# CFSF - Change Design Section

Form:  Select Sections

Because design is an iterative process, after a cold-formed steel frame design has been run, it may be necessary to change the design section property assigned to one or more objects. SAP2000 allows multiple design iteration runs without rerunning the analysis, which can save computing time.

Change a design section and redesign the structure without rerunning the analysis as follows:

1. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to analyze your model.
2. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Start Design / Check of Structure command to complete the initial design. As necessary, use the Design menu > Cold-Formed  Steel Frame Design > Interactive Steel Frame Design command to evaluate the results.
3. Select the line object(s) to be changed. If no line objects are selected, the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Change Design Section command will not be available.
4. Select the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Change Design Section command to access the Select Sections form. Choose the new section from the display list.

TIP:  If nothing is shown in the list, additional cold formed steel frame section definitions should be added to the model using the [Define menu > Frame Sections command](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md).

5. Repeat Steps 2 through 4 as necessary.

Note:  The Change Design Section command changes only the design section for the selected line object(s). The forces used in the design are not based on this new section size but are instead based on whatever section was used in the last analysis. Recall, however, that the design section property is used for the next analysis section property. Thus changing the design section property also changes the next analysis section property. If an [auto select section](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) is assigned to a frame/cable, control the section property used for that frame/cable in the next analysis by setting the design section property to the desired section using the Change Design Section command and then rerunning the analysis.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Delete_Cold_Formed_Steel_Design_Results.htm | CFSF Delete Cold Formed Steel Design Results -->

# CFSF - Delete Cold-Formed Steel Design Results

The Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Delete Cold-Formed Steel Design Results command deletes all of the cold-formed steel frame design results. It is not necessary to make a selection before using this command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with the Cold-Formed Steel Frame design procedure.

Deleting your cold-formed steel frame design results will reduce the size of your SAP2000 database (\*.SBD) file.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Display_Design_Info.htm | CFSF Display Design Info -->

# CFSF - Display Design Info

Form:  Display Cold-Formed Steel Design Results

Review some of the results of the cold-formed steel frame design directly on the SAP2000 model (i.e., on screen) using the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Display Design Info command. This command displays the Display Cold-Formed Steel Design Results form.

Display design information on screen as follows:

1. Run an analysis.
2. Perform at least one design using the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command.
3. Select the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Display Design Info command to access the Display Cold-Formed Steel Design Results form.

Select the Input or Output option and choose from the drop-down list the type of information to be displayed on screen.

- Right click on a frame object to display the [Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check Information form](CFSF_Interactive_Cold_Formed_Steel_Frame_Design.md), which also can be displayed using the Interactive Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design command.
- Use the Assign menu > Clear Display of Assigns command to remove the on-screen display of design information.

TIP:  When selecting to display design ratios a check box is available giving you the option to specify the minimum ratio for which results will be displayed.  For example, you can specify the only ratios above 0.90 are to be displayed.  In addition, another check box is available giving you the option to select the frame objects for which results are displayed.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Interactive_Cold_Formed_Steel_Frame_Design.htm | CFSF Interactive Cold Formed Steel Frame Design -->

# CFSF - Interactive Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design

Form:  Cold-Formed
Steel Stress Check Information

Interactive cold-formed steel frame design allows
you to review the design results for any frame object and to interactively
change the design overwrites and immediately view the results.

After completing the
[Modeling Process](../../../Getting_Started/Modeling_Process.md)
using [cold-formed
steel frames](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md), access Interactive Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design as
follows:

1. Select the Analyze
   menu > [Run
   Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to analyze the model.
2. Select the Design
   menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > [Start
   Design / Check of Structure](CFSF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md) command.
3. Right click on a frame
   object while the design results are displayed on it to access the
   Cold-Formed Steel
   Stress Check Information form and enter the interactive design
   mode to interactively design the object.

If design results are
not currently displayed, click the Design menu >
Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Interactive Cold Formed Steel Frame
Design command and then right click a cold-formed steel frame object
to enter the interactive design mode for that object.

4. Use the various areas
   of the Cold-Formed Steel
   Stress Check Information form to review the design:

   - Frame ID: The
     label associated with a frame object.
   - Design Code: The design code
     selected using the [Cold-Formed Steel
     Frame Design Preferences form](CFSF_View_Revise_Preferences.md).
   - Analysis Section: The section
     property that was used for this frame object in the last analysis.
     Thus the design forces are based on a frame object with this section
     property.
   - Design Section: The current
     design section property. If the frame object is assigned an auto
     select list, the section displayed in this form initially defaults
     to the optimal section. If no auto select list has been assigned
     to the frame object, the object design is performed for the section
     property specified in this edit box.  
       
     It is important to note that subsequent analyses use the section
     property specified in this list box for the next analysis section
     for the frame object. Thus the forces and moments obtained in
     the next analysis are based on this section. Change the Design
     section property by clicking the Overwrites
     button and making the changes on the resulting form.

Note:
 For final design iteration, the Analysis Section and the Design
Section property should be the same. Use the [Verify Analysis vs Design Section command](CFSF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.md)
to determine if this is the case. If it is not, repeat steps 1 through
4 until the analysis and design sections match. As appropriate, use the
Overwrites button and the [Cold-Formed Steel Frame Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this))
to change the design parameters. Thus, while the Analysis Section is changed/updated
by rerunning the analysis, the Design Section is changed by selecting
a new section on the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design
Overwrites form.

Use the Cold-Formed
Steel Frame Design Overwrites form to
make revisions to the cold-formed steel frame design parameters, such
as unbraced length ratio, effective length factor, bending coefficient,
tensile strength, major and minor bending stress and major and minor
shear stress, among others. Then use the Details
buttons on the Cold-Formed Steel
Stress Check Information form to immediately see the new design
results.

If you modify some
overwrites in this mode and exit both the Cold-Formed
Steel Frame Design Overwrites form and
the Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check Information
form by clicking their respective OK buttons,
the changes made to the overwrites are permanently saved. When you
exit the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Overwrites
form by clicking the OK button the changes
are temporarily saved. If you then exit the Cold-Formed
Steel Stress Check Information form by clicking the Cancel
button, the changes made to the cold-formed steel frame overwrites
are considered temporary only and are not permanently saved. Permanent
saving of the overwrites does not actually occur until you click the
OK button in the Cold-Formed
Steel Stress Check Information form.

1. - Table Showing Stress Details:
     This table shows the stress ratios obtained for each design load
     combination at each output station along the frame object. Initially
     the worst stress ratio is highlighted. Following are the headings
     in the table.
   - - Combo
       ID: The name of the design load combination considered.
     - Station
       location: The location of the station considered measured
       from the i-end of the frame object.
     - Ratio:
       The total PMM stress ratio for the object. When stress ratios
       are reported for this item, they are followed by either (T)
       or (C). The (T) item indicates that the axial component of
       the stress ratio is tension. The (C) item indicates that the
       axial component of the stress ratio is compression. Note that
       typically the interaction formulas are different depending
       on whether the axial stress is tension or compression.
     - Axl:
       The axial component of the PMM stress ratio.
     - B-Maj: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the major axis.
     - B-Min: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the minor axis.
     - Maj
       Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio for shear acting
       in the major direction of the frame object.
     - Min
       Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio for shear acting
       in the minor direction of the frame object.
   - Overwrites button. Click the Overwrites
     button to access the [Cold-Formed Steel Frame Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

     Use the Cold-Formed Steel
     Frame Design Overwrites form to make revisions to the
     cold-formed steel frame design parameters, such as unbraced
     length ratio, effective length factor, bending coefficient,
     tensile strength, major and minor bending stress and major
     and minor shear stress, among others. Then use the Details
     buttons on the Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check Information form
     to immediately see the new design results.

     If you modify
     some overwrites in this mode and exit both the Cold-Formed
     Steel Frame Design Overwrites
     form and the Cold-Formed Steel Stress
     Check Information form by clicking their respective
     OK buttons, the changes made to
     the overwrites are permanently saved. When you exit the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Overwrites
     form by clicking the OK button
     the changes are temporarily saved. If you then exit the Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check Information
     form by clicking the Cancel button,
     the changes made to the cold-formed steel frame overwrites
     are considered temporary only and are not permanently saved.
     Permanent saving of the overwrites does not actually occur
     until you click the OK button
     in the Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check
     Information form.
   - Summary button. Click the Summary
     button to display the design details for the selected design combination
     and station location. Print this information by selecting File menu > Print command at the top
     of the form.
   - Effective button. Click the Effective
     button to display the details for the effective area, effective
     major and minor moments of inertia, and deflection design. Click
     on the display and drag it to reveal areas not visible in the
     available window. Print this information by selecting File
     menu > Print command at the top of the form.
   - Tabular Data button. Click the Tabular
     Data button to access the Cold-Formed
     Steel Details (Database) form. Use
     the various [menu
     commands](../../../Database_Tables/Database_Table_Form.md) on the form to export, display, and print the data
     table.
   - Table Format File button. Click the Table Format File button to access the Set Database Table Formats File form.
     Use that form to specify the Use
     Program Default Table Formats option or the Use
     Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option. When
     the Use Formats from User Defined
     Table Formats File option is chosen, also click the Select button to locate a previously defined
     format file. Table formats are defined using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).
     The default or selected table format will be applied to output
     (export, display or print) of the data.

# CFSF - Make Auto Select Section Null

This command replaces the [Auto
Select section assignments](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) for the selected members with the current
design section previously chosen from the auto select group. This is an
irreversible action, i.e. once the Auto Select sections are turned off
they will no longer be available for optimal design. After using this
command, Auto Select sections would need to be reassigned if they were
to once again be included in the design selection process.

1. Select the frame members
   for which the Auto Select sections are to be replaced with the current
   design section.
2. Click the Design
   menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Make Auto Select Section
   Null command.
3. SAP2000 will issue a
   warning message that the Auto-Selected Sections Assignments will be
   replaced by the current design sections for the selected members.
   Click OK if acceptable; otherwise, click
   Cancel.

Note: This option
should only be used after the final design cycle.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Reset_All_Cold_Formed_Steel_Overwrites.htm | CFSF Reset All Cold Formed Steel Overwrites -->

# CFSF - Reset All Cold-Formed Steel Overwrites

The Design menu > Cold-Formed
Steel Frame Design > Reset All Cold-Formed Steel Overwrites
command resets the [overwrites](CFSF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md)
for all frame sections with the Cold-Formed Steel Frame design procedure
to their default values. It is not necessary to make a selection before
using the Reset All Cold-Formed Steel Overwrites
command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with
the Cold-Formed Steel Frame design procedure. . The command can be used
to reverse changes made using the [View/Review Overwrites command](CFSF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md).

Resetting your overwrites will reduce the size of
your SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file. zxvc

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Reset_Design_Section_to_Last_Analysis.htm | CFSF Reset Design Section to Last Analysis -->

# CFSF - Reset Design Section to Last Analysis

In some instances design sections may change several times (before the analysis is rerun) and then the design section for one or more frame objects may need to be restored to match the last used analysis section (i.e., the design section and the analysis section must match or the model may not have been designed for the correct forces).

While rerunning the analysis updates the analysis section to match the design section, the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command is a quick and easy way to reset the design section to match the last analysis section. The anticipated process would be as follows:

1. Run the analysis and use the [Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure.](CFSF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md)
2. Use the [Interactive Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design](CFSF_Interactive_Cold_Formed_Steel_Frame_Design.md) or [Change Design Section](CFSF_Change_Design_Section.md)  command to change the design sections.
3. Use the Start Design/Check of Structure command to update the design. For this example process, after review, portions of the updated design have been determined to be unnecessary or unacceptable.
4. Select the objects whose design sections are to be reset. If no objects have been selected, this command will not be available.
5. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command to immediately reset the design section to match the last analysis section.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Select_Design_Combos.htm | CFSF Select Design Combos -->

# CFSF - Select Design Combinations

Form:  Design Load Combinations Selection

Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Select Design Combo command to open the Design Load Combinations Selection form.  It is not necessary to run the analysis or select an object before using the command; however, the program will not generate the code-generated automatic load combinations until at least one analysis and design iteration has been run, and therefore, the automatic load combinations will not be shown until design has been run. Use the form to review and modify the design load combinations used during design.

- Load Combination Type selection box. Select the type of design combination to review or specify (i.e., Strength, Deflection).
- Select Load Combinations area. All of the available design load combinations are listed in the List of Load Combinations list box. The design load combinations actually used in the design are listed in the Design Load Combinations list box. All three of the following buttons act on the highlighted design load combination in those two list boxes.

1. - Use the Add and Remove buttons to move load combinations into and out of the Design Combos list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections in this form for use with the Add and Remove buttons.
   - Use the Show button to review the definition of a design load combination.

Note:   If a user-defined combination(s) is to be used in design, it must be selected as described herein, regardless of whether the combo was created manually ([Define menu options](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)) or if the combination(s) is based on code (Define menu, [Add Default Design Combos button](../../Define/Load_Combination/Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md))  The program automatically selects those combos that are created when the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box is checked (see next bullet). Note also that these automatically generated combos are regenerated (i.e., replaced) after each design run.

- Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box. When this check box is checked, the design load combinations generated based on the selected code (i.e., the code selected using the [Design menu > Cold-Form Steel Frame > View/Revise Preferences command](CFSF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)) are added to the List of Load Combinations.
- - Set Automatic Design Load Combination Data button. With the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box checked, click this button to access the [Code Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Code} form](../Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.md). Use that form to make changes to the automatically generated code-based design load combinations to be applied during model design.

The default cold-formed steel frame design load combinations have names such as DCLD1, DCLD2 and so forth.

## See Also

[Load Combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Select_Design_Groups.htm | CFSF Select Design Groups -->

# CFSF - Select Design Groups

Form: Cold-Formed Steel Design Group Selection

In SAP2000, objects can be grouped for cold-formed steel frame design. When a group is specified for design, all objects in the group are given the same section.

1. Define the groups by selecting the frame objects and clicking the Assign menu > Group Names command. Designing with groups only works if you have assigned [auto select sections](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) to the frame objects. Typically, assign the same auto select section to each frame object to be used in a design group, although this is not absolutely necessary. Any frame object in a design group not assigned an auto select section will be ignored for group design and will be designed individually.
2. After the group has been defined, use the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Select Design Group command to access the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Group Selection form. All of the available groups are listed in the List of Groups list box. The groups actually in use are listed in the Design Groups list box.
3. Use the Add and Remove buttons to move groups into and out of the Design Groups list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections before using the Add and Remove buttons.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Set_Displacement_Targets.htm | CFSF Set Displacement Targets -->

# CFSF - Set Displacement Targets

Form: Lateral Displacement Targets

For displacement optimization, SAP2000 predicts which members should be increased in size to control the displacements based on the energy per unit volume in the members. The members with more energy per unit volume are increased in size a larger percentage than those with smaller energies per unit volume. Some members with small energy per unit volume may be decreased in size if they are still acceptable for strength considerations.

Note: [Auto select lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to the frame objects for the displacement optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the desired displacement target may never be reached no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Specify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form, which can be used to specify displacement targets for various load cases. The intent is that a point is picked, typically at the roof level of the model, and a maximum displacement target (in any direction) is specified for one or more load cases on that point.
2. In the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form, select the load case from the drop-down list for which the displacement is to be optimized.
3. Specify the location for the displacement by specifying a Point.
4. Specify the target displacement.
5. Click the Add button.
6. Repeat Steps 1 through 5 as needed.
7. Run the design (Design menu > Cold Formed Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure) and then rerun the analysis (Analyze menu > Run Analysis) with the new section sizes to view the displacements by right clicking on selected points. Displacement optimization is an iterative process that typically requires rerunning the analysis and design multiple times. There is no guarantee that the displacement target will be reached using this option.

Tip:  To rerun the analysis, it will be necessary to delete the design results (i.e., unlock the model, or use the Delete Results button on the Set Analysis Cases to Run form). This will not adversely affect the specification of displacement targets.

Modify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be modified in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form. Note that the data for the specification appears in the boxes at the top of the Loads area. Modify the data in the boxes as desired.
3. Click the Modify button.
4. Rerun your analysis with the new section sizes to review the displacements.

Delete a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be deleted in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
3. Click the Delete button.

Deactivate Targets check box. Check the Deactivate Targets check box to exclude the displacements from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include displacements in design.

## See Also

[Set Time Period Targets](CFSF_Set_Time_Period_Targets.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Set_Time_Period_Targets.htm | CFSF Set Time Period Targets -->

# CFSF - Set Time Period Targets

Form: Time Period Targets

For time period targets, specify a mode and a target period for that mode. Then, during design, SAP2000 automatically optimizes the structure to meet the target period using energy considerations. During the optimization process, members with large energy per unit volume are changed more than those with small energy per unit volume.

Note: [Auto select section lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to frame objects for the time period optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select section list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the displacement target may never be met, no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Use the Design menu > Cold Formed Steel Frame Design > Set Time Period Targets command to display the Time Period Targets form.

- Modal Load Case. Select the modal load case for which time period targets are being set.
- Add a Target.
- 1. Enter a number in the Mode Number edit box.
  2. SAP2000 will suggest a value in the Target Period edit box. Use this target period or type a revised value in the edit box.
  3. Click the Add button.
- Modify a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be modified in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Type revised value in the Target Period edit box.
  3. Click the Modify button.
- Delete a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be deleted in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Click the Delete button.

- Deactivate Time Period Targets check box. Check the Deactivate Time Period Targets check box to exclude the time periods from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include time periods in design.

## See Also

[Set Displacement Targets](CFSF_Set_Displacement_Targets.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.htm | CFSF Start Design-Check of Structure -->

# CFSF - Start Design/Check of Structure

The Design menu > Cold-Formed
Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command
starts the cold-formed steel frame design process.

Run a cold-formed steel
frame design as follows:

1. 1. Click the [Analyze
      menu > Run Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of
      the model.
   2. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design
      > Start Design/Check of Structure command.

Note:  
  
This command is unavailable if no frame objects with the Cold-Formed Steel
Frame design procedure have been included in the model.  
  
If frame objects were selected when this command is clicked, only the selected
frame objects are designed. If no frame objects are selected when this
command is used, all frame objects with the Cold-Formed Steel Frame design
procedure are designed.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Verify_All_Members_Passed.htm | CFSF Verify All Members Passed -->

# CFSF - Verify All Members Passed

When the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command is used, the program reports if structural members passed the stress/capacity check.

Use the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command as follows:

1. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis.
2. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to run the design.
3. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command.

SAP2000 will display a pop-up box indicating the outcome of the verification. If members do not pass the check, the [Change Design Section command](CFSF_Change_Design_Section.md) can be used to change the design section.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.htm | CFSF Verify Analysis vs Design Section -->

# CFSF - Verify Analysis vs Design Section

When the iterative design process is complete, the
last used analysis section property for a frame object and the current
design section property for that frame object should be the same. If this
is not the case, the frame object may not have been designed for the correct
forces. The Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame
Design > Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is useful
for verifying that the last used analysis section and the current design
section are the same for all steel frame objects in the model.

When the Verify Analysis vs
Design Section command is used, SAP2000 identifies how many frame
objects with the Cold-Formed Steel Frame design procedure have different
analysis and design sections and then selects those frame objects, if
asked to do so. Typically this command would be used after the final design
iteration to verify that the analysis and design properties used are consistent.

It is not necessary to select any frame objects before
using the Verify Analysis vs Design Section
command. This command automatically checks all frame sections with the
Cold-Formed Steel Frame design procedure.

Note: Update the
Analysis Section by rerunning the analysis, perhaps several times in a
complex model. Update the Design Section using the [Interactive Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design
command](CFSF_Interactive_Cold_Formed_Steel_Frame_Design.md) and the Overwrites button or use
the [Change
Design Section command](CFSF_Change_Design_Section.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm | CFSF View Revise Overwrites -->

# CFSF - View/Revise Overwrites

Form:  Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Overwrites for {Code}

Cold-formed steel  frame design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the frame/cable objects to which they are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all cold-formed steel frame overwrite items. Thus, it is not required that overwrites be specified. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items and if necessary change them to make sure they are acceptable.

Some of the default overwrite values are based on cold-formed steel frame preferences. Thus define the preference before defining the overwrites (and before designing or checking any cold-formed steel frame members).

When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the objects to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the objects that are selected when the overwrites are changed.

Change an overwrite as follows:

Be sure to check, and as necessary change, the [Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Preferences](CFSF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)  before completing the following steps.

1. Select the frame object(s) for which overwrites are to be specified.
2. Click the Design menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Overwrites command, which brings up the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Overwrites form. The cold-formed steel frame overwrites are displayed with an Item column and a Value column. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the overwrite item.

Note:  The Overwrites button on the Cold-Formed Steel Stress Check Information form can also be used to display the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Overwrites form.

3. Left click in the Value column to activate a drop-down box or to highlight the contents of the cell.

- If the drop-down box appears, select a value from the box. The values in the drop-down boxes can not be changed.
- If the cell contents becomes highlighted, type in the desired value.

- Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.
- - Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default.
  - Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.
- Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.
- - Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values.
  - Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_View_Revise_Preferences.htm | CFSF View Revise Preferences -->

# CFSF View/Revise Preferences

Form:  Cold-Formed
Steel Frame Design Preferences for {Code}

Preferences are basic settings that control design
parameters. Use the Cold-Formed Steel
Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form to access those design
parameters, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect
the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters
is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to
ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using
this form.

1. Click the Design
   menu > Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences
   command to display the Cold-Formed Steel Frame Design Preferences for {Code}
   form.

   - Item/Value. Click in any of
     the drop-down lists or edit boxes in the Value
     column to change the default values to your specific choices.
   - Item Description. The Item Description area displays
     a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description
     is provided to help you recall the purpose of the preference item.
   - Explanation of Color Coding for Values
     area. The items in this area are color-coded blue, black or red.
     The meaning of each color code is defined in the this area of
     the form.
   - Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected
     Items buttons. Click the All Items
     button at any time to reset all items to the program default.
     Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value
     column to select the item and then click the Selected
     Item button to restore that item to the program default.
   - Reset
     to Previous Values and All Items
     and Selected Items buttons. Click
     the All Items button at any time to
     reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the
     edit box or drop-down list in the Value
     column to select the item and then click the Selected
     Item button to restore that item to the previously specified
     value.

2. Click
   on the OK button when finished making
   the necessary selections.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Conc_Shell_Design/CSD_-_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm | CSD - View/Revise Overwrites -->

# Concrete Shell Design - View/Revise Overwrites>

Form:  Concrete Shell Design Overwrites for {Code}

Concrete shell design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the area objects to which they  are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all concrete shell overwrite items. Thus, it is not required that you specify or change any of the overwrites. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items to make sure they are acceptable.

Some of the default overwrite values are based on concrete shell preferences. Thus [define the preferences](CSD_View_Revise_Preferences.md) before defining the overwrites (and before designing or checking any concrete shell elements).

When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the objects to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the objects that are selected when the overwrites are changed.

Change an overwrite as follows:

Be sure to check, and as necessary, change the [Concrete shell Design Preferences](CSD_View_Revise_Preferences.md)  before completing the following steps.

1. Select the area object(s) for which overwrites are to be specified.
2. Click the Design menu > Concrete shell Design > View/Revise Overwrites command, which brings up the Concrete shell Design Overwrites form. The concrete shell overwrites are displayed with an Item column and a Value column. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the overwrite item.
3. Left click in the Value column to activate a drop-down box or to highlight the contents of the cell.

- If the drop-down box appears, select a value from the box. The values in the drop-down boxes cannot be changed.
- If the cell contents becomes highlighted, type in the desired value.

4. Click the OK button to close the form. The program then changes all of the overwrite items whose associated check boxes are checked for the selected shell / area object(s).

- Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.
- - Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default.
  - Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.
- Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.
- - Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values.
  - Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.

# Define Design Requests

Form:  Concrete Shell Design Requests – {Code}

The Design menu > Concrete Shell Design > Define Design Requests command specifies the design to be performed. The name of the request, group(s) of area objects, and load combination(s) must be added in the Concrete Shell Design Request Data form to define a design request properly.

- **Name:** Type a name for the design request in this cell
- **Choose Groups:** Select group(s) in the List of Groups and click Add -> to include the group(s) of area objects to be designed in the design request
- **Load Combinations for Design:** Select load combination(s) in the List of Load Combinations and click Add -> to include the load combination(s) for which the selected group(s) of area objects to be designed in the design request.
- **Automatic Design Load Combinations:** Click Create Automatic Design Load Combination Data to access the Code-Generated Automatic Load Combinations for Concrete Shell Design – {Code} form, which is used to make changes to the automatically generated code-based design load combinations to be applied during model design. The default concrete shell design load combinations have names such as *{Request Name}\_DCONS1, {Request Name}\_DCONS2 and so forth.*
- Use the Reset Defaults button to restore all values or suggested text to the program defaults.

# Concrete Shell Design - Delete Design Results

The Design menu > Concrete Shell Design > Delete Concrete Shell Design Results command deletes all of the concrete shell design results. It is not necessary to make a selection before using the Delete Concrete Shell Design Results command. This command automatically applies to all area objects with the Concrete Shell design procedure.

SAP2000 will request confirmation to delete all concrete shell design results. Click the OK button to delete the results, or the Cancel button to close the form without deleting the results.

Deleting your concrete shell design results will reduce the size of your SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file.

# Concrete Shell Design - Reset Overwrites

The Design menu > Concrete Shell Design > Reset All Concrete Overwrites command resets the overwrites for all shell sections with the Concrete Shell design procedure to their default values. It is not necessary to make a selection before using the Reset All Concrete Overwrites command. This command automatically applies to all shell sections with the Concrete Shell design procedure.

1. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Reset All Concrete Overwrites command. SAP2000 will request confirmation to reset overwrites and warns that current design results will be deleted.
2. Click the OK button to reset overwrites or the Cancel button to close the form without resetting overwrites.

Resetting your overwrites will reduce the size of your SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file.

# Concrete Shell Design - View/Revise Preferences
