Preferences are basic settings that control design parameters. Use the Concrete Shell Design Preferences for {Code} form to access those design parameters, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using this form.

Preferences are basic settings that control design parameters. Use the Concrete Shell Design Preferences for {Code} form to access those design parameters, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using this form.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Change_Design_Section.htm | CF Change Design Section -->

# CF - Change Design Section

Form:  Select Sections

Because design is an iterative process, after a concrete frame design has been run, the design section property assigned to one or more frame object may need to be changed. SAP2000 allows multiple design iteration to be run without rerunning the analysis, which can save computing time.

Change a design section and redesign the structure without rerunning the analysis as follows:

1. Select the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to analyze the model.
2. Select the [Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design / Check of Structure](CF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md) command to complete the initial design. As necessary, use the [Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Interactive Concrete Frame Design](CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.md) command to evaluate the results.
3. Select the frame object(s) for which the section is to be changed.
4. Select the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Change Design Section command to access the Select Sections form. Choose the new section from the display list.

TIP:  If nothing is shown in the list, additional concrete frame section definitions should be added to the model using the [Define menu > Frame Sections command](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md).

5. Repeat Steps 2 through 4 as necessary.

The Change Design Section command only changes the design section for the selected frame object(s). The forces used in the design are not based on this new section size but are instead based on whatever section was used in the last analysis.

Recall, however, that the design section property is used for the next analysis section property. Thus, changing the design section property also changes the next analysis section property.

# CF - Display Design Info

Form:  Display Design Results

Review some of the results of the concrete frame design directly on the SAP2000 model (i.e., on screen) using the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Display Design Info command. This command displays Design Input and Output parameters.

Display design information on screen as follows:

1. Run an analysis.
2. Perform at least one design using the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command.
3. Select the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Display Design Info command to access the Display Design Results form.

Select the Input or Output option and choose from the drop-down list the type of information to be displayed on screen.

- Right click on a frame object to display the [Concrete Column Design Information form](CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.md) or [Concrete Beam Design Information form](CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.md), which also can be displayed using the Interactive Concrete Frame Design command.
- Use the Assign menu > Clear Display of Assigns command to remove the on-screen display of design information.

TIP:  When selecting to display design ratios a check box is available giving you the option to specify the minimum ratio for which results will be displayed.  For example, you can specify the only ratios above 0.90 are to be displayed.  In addition, another check box is available giving you the option to select the frame objects for which results are displayed.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem H](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_H.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.htm | CF Interactive Concrete Frame Design -->

# CF - Interactive Concrete Frame Design

Form: Concrete
Column Design Information {Code} or Concrete Beam Design Information {Code},
Interaction Surface for Section {Name}{Code}

Interactive concrete frame design allows you to review
the design results for any frame object and to interactively change the
design overwrites and immediately view the results.

After completing the [Modeling
Process](../../../Getting_Started/Modeling_Process.md) using [concrete
frames](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md), access Interactive Concrete Frame Design as follows:

1. Select the Analyze
   menu > Run Analysis command to analyze the model.
2. Select the Design
   menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design / Check of Structure
   command.
3. Right click on a frame
   object while the design results are displayed on it to enter the interactive
   design mode and interactively design the object using the Concrete
   Column Design Information {Code} or Concrete
   Beam Design Information {Code} form, depending on whether the
   frame object is a column or a beam. If design results are not currently
   displayed, click the Design menu > Concrete
   Frame Design > Interactive Concrete Frame Design command
   and then right click a frame object to enter the interactive design
   mode for that object.

Note:
The Concrete Column Design Information {Code}
or Concrete Beam Design Information {Code}
form also can be displayed as follows:  (a) click the Design
menu > Concrete Frame Design > Display Design Info command
to access the Display Design Results form,
(b) select the input/output option and the type of information to be displayed,
and (c)  right click on a frame object.

4. Use the various areas
   of the Concrete Column Design Information {Code}
   or Concrete Beam Design Information {Code}
   form to review the design:

   - Frame
     ID: The label associated with
     a frame object that has been assigned a concrete frame section
     property that is designated as a beam
     or a column.

Important
Note: A
concrete frame object is designed as either a beam or a column depending
on how its frame section property was designated when it was defined using
the [Define menu > Frame Sections command](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Add_Frame_Section_Property_Form.md).
Note that when using that command, after a section has been specified
to have a concrete material property, click the Reinforcement
button
and specify whether the section is a beam or a column.

1. - Design
     Code: The design code selected using the  [Concrete
     Frame Design Preferences form](CF_View_Revise_Preferences.md).
   - Analysis
     Section: The section property that was used for this frame
     object in the last analysis. Thus the design forces are based
     on a frame object with this section property.
   - Design
     Section: The current design section property. It is important
     to note that subsequent analyses use the section property specified
     in this list box for the next analysis section for the frame object.
     Thus the forces and moments obtained in the next analysis are
     based on this section. Change the Design section property by clicking
     the [Overwrites
     button](CF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md) and making the changes on the resulting form.

Note:
 For final design iteration, the Analysis Section and the Design
Section property should be the same. Use the [Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Verify
Analysis vs Design Section command](CF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.md) to determine if this is
the case. If it is not, repeat steps 1 through 4 until the analysis and
design sections match. As appropriate, use the Overwrites
button to display the [Concrete Frame Design Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this))
and change the design parameters. Thus, the Analysis Section is changed/updated
by rerunning the analysis. The Design Section is changed by selecting
a new section on the Concrete Frame Design Overwrites
form.

When changes are made to overwrite items, the
program applies the changes to the elements that are selected when
the overwrites are changed. Thus, the overwrites apply to the frame
elements selected before you selected the Design
menu > Concrete Frame Design > Interactive Concrete Frame Design
command and clicked the Overwrites button.
Use the form to make revisions to the concrete frame overwrites and
then immediately see the new design results.

For more information about overwrites, use the
Help menu > Documentation and Tutorials
command and locate the appropriate Concrete Frame Design code.

1. - Table
     Showing Reinforcement Information This table shows the
     output information obtained for each design load combination at
     each output station along the frame object. For columns that are
     designed by SAP2000, the item with the largest required amount
     of longitudinal reinforcing is initially highlighted. For columns
     that are checked by SAP2000, the item with the largest capacity
     ratio is initially highlighted. For beams, the item with the largest
     required amount of longitudinal steel (either top or bottom) is
     initially highlighted.
   - - Combo
       ID: The design load combination considered.
     - Station
       location: The location of the station, measured from
       the i-end of the frame object.
     - Columns
       only:
     - - Longitudinal
         reinforcement: Applies specifically to columns
         for which SAP2000 designs the longitudinal reinforcing.
         It is the total required area of longitudinal reinforcing
         steel.
       - Capacity
         ratio: Applies specifically to columns for which
         you have specified the location and
         size of reinforcing bars and thus SAP2000 checks the design.
         The capacity ratio is determined by first extending a
         line from the origin of the PMM interaction surface to
         the point representing the P, M2 and M3 values for the
         designated load combination. Call the length of this first
         line L1. Next a second line is extended from the origin
         of the PMM interaction surface through
         the point representing the P, M2 and M3 values for the
         designated load combination until it intersects the interaction
         surface. Call the length of this line from the origin
         to the interaction surface L2. The capacity ratio is equal
         to L1/L2.
       - Major
         shear reinforcement: The total required area of
         shear reinforcing per unit length for shear acting in
         the column major direction.
       - Minor
         shear reinforcement: The total required area of
         shear reinforcing per unit length for shear acting in
         the column minor direction.
     - Beams
       only:
     - - Top
         steel: The total required area of longitudinal
         top steel at the specified station.
       - Bottom
         steel: The total required area of longitudinal
         bottom steel at the specified station.
       - Shear
         steel: The total required area of shear reinforcing
         per unit length at the specified station for loads acting
         in the local 2-axis direction of the beam.

1. - Overwrites button.
     Click the Overwrites button to access
     the [Concrete Frame Design Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

     When changes are made to overwrite items,
     the program applies the changes to the elements that are selected
     when the overwrites are changed. Thus, the overwrites apply
     to the frame elements selected before you selected the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design >
     Interactive Concrete Frame Design command and clicked
     the Overwrites button. Use the
     form to make revisions to the concrete frame overwrites and
     then immediately see the new design results.

     For more information about overwrites,
     use the Help menu > Documentation
     and Tutorials command and locate the appropriate Concrete
     Frame Design code.

1. - Summary
     button. Click the Summary button to
     display a summary of the design data for the highlighted section.
     Print the information using File menu >
     Print command at the top of the form.

1. - Flex.
     Details button. Click the Flex. Details
     button to display the axial force and biaxial moment design for
     PU, M2 and M3, factored and minimum biaxial moments, axial force,
     biaxial moment factors and other details for the highlighted section.
     Print the information using File menu >
     Print command at the top of the form.

1. - Shear
     Details Button. Click the Shear Details
     button to display the shear design for V2 and V3, design forces,
     capacity shear, design basis, concrete shear capacity shear rebar
     design, and other details for the highlighted section. Print the
     information using File menu > Print
     command at the top of the form.
   - Columns
     only:

1. 1. - Interaction
        button.  Click the Interaction
        button to display the [Interaction Surface for Section {Name} {Code}
        form](CF_Interaction_Surface_for_Section_Form.md).

1. 1. - Joint
        Shear button. Click the Joint
        Shear button to display the compression, tension bending,
        shear and overstrength factors for the highlighted section.
        Print the information using File menu
        > Print command at the top of the form.

1. - - B/C
       Details button.  Click the B/C
       Details button to display the Beam/Column Capacity
       Ratio details. Print the information using File
       menu > Print command at the top of the display window.
   - Tabular Data Button
     Click the Tabular Data button to access
     the Concrete Details (Database)
     form. Use the various [menu
     commands](../../../Database_Tables/Database_Table_Form.md) on the form to export, display, and print the data
     table.
   - Table
     Format File button.
     Click the Table Format File button
     to access the Set Database Table Formats
     File form and specify the format (i.e., stylesheet) to
     be applied to the output (i.e., export, display or print). Use
     the form to specify the Use
     Program Default Table Formats option or the Use
     Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option. When
     the Use Formats from User Defined
     Table Formats File option is chosen, also click the Select button to locate a previously defined
     format file. Table formats are defined using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).
     The default or selected table format will be applied to output
     (i.e., export, display or print) of the data.

# CF - Reset All Concrete Overwrites

The Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Reset All Concrete Overwrites command resets the overwrites for all frame sections with the Concrete Frame design procedure to their default values. It is not necessary to make a selection before using the Reset All Concrete Overwrites command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with the Concrete Frame design procedure.

1. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Reset All Concrete Overwrites command. SAP2000 will request confirmation to reset overwrites and warns that current design results will be deleted.
2. Click the OK button to reset overwrites or the Cancel button to close the form without resetting overwrites.

Resetting your overwrites will reduce the size of your SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Reset_Design_Section_to_Last_Analysis.htm | CF Reset Design Section to Last Analysis -->

# CF - Reset Design Section to Last Analysis

In some instances design sections may change several times (before the analysis is rerun) and then the design section for one or more frame objects may need to be restored to match the last used analysis section (i.e., the design section and the analysis section must match or the model may not have been designed for the correct forces).

While rerunning the analysis updates the analysis section to match the design section, the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command is a quick and easy way to reset the design section to match the last analysis section. The anticipated process would be as follows:

1. Run the analysis and use the [Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure](CF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md).
2. Use the [Interactive Concrete Frame Design](CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.md) or [Change Design Section](CF_Change_Design_Section.md) command to change the design sections.
3. Use the Start Design/Check of Structure command to update the design. For this example process, after review, portions of the updated design have been determined to be unnecessary or unacceptable.
4. Select the objects whose design sections are to be reset.
5. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command to immediately reset the design section to match the last analysis section.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Select_Design_Combos.htm | CF Select Design Combos -->

# CF - Select Design Combinations

Form:  Design Load Combinations Selection

Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Select Design Combo command to open the Design Load Combinations Selection form.  It is not necessary to run the analysis or select an object before using the command; however, the program will not generate the code-generated automatic load combinations until at least one analysis and design iteration has been run, and therefore, the automatic load combinations will not be shown until design has been run. Use the form to review and modify the design load combinations used during design.

- Load Combination Type selection box. Select the type of design combination to review or specify (i.e., Strength, Deflection).
- Select Load Combinations area. All of the available design load combinations are listed in the List of Load Combinations list box. The design load combinations actually used in the design are listed in the Design Load Combinations list box. All three of the following buttons act on the highlighted design load combination in those two list boxes.

1. - Use the Add and Remove buttons to move load combinations into and out of the Design Combos list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections in this form for use with the Add and Remove buttons.
   - Use the Show button to review the definition of a design load combination.

Note:   If a user-defined combination(s) is to be used in design, it must be selected as described herein, regardless of whether the combo was created manually ([Define menu options](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)) or if the combination(s) is based on code (Define menu, [Add Default Design Combos button](../../Define/Load_Combination/Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md))  The program automatically selects those combos that are created when the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box is checked (see next bullet). Note also that these automatically generated combos are regenerated (i.e., replaced) after each design run.

- Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box. When this check box is checked, the design load combinations generated based on the selected code (i.e., the code selected using the [Design menu > Concrete Frame > View/Revise Preferences command](../Cold-Formed_Steel_Frame_Design/CFSF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)) are added to the List of Load Combinations.
- - Set Automatic Design Load Combination Data button. With the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box checked, click this button to access the [Code Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Code} form](../Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.md). Use that form to make changes to the automatically generated code-based design load combinations to be applied during model design.

The default concrete frame design load combinations have names such as DCON1, DCON2 and so forth.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem H](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_H.md).

See Also

[Load Combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.htm | CF Start Design-Check of Structure -->

# CF - Start Design/Check of Structure

The Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command starts the concrete frame design process.

Run a concrete frame design as follows:

1. 1. Click the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of the model.
   2. Click Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to begin the design process.

Note:  
  
This command is unavailable if no line objects with the Concrete Frame design procedure have been included in the model.  
  
If you have selected line objects when you click this command, only the selected line objects are designed. If no line objects are selected when you click this command, all concrete line objects with the Concrete Frame design procedure are designed.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem H](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_H.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Verify_All_Members_Passed.htm | CF Verify All Members Passed -->

# CF - Verify All Members Passed

When the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command is used, the program reports if structural members passed the stress/capacity check.

Use the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command as follows:

1. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis.
2. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to run the design.
3. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command.

SAP2000 will display a pop-up box indicating the outcome of the verification. If structural members failed, the program will select those members if instructed to do so.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.htm | CF Verify Analysis vs Design Section -->

# CF - Verify Analysis vs Design Section

When the iterative design process is complete, the last used analysis section property for a frame object and the current design section property for that frame object should be the same. If this is not the case, the frame object may not have been designed for the correct forces. The Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is useful for verifying that the last used analysis section and the current design section are the same for all concrete frame objects in the model. It is not necessary to select any objects before using the Verify Analysis vs Design Section command. This command automatically checks all frame sections with the Concrete Frame design procedure.

When the Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is used, SAP2000 displays how many frame objects with the Concrete Frame design procedure have different analysis and design sections and then selects those frame objects, if instructed to do so. Typically this command is used after the last design iteration has been run to verify that the analysis and design properties used are consistent.

Note: Update the Analysis Section by rerunning the analysis, perhaps several times in a complex model. Update the Design Section using the [Interactive Concrete Frame Design command](CF_Interactive_Concrete_Frame_Design.md) and the Overwrites button or use the [Change Design Section command](CF_Change_Design_Section.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm | CF View Revise Overwrites -->

# CF - View/Revise Overwrites

Form:  Concrete Frame Design Overwrites for {Code}

Concrete frame design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the frame objects to which they  are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all concrete  frame overwrite items. Thus, it is not required that you specify or change any of the overwrites. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items to make sure they are acceptable.

Some of the default overwrite values are based on concrete frame preferences. Thus [define the preferences](CF_View_Revise_Preferences.md) before defining the overwrites (and before designing or checking any concrete frame members).

When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the objects to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the objects that are selected when the overwrites are changed.

Change an overwrite as follows:

Be sure to check, and as necessary, change the [Concrete Frame Design Preferences](CF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)  before completing the following steps.

1. Select the frame object(s) for which overwrites are to be specified.
2. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > View/Revise Overwrites command, which brings up the Concrete Frame Design Overwrites form. The concrete frame overwrites are displayed with an Item column and a Value column. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the overwrite item.

Note:  The Overwrites button on the Concrete Column Design Information {Code} or Concrete Beam Design Information {Code} form can also be used to display the Concrete Frame Design Overwrites form.

3. Left click in the Value column to activate a drop-down box or to highlight the contents of the cell.

- If the drop-down box appears, select a value from the box. The values in the drop-down boxes cannot be changed.
- If the cell contents becomes highlighted, type in the desired value.

4. Click the OK button to close the form. The program then changes all of the overwrite items whose associated check boxes are checked for the selected frame/cable object(s).

- Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.

- Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default.
- Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.

- Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons.

- Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values.
- Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_View_Revise_Preferences.htm | CF View Revise Preferences -->

# CF View/Revise Preferences

Form:  Concrete Frame Design Preferences for {Code}

Preferences are basic settings that control design parameters. Use the Concrete Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form to access those design parameters, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using this form.

1. Click the Design menu > Concrete Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences command to display the Concrete Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form.

1. - Item/Value. Click in any of the drop-down lists or edit boxes in the Value column to change the default values to your specific choices.
   - Item Description. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the preference item.
   - Explanation of Color Coding for Values area. The items in this area are color-coded blue, black or red. The meaning of each color code is defined in the this area of the form.
   - Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.
   - Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.

2. Click the OK button when finished making the necessary selections.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Lateral_Bracing.htm | Lateral Bracing -->

# Lateral Bracing

Forms:  Lateral Bracing, Point Braces, Uniform Braces

Use the Design menu > Lateral Bracing command to specify design of lateral bracing for the selected frame object(s).

1. Select the frame object(s) for which lateral bracing is to be designed.
2. Click the  Design menu > Lateral Bracing command to access the Lateral Bracing form.

   - Program Determined option. When this option is selected, the program will determine the lateral bracing.
   - User Specified option. When this option is selected, the point and uniform braces buttons are enabled. Both point and uniform braces can be specified.
   - - Specify Point Bracing button.  Clicking this button displays the Point Braces form. Use that form to specify the Location of a point brace by specifying the distance of the point brace from the start of the frame object. Note that the distance can be specified as a Relative Distance from End-I or an Absolute Distance from End-I by choosing the appropriate option in the lower portion of the form. Use the Type drop-down list to specify that the point brace(s) be added to the Top, Bottom, or All sides of the frame object.
     - - Add button. After specifying the location and type, click this button to add a point brace to be designed.
       - Modify button. Highlight an existing point brace definition and use the Location edit box or Type drop-down list to change the location or type and click the Modify button to make the change.
       - Delete button. Highlight an existing point brace definition and click this button to delete the definition.
     - Specify Uniform Bracing button. Clicking this button displays the Uniform Braces form. Use that form to specify the Start and End of the uniform bracing by specifying the distances of the starting and ending points for the bracing as measured from the start of the frame object. Note that the distances can be specified as a Relative Distance from End-I or an Absolute Distance from End-I by choosing the appropriate option in the lower portion of the form. Use the Type drop-down list to specify that the uniform bracing be added to the Top, Bottom, or All sides of the frame object.
     - - Add button. After specifying the start, end, and type, click this button to add the uniform bracing to be designed.
       - Modify button. Highlight an existing uniform bracing definition and use the Start and End edit boxes or Type drop-down list to change the locations or type and click the Modify button to make the change.
       - Delete button. Highlight an existing uniform bracing definition and click this button to delete the definition.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Overwrite_Frame_Design_Procedure.htm | Overwrite Frame Design Procedure -->

# Overwrite Frame Design Procedure

Form:  Overwrite Frame Design Procedure

The Design menu > Overwrite Frame Design Procedure command can be used to specify that a line object should not be designed. Line objects without a designated design procedure display None for the Design Procedure on the [Line Information form](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Information_Forms/Line_Information_Form.md).

1. Select the line object that is to have its design procedure overwritten.
2. Click the Design menu > Overwrite Frame Design Procedure command to display the Overwrite Frame Design Procedure form.
3. Choose a design option. When the Default from Material option is used, SAP2000 uses the design option specified for the [material property](../Define/Material/Define_Materials.md) assigned to the [frame section](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md), [cable section](../Assign/Cable/Cable_Properties.md) or [tendon section](../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) that has been assigned to the selected line object.

[Concrete Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences](Concrete_Frame_Design/CF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)

[Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences](Steel_Frame_Design/SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/API_Fatigue_Design_Check/SF_API_Punching_Load_Joint_Assigns.htm | SF API Punching Load Joint Assigns -->

# SF API Punching Load Joint Assigns

Form:  API Punching Load Assignments

Use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > API Punching Load Assigns command to access the Punching Load Assignments form and display all of the punching load assignments made to the selected joint.

Note:  The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > API Punching Load Assigns command is available only when the [steel design code](../SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md) is set to API RP2A-WSD2000 or API RP2A-LFRD97.

1. Select the joint(s) for which punching load assignments are to be displayed.
2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > API Punching Load Assigns command to access the Punching Load Assignments form.

   - If multiple joints were selected before the command was used, the Punching Load Assignments form will display only the Do NOT check this joint check box. When this check box is checked, all of the selected joints will be flagged to be skipped when the punching load check is performed.
   - If one joint was selected before the command was used, the form has the following areas:
   - - Joint Name display box. Identifies the name of the selected joint.
     - Do NOT check this joint check box. When this check box is checked, the selected joint will be flagged to be skipped when the punching load check is performed.
     - Current Punching Load Check Status for this Joint area. This area of the form indicates if the program will check the joint. Typically, if the program will not check the joint, the reason for not checking it is displayed in this area.
     - Joint Check Parameters spreadsheet. This spreadsheet summarizes the punching load assignments for the selected joint. The steel design code (API RP2A-WSD2000 or API RP2A-LRFD 97) selected in the steel design preferences determines the availability of some parameters (for example, phi factors and Vwa).  When you click on an item in the Joint Check Parameters spreadsheet, a description of that item displays in the Item Description area. The first column in the Joint Check Parameters spreadsheet lists the punching load assignment items. The other columns list the assignments for each of the line objects (frame members) that are connected to the joint. All of the data for a single line object is contained in a single column in the table. The line object name is given in the second row of the table.

1. 1. - Set to Default or Previous Values. Depending on the option selected, the values displayed in the Joint Check Parameters spreadsheet will be restored to default values or to the values specified when the form was opened.
      - - Selected Items option. Choose this option to set values for the selected item only.
        - Selected Column option. Choose this option to set all values in the selected column.
        - Selected Row option. Choose this option to set all values in the selected row.
        - All option. Choose this option to set all values in the spreadsheet
        - Set to Default Values button. Click this button to reset the specified value(s) to defaults.
        - Set to Previous Values button. Click the button to reset the specified value(s) to the values specified when the form was opened.

- Explanation of Color Coding for Values area. The items in the Joint Check Parameters area are color-coded blue, black or red. The meaning of each color code is defined in the this area of the form.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/API_Fatigue_Design_Check/SF_Interactive_API_Punching_Load_Check.htm | SF Interactive API Punching Load Check -->

# SF Interactive API Punching Load Check

Form:  Interactive API Punching Load Check

Use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive API Punching Load Check command to access the Interactive API Punching Load Check form.

Note:  The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive API Punching Load Check command is available only when the [steel design code](../SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md) is set to API RP2A-WSD2000 or API RP2A-LFRD97 and after a [punching load check](SF_Start_API_Punching_Load_Check.md) has been run.

1. Click the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of the model.
2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to initiate the design process.
3. Click Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start API Punching Load Check command to start the punching load check process. SAP2000 will display the check output on screen.
4. With the check output results displayed on screen, right click on a joint to display the Interactive API Punching Load Check form or click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive API Punching Load Check command. The form has the following areas:

   - Joint Label display box. Displays the name of the selected joint.
   - Design Results table. A single row in the design results table presents a summary of the punching load check results obtained for a single chord, brace and design combination. Results are reported for all possible chord-brace-combination permutations. The following fields are present in the design results table.

- Chord: Name of the considered chord member.
- Brace: Name of the considered brace member.
- Combo: Name of the considered design combination.
- Equation: The code equation that gives the largest ratio for the specified chord, brace and design combination.
- Ratio: The largest ratio for the specified chord, brace and design combination.
- Warnings: This field indicates if any design warnings were produced for the specified chord, brace and design combination. It is either “None” or “Yes, n” where n is the number of design warnings produced. If warnings exist, they will appear in the Design Messages area of the form when a cell in the table row containing the chord, brace and design combination is selected.
- Errors: This field indicates if any design errors were produced for the specified chord, brace and design combination. It is either “None” or “Yes, n” where n is the number of design errors produced. If errors exist, they will appear in the Design Messages area of the form when a cell in the table row containing the chord, brace and design combination is selected.

- - Punching Load Assigns button. Clicking this button accesses the [API Punching Load Assignments form](SF_API_Punching_Load_Joint_Assigns.md). Any changes made on that form are immediately reflected in the results displayed on the Interactive API Punching Load Check form when the OK button is clicked. Then click the OK button on the Interactive API Punching Load Check form to permanently save the changes. Click the Cancel button to close the form without saving the changes.
  - Temporary Combos button. Click this button to access the [Design Load Combinations Selection form](../SF_Select_Design_Combos.md). Use the form to modify which of the currently defined design load combinations are to be considered for interactive design. Any changes made on that form are immediately reflected in the results displayed on the Interactive API Punching Load Check form when the OK button is clicked. Then click the OK button on the  Interactive API Punching Load Check form to permanently save the changed. Click the Cancel button to close the form without saving the changes.
  - Tabular Data button. Click this button to display a API Punch Details form. Use the drop-down list in the upper right corner of the form to specify the standard tabular display or a more detailed tabular display with additional fields that provide information about each chord-brace-combination permutation. Use the options on that form to format and then print, display, or export the data. See the [Database Tables form](../../../../Database_Tables/Database_Table_Form.md) for an explanation of the functions of the various commands used on the form.
  - Table Format File button. Click this button to access the Set Database Table Formats File form. Select the Use Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option and click the Select button to locate a previously defined format file. Table formats are defined using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).

# SF Start API Punching Load Check

The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start API Punching Load Check command starts the punching load check.

Run a punching load check as follows:

Note:  The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start API Punching Load Check command is available only when the [steel design code](../SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md) is set to API RP2A-WSD2000 or APR RP2A-LFRD97 and after an analysis has been run.

1. 1. Click the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of the model.
   2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to initiate the design process.
   3. Click Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start API Punching Load Check command to start the punching load check process. SAP2000 will display the check output on screen.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Change_Design_Section.htm | SF Change Design Section -->

# SF - Change Design Section

Form:  Select Sections

Because design is an iterative process, after a steel frame design has been run, it may be necessary to change the design section property assigned to one or more elements. SAP2000 allows multiple design iteration runs without rerunning the analysis, which can save computing time.

Change a design section and redesign the structure without rerunning the analysis as follows:

1. Select the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to analyze your model.
2. Select the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design / Check of Structure command to complete the initial design. As necessary, use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive Steel Frame Design command to evaluate the results.
3. Select/click on the section(s) to be changed. If no sections are selected, the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Change Design Section command will not be available.
4. Select the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Change Design Section command to access the Select Sections form. Choose the new section from the display list.
5. Repeat Steps 2 through 4 as necessary.

Note:  The Change Design Section command changes only the design section for the beam. The forces used in the design are not based on this new section size but are instead based on whatever section was used in the last analysis. Recall, however, that the design section property is used for the next analysis section property. Thus changing the design section property also changes the next analysis section property. If an [auto select section](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) is assigned to a frame/cable, control the section property used for that frame/cable in the next analysis by setting the design section property to the desired section using the Change Design Section command and then rerunning the analysis.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Delete_Steel_Design_Results.htm | SF Delete Steel Design Results -->

# SF - Delete Steel Design Results

The Design menu > Steel
Frame Design > Delete Steel Design Results command deletes all
of the steel frame design results. It is not necessary to make a selection
before using the Delete Steel Design Results
command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with
the Steel Frame design procedure.

SAP2000 will request confirmation to delete all steel
frame design results. Click the OK button
to delete the results, or the Cancel button
to close the form without deleting the results.

Deleting steel frame design results will reduce the
size of the SAP2000 database (\*.SBD) file.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Display_Design_Info.htm | SF Display Design Info -->

# SF - Display Design Info

Form:  Display Steel Design Results

Review some of the results of the steel frame design directly on the SAP2000 model (i.e., on screen) using the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Display Design Info command. This command can be used to display Design Input and Output parameters.

Display design information on screen as follows:

1. Run an analysis.
2. Perform at least one design using the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command.
3. Select the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Display Design Info command to access the Display Steel Design Results form.

Select the Design Input or Design Output option and then select from the drop-down list the type of data to be displayed on screen. Note the following with respect to an alternative method to display design results and a method to remove the results after on-screen viewing.

- Right click on a frame element to display the [Steel Stress Check Information form](SF_Interactive_Steel_Frame_Design.md). When the Steel Stress Check Information form is displayed using this method, the data is for informational purposes only and cannot be edited. Note that the data can be edited when this form is displayed using the Interactive Steel Frame Design command
- Use the Assign menu > Clear Display of Assigns command to remove the on-screen display of design data.

TIP:  When selecting to display design ratios a check box is available giving you the option to specify the minimum ratio for which results will be displayed.  For example, you can specify the only ratios above 0.90 are to be displayed.  In addition, another check box is available giving you the option to select the frame objects for which results are displayed.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Interactive_Steel_Frame_Design.htm | SF Interactive Steel Frame Design -->

# SF - Interactive Steel Frame Design

Form:  Steel
Stress Check Information

Interactive steel frame design can be used to review
the design results for any frame element and to interactively change the
design overwrites and immediately view the results.

Access
Interactive Steel Frame Design as follows:

1. Select the Analyze
   menu > [Run
   Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to analyze the model.
2. Select the Design
   menu > Steel Frame Design > [Start
   Design / Check of Structure](SF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md) command.
3. Right click on a frame
   element while the design results are displayed on it to access the
   Steel Stress Check Information form
   and enter the interactive design mode to interactively design the
   element.

If design results are
not currently displayed, click the Design menu >
Steel Frame Design > Interactive Steel Frame Design command
and then right click a frame element to enter the interactive design mode
for that element.

4. Use the various areas
   of the Steel Stress Check Information
   form to review the design:

   - Frame ID display
     box. The label associated
     with a frame element.
   - Design Code display box. The
     design code selected using the [Steel
     Frame Design Preferences](SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md) form.
   - Analysis Section display box.
     The section property that was used for this frame element in the
     last analysis. Thus the design forces are based on a frame element
     of this section property. For your final design iteration, the
     Design section property and the Analysis section property should
     be the same.
   - Design Section display box.
     The current design section property. If the frame element is assigned
     an auto select list, the section displayed in this form initially
     defaults to the optimal section. If no auto select list has been
     assigned to the frame element,  the element design is performed
     for the section property specified in this edit box.  
       
     It is important to note that subsequent analyses use the section
     property specified in this list box for the next analysis section
     for the frame element. Thus the forces and moments obtained in
     the next analysis are based on this section. Change the Design/Analysis
     section property by clicking the Overwrites
     button and making the changes on the resulting form.

Note:
 For final design iteration, the Analysis Section and the Design
Section property should be the same. Use the [Verify Analysis vs Design Section command](SF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.md)
to determine if this is the case. If it is not, repeat steps 1 through
4 until the analysis and design sections match. As appropriate, use the
Overwrites button and the [Steel Frame Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this))
to change the design parameters. Thus, the Analysis Section is changed/updated
by rerunning the analysis. The Design Section is changed by selecting
a new section on the Steel Frame Design Overwrites
form.

Use the [Steel Frame Design Overwrites form](SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md) to
make revisions to the steel frame design parameters, such as unbraced
length ratio, effective length factor, bending coefficient, tensile
strength, major and minor bending stress and major and minor shear
stress, among others. Then use the
Details buttons on the Steel
Stress Check Information form
to immediately see the new design results.

If you modify some
overwrites in this mode and exit both the Steel
Frame Design Overwrites form and the Steel
Stress Check Information form by clicking their respective
OK buttons, the changes made to the overwrites
are permanently saved. When you exit
the Steel
Frame Design Overwrites form
by clicking the OK
button the changes are temporarily
saved. If you then exit the Steel
Stress Check Information form
by clicking the Cancel
button, the changes made to the steel
frame overwrites are considered temporary only and are not permanently
saved. Permanent saving of the overwrites does not actually occur
until you click the OK
button in the Steel Stress Check Information form.

4. - Table Showing Stress Details:
     This table shows the stress ratios obtained for each design load
     combination at each output station along the frame element. Initially
     the worst stress ratio is highlighted. Following are the headings
     in the table.
   - - Combo
       ID: The name of the [design
       load combination](SF_Select_Design_Combos.md) considered.
     - Station
       location: The location of the station considered measured
       from the i-end of the [frame](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Output_Stations.md)
       or [cable](../../Assign/Cable/Cable_Output_Stations.md)
       element.
     - Ratio:
       The total PMM stress ratio for the element. When stress ratios
       are reported for this item, they are followed by (T) or (C).
       The (T) item indicates that the axial component of the stress
       ratio is tension. The (C) item indicates that the axial component
       of the stress ratio is compression. Note that typically the
       interaction formulas are different depending on whether the
       axial stress is tension or compression.
     - Axl:
       The axial component of the PMM stress ratio.
     - B-Maj: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the major axis.
     - B-Min: The bending component of the
       PMM stress ratio for bending about the minor axis.
     - Maj Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio
       for shear acting in the major direction of the frame element.
     - Min
       Shr Ratio: The shear stress ratio for shear acting
       in the minor direction of the frame element.
   - Overwrites button. Click the Overwrites
     button to access the [Steel Frame Design Overwrites form](javascript:TextPopup(this)).
      Use this form to change design parameters, including the
     design section.

     Use the [Steel
     Frame Design Overwrites form](SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md) to make revisions
     to the steel frame design parameters, such as unbraced length
     ratio, effective length factor, bending coefficient, tensile
     strength, major and minor bending stress and major and minor
     shear stress, among others. Then use the Details
     buttons on the Steel Stress Check Information
     form to immediately see the new design results.

4. - Details button. Clicking the Details
     button displays the Steel Stress Check
     Data form, which shows the design details for the selected
     design combination and station location.  Values that are
     not applicable are reported as N/A. Similarly, N/C and N/N indicate
     an item is “Not Calculated” and “Not Needed.” Print this information
     by selecting File menu > Print
     command at the top of the form.
   - Tabular Data button. Click the Tabular
     Data button to access the Steel
     Details (Database) form. Use the various [menu
     commands](../../../Database_Tables/Database_Table_Form.md) on the form to export, display, and print the data
     table.
   - Table Format File button. The program default
     format or a selected table format can be applied to the data output
     (export, display or print). Click the Table
     Format File button to access the Set
     Database Table Formats File form and select the Use
     Program Default Table Formats option or the Use
     Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option. When
     the Use Formats from User Defined
     Table Formats File option is chosen, also click the Select button to locate a previously defined
     format file. Table formats are defined using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Make_Auto_Select_Section_Null.htm | SF Make Auto Select Section Null -->

# SF - Make Auto Select Section Null

This command replaces the [Auto Select section assignments](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) for the selected members with the current design section previously chosen from the auto select group. This is an irreversible action, i.e. once the Auto Select sections are turned off they will no longer be available for optimal design. After using this command, Auto Select sections would need to be reassigned if they were to once again be included in the design selection process.

1. Select the frame members for which the Auto Select sections are to be replaced with the current design section.
2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Make Auto Select Section Null command.
3. SAP2000 will issue a warning message that the Auto-Selected Sections Assignments will be replaced by the current design sections for the selected members. Click OK if acceptable; otherwise, click Cancel.

Note: This option should only be used after the final design cycle.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Reset_All_Steel_Overwrites.htm | SF Reset All Steel Overwrites -->

# SF - Reset All Steel Overwrites

The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Reset All Steel Overwrites command resets the [overwrites](SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md) for all frame sections with the Steel Frame design procedure to their default values. It is not necessary to make a selection before using the Reset All Steel Overwrites command. This command automatically applies to all frame sections with the Steel Frame design procedure. The command can be used to reverse changes made using the [View/Review Overwrites command](SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.md).

1. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Reset All Steel Overwrites command.
2. SAP2000 will request confirmation to reset overwrites and warns that current design results will be deleted.
3. Click the OK button to reset overwrites or the Cancel button to close the form without resetting overwrites.

Resetting the overwrites will reduce the size of a SAP2000 database (\*.SDB) file.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Reset_Design_Section_to_Last_Analysis.htm | SF Reset Design Section to Last Analysis -->

# SF - Reset Design Section to Last Analysis

In some instances design sections may change several times (before the analysis is rerun) and then the design section for one or more frame elements may need to be restored to match the last used analysis section. The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command is a quick and easy way to reset the design section to match the last analysis section. The anticipated process would be as follows:

1. Run the analysis and use the [Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure](SF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.md) command.
2. Use the [Interactive Steel Frame Design](SF_Interactive_Steel_Frame_Design.md) or [Change Design Section](SF_Change_Design_Section.md) command to change the design sections.
3. Use the Start Design/Check of Structure command to update the design. For this example process, after review, portions of the updated design have been determined to be unnecessary or unacceptable.
4. Select the elements whose design sections are to be reset.
5. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Reset Design Section to Last Analysis command to immediately reset the design section to match the last analysis section.

Note:  Rerunning the analysis updates the Analysis Section to match the Design Section.

<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Select_Design_Combos.htm | SF Select Design Combos -->

# SF - Select Design Combinations

Form:  Design Load Combinations Selection

Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Select Design Combo command to open the Design Load Combinations Selection form.  It is not necessary to run the analysis or select an object before using the command; however, the program will not generate the code-generated automatic load combinations until at least one analysis and design iteration has been run, and therefore, the automatic load combinations will not be shown until design has been run. Use the form to review and modify the design load combinations used during design.

- Load Combination Type selection box. Select the type of design combination to review or specify (i.e., Strength, Deflection).
- Select Load Combinations area. All of the available design load combinations are listed in the List of Load Combinations list box. The design load combinations actually used in the design are listed in the Design Load Combinations list box. All three of the following buttons act on the highlighted design load combination in those two list boxes.

1. - Use the Add and Remove buttons to move load combinations into and out of the Design Combos list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections in this form for use with the Add and Remove buttons.
   - Use the Show button to review the definition of a design load combination.

Note:   If a user-defined combination(s) is to be used in design, it must be selected as described herein, regardless of whether the combo was created manually ([Define menu options](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)) or if the combination(s) is based on code (Define menu, [Add Default Design Combos button](../../Define/Load_Combination/Add_Code_Generated_User_Load_Combinations_Form.md))  The program automatically selects those combos that are created when the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box is checked (see next bullet). Note also that these automatically generated combos are regenerated (i.e., replaced) after each design run.

- Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box. When this check box is checked, the design load combinations generated based on the selected code (i.e., the code selected using the [Design menu > Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences command](SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)) are added to the List of Load Combinations.
- - Set Automatic Design Load Combination Data button. With the Automatically Generate Code-Based Design Load Combinations check box checked, click this button to access the [Code Generated Automatic Load Combinations for {Code} form](../Code-Generated_Automatic_Load_Combinations_for_Type_Code_Form.md). Use that form to make changes to the automatically generated code-based design load combinations to be applied during model design.

The default steel frame design load combinations have names such as DSTL1, DSTL2 and so forth.

## See Also

[Load Combinations](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)
