<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Select_Design_Groups.htm | SF Select Design Groups -->

# SF - Select Design Groups

Form: Steel Design Group Selection

In SAP2000, elements can be grouped for steel frame design. When a group is specified for design, all elements in the group are given the same section.

1. Define the groups by selecting the frame elements and clicking the [Assign menu > Assign to Groups command](../../Assign/Assign_to_Groups.md). Designing using groups works only when [auto select sections](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) have been assigned to the beams. Typically, assign the same auto select section to each frame element to be used in a design group, although this is not absolutely necessary. Any frame elements in a design group not assigned an auto select section will be ignored for group design and will be designed individually.
2. After the group has been defined, use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Select Design Group command to access the Steel Design Group Selection form. All of the available groups are listed in the List of Groups list box. The groups actually in use are listed in the Design Groups list box.
3. On the Steel Design Group Selection form, use the Add and Remove buttons to move groups into and out of the Design Groups list box. Use the Ctrl and Shift keys to make multiple selections before using the Add and Remove buttons.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Set_Displacement_Targets.htm | SF Set Displacement Targets -->

# SF - Set Displacement Targets

Form: Lateral Displacement Targets

For displacement optimization, SAP2000 predicts which members should be increased in size to control the displacements based on the energy per unit volume in the members. The members with more energy per unit volume are increased in size a larger percentage than those with smaller energies per unit volume. Some members with small energy per unit volume may be decreased in size if they are still acceptable for strength considerations.

Note: [Auto select lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to the frame members for the displacement optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the desired displacement target may never be reached no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Specify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to open the Lateral Displacement Targets form, which can be used to specify displacement targets for various load cases. The intent is that a point is picked, typically at the roof level of the model, and a maximum displacement target (in any direction) is specified  for one or more load cases on that point.
2. From the Static Linear Case drop-down list in the Loads area of the form, select the [load pattern](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) for which the displacement is to be optimized.
3. Specify the location for the displacement by specifying a Point.
4. Specify the target displacement in the Max Displacement edit box.
5. Click the Add button.
6. Repeat Steps 1 through 5 as needed.
7. Run the design (Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure) and then rerun the analysis (Analyze menu > Run Analysis) using the new section sizes to view the displacements by right clicking on selected points. Displacement optimization is an iterative process that typically requires that the analysis and design be run multiple times. There is no guarantee that the desired displacement target will be reached using this option.

Tip:  To rerun the analysis, it will be necessary to delete the design results (i.e., unlock the model, or use the Delete Results button on the Set Analysis Cases to Run form). This will not adversely affect the specification of displacement targets.

Modify a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to access the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be modified in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form. Note that the data for the specification appears in the boxes at the top of the Loads area. Modify the data in the boxes as desired.
3. Click the Modify button.
4. Rerun the analysis using the new section sizes to review the displacements.

Delete a displacement optimization specification as follows:

1. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Set Displacement Targets command to access the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
2. Highlight the displacement optimization specification to be deleted in the Loads area of the Lateral Displacement Targets form.
3. Click the Delete button.

Deactivate Targets check box. Check the Deactivate Targets check box to exclude the displacements from a design iteration(s) without deleting it. Uncheck the check box to include displacements in the design.

## See Also

[Set Time Period Targets](SF_Set_Time_Period_Targets.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Set_Time_Period_Targets.htm | SF Set Time Period Targets -->

# SF - Set Time Period Targets

Form: Time Period Targets

For time period targets, specify a mode and a target period for that mode. Then, during design, SAP2000 automatically optimizes the structure to meet the target period using energy considerations. During the optimization process, members with large energy per unit volume are changed more than those with small energy per unit volume.

Note: [Auto select section lists](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Auto_Select_List.md) must be assigned to frame members for the time period optimization to work. When SAP2000 increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select section list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the displacement target may never be met, no matter how many times the analysis and design are rerun.

Use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Set Time Period Targets command to display the Time Period Targets form.

- Modal Load Case. Select the modal load case for which time period targets are being set.
- Add a Target.
- 1. Enter a number in the Mode Number edit box.
  2. SAP2000 will suggest a value in the Target Period edit box. Use this target period or type a revised value in the edit box.
  3. Click the Add button.
- Modify a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be modified in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Type a revised target period in the Target Period edit box.
  3. Click the Modify button.
- Delete a Target.
- 1. With the Time Period Targets form displayed, highlight the name of the target to be deleted in the Modes area of the form.
  2. Click the Delete button.

Deactivate Time Period Targets check box. Check this check box to exclude the time periods from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include time periods in design.

## See Also

[Set Displacement Targets](SF_Set_Displacement_Targets.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Start_Design-Check_of_Structure.htm | SF Start Design-Check of Structure -->

# SF - Start Design/Check of Structure

The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command starts the steel frame design process.

Run a steel frame design as follows:

1. 1. Click the [Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) command to run an analysis of the model.
   2. Click Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to begin the design process.

Note: This command is unavailable if no line objects with the Steel Frame design procedure have been included in the model. If line objects are selected when this command is used, only the selected line objects are designed. If no line objects are selected when this command is clicked, all steel line objects with the Steel Frame design procedure are designed.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md) and [Problem K](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_K.md),.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Verify_All_Members_Passed.htm | SF Verify All Members Passed -->

# SF - Verify All Members Passed

When the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command is used, the program reports if structural members passed the stress/capacity check.

Use the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command as follows:

1. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis.
2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check of Structure command to run the design.
3. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Verify All Members Passed command.

SAP2000 will display a pop-up box indicating the outcome of the verification. If members do not pass the check, the [Change Design Section command](SF_Change_Design_Section.md) can be used to change the design section.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.htm | SF Verify Analysis vs Design Section -->

# SF - Verify Analysis vs Design Section

When the iterative design process is complete, the last used analysis section property for a frame element and the current design section property for that frame element should be the same. If this is not the case, the frame element may not have been designed for the correct forces. The Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is useful for verifying that the last used analysis section and the current design section are the same for all steel frame elements in the model.

When the Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is used, SAP2000 identifies how many frame elements with the Steel Frame design procedure have different analysis and design sections and then selects those frame elements, if you ask it to. Typically this command would be used after the final design iteration to verify that the analysis and design properties used are consistent.

It is not necessary to select any elements before using the Verify Analysis vs Design Section command. This command automatically checks all frame sections with the Steel Frame design procedure.

Note: Update the Analysis Section by rerunning the analysis, perhaps several times in a complex model. Update the Design Section using the [Interactive Steel Frame Design command](SF_Interactive_Steel_Frame_Design.md) and the Overwrites button or the [Change Design Section command](SF_Change_Design_Section.md).

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm | SF View Revise Overwrites -->

# SF - View/Revise Overwrites

Form:  Steel Frame Design Overwrites for {Code}

Steel  frame design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the frame/cable elements to which they are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all steel frame overwrite items. Thus, it is not required that overwrites be specified. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items and change them if necessary to make sure they are acceptable.

Some of the default overwrite values are based on steel frame preferences. Thus define the preferences before defining the overwrites (and before designing or checking any steel frame members).

When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the elements to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the elements that are selected when the overwrites are changed.

Change an overwrite as follows:

Be sure to check, and as necessary, change the [Steel Frame Design Preferences](SF_View_Revise_Preferences.md)  before completing the following steps.

1. Select the frame element(s) to be specified overwrites.
2. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Overwrites command to access the Steel Frame Design Overwrites form. The steel frame overwrites are displayed with an Item column and a Value column. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the overwrite item.

Note:  The Overwrites button on the Steel Stress Check Information form can also be used to display the Steel Frame Design Overwrites form.

4. Left click in the Value column to activate a drop-down box or to highlight the contents of the cell.

- If the drop-down list appears, select a value from the box. Values in the drop-down lists cannot be changed.
- If the cell contents becomes highlighted, type in the desired revised value.

- Set to Prog Determined (Default) Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program defaults. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.

5. Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md) and [Problem K](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_K.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_View_Revise_Preferences.htm | SF View Revise Preferences -->

# SF View/Revise Preferences

Form:  Steel Frame Design Preferences for {Code}

Preferences are basic settings that control design parameters. Use the Steel Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form to access the preferences, including the design code. Default values that generally reflect the design code are provided so that specification of the individual parameters is not necessary; however, it is advisable to review the preferences to ensure that they are acceptable, and where needed to change them using this form.

1. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Preferences command to display the Steel Frame Design Preferences for {Code} form.

1. - Item/Value. Click in any of the drop-down lists or edit boxes in the Value column to change the default values to your specific choices.
   - Item Description. The Item Description area displays a short description of any item selected in the Item/Value columns. The description is provided to help you recall the purpose of the preference item.
   - Explanation of Color Coding for Values area. The items in this area are color-coded blue, black or red. The meaning of each color code is defined in the this area of the form.
   - Set to Default Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default.
   - Reset to Previous Values and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value.

2. Click on the OK button when finished making the necessary selections.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md)  and [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Display/Save_Named_Display.htm | Save Named Display -->

# Save Named Display

Form:  Named Displays and Views

Use the Display menu > Save Named Display command to display the Named Displays and Views form. Use the form to save a window view with all of its settings.

1. Use the various options in the program to set up the display of the model in the window.
2. Click the Display menu > Save Named Display command to display the Named Displays and Views form.
3. Use the default or type a new name in the Display edit box to name the display.
4. Click the Add New Named Display button to add the named display to the model file. The [Display menu > Show Named Display command](Show_Named_Display.md) subsequently can be used to recall the display settings. Note that if a Named Display is created of a deformed shape (i.e., after an analysis), but then the model is unlocked, the program will be unable to display the Named Display because the results will have been deleted.

   - Change Named Display Name button. Highlight an existing Named Display; type a new name in the Display edit box; and click this button to change the name of the Named Display.
   - Delete Named Display button. Highlight an existing Named Display and click this button to delete a Named Display.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Deformed_Shape.htm | Show Deformed Shape -->

# Show Deformed Shape

Form:  Deformed Shape

After an analysis has been run, SAP2000 will automatically display a deformed shape of the model. Use the Display menu > Show Deformed Shape command to display the Deformed Shape form and select additional display options.

- Case/Combo Name drop-down list. Select the name of a Load Case or Load Combination to be displayed. The selection made in this area of the form determines the other input required on the form.
- Multivalued Options The type of load case/combination determines which option is available:
- - For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown.
  - For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to view the maximum and/or minimum results over all steps.

Caution: When envelopes are displayed, the deformed shape is based on the maximum or minimum displacement at each degree of freedom, whichever has the larger absolute value. The result is a deformed shape that may not correspond to any particular state.

- - For steady-state load cases only, choose the phase angle for which results are to be shown, or choose Magnitude to view the resultant of the in-phase and out-of-phase components (see Area Contours/Draw Displacement Contours on Area Objects check box, below).
- Scaling options. Select the Scaling method. The Auto option will automatically set the scale factor. The Scale Factor option can be used to exaggerate the displacements relative to the geometry of the structure. If Auto was selected previously, the Scale Factor edit box will display the scale factor previously used.
- Area Contours area and Draw Displacement Contours on Area Objects check box. When this check box is checked, additional options are available on the form, including:
- - Draw Displacement Contours on Area Objects option. With this option, SAP2000 will draw displacement contours on area objects.
  - Show Displacement Contours as Lines option. With this option, SAP2000 will show the displacement contours as lines.
  - Area Contour Components options. Select the contour components to be displayed (Ux, Uy, Ux, Area 1Axis, Area 2 Axis, Area 3 Axis).
  - Resultant Magnitude check box. With this option, SAP2000 will display the resultant of the in-phase and out-of-phase components.
  - Area Contour Range option. Use the Min and Max edit boxes to specify the range for the contour to be displayed.

Note:  When the Options menu > Show Result Value While Scrolling command is preceded by a check mark (i.e., is enabled), a small text box of results will display when the mouse cursor is moved over a deformed shape.

Note:  The Area Contours ares will not appear on the form if no areas are included in the model.

- Options
- - Wire Shadow check box. Checking the Wire Shadow check box will also display the undeformed shape as a reference for comparison with the deformed shape.
  - Cubic Curve check box. Checking the Cubic Curve check box will display the deformed frame objects using a cubic-curve fit.
- Click the OK button to update the display.

With the Deformed Shape displayed on screen, click the Start Animation button on the status bar to animate the deformed shape. Change the animation speed using the slide control next to the Start Animation button. To stop the animation, click the Stop Animation button. Use the Options menu > Sound command to toggle accompanying sound on and off.

Joint Displacement

View the displacement components for a single joint by right clicking on a joint. The selected joint is highlighted and values are displayed in a floating Joint Displacements window. Clicking on any other joint updates the display. Clicking anywhere except on a joint closes the Joint Displacements window.

Note: Joint displacements can not be displayed during animation.

## See Also

[Step-by-Step Hinge Formation](Step-by-Step_Hinge_Formation.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Force_Stresses_Joints.htm | Show Force Stresses Joints -->

# Show Force/Stresses - Joints

Form:  Joint Reaction Forces

Use the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Joints command to display joint reactions as numerical values or arrows on the active window.

1. Define an [load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) (or use the default DEAD or MODAL cases) and [run an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md).
2. Click the  Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Joints command to display the Joint Reaction Forces form. Use the form to specify the parameters for the display.

1. - Case/Combo Name drop-down list. Select the load case or combination to be displayed. The selection made in this area of the form determines the other input required on the form.
   - Multivalued Options The type of load case/combination determines which option is available:
   - - For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown.
     - For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to see the maximum and/or minimum results over all steps.
   - Type area

1. 1. - Show as Arrows check box. When this check box is checked, the joint reactions will be displayed as arrows. If this check box is not checked, numerical values are displayed.

Note: Reactions are displayed for restraints, springs, and grounded links (one joint) only.

2. Click the OK button to update the display.

Tips: To display the details for a single object, right click on that object. This will open a floating window that displays the variation of the selected component over the length or area of the object. If more than one object exists within the tolerance of the cursor, a list box of the objects is displayed; select the desired element from the list. Click anywhere in the main display window to close the object window.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md), [Problem D](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_D.md), [Problem G](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_G.md), [Problem M](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_M.md), [Problem V](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_V.md), and [Problem Y](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Y.md).

## See Also

[Joint Element Output Conventions](../../../Output/Joint_Element_Output_Conventions.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Force_Stresses_Links.htm | Show Force Stresses Links -->

# Show Force/Stresses - Links

Form:  Member Force Diagram for NLLinks

Use the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Links command to display force diagrams for links on the active window.

1. Click the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Links command to display the Member Force Diagram for NLLinks  form. Use the form to specify the parameters for the display.

   - Case/Combo Name drop-down list. Select the [Load Case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) or [Combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) to be displayed.
   - Multivalued Options. For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown. For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to view the maximum or minimum results over all steps.

For steady-state load cases only, choose the phase angle for which results are to be shown, or choose Magnitude to view the resultant of the in-phase and out-of-phase components.

1. - Component options. Select the desired member force component, (i.e, Axial Force, Shear 2-2, Shear 3-3, Torsion, Moment 2-2, or Moment 3-3).
   - Scaling options. Select the Auto option to have SAP2000 automatically determine a scaling factor. Select the Scale Factor option to specify a scale factor.

SAP2000 calculates the scale factor as a multiple of the default font size. The advantage to determining the scale factor as a multiple of the default font size is that the default font size is limited by a specified minimum and maximum size that is specified using the Option menu > Preference > Dimensions/Tolerances command. This helps keep the automatically determined scale factor within a reasonable range most of the time. If the automatic scale factor seems to cause a display problem, use the Scale Factor option and specify a factor.

## See Also

[Link Element Internal Forces](../../../Output/Link_Element_Internal_Force_Output_Convention.md)

# Show Forces Stresses - Asolids

Form:  Element
Stress Contours for Asolids

Use the Display menu > Show
Forces/Stresses > Asolids command to display stresses for asolids
on the active window.

1. Define a [load
   case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) (or use the default DEAD or MODAL cases) and [run
   an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) of a model containing [Asolid
   objects](../../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md).
2. Click the Display
   menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Asolids command to display
   the Element Stress Contours for Asolids
   form. Use the form to specify the parameters for the display.

1. - Case/Combo
     Name drop-down list. Choose the load case or [combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md)
     whose asolid element stresses are to be displayed.
   - Multivalued
     Options. For multi-step cases, choose the step number,
     time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to view the maximum
     or minimum results over all steps.
   - Component
     options. Specify which component of stress is to be displayed.
     Click [here
     for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about the possible components
     for asolid internal stresses

     - S11:
       Direct stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
       and negative 1 faces in the 1-axis direction.
     - S22:
       Direct stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
       and negative 2 faces in the 2-axis direction.
     - S33: Direct stress (force per
       unit area) acting on the positive and negative 3 faces
       in the 3-axis direction.
     - S12:
       Shearing stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
       and negative 1 faces in the 2-axis direction and acting
       on the positive and negative 2 faces in the 1-axis direction.
     - SMAX:
       Maximum principal stress (force per unit area). Note that
       by definition, principal stresses are oriented such that
       the associated shearing stress is zero.
     - SMIN:
       Minimum principal stress (force per unit area). Note that
       by definition, principal stresses are oriented such that
       the associated shearing stress is zero.
     - SVM:
       [Von Mises stress](Von_Mises_Stress.md) (force
       per unit area).
   - Contour
     Range area. The asolid element internal stresses are displayed
     as colored contours. Specify two values:
   - - Min:
       Any element with a stress less than the value shown here is
       displayed in the color associated with Min in the Contours
       area of the [Assign Output Colors form](../../Options/Colors.md). Note
       that the color associated with Min is the top color in the
       form.
     - Max:
       Any element with stress greater than or equal to the value
       shown here is displayed in the color associated with Max in
       the Contours area of the Assign Output
       Colors form. Note that the color associated with Max
       is the bottom color in the form.

The program spaces the
intermediate range values equally between the specified Min
and Max values. If the Min and Max
values are set to zero, SAP2000 will automatically create a contour range
that includes all values. This is the default.

1. - ![](../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_1907862541.gif)Stress Averaging: Specify if
     stress averaging is to be used when displaying the stresses. Consider
     the four elements labeled A, B, C and D shown in the sketch at
     right. These four elements all have a common point, labeled 1,
     in the sketch. Each of the elements has an associated internal
     force or stress at joint 1. Typically the forces or stresses at
     common points in different elements are different. The finer the
     [mesh](../../Assign/Area/Area_Automatic_Area_Mesh.md)
     the closer the values become.

The options available
for stress averaging are None
for no stress averaging, At All Joints
for stress averaging at all joints or over
Objects & Groups for stress averaging at points selected just
before plotting the plane stresses, or for stress averaging of groups
selected using the Set Groups button.

If the None
option is used so that the stress contours are plotted with no stress
averaging at the common points, the changes in stress from element to
element typically will appear abrupt. Large stress variations between
elements may indicate that the model is not properly meshed and may need
to be refined to properly capture the variation in stress. Therefore,
use this option to determine if the model is meshed properly.

Stress averaging using
the At All Joints or over
Objects & Groups option tends to eliminate abrupt changes in
the plot and smooths the contours. Thus, after the meshing of the model
has been shown to be acceptable using the None
option, the At All Joints option
will give better results of the stress in the elements by averaging the
stress between elements and reducing the error because of the stress on
each individual element. The over Objects
& Groups option should be used if a discontinuity, such as
two planes meeting at an angle, is included in the model. In that case,
each plane should be averaged independently using the over
Objects & Groups option. This will avoid the problem of averaging
across the two planes, which would give incorrect result. The results
would be incorrect because the stress along the two planes is not continuous
relative to the elements' local axes.

1. - Show
     Deformed Shape check box. When this check box is checked,
     the asolid stresses will be displayed on the deformed shape.

# Show Forces/Stresses - Frames/Cables/Tendons

Form:  Member Force/Stress Diagram for Frames, Diagrams for Frame Object

Use the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Frames/Cables/Tendons command to display column, beam, brace, cable, or tendon forces/stresses directly on the SAP2000 model.

1. Define a [load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) (or use the default DEAD or MODAL cases) and [run an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md).
2. Click the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Frames/Cables/Tendons command to display the Member Force Diagram for Frames form. Use the form to specify the parameters for the display.

1. - Case/Combo Name drop-down list. Choose the Load Case or [Combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) to be displayed.
   - Multivalued Options. The type of load case/combination determines the option(s) available:
   - - For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown.
     - For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; choose Envelope to view the maximum and/or minimum results over all steps.
     - For Steady-State load cases, choose the phase angle or resultant.
   - Type options. Specify whether to display internal forces or stresses.
   - - Forces: Internal forces are available for all frame and cable sections.
     - Stresses: Axial stress S11 is available for all frame and cable sections. The shear stresses S12 and S13 are available for certain types of frame sections. When shear stresses are available, principal stresses Smax and SMin and von Mises stress SVM are also available for algebraic (non-envelope) load cases and combinations. See Technical Note "Frame Stress Calculation" for more information.
   - Component options.   Specify which component of force or stress is to be displayed. Only one component can be displayed at a time. For stress components, also choose the Stress Point:
   - - Point 0 is the centroid for all sections except the tube and pipe. This is the only location available for cable objects.
     - Points 1, 2, 3, etc., are specific to each different type of frame section property. The range available corresponds to the maximum number of points for any type of frame section property present in the model. Zero stress will be plotted for objects that do not report at the selected stress point. See Technical Note “Frame Stress Calculation” for more information.
     - Stress Max plots the maximum stress over all the stress points at each station. When an enveloping load case or combination is displayed, this is the maximum stress at any point for the envelope maximum, and the maximum stress at any point for the envelope minimum.
     - Stress Min plots the minimum stress over all stress points at each station. When an enveloping load case or combination is displayed, this is the minimum stress at any point for the envelope maximum, and the minimum stress at any point for the envelope minimum.
     - Stress Max/Min plots either or both the maximum and minimum stresses over all stress points at each station. When a single-valued load case or combination results are displayed, this is either the maximum stress or the minimum stress at any point, whichever has the larger absolute value. When an enveloping load case or combination is displayed, this is the maximum stress at any point for the envelope maximum and the minimum stress at any point for the envelope minimum.
   - Scaling options.  Select the Auto option to have SAP2000 automatically determine a scaling factor. Select the Scale Factor option to specify a scale factor.

SAP2000 calculates the scale factor as a multiple of the default font size. The advantage to determining the scale factor as a multiple of the default font size is that the default font size is limited by a specified minimum and maximum size that is specified using the Option menu > Preference > Dimensions/Tolerances command. This helps keep the automatically determined scale factor within a reasonable range most of the time. If the automatic scale factor does not give the desired results, use the Scale Factor option and specify a factor.

1. - Options. Choose the Fill diagram or Show Values on Diagram option:
   - - Fill Diagram: Display diagrams filled with color, but without text values.
     - Show Values on Diagram: Display diagrams unfilled and show controlling values as text.

With forces/stresses displayed on the model, note the following:

- - Use the left and right arrow buttons on the status bar to quickly display forces/stresses for other single-step analysis cases, or other steps in the current load case.
  - Multi-valued cases and combinations plot a range of values.
  - For frame elements, exact values are plotted at all output station locations. Those exact values are then connected by straight-line segments to complete the force diagram.
  - Force and stress values are not shown within the end offsets specified for each member.
  - Right click on a member to pop up a detailed frame results window (i.e., Diagrams for Frame Object form). Use the drop-down lists and buttons on that form to control the display:
  - - Load Case/Combo
    - Step number or Envelope type
    - Result Type and Component (Item)
    - Stress Point, when applicable

These controls are similar to those described above. In addition, the user can control where the results are displayed using the Display Options:

- - - Scroll for Values: Click and drag the mouse over the display areas to show values at the corresponding stations, or enter a specific station in the Location edit box.
    - Show Max: Show the station with the maximum absolute value.
    - I-End and J-End buttons: These move the cursor to the respective end of the member.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem I](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_I.md) and [Problem J](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_J.md).

## See Also

[Frame Element Internal Forces Output Conventions](../../../Output/Frame_Element_Internal_Forces_Output_Conventions.md)

[Step-by-Step Pushover Forces](../Step-by-Step_Pushover_Forces.md)

Technical Note "Frame Stress Calculation", available by using command Help > Documentation > Technical Notes.

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Shells.htm | Show Forces Stresses Shells -->

# Show Forces/Stresses - Shells

Form:  Display Shell Stresses

1. Click the Display > Show Forces/Stresses-Shells  command to access the Display Shell Stresses form.
2. Click the appropriate button to complete the required action:

Important note: The internal shell element forces are forces per unit length acting along the midsurface of the shell element (area object). The internal shell element stresses are stresses acting on the edges (not positive 3-axis face and negative 3-axis face) of the shell element (area object). See [Sign Conventions](../../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Sign_Convention.md) for more information about the faces of shell objects. Shell strains are available on a one-for-one basis corresponding to the shell stresses.

1. - Case/Combo Name edit box. Choose the load case or [combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) whose shell element forces or stresses are to be displayed.
   - Multivalued Options: For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown. For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to view the maximum or minimum results over all steps.
   - Component Type options. Choose the type of component to be displayed. The options available depend on the sections assigned in the model, and the option selected determines the other input required on the form.
   - - Resultant Forces option. When this option is selected, also select the Component.
     - Shell Stresses option. When this option is selected, specify the Output Type (i.e., display the stresses for the Visible Face, Top Face or Bottom Face, or the Maximum stress, Minimum stress or Absolute Maximum stress) and the Component.

     Note: When plotting Shell Stresses or Shell Layer Stresses, you can select the option to normalize the stresses with respect to the material strength. The strength used for this purpose is the yield strength (Fy) for steel, cold-formed steel, rebar, and tendon materials; the minimum of the two yield strengths (Fcy or Fty) for aluminum materials; and the compressive strength (f'c) for concrete materials. Zero normalized stresses will be plotted for other materials.

     - Shell Strains option. This is similar to the Shell Stresses option. Strain components are available corresponding one-for-one to the stress components. Shear strains are of the engineering type gij, double the tensorial shear strains, eij.

     Note: When plotting Shell Strains or Shell Layer Strains, you can select the option to normalize the strains with respect to the material strength divided by Young’s modulus. The strength used for this purpose is the yield strength (Fy/E) for steel, cold-formed steel, rebar, and tendon materials; the minimum of the two yield strengths (Fcy/E or Fty/E) for aluminum materials; and the compressive strength (f'c/E) for concrete materials. Zero normalized strains will be plotted for other materials.
   - - Shell Layer Stresses option. When this option is selected, specify to display the stresses By Area Section and Layer Name or By Layer Name Only. To display the stresses by area section, specify the area section by selecting it from the Area Section Property drop-down list. Then for both options, select the Layer Name and the Thickness Location within the layer from the drop-down lists. See note in Shell Stresses option above.
     - Shell Layer Strains option. This is similar to the Shell Layer Stresses option. Strain components are available corresponding one-for-one to the stress components. Shear strains are of the engineering type gij, double the tensorial shear strains, eij.
     - Concrete Design option. When this option is selected, specify the Output Type (i.e., display the member force for the Visible Face, Top Face or Bottom Face, or the Maximum, Minimum or Absolute Maximum member force) and the Component.
     - Component options. Specify which component of force, stress or strain is to be displayed.

Click [here for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about possible components of the shell element internal forces.

1. 1. - F11:
        Direct force per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 1 faces in
        the 1-axis direction.
      - F22:
        Direct force per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 2 faces in
        the 2-axis direction.
      - F12:
        Shearing force per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 1 faces in
        the 2-axis direction, and acting on the positive and negative
        2 faces in the 1-axis direction.
      - FMAX:
        Maximum principal force per unit length acting at the
        midsurface of the element. Note that by definition, principal
        forces are oriented such that the associated shearing
        force per unit length is zero.
      - FMIN:
        Minimum principal force per unit length acting at the
        midsurface of the element. Note that by definition, principal
        forces are oriented such that the associated shearing
        force per unit length is zero.
      - FVM:
         See [Von Mises Stress](Von_Mises_Stress.md)
      - M11:
        Direct moment per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 1 faces about
        the 2-axis.
      - M22:
        Direct moment per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 2 faces about
        the 1-axis.
      - M12:
        Twisting moment per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 1 faces about
        the 1-axis, and acting on the positive and negative 2
        faces about the 2-axis.
      - MMAX:
        Maximum principal moment per unit length acting at the
        midsurface of the element. Note that by definition, principal
        moments are oriented such that the associated twisting
        moment per unit length is zero.
      - MMIN:
        Minimum principal moment per unit length acting at the
        midsurface of the element. Note that by definition, principal
        moments are oriented such that the associated twisting
        moment per unit length is zero.
      - V13:
        Out-of-plane shear per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 1 faces in
        the 3-axis direction.
      - V23:
        Out-of-plane shear per unit length acting at the midsurface
        of the element on the positive and negative 2 faces in
        the 3-axis direction.
      - VMAX:
        Maximum principal shear per unit length acting at the
        midsurface of the element. Note that by definition, principal
        shears are oriented on faces of the element such that
        the associated shears per unit length on perpendicular
        faces are zero.

Click [here for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about the possible components for shell element internal stresses.

1. 1. - S11:
        Direct stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
        and negative 1 faces in the 1-axis direction.
      - S22:
        Direct stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
        and negative 2 faces in the 2-axis direction.
      - S12:
        Shearing stress (force per unit area) acting on the positive
        and negative 1 faces in the 2-axis direction and acting
        on the positive and negative 2 faces in the 1-axis direction.
      - SMAX:
        Maximum principal stress (force per unit area). Note that
        by definition, principal stresses are oriented such that
        the associated shearing stress is zero.
      - SMIN:
        Minimum principal stress (force per unit area). Note that
        by definition, principal stresses are oriented such that
        the associated shearing stress is zero.
      - SVM:
        [Von Mises stress](Von_Mises_Stress.md) (force
        per unit area).
      - S13:
        Out-of-plane shearing stress (force per unit area) acting
        on the positive and negative 1 faces in the 3-axis direction.
      - S23:
        Out-of-plane shearing stress (force per unit area) acting
        on the positive and negative 2 faces in the 3-axis direction.
      - SMAXV:
        Maximum principal shearing stress (force per unit area).
        Note that by definition, principal shearing stresses are
        oriented on faces of the element such that the associated
        shears per unit length on perpendicular faces are zero.

Click [here for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about the possible components for shell element internal strains.

1. 1. - E11:
        Direct strain in the 1-axis direction.
      - E22:
        Direct strain in the 2-axis direction.
      - G12:
        Engineering shear strain in the 1-2 plane.
      - EMAX:
        Maximum principal strain. Note that by definition, principal
        strains are oriented such that the associated shear strain
        is zero.
      - EMIN:
        Minimum principal strain. Note that by definition, principal
        strains are oriented such that the associated shear strain
        is zero.
      - EVM:
        [Von Mises strain](Von_Mises_Stress.md), also
        known as the equivalent strain.
      - G13:
        Out-of-plane engineering shear strain in the 1-3 plane.
      - G23:
        Out-of-plane engineering shear strain in the 2-3 plane.
      - GMAXV:
        Maximum principal transverse shearing strain. This is
        the vector resultant of G13 and G23.

1. - Contour Range: The shell element internal forces, stresses and strains are displayed as colored contours. Specify two values:

1. 1. - Min: Any element with a force/stress/strain less than the value shown here is displayed in the color associated with Min in the Contours area of the [Assign Output Colors form](../../Options/Colors.md). Note that the color associated with Min is the top color in the form.
      - Max: Any element with a force/stress/strain greater than or equal to the value shown here is displayed in the color associated with Max in the Contours area of the Assign Output Colors form. Note that the color associated with Max is the top color in the form.

The program spaces the intermediate range values equally between the specified Min and Max values. If the Min and Max values are set to zero, SAP2000 will automatically create a contour range that includes all values. This is the default. Click the Set To Default Contour Range button to apply the default values

1. - ![](../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_1907862541.gif)Stress Averaging: Specify if stress averaging is to be used when displaying the force/stress/strain. Consider the four elements labeled A, B, C and D shown in the sketch at right. These four elements all have a common point, labeled 1, in the sketch. Each of the elements has an associated internal force or stress at joint 1. Typically the values at common points in different elements are different. The finer the [mesh](../../Assign/Area/Area_Automatic_Area_Mesh.md) the closer the values become.

The options available for stress averaging are None for no stress averaging, At All Joints for stress averaging at all joints or over Objects & Groups for stress averaging at points selected just before plotting the shell force/stress/strain, or for stress averaging of groups selected using the Set Groups button.

If the None option is used so that the force/stress/strain contours are plotted with no stress averaging at the common points, the changes in value from element to element typically will appear abrupt. Large variations between elements may indicate that the model is not properly meshed and may need to be refined to properly capture the variation in stress. Therefore, use this option to determine if the model is meshed properly.

Stress averaging using the At All Joints or over Objects & Groups option tends to eliminate abrupt changes in the plot and smooths the contours. Thus, after the meshing of the model has been shown to be acceptable using the None option, the At All Joints option will give better results of the stress in the elements by averaging the stress between elements and reducing the error because of the stress on each individual element. The over Objects & Groups option should be used if a discontinuity, such as two planes meeting at an angle, is included in the model. In that case, each plane should be averaged independently using the over Objects & Groups option. This will avoid the problem of averaging across the two planes, which would give incorrect result. The results would be incorrect because the stress along the two planes is not continuous relative to the elements' local axes.

1. - Show Deformed Shape check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will display the model using color-coded contours with distortions to show where the model is subject to the effects of the forces and stresses.

Note: Shell element stresses and strains (not forces) actually have different values at the top and bottom of the shell elements as a result of bending. Thus, depending on which side of the object is being displayed, different stresses or strains will be shown. Two-dimensional views always look at area objects from the same side. To view stresses or strains on the other side of the area object, switch to a 3D view or right click on the object while stresses/strains are displayed to access the Shell Diagram form and click the Switch Face button.

Note: When forces/stresses/strains are plotted for multi-valued combinations, SAP2000 displays whichever of the maximum and minimum values has the largest absolute value.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem S](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md).

## See Also

[Shell Element Internal Forces/Stresses Output Convention](../../../Output/Shell_Element_Internal_Forces_Stresses_Output_Convention.md)

# Show Force/Stresses - Solids

Form:  Display Solid Stresses

Use the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Solids command to display stresses or strains for solids on the active window.

1. Define a [load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) (or use the default DEAD or MODAL cases) and [run an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md).
2. Click the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Solids command to display the Display Solid Stresses form. Use the form to specify the parameters for the display.

1. - Case/Combo Name drop-down list. Choose the load case or [combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) whose solid element stresses are to be displayed.
   - Multivalued Options: For multi-mode cases, choose the mode number for which results are to be shown. For multi-step cases, choose the step number, time step, or frequency step; or choose Envelope to view the maximum or minimum results over all steps. For steady-state analysis cases only, choose the phase angle for which results are to be shown, or choose Magnitude to view the resultant of the in-phase and out-of-phase components.
   - Component Type: Specify whether to plot stresses or strains for the solid objects
   - Component options. Specify which component of stress is to be displayed.
   - - Click [here for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about the possible components for solid stresses

       - S11: Direct stress
         (force per unit area) acting on the positive and negative
         1 faces in the 1-axis direction.
       - S22: Direct stress
         (force per unit area) acting on the positive and negative
         2 faces in the 2-axis direction.
       - S33: Direct stress
         (force per unit area) acting on the positive and negative
         3 faces in the 3-axis direction.
       - S12: Shearing stress
         (force per unit area) acting on the positive and negative
         1 faces in the 2-axis direction and acting on the
         positive and negative 2 faces in the 1-axis direction.
       - S13: Out-of-plane
         shearing stress (force per unit area) acting on the
         positive and negative 1 faces in the 3-axis direction.
       - S23: Out-of-plane
         shearing stress (force per unit area) acting on the
         positive and negative 2 faces in the 3-axis direction.
       - SMAX: Maximum principal
         stress (force per unit area). Note that by definition,
         principal stresses are oriented such that the associated
         shearing stress is zero.
       - SMID: Middle principal
         stress (force per unit area).  Note that by definition,
         principal stresses are oriented such that the associated
         shearing stress is zero.
       - SMIN: Minimum principal
         stress (force per unit area). Note that by definition,
         principal stresses are oriented such that the associated
         shearing stress is zero.
       - SVM: Von Mises stress
         (force per unit area). See also [Von
         Mises Stress](Von_Mises_Stress.md)
     - Click [here for information](javascript:TextPopup(this)) about the possible components for solid strains

       - E11: Direct strain
         in the 1-axis direction.
       - E22: Direct strain
         in the 2-axis direction.
       - E33: Direct strain
         in the 3-axis direction.
       - G12: Out-of-plane
         engineering shear strain in the 1-2 plane.
       - G13: Out-of-plane
         engineering shear strain in the 1-3 plane.
       - G23: Out-of-plane
         engineering shear strain in the 2-3 plane.
       - EMAX: Maximum principal
         strain. Note that by definition, principal strains
         are oriented such that the associated shear strain
         is zero.
       - EMID: Middle principal
         strain Note that by definition, principal strains
         are oriented such that the associated shear strain
         is zero.
       - EMIN: Minimum principal
         strain area. Note that by definition, principal strains
         are oriented such that the associated shear strain
         is zero.
       - EVM: Von Mises strain.
         See also [Von Mises
         Stress](Von_Mises_Stress.md)
   - Contour Range: The solid element internal stresses or strains are displayed as colored contours. Specify two values:
   - - Min: Any element with a stress/strain less than the value shown here is displayed in the color associated with Min in the Contours area of the [Assign Output Colors form](../../Options/Colors.md). Note that the color associated with Min is the top color in the form.
     - Max: Any element with stress/strain greater than or equal to the value shown here is displayed in the color associated with Max in the Contours area of the Assign Output Colors form. Note that the color associated with Max is the bottom color in the form.

1. - Stress Averaging: Specify if stress averaging is to be used when displaying the stresses or strains. Consider the four elements labeled A, B, C and D shown in the sketch at right. These four elements all have a common point, labeled 1, in the sketch. Each of the elements has an associated stress or strain at joint 1. Typically the values at common points in different elements are different. The finer the [mesh](../../Assign/Area/Area_Automatic_Area_Mesh.md) the closer the values become. ![](../../../assets/images/Images/ebx_1907862541.gif)

The options available for stress averaging are None for no stress averaging, At All Joints for stress averaging at all joints or over Objects & Groups for stress averaging at points selected just before plotting the plane stresses, or for stress averaging of groups selected using the Set Groups button.

If the None option is used so that the stress/strain contours are plotted with no stress averaging at the common points, the changes in stress or strain from element to element typically will appear abrupt. Large stress variations between elements may indicate that the model is not properly meshed and may need to be refined to properly capture the variation in response. Therefore, use this option to determine if the model is meshed properly.

Stress averaging using the At All Joints or over Objects & Groups option tends to eliminate abrupt changes in the plot and smooths the contours. Thus, after the meshing of the model has been shown to be acceptable using the None option, the At All Joints option will give better results of the stress or strain in the elements by averaging the value between elements and reducing the error because of the stress on each individual element. The over Objects & Groups option should be used if a discontinuity, such as two planes meeting at an angle, is included in the model. In that case, each plane should be averaged independently using the Over Objects and Groups option. This will avoid the problem of averaging across the two planes, which would give incorrect result. The results would be incorrect because the stress or strain along the two planes is not continuous relative to the elements' local axes.

1. - Show Deformed Shape check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will display the model using color-coded contours with distortions.
   - Show As Arrows check box. When this check box is checked, principal stresses will be displayed as arrows rather than as contours.

# Von Mises Stress and Strain

The von Mises Stress provides a measure of the shear, or distortional, stress in the material. This type of stress tends to cause yielding in metals. It is independent of the amount of hydrostatic stress (s1=

In a state of pure tension, say

For materials, initial yielding can be expected when 
s
vm=sy, where 
s
y is the tensile yield stress, or when 
s
vm=Ö3 
t
y, where 
t
y is the yield stress in shear. For other materials, particularly frictional materials such as soil and concrete, the von Mises Stress may have no value in predicting yield or failure.

The von Mises Strain, or equivalent strain, is identified in terms of the principal strains as:

evm=Ö{2/9[(e1- e2)2+( e1- e3)2+( e2- e3)2]}.

This is intended to be a measure of plastic deformation, which is assumed to incompressible in metals. In this case, **e11 +e22+e33=0** , which is also true when Poisson’s ratio is 0.5.

In a state of pure tension, say s11=s and all other stresses are zero, then evm=e11=s/E, provided that Poisson’s ratio is 0.5. In a state of pure shear, say s12=t and all other stresses are zero, then **evm = Ö(1/3)** **g12 = Ö(1/3) t/G**, since pure shear satisfies the incompressibility requirement.

Note that for incompressible behavior, the von Mises stress and strain are energy conjugates. For example, **svmevm =((Ö3** **t) (Ö(1/3)** **g12) = t2 / G**, as expected.

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Hinge_Results.htm | Show Hinge Results -->

# Show Hinge Results

Form:  Hinge Results

Use the Hinge Results form to view hinge hysteresis plots for multi-step nonlinear load cases, such as Nonlinear Static, Staged Construction, Nonlinear Direct-Integration Time-History and FNA load cases.

1. - Select Hinge drop-down list. Choose the hinge for which results are to be plotted.
   - Show Hinge on Selected Objects Only check box. If frame or area objects were selected before the Display menu > Show Hinge Results command was used, this check box will be checked, and only the hinges for the selected object will be available in the Select Hinge drop-down list.

TIP: The Select menu > Select Hinge command on this form can be used to select an object and thus limit the hinges available in the Select Hinge drop-down list to only those on the selected object.

1. - Show Hinge Property Definition button. Click the button to display the [Hinge Property Data Form](../Define/Section_Properties/Hinge_Properties/Hinge_Property_Data_Form.md). Use the Modify/Show Hinge Property button on that form to display the Hinge Property Data for {Property Name} form. The form is for review purposes only and cannot be edited here.
   - Hinge Location and Behavior area
   - - Frame / Area Object display box. The frame or area object to which the hinge is assigned is displayed in this box.
     - Relative Distance display box: The value shown in this display box is the relative distance specified when the [hinge was assigned](../Assign/Frame/Hinges/Frame_Hinges.md) to the frame object. This display box is only shown for Frame hinges.
     - **Layer and Direction** display box. The value shown in this display box is the layer name and the direction (S11 or S22) associated with the selected hinge in the [hinge-type layered shell section property](../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Layer_Definition_Form.md) assigned to the area element. This display box is only shown for Area hinges.
     - Hinge Behavior display box. This is the hinge behavior that was specified when the hinge was defined.
   - Units drop-down list. Use the currently displayed units for the values entered in this form or choose another from this drop-down list. The selected units will be used in the display of the hinge results.
   - Hinge Results display area. The plot of the hinge chosen in the Select Hinge drop-down list will display in this area. The type of plot depends on the type of hinge.
   - - Select Load Case drop-down list and Step scroll buttons. Use the drop-down list to choose the load case for which the hinges are to be plotted. Use the scroll buttons to select the Step in the analysis.
     - Current Hinge Data are, including Hinge DOF drop-down list and Hinge State and Hinge Status display boxes. Select the degree of freedom to be plotted from the Hinge DOF drop-down list. Various display boxes will be added in this area of the form to provide the current data for the hinge plot. The names of the edit boxes and the values in them depend on the type of hinge being plotted. The Hinge State display box shows the location of the plot (i.e., mouse pointer) with respect to the A, B, C, D, and E values for the load deformation. The Hinge Status display box shows the location of the plot (mouse pointer) with respect to the Acceptance Criteria IO, LS and CP. See the [Hinge Property Data for Name Form](../Define/Section_Properties/Hinge_Properties/Frame_Hinge_Property_Data_for_Property_Name_Form_Deformation_Controlled.md) topic for more information.
     - Plot Control Parameters area. The check boxes in this area of the form control the graphic in the display area. When the check appears in a check box, that control is enabled. The function of the control is assumed to be self-explanatory. Click the small color box to display the Color form and select a new color for displaying the hinge backbone.
     - Slide bar and Horiz and Vert display boxes. Use the slide bar below the plot to move the mouse pointer along the plot of the hinge. Alternatively, move the mouse pointer over the display area and the location of the mouse pointer will display in the Horiz and Vert display boxes.

The Hinge Results form also has a File menu and a Select menu with subcommands.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Command | Function |
| File menu > |  |
| Print Setup for Graphics | Use this command to access the print setup form of the printer connected to the computer displaying the hinge results. |
| Use Color Printer | This is a toggle. When a check mark precedes this command, the command is enabled and the graphic can be printed in color assuming that the printing device prints in color. |
| Print Graphics | Immediately sends the plot to the printer. |
| Display Tables | Displays the Table Display form. That form shows the hinge results data in tabular format. Use the File menu commands on that form to export the hinge data to Excel or Access. Use the commands on the Edit menu to apply or remove filtering and sorting criteria for the data on the Table Display form. |
| Capture Picture> |  |
| Entire Screen | Creates a .bmp file of the entire screen showing the hinge plot. |
| Form Including Title Bar | Creates a .bmp file of the active window, plus the title bar. |
| Form Without Title Bar | Creates a .bmp file of the active window without the title bar. |
| Select menu > |  |
| Select Hinge | Click the command to display the Choose Hinge form. The type of object available in the Choose Hinge form depends on the type of hinge that was selected in the **Select Hinge** drop-down list in this form. Use the Choose a Frame / Area Object with Hinges drop-down list to select a frame object for which the hinge results are to be plotted. Use the Choose a Hinge on the Frame / Area Object drop-down list to select the hinge for which results are to be plotted. |

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Influence_Lines.htm | Show Influence Lines -->

# Show Influence Lines

Forms:  Show
Influence Lines, Select Frame Relative Distance

After paths have been defined and a moving load case
has been defined and run, click the Display menu
> Show Influence Lines command to display the Show
Influence Lines form.

The influence lines
can be displayed for the various displacements, reactions, forces, moments,
shears, and torsion or axial loads on joints, frames, shells, planes,
asolids, solids, and links resulting from a unit load on a defined path
in the structure.

The process for displaying
influence lines is as follows:

1. [Define
   paths](../Define/Moving_Loads/Path_Data_Form.md)
2. [Assign
   frame path](../Assign/Frame/Frame_Path.md)
3. [Define
   vehicles](../Define/Moving_Loads/Vehicle_Class_Data_Form.md)
4. [Define
   vehicles classes](../Define/Moving_Loads/Vehicle_Class_Data_Form.md)
5. [Define
   a moving load results to save](../Define/Moving_Loads/Define_Moving_Load_Case_Results_Saved.md)
6. [Define
   a moving load load case(s)](../Define/Load_Cases/Moving_Load_Form.md)
7. Run the analysis
8. Click the Display
   menu > Show Influence Lines command to display the Show Influence Lines form. Use the form to
   specify the influence lines to be plotted:

1. - Select
     One or More Paths selection list. Select the path(s) for
     which influence lines are to be displayed by clicking on the path
     name in this selection list. Use the Select
     All Paths button to select all of the displayed paths.
     Use the Clear All Paths button to
     deselect all selected paths. Use the Shift and the Ctrl keys with
     the mouse to make multiple selection.
   - Load
     Case Name drop-down list. Choose the load case for which
     the influence lines are to be displayed by clicking on the load
     case name in this drop-down list.
   - Plot
     Parameters. Choose an option to determine if the plot should
     be a wire frame or a contour. The sub-options offer further refinement
     of the display with respect to showing or hiding the deck and
     vertical objects.
   - - Show
       Table button. Click the Show Table
       button to display the influence line data points in tabular
       form. The data in the table is for display purposes and cannot
       be edited here. Make changes to the table by adjusting the
       [path definition](../Define/Moving_Loads/Path_Data_Form.md).
       Data in the table can be copied using the Copy
       Entire Table or Copy Selected
       Cells buttons. The copied data can then be pasted into
       another program.
     - Contour
        Transparency area.. Use the Contour
       Transparency Factor drop-down list to specify the degree
       of transparency for the contour display. The lower the number,
       the more transparent the contour.
   - Scaling.
     Select the Auto option
     to have SAP2000 automatically determine a scaling factor. Select
     the Scale Factor option
     to specify a scale factor. SAP2000 calculates the scale factor
     as a multiple of the default font size, which is determined as
     a multiple of the average story height. The advantage to determining
     the scale factor as a multiple of the default font size is that
     the default font size is limited by a specified minimum and maximum
     size that is specified using the Options
     menu > Preference > Dimensions/Tolerances command.
     This helps keep the automatically determined scale factor within
     a reasonable range most of the time. If the automatic scale factor
     seems to cause a display problem, use the Scale
     Factor option (on the [Dimensions/Tolerances Preferences form](../Options/Dimensions_Tolerances.md))
     and specify a factor.

1. - Plot
     Influence Line for This Element Type area. Choose the element
     type for which the influence line is to be displayed. The option
     chosen here determines the options available in the lower right
     portion of the form. If an element type is not available, that
     element type is not included in the model.
   - - Joint option.
     - - Joint
         Label edit box. Type the Joint number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Joint
         Result Type. Select the Joint Result Type as displacement
         or joint reaction. Depending on the structural configuration,
         some of the types may have no influence lines.
       - Component.
         Select the component of joint displacement or joint reaction
         to be displayed.
     - Frame option.
     - - Frame
         Label edit box. Type the frame number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Relative
         Distance. This display box will show a default
         station along the frame object, typically the midpoint
         of the span. Click the Set Relative
         Distance to Fall on Path Load Point button to display
         the Select Frame Relative Distance
         form. Select one of the program-calculated values on this
         form to specify a load point on the frame.
       - Component.
         Select the component of moment, shear, torsion or axial
         load to be displayed. Depending on the structural configuration,
         some of the components may have no influence lines.
     - Shell option.
     - - Area
         Label edit box. Type the shell number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Shell
         Result Type. Select the Shell Result Type as resultant
         force, top stress or bottom stress. Depending on the structural
         configuration, some of the types may have no influence
         lines.
       - Joint
         Label drop-down list. The influence line for the
         shell object will be plotted relative to the joint selected
         in this drop-down list.
       - Component.
         Select the component and direction of force, moment, or
         stress to be displayed.
     - Plane option.
     - - Plane
         Label edit box. Type the plane number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Joint
         Label edit box. The influence line for the plane
         object will be plotted relative to the joint selected
         in this drop-down list.
       - Component.
         Select the component and direction of stress to be displayed.
     - Asolid option.
     - - Asolid
         Label edit box. Type the asolid number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Joint
         Label edit box. The influence line for the asolid
         object will be plotted relative to the joint selected
         in this drop-down list.
       - Component.
         Select the component and direction of stress to be displayed.
     - Solid option.
     - - Solid
         Label edit box. Type the solid number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Joint
         Label edit box. The influence line for the solid
         object will be plotted relative to the joint selected
         in this drop-down list.
       - Component.
         Select the component and direction of stress to be displayed.
     - Link option.
     - - Link
         Label edit box. Type the link number for which
         the results are to be reported.
       - Link
         Result Type. Select the Shell Result Type as internal
         deformation, I-End force or J-End force. Depending on
         the structural configuration, some of the types may have
         no influence lines.
       - Component.
         Select  the direction of the deformation or the axial
         load, shear, torsion or moment of the force to be displayed.
   - Click the OK button to view the Influence line or
     the Cancel button to close the form
     without viewing the influence lines.

# Show Load Assigns - Areas

Form:  Show Area Loads

Click the Display menu > Show Load Assigns > Areas command to display the Show Area Loads form and specify the area loads to be shown on the model in the active window.

- Load Pattern Name drop-down list. Select the [load pattern](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) for which the loading is to be displayed.
- Load Type options. This area of the form will have several selections, some of which will not be available because that type of loading has not been included in the model. Select the Load Type, and where appropriate, the Coordinate System,  the Direction, Distribution and Face.
- Click the OK button. If the OK button is not available, no loads have been assigned to areas in the model.

Note:  Only one loading can be displayed on the model at a time.

Note:  The Show Area Loads form also displays when the Modify Display button is clicked on the Point Information form and Loads tab has been selected.

# Show Load Assigns - Frame/Cable/Tendon

Form:  Show Frame Loads

Click the Display menu > Show Load Assigns > Frame/Cable/Tendon command to display the Show Frame Loads form and specify the frame loads to be shown on the model in the active window.

- Load Pattern Name drop-down list. Select the [load pattern](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) for which the loading is to be displayed.
- Load Type options. This area of the form will have several selections, some of which will not be available because that type of loading has not been included in the model. Select the Load Type, and where applicable, the Coordinate System, Component, and Load Step.
- Show Joint Loads with Span Loads check box. Check this check box to view the joint loads in addition to the span loading.
- Show Span Loading Values check box. Check this check box to view loading values.
- Click the OK button. If the OK button is not available, no loads have been assigned to frames, cables, and tendons in the model.

Note: Certain options on the form will be inactive depending on the type of loading defined on the model. Only one loading can be displayed on the model at a time.

Note:  If the Tendon Calculated Load Data option is selected, with the loads displayed on the screen, right click on the tendon to display another form that shows the loads in tabular format.

# Show Load Assigns - Joints

Form:  Show Joint Loads

Click the Display menu > Show Load Assigns > Joints command to display the Show Joint Loads form and specify the joint loads to be shown on the model in the active window.

- Load Pattern Name drop-down list. Select the [load pattern](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) for which the loading is to be displayed.
- Coordinate System drop-down list. Select the Coordinate System on which the forces are to be resolved.
- Load Type options. Select to display Forces or Displacements. If the options are not available, the loads have not been included in the model.
- Show Loading Values check box. Check this check box to view loading values on the model.
- Click the OK button. If the OK button is not available, no loads have been assigned to joints in the model.

Note:  The Show Joint Loads form also displays when the Modify Display button is clicked on the Point Information form and the Loads tab has been selected.

# Show Load Assigns - Solids

Form:  Show Solid Loads

Click the Display menu > Show Load Assigns > Solids command to display the Show Solid Loads form and specify the solid loads to be shown on the model in the active window.

- Load Pattern Name. Select the [load pattern](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) for which the loading is to be displayed.
- Load Type. This area of the form will have several selections, some of which will not be available because that type of loading has not been included in the model. Select the Load Type, and where applicable, the Coordinate System, Face and Component.  Choose to display values or contours.

# Show Named View

Form: Select Named View

Use the Display menu > Show Named View command in conjunction with the [Display menu > Save Named Display command](Show_Named_Display.md). The Display menu > Show Named View command differs from the [Display menu > Show Named Display command](Show_Named_Display.md) in that it retains the type of display in the active window and only changes the view direction, zoom, and object visibility to what is stored in the saved display.
