<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Plot_Function/Asolid_Plot_Functions_Form.htm | Asolid Plot Functions Form -->

# Asolid Plot Functions Form

Use the Asolid Plot Function form to specify the parameters for displaying Asolid stress functions.

1. Specify the asolid plot function to be displayed using the various options on the form:

1. - Plot Function Name edit or display box.
   - - If the Asolid Plot Functions form was accessed by highlighting a previously defined asolid plot function definition on the Plot Functions form, this box displays the name of that function. If necessary, click in the edit box and type a new name for the plot function.
     - If the Asolid Plot Functions form was accessed by clicking the Add Plot Function button on the  Plot Functions form, this display box will be empty until a value has been entered in the Element ID edit box. When a value is entered in the Element ID edit box, SAP2000 will display a default Plot Function Name. The default name can not be edited directly. To change the name, complete the definition of the plot; highlight that function name in the Plot Functions list on the Plot Functions form; click the Modify/Show Plot button to redisplay the Asolid Plot Functions form and then change the name.
   - Element ID edit or display box.
   - - If the Asolid  Plot Functions form was accessed by highlighting a previously defined asolid plot function definition on the Plot Functions form, this display box shows the name of the element associated with that previously defined plot function. This value can not be edited directly.
     - If the Asolid  Plot Functions form was accessed by clicking the Add Plot Function button on the  Plot Functions form, this is an edit box. Enter the Element ID for which the plot function is being prepared (e.g., 18 for asolid element 18).  SAP2000 will automatically provide a default Plot Function Name when a value is entered in this edit box.
   - Mode Number. Recover the time history for a particular mode as follows:
   - 1. Select the Include One option.
     2. Enter the mode number directly, or, use the spin button up and down arrows to select from the list.

Note:  If the Include All option is the only option available, the load case selected on the Plot Functions form is not a time history load case.

1. - Component area. Select the appropriate component.
   - Specify Output Location area. Use the options in this area to specify the location for reporting the Stresses.
   - - Output Location Reference Point area. Choose the appropriate option for determining the reference point for the asolid element:
     - - Reference to Selected Coordinate System Origin option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the coordinate system origin by applying the distances specified in the Offset Global X, Y and Z edit boxes.
       - Reference to Selected Joint option and drop-down list. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the joint selected from the drop-down list. SAP2000 will apply the distances specified in the Offset Global X, Y and Z edit boxes.
     - Coordinate System drop-down list. Choose the [coordinate system](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) to be used for determining the reference point. If the Local option is selected from the drop-down list, any offset must be relative to the selected joint (i.e., Reference to Selected Joint will be the only option available in the Output Location Reference Point area).
     - Offsets From Reference Point To Output Location:
     - - Offset 1/Global X, Offset 2/Global Y, Offset 3/Global Z edit boxes. Enter a distance in the current units to offset the location of the output results in the selected direction. These options depend on the Coordinate System selected.
     - Move Output Location to Closest Joint check box. During analysis, SAP2000 internally meshes asolid elements, resulting in program-generated analysis model joints. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 moves the location for reporting results to the analysis model joint closest to the location specified using the other options on this form.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the asolid plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the asolid plot function.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Asolid Plot Function form as follows:   1. [Construct a model](../../../Getting_Started/Modeling_Process.md) with areas that have an [Asolid type section property](../../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Axisymmetric_Solid_Asolid_Section_Data_Form.md). 2. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History Load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 3. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 4. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. 5. Select the Add Asolid Stresses option from the Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add Plot Function button, or highlight a previously defined asolid plot function definition and click the Modify/Show Plot button to display the Asolid Plot Function form. If the Add Asolid Stresses option is not available, no asolid section properties have been assigned to the model. |

# Base Functions Form

Use the Base Functions form to specify the parameters for displaying plot functions of base shear and moment.

1. Choose the base functions to be displayed by checking the appropriate check boxes.

1. - Base Shear: The total force reaction on all the supports in the global direction, X, Y, Z.
   - Base Moment: The total moment (overturning or torsional) on the supports of the structure about the global axis, X, Y, Z.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the base plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the base plot function.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Base Functions form as follows:   1. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History Load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 3. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. 4. Select the Add Base Functions option from the Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add Plot Function button, or highlight a previously defined base function definition and click the Modify/Show Plot button to display the Base Functions form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Plot_Function/Energy_Functions_Form.htm | Energy Functions Form -->

# Energy Functions Form

Use the Energy Function form to specify the parameters for displaying functions of input, kinetic, potential, model damping, link damper, link hysteretic, and error energy.

1. Choose the energy functions to be displayed by checking the check boxes.

1. - Input Energy check box. Work done on the structure by force and acceleration functions. In an exact solution, this would equal the sum of the Kinetic, Potential, Modal Damping, Link Damper, and Link Hysteretic energies.
   - Kinetic Energy check box. A function of the sums of the masses and their corresponding velocity for the structure.
   - Potential Energy check box. A function of the sums of the elastic constants and their corresponding displacement for the structure. The sum includes NLLink members.
   - Modal Damping Energy check box. The energy absorbed through model damping.
   - Link Damper Energy check box. The energy absorbed through NLLink damping.
   - Link Hysteretic check box. The energy absorption by Plastic 1, Isolator1 and Isolator2 NLLink elements. Damper, Gap and Hook NLLink elements are not included.
   - Error Energy  check box. An estimate of the error in the analysis. It is the difference between the input energy and the sum of the remaining energy components.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the energy plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the energy plot function.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Energy Functions form as follows:   1. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History Load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 3. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. 4. Select the Add Energy Functions option and click the Add Plot Function button to display the Energy Functions form. 5. Select the Add Energy Functions option from the Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add Plot Function button, or highlight a previously defined energy function definition and click the Modify/Show Plot button to display the Energy Functions form. |

To change the name, complete the definition of the plot; highlight that function name in the Plot Functions list on the Plot Functions form; click the Modify/Show Plot button to redisplay the Plane Plot Functions form and then change the name.
   - Element ID edit or display box.
   - - If the Plane Plot Functions form was accessed by highlighting a previously defined plane plot function definition on the Plot Functions form, this display box shows the name of the element associated with that previously defined plot function. This value can not be edited directly.
     - If the Plane Plot Functions form was accessed by clicking the Add Plot Function button on the  Plot Functions form, this is an edit box. Enter the Element ID for which the plot function is being prepared (e.g., 18 for plane element 18).  SAP2000 will automatically provide a default Plot Function Name when a value is entered in this edit box.
   - Mode Number. Recover the time history for a particular mode as follows:
   - 1. Select the Include One option.
     2. Enter the mode number directly, or, use the spin button up and down arrows to select from the list.

Note:  If the Include All option is the only option available, the load case selected on the Plot Functions form is not a time history analysis.

1. - Component area. Select the component to be plotted.
   - Specify Output Location area. Use the options in this area to specify the location for reporting the Stresses.
   - - Output Location Reference Point area. Choose the appropriate option for determining the reference point for the plane element:
     - - Reference to Selected Coordinate System Origin option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the coordinate system origin by applying the distances specified in the Global X, Y and Z edit boxes.
       - Reference to Selected Joint option and drop-down list. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the selected joint by applying the distances specified in the Global X, Y and Z edit boxes.
     - Coordinate System for Offset from Reference Location and Coordinate System drop-down list. Choose the [coordinate system](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) to be used for determining the reference point. If the Local option is selected from the drop-down list, any offset must be relative to the selected joint (i.e., Reference to Selected Joint will be the only option available in the Output Location Reference Point area).
     - Offsets From Reference Point To Output Location:
     - - Offset 1/Global X, Offset 2/Global Y, Offset 3/Global Z edit boxes. Enter a distance in the current units to offset the location of the output results in the selected direction. These options depend on the Coordinate System selected.
     - Move Output Location to Closest Joint check box. During analysis, SAP2000 internally meshes plane elements, resulting in program-generated analysis model joints. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 moves the location for reporting results to the analysis model joint closest to the location specified using the other options on this form.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the plane plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the plane plot function.

| --- |
| Access the Plane Plot Function form as follows:   1. [Construct a model](../../../Getting_Started/Modeling_Process.md) with areas that have a [plane type section property](../../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Plane_Section_Data_Form.md). 2. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History Load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 3. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 4. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. 5. Select the Add Plane Stresses option from the Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add Plot Function button, or highlight a previously defined plane plot function definition and click the Modify/Show Plot button to display the Plane Plot Function form. If the Add Plane Stresses option is not available, no plane section properties have been assigned to the model. |

# Plot Function Trace Named Sets Form

Use the Plot Function Trace Named Sets form to add, modify, or delete a plot function definition as specified using the various options on the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form.

- Add New PF Set button.
- 1. After the parameters on the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form have been specified and the Save Named Set button has been clicked, type a name in the edit box at the top of the Plot Function Set display area.
  2. Click the Add New PF Set button. This will save the specified parameters to the Named Set.
- Change PF Set Name button
- 1. Highlight a previously defined named set in the Plot Function Set display area. The highlighted name appears in the edit box at the top of the Plot Function Set display area.
  2. Type the revised name in the edit box.
  3. Click the Change PF Set Name button to change the name of the Named Set.
- Delete PF Set button
- 1. Highlight a previously defined named set in the Plot Function Set display area.
  2. Click the Delete PF Set button to delete a Named Set.

## See Also

[Select Plot Function Trace Named Set Form](Select_Plot_Function_Trace_Named_Set_Form.md)

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Plot Function Trace Name Sets form as follows:   1. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Use the various options on the form to specify a plot function definition and display. 3. Click the Save Named Set button to display the Plot Function Trace Name Sets form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Plot_Function/Plot_Functions.htm | Plot Functions -->

# Plot Functions

Form:  Plot Function Trace Display Definition, Display Plot Function Traces

After a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) have been defined and an [analysis has been run](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md), click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command or the Define menu > Named Set > Plot Function Traces command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Use the form to specify the analysis case and the function to be displayed.

Note: The Display menu command enables the plot function to be displayed, printed and captured as a .bmp file. The Define menu command can be used to save the settings specified for the display, print or capture so that those settings can be quickly and easily applied to another plot function.

- Analysis Case (Multi-Stepped Cases) drop-down list. Choose the analysis case for which the plot function is to be displayed.
- Choose Plot Functions area
- - Define Plot Functions button. Click this button to display the [Plot Functions form](Plot_Functions_Form.md). Use the form to add, modify, or delete plot functions.
  - List of Functions display area. All available functions are listed in this display area.
  - 1. Select a plot function from this list by highlighting it.
    2. Click the Add button to move the selected plot function into the Vertical Functions display list. The plot functions in this list will be displayed on the vertical axis.

       - Remove button. Highlight a function in the Vertical Functions display area and click the Remove button to remove the function from the list of functions to be displayed.
       - Show button. With a function highlighted in the List of Functions display area, click the Show button to display the [form](Plot_Functions_Form.md) used to define the function. No changes can be made to the form in this mode. To make changes, click the Define Plot Functions button and choose the appropriate function type.
    3. Review and where appropriate make selections or provide data for the other areas of the form:

       - Horizontal Plot Function drop-down list. Choose a plot function from the drop-down list to plot the variations of one function against another. The function(s) chosen in the Vertical Functions display area will be displayed, showing the variations with the function chosen from this drop-down list.
       - Selected Plot Function Line Options area. If the options in this area of the form are not available, highlight a function name in the Vertical Functions display list.
       - - Solid Line, Dashed Line, Dotted Line options. Choose the option for displaying the function line.
         - Vertical Scale Factor option. Use this edit box to specify the vertical scale factor. The default is 1.
         - Line Color. The function line will display in the color shown. To change that color, click the Line Color display box to display the Color form. Click on the new color in the palette and click the OK button to close the Color form.
       - Time Range and Reset Defaults button. Use the From and To edit boxes to specify the time range. Use the Reset Defaults button to restore the default settings. By default, the full time range is selected.
       - Axis Range Override area. If necessary, specify the Horizontal maximum/minimum and Vertical maximum/minimum values for displaying the plot. The values specified here override the Vertical Scale Factor and Time Range values.
       - Axis Labels area. Use the Horizontal and Vertical edit boxes to specify labels for the axes of the plot.
    1. - Grid Overlay check box. When this check box is checked, the function will be plotted on a graph-paper type grid.
    4. After the other options on the form have been specified, your choices can be saved as a "named set," which can be recalled late (note that this accomplishes the same thing as using the Define menu > Named Set > Plot Function Traces command). This is useful if you want to use the same options repeatedly. Clicking the Save Named Set button accesses the Plot Function Traces Named Sets form. Type a name in the Plot Function Set edit box and click the Add New PF Set button to save the current settings on the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form as a Named Set. Highlight an existing Named Set, type a new name in the Plot Function Set edit box, and then click the Change PF Set button to change the name of the Named Set. Highlight a Named Set and click the Delete PF Set to deleted the highlighted Named Set.

       - Show Named Set button. Click this button to access the Select Plot Function Traces Named Set form; use that form to select a Named Set defined using the Save Named Set button. Using a Named Set will make automatic selections on the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form with regard to the settings described in this topic.
    5. Display button. Click the Display button to display the Display Plot Function Traces form on which functions are displayed graphically. A small Legend window displays the maximum and minimum numerical values for the functions and another small window just below it displays the coordinates of the pointer. The commands on the form's File menu can be used to print the plot or capture the point as a .bmp file.

Note:  The plot displays graphically only when the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command is used to access the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form.

- Done button. Click the Done button to close the form.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem L](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_L.md) and [Problem O](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_O.md).

# Plot Functions Form

Additional form:  Modify Multiple Plot Functions

Use the Plot Functions form to add, modify, or delete plot functions.

- Plot Functions display list. All previously defined plot functions will be displayed in this list.
- Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list. The following list identifies the possible function types. Depending on what has been defined in the model, some of those items may not be available.
- - [Add Load Functions](Time_History_Load_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Energy Functions](Energy_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Base Functions](Base_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Joint Disps/Forces](Joint_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Frame Forces](Frame_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Shell Forces/Stresses](Shell_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Solid Stresses](Solid_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Link Forces/Deformation](Link_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Add Section Cuts Forces](Section_Cut_Plot_Function.md)
  - [Add Generalized Displacements](Generalized_Displacement_Plot_Functions.md)
  - [Asolid Plot Functions Form](Asolid_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
  - [Plane Plot Functions Form](Plane_Plot_Functions_Form.md)
- Add Plot Function button
- 1. In the Choose Function Type to Add area of the form, select the function type to be added.
  2. Click the Add Plot Function button to display a form specific to the type of function chosen.
- Modify/Show Plot Function button
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously defined plot function in the Plot Functions display list.
  2. Click the Modify/Show Plot Function button to display the form specific to the type of function chosen.
- Modify Multiple Plot Functions button
- 1. Select multiple plot functions of the same type (e.g., joint, frame, etc.) in the Plot Functions display list.
  2. Click the Modify Multiple Plot Functions button to display the Modify Multiple Plot Functions form. This button is only available when multiple functions of the same type have been defined in the model. The Modify Multiple Plot Functions form has the following areas:

     - Function Type drop-down list. This drop-down list displays the types of plot functions for which multiple functions of the same type have been defined in the model.
     - List of Plot Functions display area. This list includes all the  functions of the type specified in the Function Type drop-down list.
     - Functions to be Modified display area. This list includes all of the functions to be modified.
     1. 1. Select the function(s) to be modified and click the appropriate button:
        1. - Add button. When this button is clicked, the selected functions will be moved from the List of Plot Functions display list and added to the Functions to be Modified display list. As indicated above, if a plot function is included in this list when the OK button is clicked, that function will be modified.
           - Remove button. When this button is clicked, the selected function(s) will be moved from the Functions to be Modified display list into the List of Plot Functions display list. In that case, if a plot function has been removed from the Functions to be Modified display list, that function will not be modified when the OK button is clicked.
           - Show button. When this button is clicked, the plot function definition is displayed. When changes are made to the definition, those changes will affect all functions of the selected type simultaneously.
- Delete Plot Functions button
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously defined plot function in the Plot Functions display list.
  2. Click the Delete Plot Functions button.

## See Also

[Plot Function Trace Named Sets Form](Plot_Function_Trace_Named_Sets_Form.md)

[Select Plot Function Trace Named Set Form](Select_Plot_Function_Trace_Named_Set_Form.md)

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Plot Functions form as follows:   1. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 3. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. |

# Section Cut Plot Function

Use the Section Cut Plot Function form to specify the parameters for displaying section cut force functions.

1. Specify the section cut plot function to be displayed using the various options on the form:

1. - Section Cut drop-down list. Select the section cut. A function name will automatically appear in the Plot Function Name text box. This is the name of the plot function for display purposes.
   - Component area. Select the appropriate component ([F1, F2, F3, M1, M2, M3](../../../Output/Section_Cut_Output_Conventions.md)).
   - Mode Number. Recover the time history for a particular mode as follows:
   - 1. Select the Include One option.
     2. Enter the mode number directly, or, use the spin button up and down arrows to select it from the list.

Note:  If the Include All option is the only option available, the analysis case selected on the Plot Functions form is not a time history analysis.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the section cut plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the section cut plot function.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Section Cut Plot Function form as follows:   1. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md); run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Define a [section cut](../../Define/Section_Cuts.md) if not already defined. 3. Click the Display menu > Show Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 4. Click the Define Plot Functions button to display the Plot Functions form. 5. Select the Add Section Cut Forces option from the Choose Function Type to Add drop-down list and click the Add Plot Function button, or highlight a previously defined section cut plot function definition and click the Modify/Show Plot button to display the Section Cut Plot Function form. |

# Select Plot Function Trace Named Set Form

Note:  A Named Set must be defined/saved before this form can be used.

To generate output, various options must be selected on the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. After being selected, those options can be saved as a Named Set using the [Plot Function Trace Named Sets form](Plot_Function_Trace_Named_Sets_Form.md). After the options have been saved, they can be reapplied quickly and easily to another output by selecting that Named Set from the Select Plot Function Trace Named Set form.

1. Highlight the Named Set to be used in the display area on the Select Plot Function Trace Named Set form.
2. Click the OK button to apply the options to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Select Plot Function Trace Named Sets form as follows:   1. Click the Display menu > Plot Functions command to display the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. 2. Click the Show Named Set button. |

# Shell Plot Functions Form

Use the Shell Plot Function form to specify the parameters for displaying shell force and stress functions.

1. Specify the shell plot function to be displayed using the various options on the form:

1. - Plot Function Name edit or display box.
   - - If the Shell Plot Functions form was accessed by highlighting a previously defined shell plot function definition on the Plot Functions form, this box displays the name of that function. If necessary, click in the edit box and type a new name for the plot function.
     - If the Shell Plot Functions form was accessed by clicking the Add Plot Function button on the  Plot Functions form, this display box will be empty until a value has been entered in the Element ID edit box. When a value is entered in the Element ID edit box, SAP2000 will display a default Plot Function Name. The default name can not be edited directly. To change the name, complete the definition of the plot; highlight that function name in the Plot Functions list on the Plot Functions form; click the Modify/Show Plot button to redisplay the Shell Plot Functions form and then change the name.
   - Element ID edit or display box.
   - - If the Shell Plot Functions form was accessed by highlighting a previously defined shell plot function definition on the Plot Functions form, this display box show the name of the element associated with that previously defined plot function. This value can not be edited directly.
     - If the Shell Plot Functions form was accessed by clicking the Add Plot Function button on the  Plot Functions form, this is an edit box. Enter the Element ID for which the plot function is being prepared (e.g., 18 for shell element 18).  SAP2000 will automatically provide a default Plot Function Name when a value is entered in this edit box.
   - Type options. Choose the type of output.
   - - Resultants option.
     - Stresses (top or bottom) option.
     - Shell Layer Stresses option. When this option is selected, specify the Layer Name and, from the Thickness Location drop-down list, the layer within which the stresses are to be plotted.
   - Mode Number. Recover the time history for a particular mode as follows:
   - 1. Select the Include One option.
     2. Enter the mode number directly, or use the spin button up and down arrows to select it from the list.

Note:  If the Include All option is the only option available, the load case selected on the Plot Functions form is not a time history analysis.

1. - Component area. Select the appropriate component (if forces [F11, F22, F12,FMAX,FMAIN,FVM, M11, M22, M12,MMAX,MMIN, V13, V23,VMAX](../../../Output/Shell_Element_Internal_Forces_Stresses_Output_Convention.md);  if stresses [S11, S22, S12, SMAX, SMIN, SVM, S13, S23, SMAX](../../../Output/Shell_Element_Internal_Forces_Stresses_Output_Convention.md) ).
   - Specify Output Location area. Use the options in this area to specify the location for reporting the Resultants or Stresses.
   - - Output Location Reference Point area. Choose the appropriate option for determining the reference point for the shell element:
     - - Reference to Selected Coordinate System Origin option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the coordinate system origin by applying the distances specified in the Offset 1/Global X, Offset 2/Global Y and Offset 3/Global Z edit boxes.
       - Reference to Selected Joint option and drop-down list. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will offset the output results from the selected joint by applying the distances specified in the Offset 1/Global X, Offset 2/Global Y and Offset 3/Global Z edit boxes.
     - Coordinate System for Offset from Reference Location and Coordinate System drop-down list. Choose the [coordinate system](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) to be used for determining the reference point. If the Local option is selected from the drop-down list, any offset must be relative to the selected joint (i.e., Reference to Selected Joint will be the only option available in the Output Location Reference Point area).
     - Offsets From Reference Point To Output Location:
     - - Offset 1/Global X, Offset 2/Global Y, Offset 3/Global Z edit boxes. Enter a distance in the current units to offset the location of the output results in the selected direction. These options depend on the Coordinate System selected.
     - Move Output Location to Closest Joint check box. During analysis, SAP2000 internally meshes shell elements, resulting in program-generated analysis model joints. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 moves the location for reporting results to the analysis model joint closest to the location specified using the other options on this form.

2. Click the OK button to complete the definition of the shell plot function and return to the Plot Function form.
3. Define another function, or click the OK button to return to the Plot Function Trace Display Definition form. Refer to the [Plot Functions](Plot_Functions.md) topic for the additional steps required to display the shell plot function.

| Access the Shell Plot Function form as follows:   1. [Construct a model](../../../Getting_Started/Modeling_Process.md) with areas that have a [shell type section property](../../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Shell_Section_Data_Form.md). 2. Define a [Time History function](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md); run an [analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 3. If the Add Shell Forces/Stresses option is not available, no shell section properties have been assigned to the model. |

     - Move Output Location to Closest Joint check box. During analysis, SAP2000 internally meshes solid elements, resulting in program-generated analysis model joints. # Show Response Spectrum Curves

Form:  Response Spectrum Generation, Response Spectrum Curves, Response Spectrum Named Sets, Select Resp Spec Named Set

Note:  A [Time History function](../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) and a [Time History load case](../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) must be defined for the model and an [analysis must be run](../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) for this command to be available.

1. Click the Display menu > Show Response Spectrum Curves command or the Define menu > Named Sets > Joint TH Response Spectrum command to display the Response Spectrum Generation form. The form has six tabs: Define, Axes, Direction, Options, Frequency and Damping. Clicking on any tab selects it. Click the appropriate tab and use the various options to set up display of the response spectrum curve.

Define Tab

1. 1. Use the [Time History Case](../Define/Load_Cases/Define_Load_Cases.md) drop-down list to select the Time History Case for which the Response Spectrum Curve is to be generated.
   2. Specify the joint for the response spectrum curve. If joints are listed in the Choose a Joint list, select a joint by clicking on it. If no joints are listed, use the following buttons to add, modify, or delete joints in the list.

      - Add Joint button. Type a joint label in the Choose a Joint edit box and click the Add Joint button to add a joint to the list. If a joint label is entered in the edit box, but that joint is not included in the model, SAP2000 will display an error message.
      - Modify Joint button. Highlight a joint in the Choose a Joint list, type the change in the edit box, and click the Modify Joint button to make the change.
      - Delete Joint button.  Highlight a joint in the Choose a Joint list and click the Delete Joint button to delete the joint from the list. Deleting the joint from the list does not remove the joint from the model.
   3. Use the other tabs on the form to complete the set up for generating the response spectrum curve.

Axes Tab

1. - Select the Abscissa to be displayed as Frequency or Period.
   - Select the Ordinate to be SD (Spectral Displacement), SV (Spectral Velocity), PSV (Pseudo Spectral Velocity), SA (Spectral Acceleration) or PSA (Pseudo Spectral Acceleration).

Direction Tab

- Select the Coordinate System for the selected joint from the drop-down list.
- Select the direction X, Y or Z  to define the direction for which the spectrum is to be generated. By default the X (global X-direction) is checked.

Options Tab

1. - Set the Abscissa scale to Arithmetic or Log. By default Log is selected.
   - Changing the percentage of Spectrum Widening will change the peaks of the response spectra curves. The default is set to zero.
   - Set the Ordinate scale to Arithmetic or Log. By default Arithmetic is selected.
   - Changing the ordinate Scale Factor will scale the spectral values. The default is 1.0.
   - Unchecking the Grid Overlay check box will turn off the generation of a grid through the major divisions of the axes.

Frequency/Period Tab

Either a Frequency or Period tab will be available depending on the Abscissa selection made on the Axes tab.

1. - Unchecking the Default check box will exclude the built-in set of frequencies/periods in the generation of response spectrum.
   - Unchecking the Structural check box will disable merging of the structural frequencies/periods into the set of frequencies used in the generation of response spectrum.
   - Check the User check box and define frequencies/periods as follows:
   - 1. Enter the value in the User Frequencies/Periods edit box.
     2. Click the Add Value button.
     3. Repeat to include all frequencies/periods.

To change a user-defined frequency/period, highlight a previously defined user frequency/period, type a new value in the User Frequencies/Periods edit box and click the Change Value button. To delete a user-defined frequency/period, highlight a previously defined user frequency/period and click the Delete Value button.

Damping Tab

Use this tab to add a new damping value or edit the default damping values.

Add Value button. Use the Add Value button to add a new damping value.

1. Type a new value in the edit box.
2. Click the Add Value button.

Change Value button. Use the Change Value button to change one of the default damping values.

1. 1. 1. Click on the damping value to be changed in the Damping Values list box.
      2. Change the value in the edit box.
      3. Click the Change Value button.

Delete Value button. Use the Delete Value button to remove one of the values from the set.

1. 1. 1. In the Damping Values list box, click on the damping value to be deleted.
      2. Click the Delete Value button

2. Click the Display button to open a floating Response Spectrum Curves form in which the response spectra are graphically displayed. (Note that when this form is accessed using the Define menu > Named Sets > Joint TH Response Spectrum command, this button is inactive.) A small Legend window displays the joint number direction, scale factor, widening percentage and damping ratios color coded to correspond to the spectra curves. Another small window just below it displays the coordinates of the pointer.

Note:  With the floating Response Spectrum Curves form displayed on screen, use the mouse to window over an area of the plot to enlarge the area enclosed within the window. Click the right mouse button to restore the original display.

2. - File menu > Print Setup for Graphics command. Click the File men > Print Setup for Graphics command at the top of the Response Spectrum Curves form to select and set up the printer to be used for printing the on-screen display.
   - File menu > Print Graphics command. To print the currently displayed response spectrum curve, click the File menu > Print Graphics command at the top of the Response Spectrum Curves form.
   - File menu > Print Tables command. To print output tables for the currently displayed response spectrum curve, click the File menu > Print Tables command at the top of the Response Spectrum Curves form.
   - File menu > Print Tables to File command. Use the File menu > Print Tables to File command to send the output tables for the currently displayed response spectrum curve to file. SAP2000 will prompt you for a file name and storage location for the file.
   - File menu > Capture Picture command. The subcommands for this command can be used to capture a picture of the Entire Form, the Form w/o (without) Title Bar, and the Plot Only. SAP2000 will prompt you for a file name and storage location of the picture file, which will be saved in .jpg format.

OK button. Click the OK button to close the Response Spectrum Curves form.

Save Named Set button. After all of the setting have been specified on all of the tabs, click the Save Named Set button to access the Response Spectrum Named Sets form.

1. - Type a name in the Resp Spec Set edit box to name the set of values specified before the Save Named Set button was clicked. Click the Save New RS Set button.
   - If the name of a previously Named Set needs to be modified, select the Named Set in the Resp Spec Set display area; type a new named in the Resp Spec Set edit box and click the Change RS Set Name button.
   - If a previously Named Set needs to be deleted, select the Named Set in the Resp Spec Set display area and click the Delete RS Set button.

Show Named Set button. The Show Named Set button will only be available if a Named Set has been saved. Click the Show Named Set button to access the Select Resp Spec Named Set form. Highlight the Named Set to be displayed. Click the OK button. The value settings stored in the Named Set will be applied to the Response Spectrum Generation form. Select a joint and click the Display button to display the response spectrum curve based on the Saved Named Set.

3. Click the Done button to exit the Response Spectrum Generation form.

# ASCE 41-13 Soil-Structure Interaction Form

Use the ASCE 41-13 Soil-Structure Interaction form to specify kinematic effects and foundation damping to be applied to the demand spectrum in accordance with ASCE 41-13.

- **Include Kinematic Effects** check box. Check this check box to include Kinematic effects for the soil-structure interaction. With the check box checked, use the default values or specify other values for the **Effective Foundation Size**, the **Foundation Embedment**, the **Shear Wave Velocity**, and the **Shear Wave Velocity Reduction Factor** in the associated edit box.
- **Include Foundation Damping** check box. Check this check box to include foundation damping. With the check box checked, use the default value or specify another value for the **Modified Damping Ratio of the System** in the associated edit box. The damping ratio specified here is the flexible-base damping ratio.
- Show Spectra Comparison for SSI Effects button. Click this button to display the [Spectra Comparison for Soil-Structure Interaction Effects](Spectra_Comparison_for_Soil-Structure_Interaction_Effects_Form.md) form, which will display the spectral displacement vs spectral acceleration, period vs spectral acceleration, or period vs spectral displacement plot, depending on the option selected.
- **Units** drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the soil-structure interaction effects curve.
- Reset Defaults button. Clicking this button will return all options on the form to program defaults.

|  |
| --- |
| *Access the ASCE 41-13 Soil-Structure Interaction form as follows:*   1. *Define a* [*nonlinear static analysis* *case*](../../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) *whose* Load Application *type is* Displacement Control *and whose* Results Saved *type is* Multiple States, *and* *[run an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md)**.* 2. *Choose Method a, b, or c to specify the display for a pushover curve, define parameters for it, or save the options as a Named Set, respectively:*     1. *Click the Display menu > Show Pushover Curve command to display the Pushover Curve form. Select*  ASCE 41-13 NSP *for the* Plot Type*, and click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing curve definition and click the Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form.*    2. *Click the Define menu > Pushover Parameter Sets > ASCE 41-13 NSP command to display the Define Pushover Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP  form; then click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing parameter set definition and click the Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form.*    3. *Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Pushover Named Sets command to display the Define Pushover Named Sets form. Then click the Add New Named Set button, or highlight a previously defined Named Set and click the Add Copy of Named Set or Modify/Show Named Set button, to display the Pushover Named Set Data form. On that form select*  ASCE 41-13 NSP *for the* Plot Type*, and click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing named set and click the Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form.* 3. *Check the Include Soil-Structure Interaction Effects check box and then click the Modify/Show SSI button.* |

  drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the

  interaction effects curve.

  Defaults button. Clicking this button will return all options
  on the form to program defaults.

# Pushover Curve Form - Kappa Factor

Section 8.2.2.1.1 of ATC-40 defines a kappa factor, k, which modifies the calculated area of the hysteresis loops to account for pinching of the loops depending on the structural behavior of the building. Structural Behavior Types A, B, and C are described, and curves for the k factor are provided (see Figure 8-15 in ATC-40). The curves describing the k factor are trilinear, with the first segment having a constant k value, the second segment having a linearly varying k value, and the third segment having a constant k value. Thus the k factor curves can be described with just two points, those at the beginning and end of the second segment. The point at the beginning of the second segment is designated Point 1, and the point at the end is Point 2.

![](../../../assets/images/Images/k-factor_wmf.gif)

# Parameters for ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum Form

Use the Parameters for ATC
40 Capacity Spectrum form to specify the parameters for displaying
pushover curves in accordance with ATC 40 guidance.

- Name
  edit box. The program will suggest a default name. Use this name or
  type a new one in this edit box.
- Units
  drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the
  list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the pushover
  curve.
- Plot
  Axes area. Choose the plot axes as Sa-Sd
  (spectral acceleration vs spectral displacement), Sa-T
  (spectral acceleration vs period) or Sd-T
  (spectral displacement vs period).
- Set
  Axis Data button. Click this button to access the [Override Axis Labels and Range form](Set_Axis_Labels_and_Range_Form.md). Use the options
  on that form to change the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical
  ranges and the axis labels for the curve.

- Demand
  Spectrum Definition. Choose to define the demand spectrum based
  on a function or user specified coefficients.
- - Function
    option, drop-down list, and SF
    (Scale Factor) edit box. When this option is selected, choose
    a previously defined [spectrum
    function](../../Define/Functions/Response_Spectrum/Define_Response_Spectrum_Functions.md) from the drop-down list and use the default scale
    factor or use the edit box to specify the SF.
  - Use
    Coeff and Ca and
    Cv (Seismic Coefficient)
    edit boxes. The shape of the demand spectrum with 5% damping is
    controlled by the values input in the Ca
    and Cv (Seismic Coefficient)
    edit boxes. Refer to ATC-40, Chapter 4, for an explanation of,
    and appropriate values for, Ca and Cv. The default value for both
    Ca and Cv is 0.4. Demand spectra for other damping levels are
    created from the 5% damped spectrum using the spectral reduction
    factors described in Section 8.2.2.1.1 of ATC-40.

- Damping
  Parameters Definition.
- - Inherent + Additional Damping
    edit box. In the Damping Parameters
    area, type a value in the Inherent/Additional
    Damping edit box. The value input into this box must be
    between 0 and 1, inclusively. The default value is 0.05. Referring
    to ATC-40 equation 8-8, the b0 term is automatically included
    by the SAP2000 analysis method, and the 5% inherent viscous damping
    term can be specified in the Inherent/Additional
    Damping edit box as 0.05. If additional viscous damping
    is provided in the structure, perhaps by viscous dampers that
    are not specifically included in the model, this damping should
    also be included in the Inherent
    + Additional Damping edit box. Thus if the damping inherent
    in the structure is assumed to be 5% of critical damping, and
    dampers that provide an additional 7% of critical damping are
    assumed to be added to the structure (although they are not actually
    in the model), the value input in the Inherent
    + Additional Damping edit box should be 0.12, since 0.05
    + 0.07 = 0.12.
  - Structural Behavior Type. Select
    one of the four [Structural
    Behavior Type](javascript:TextPopup(this)) options in the Damping
    Parameters area. The Structural
    Behavior Types A, B
    and C default to the
    values defined for those structural behavior types in Section
    8.2.2.1.1 of [ATC-40](../../../Introduction/Bibliography.md)
    .

    Section 8.2.2.1.1 of ATC-40 defines a
    kappa factor, k,
    that modifies the calculated area of the hysteresis loops
    for different types of structural behavior. That section also
    describes Structural Behavior Types A, B, and C and provides
    curves for the kappa factor associated with each behavior
    type (see Figure 8-15 in ATC-40).
  - - User option - Modify/Show
      button. The User
      option allows the user to input kappa (k)
      values other than those provided by behavior Types A, B, and
      C.  With the User
      option selected, click the associated Modify/Show
      button to display the [Override Structural Behavior Type
      form](Override_Structural_Behavior_Type_Form.md).
- Items
  Visible On Plot area. Choose the items to be displayed on the
  plot.
- - Show Capacity Curve check box.
    Checking this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the capacity curve is green. Click the
      color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Show Family of Demand Spectra
    check box. Checking this check box overlays a family of demand
    spectra on the capacity curve in the ADRS format.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the family of demand spectrum curves
      is red. Click the color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the demand spectra.
    - Damping
      Ratios. The family of curves can include up to four
      demand spectra curves, each with a different effective damping
      ratio, beff. By default, the program
      plots curves with beff
      = 0.05, 0.1, 0.15 and 0.2. The damping ratios for any of the
      four curves can be changed by editing the value in one of
      the four Damping Ratios, beff
      edit boxes. The values input into the beff
      edit boxes must be between 0 and 1, inclusively. A value of
      0, or a blank edit box, means to omit that demand spectrum
      curve.

1. - Show
     Single Demand Spectrum (ARDS) (Variable Damping). Check
     the Show Single Demand Spectrum
     (Variable Damping) check box to display the demand spectrum
     as a single curve.
   - - Color.
       The default color for the single modified demand spectrum
       curve is yellow. Click the color box to display the Color form and change the color of
       the demand spectrum.

The family of demand spectra
and the single demand spectrum (variable damping) can be displayed at
the same time, or they can be displayed separately.

1. - Show
     Constant Period Lines At check box. Check the Show
     Constant Period Lines At check box to display lines of
     constant period. These lines appear as radial lines on the capacity
     spectrum plot. By default the program plots lines for T = .5,
     1, 1.5 and 2 seconds. The periods for any of the four curves can
     be changed by editing the value in one of the four associated
     edit boxes. A value of 0, or a blank edit box, means to omit that
     period line.
   - - Color. The default color for
       the period lines is gray. Click the color box to display the
       Color form and change the color
       of the period lines.
   - Reset
     Default Colors button. Click the Reset
     Default Colors button to reset all of the colors to the
     defaults.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Parameters for ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum form as follows:  Method 1 - This method can be used to specify parameters for displaying a pushover curve before a static nonlinear analysis has been run.   1. Click    the Define    menu > Pushover Parameter Sets > ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum    command to display the Define Pushover    Parameters for ATC40 Capacity Spectrum form. 2. Click    the Add New    Parameters button,    or select an existing parameter set definition and click the    Add Copy    of Parameters or    Modify/Show    Parameters button.   Method 2 - Use this method to display a pushover curve after an analysis has been run.   1. Define    a [nonlinear    static analysis](../../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) case whose Load    Application type is Displacement    Control and whose Results    Saved type is Multiple    States; [run    an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click    the Display    menu > Show Static Pushover Curve command to display    the Pushover Curve form. 3. Select    the ATC-40 Capacity Spectrum    option from the Plot Type    drop-down list. 4. Click    the Add New    Parameters, Add    Copy of Parameters, or Modify/Show    Parameters buttons.   Method 3 - Use this method to save the parameters specified for displaying a pushover curve as a Named Set for reuse in the future.   1. Define    a [nonlinear    static analysis](../../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) case whose Load    Application type is Displacement    Control and whose Results    Saved type is Multiple    States; [run    an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Click    the Define    menu > Named Sets > Pushover Named Sets command    to display the Define Pushover Named    Sets form. 3. Click    the Add New    Named Set button, or highlight a previously defined    Named Set and click the Add    Copy of Named Set or Modify/Show    Named Set button, to display the Pushover    Named Set Data form. 4. Select    the ATC-40 Capacity Spectrum    option from the Plot Type    drop-down list. 5. Click    the Add New    Parameters, Add    Copy of Parameters, or Modify/Show    Parameters buttons. |

# Parameters for Base Shear vs Monitored Displ Form

Use the Parameters for Base
Shear vs Monitored Displ form to specify the parameters for displaying
base shear versus monitored displacement pushover curves.

- Pushover
  Parameters Name edit box. The program will suggest a default
  name in this edit box. Use the suggested name or type a new name in
  the box.
- Base
  Shear vs Monitored Displacement Curve Color box. The color
  shown in this box will be used to display the curve. Click on the
  color to display the Color form and
  select a new color if desired.
- Reset
  Default Color button. Click this button to reset the display
  color for the curve to the program default.
- Units
  drop-down list. Use the units shown in this drop-down list or select
  other units from the list. These units will be used when the curve
  is displayed.
- Set
  Axis Data button. Click this button to access the [Override Axis Labels and Range form](Set_Axis_Labels_and_Range_Form.md). Use the options
  on that form to change the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical
  ranges and the axis labels for the curve.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Parameters for Base Shear vs Monitored Displ form as follows:  Method 1- This method can be used to specify parameters for displaying a pushover curve before a static nonlinear analysis has been run.   1. Click    the Define    menu > Pushover Parameter Sets > Force vs Displacement    command to display the Define Pushover    Parameters for Base Shear vs Displ form. 2. Click    the Add New    Parameters button,    or select an existing parameter set definition and click the    Add Copy    of Parameters or    Modify/Show    Parameters button.   Method 2 - Use this method to display a pushover curve after an analysis has been run.   1. # Parameters for FEMA 356 Coefficient Method Form

Use the Parameters for FEMA
356 Coefficient Method form to specify the parameters for displaying
pushover curves in accordance with FEMA 356 guidance.

- Name
  edit box. The program will suggest a default name. Use this name or
  type a new one in this edit box.
- Units
  drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the
  list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the pushover
  curve.
- Demand
  Spectrum Definition area
- - Effective Viscous Damping edit
    box. Use the default value or specify a revised value. The value
    must be greater than zero but less than one.
  - Defined Function option and
    drop-down list. Use this option to define the demand spectrum
    using a [defined
    function](../../Define/Functions/Response_Spectrum/Define_Response_Spectrum_Functions.md). Select the function from the drop-down list.
  - - Scale
      Factor edit box. Specify the scale factor, if any,
      to be applied to the function.
    - Characteristic
      Period of Resp Spec, Ts edit
      box. Specify the period where the response spectrum switches
      from constant acceleration to constant velocity.
  - FEMA 356 General Response Spectrum
    option. Use
    this option to define the demand spectrum using FEMA 356 General
    Response Spectrum.
  - - Mapped
      Spectral Accel at Short Period, Ss edit box. Use the
      default or specify another value for the spectral acceleration
      at short periods.
    - Mapped
      Spectral Accel at 1 Sec Period, S1 edit box. Use the
      default or specify another value for spectral acceleration
      at a one second period.
    - Site
      Class drop-down list. Select the classification for
      the site from the drop-down list. The classifications are
      as defined in FEMA 356.
- Selected
  Coefficients area
- - User
    Value for C2 option and edit box. Checking this check box
    will make the program use the user specified value of C2 entered
    in the edit box. If the check box is not checked, the program
    will automatically calculate the C2 value.
  - User
    Value for C3 option and edit box.  Checking this check
    box will make the program use the user specified value of C3 entered
    in the edit box. If the check box is not checked, the program
    will automatically calculate the C3 value.
  - User
    Value for Cm option and edit box.  Checking this check
    box will make the program use the user specified value of Cm entered
    in the edit box. If the check box is not checked, the program
    will automatically calculate the Cm value.
- Items
  Visible On Plot area

- - Show Capacity Curve check box.
    Checking this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the capacity curve is green. Click the
      color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Show Idealized Bilinear Force-Displ Curve check box. Checking
    this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the idealized bilinear force-displacement
      curve is green. Click the color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Reset Default Color button. Click this button
    to reset all of the display colors to the program default.
- Set
  Axis Labels and Range button. Click this button to access the
  [Override
  Axis Labels and Range form](Set_Axis_Labels_and_Range_Form.md). Use the options on that form
  to change the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical ranges and
  the axis labels for the curve.

# Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP Form

Use the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form to specify the parameters for displaying pushover curves in accordance with ASCE 41-13 NSP guidance.

- Name edit box. The program will suggest a default name. Use this name or type a new one in this edit box.
- Units drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the pushover curve.
- Demand Spectrum Definition area
- - Effective Viscous Damping edit box. Use the default value or specify a revised value. The value must be greater than zero but less than one.
  - Defined Function option and drop-down list. Use this option to define the demand spectrum using a [defined function](../../Define/Functions/Response_Spectrum/Define_Response_Spectrum_Functions.md). Select the function from the drop-down list.
  - - Scale Factor edit box. Specify the scale factor, if any, to be applied to the function.
    - Characteristic Period of Resp Spec, Ts edit box. Specify the period where the response spectrum switches from constant acceleration to constant velocity.
  - ASCE 7-10 General Response Spectrum option. Use this option to define the demand spectrum using ASCE 7-10 General Response Spectrum.
  - - Mapped Spectral Accel at Short Period, Ss edit box. Use the default or specify another value for the spectral acceleration at short periods.
    - Mapped Spectral Accel at 1 Sec Period, S1 edit box. Use the default or specify another value for spectral acceleration at a one second period.
    - Site Class drop-down list. Select the classification for the site from the drop-down list. The classifications are as defined in ASCE 7-10.
    - Long Period Transistion, Tl edit box.  Use the default or specify another value for the long-period transition period as defined in ASCE 7-10.
- Include Soil-Structure Interaction Effects check box.  Checking this box will add soil-structure interaction effects to the plot and will also enable the Modify/Show SSI button. Click that button to display the [ASCE 41-13 Soil-Structure Interaction form](FEMA_440_Soil-Structure_Interaction_Form.md). Use the options on that form to specify the Kinematic effects and foundation damping parameters for the SSI interaction effects.
- Selected Coefficients area
- - User Value for C2 option and edit box. Checking this check box will make the program use the user specified value of C2 entered in the edit box. If the check box is not checked, the program will automatically calculate the C2 value.
  - User Value for Cm option and edit box.  Checking this check box will make the program use the user specified value of Cm entered in the edit box. If the check box is not checked, the program will automatically calculate the Cm value.
- Items Visible On Plot area

  - Show Capacity Curve check box. Checking this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
- - - Color. The default color for the capacity curve is green. Click the color box to display the Color form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Show Idealized Bilinear Force-Displ Curve check box. Checking this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
  - - Color. The default color for the idealized bilinear force-displacement curve is green. Click the color box to display the Color form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Reset Default Color button. Click this button to reset all of the display colors to the program default.
- Set Axis Labels and Range button. Click this button to access the [Override Axis Labels and Range form](Set_Axis_Labels_and_Range_Form.md). Use the options on that form to change the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical ranges and the axis labels for the curve.

# Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization Form

Additional forms:  FEMA 440 Coefficients for Beff,
FEMA 440 Coefficients for Teff

Use the Parameters for FEMA
440 Equivalent Linearization form to specify the parameters for
displaying pushover curves in accordance with FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization
guidance.

- Name
  edit box. The program will suggest a default name. Use this name or
  type a new one in this edit box.
- Units
  drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the
  list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the pushover
  curve.
- Plot
  Axes area. Choose the plot axes as Sa-Sd
  (spectral acceleration vs spectral displacement), Sa-T
  (spectral acceleration vs period) or Sd-T
  (spectral displacement vs period).
- Set
  Axis Data button. Click this button to access the [Override Axis Labels and Range form](Set_Axis_Labels_and_Range_Form.md). Use the options
  on that form to change the minimum and maximum horizontal and vertical
  ranges and the axis labels for the curve.
- Demand
  Spectrum Definition. Choose to define the demand spectrum based
  on a function or user specified coefficients.
- - Function
    option, drop-down list, and SF
    (Scale Factor) edit box. When this option is selected, choose
    a previously [defined
    spectrum function](../../Define/Functions/Response_Spectrum/Define_Response_Spectrum_Functions.md) from the drop-down list and use the default
    scale factor or use the edit box to specify the SF.
  - Use
    Coeff and Ca and
    Cv (Seismic Coefficient)
    edit boxes. The shape of the demand spectrum with 5% damping is
    controlled by the values input in the Ca
    and Cv (Seismic Coefficient)
    edit boxes. Refer to ATC-40, Chapter 4, for an explanation of,
    and appropriate values for, Ca and Cv. The default value for both
    Ca and Cv is 0.4. Demand spectra for other damping levels are
    created from the 5% damped spectrum using the spectral reduction
    factors described in Section 8.2.2.1.1 of ATC-40.
  - Include
    Soil-Structure Interaction Effects check box.  Checking
    this box will add soil-structure interaction effects to the plot
    and will also enable the Modify/Show SSI button. Click that button to display the
    [FEMA
    440 Soil-Structure Interaction form](FEMA_440_Soil-Structure_Interaction_Form.md). Use the options
    on that form to specify the Kinematic effects and foundation damping
    parameters for the SSI interaction effects.
- Damping
  and Period Parameters Definition.
- - Inherent + Additional Damping
    edit box. In the Damping Parameters
    area, type a value in the Inherent/Additional
    Damping edit box. The value input into this box must be
    between 0 and 1, inclusively. The default value is 0.05. Referring
    to ATC-40 equation 8-8, the b0 term is automatically included
    by the SAP2000 analysis method, and the 5% inherent viscous damping
    term can be specified in the Inherent/Additional
    Damping edit box as 0.05. If additional viscous damping
    is provided in the structure, perhaps by viscous dampers that
    are not specifically included in the model, this damping should
    also be included in the Inherent
    + Additional Damping edit box. Thus if the damping inherent
    in the structure is assumed to be 5% of critical damping, and
    dampers that provide an additional 7% of critical damping are
    assumed to be added to the structure (although they are not actually
    in the model), the value input in the Inherent
    + Additional Damping edit box should be 0.12, since 0.05
    + 0.07 = 0.12.
  - User Defined Effective Damping, Beff. Checking this check box and clicking
    the Modify/Show button will display
    the FEMA 440 Coefficients for Beff
    form. Use that form to specify the effective damping coefficients.
  - User Defined Effective Period, Teff.
    Checking this check box and clicking the Modify/Show
    button will display the FEMA 440 Coefficients
    for Teff form. Use that form to specify the effective period
    coefficients.
- Items
  Visible On Plot area. Choose the items to be displayed on the
  plot.
- - Show Capacity Curve check box.
    Checking this check box will show the capacity curve on the plot.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the capacity curve is green. Click the
      color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the capacity curve.
  - Show Family of Demand Spectra (MADRS) check box. Checking this check box
    overlays a family of demand spectra on the capacity curve in the
    ADRS format.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the family of demand spectra curves
      is red. Click the color box to display the Color
      form and change the color of the demand spectra.
    - Ductility
      Ratios. The family of curves can include up to four
      demand spectrum curves, each with a different ductility. By
      default the program plots curves with ductilities of 1, 1.5,
      2 and 2.5. The ductility ratios for any of the four curves
      can be changed by editing the values in one of the Ductility
      Ratio edit boxes.
  - Show
    Single Demand Spectrum (MADRS) (Variable Damping). Check
    the Show Single Demand Spectrum
    (Variable Damping) check box to display the demand spectrum
    as a single curve.
  - - Color.
      The default color for the single modified demand spectrum
      curve is yellow. Click the color box to display the Color form and change the color of
      the demand spectrum.

The family of demand spectra
and the single demand spectrum (variable damping) can be displayed at
the same time, or they can be displayed separately.

- Show
  Constant Period Lines At check box. Check the Show
  Constant Period Lines At check box to display lines of constant
  period. These lines appear as radial lines on the capacity spectrum
  plot. By default the program plots lines for T = .5, 1, 1.5 and 2
  seconds. The periods for any of the four curves can be changed by
  editing the value in one of the four associated edit boxes. A value
  of 0, or a blank edit box, means to omit that period line.
- - Color. The default color for the
    period lines is gray. Click the color box adjacent to display
    the Color form and change the color
    of the period lines.
- Reset
  Default Colors button. Click the Reset
  Default Colors button to reset all of the colors to the defaults.

|  |

# Pushover Curve Form

Use the Pushover
Curve form to specify the pushover curve to be displayed and to
save those settings to a Named Set for quick reuse in the future.

- Static
  Nonlinear Case drop-down list. Select the Static Nonlinear
  Case for which a pushover curve is to be displayed.
- Plot
  Type drop-down list. Select the type of plot to be plotted.
- Units
  drop-down list. Use the units shown or select others from the drop-down
  list. The selected units will be used on the plot.
- Graphical
  Display Area. The pushover
  curve is plotted in this area of the form.
- Current
  Plot Parameters drop-down list. Choose the parameters to be
  applied to the pushover display. The parameters are specified and
  given names using the individual forms listed below.
- Add
  New Parameters button. When this button is clicked, one of
  the following forms will display, depending on the type of plot selected;
  the form will display default parameters unless others have been specified
  by the user. Use the form to modify the default parameters for displaying
  the pushover curve.
- - When Resultant
    Base Shear vs Monitored Displacement is selected as the
    Plot Type, the [Parameters for Base Shear vs Monitored Displ
    form](Parameters_for_Base_Shear_vs_Monitored_Displ_Form.md) will display.
  - When ATC-40
    Capacity Spectrum is selected as the Plot
    Type, the [Parameters for ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum
    form](Parameters_for_ATC_40_Capacity_Spectrum_Form.md) will display.
  - When FEMA 356 Coefficient
    Method is selected as the Plot
    Type, the [Parameters for FEMA 356 Coefficient Method
    form](Parameters_for_FEMA_356_Coefficient_Method_Form.md) will display.
  - When FEMA 440 Equivalent
    Linearization is selected as the Plot
    Type, the [Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization
    form](Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Equivalent_Linearization_Form.md) will display.
  - When ASCE 41-13
    NSP is selected as the Plot
    Type, the [Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form](Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Displacement_Modification_Form.md)
    will display.
- Add
  Copy of Parameters button. Click this button to add a copy
  of the previously defined display parameters to the model. When this
  button is clicked, one of the forms listed above will display, depending
  on the Plot Type selected.
  The option adds another set of parameters to the model.
- Modify/Show
  Parameters button. Click this button to display one of the
  forms listed above, depending on the Plot
  Type selected. Use the forms to modify the parameters without
  adding another set of parameters to the model.

Additional information
will appear on the form depending on the Plot
Type selected. Follow the hyperlinks for the individual form topics
(above) for more information.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Command | Function |
| File menu > |  |
| Print Setup for Graphics | Use this command to access the print set up form of the printer connected to the computer displaying the hinge results. |
| Use Color Printer | This is a toggle. When a check mark precedes this command, the command is enabled and the graphic can be printed in color assuming that the printing device prints in color. |
| Print Graphics | Immediately sends the plot to the printer. |
| Display Tables | Displays the Table Display form. That form shows the hinge data in tabular format. Use the File menu commands on that form to export the hinge data to Excel or Access. Use the commands on the Edit menu to apply or remove filtering and sorting criteria for the data on the Table Display form. |
| Capture Picture> |  |
| Entire Screen | Creates a .bmp file of the entire screen showing the hinge plot. |
| Form Including Title Bar | Creates a .bmp file of the active window, plus the title bar. |
| Form Without Title Bar | Creates a .bmp file of the active window without the title bar. |
| Save Named Set | Use this command to access the Pushover Named Set form. Use that form to specify a name for the options/settings that have been applied to display the pushover curve plot. The Named Set can then be opened to quickly reapply the options/settings to display another pushover curve. The Pushover Named Set form can also be used to change the name of the Named Set, or to delete a Named Set. |
| Open Named Set | Use this command to display the Select Pushover Named Set form. Use the form to select a Named Set and apply the setting to the display of a pushover curve. |

Static Analysis](../../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md)

Frame/Cable Hinges (Pushover)](../../Assign/Frame/Hinges/Frame_Hinges.md)

Click    the Display    menu > Show Static Pushover Curve command or the    Define menu    > Named Sets > Nonlinear Static Curves command. |
