# Set Axis Labels and Range Form

Use the Set Axis Labels And
Range form to change the labels and ranges used on pushover curves.

- Specify the horizontal
  axis range for the curve display by typing values in the Min and Max
  edit boxes in the Horizontal Range
  area.
- Specify the vertical
  axis range for the curve display by typing values in the Min and Max
  edit boxes in the Vertical Range
  area.
- Use the default labels
  for the horizontal and vertical axis, or type new labels in the appropriate
  edit boxes in the Axis Labels
  area.
- Use the edit box in
  the Additional Notes for Printed
  Graphical Output area to add notes to the curve display. The
  notes will only appear when the curve is printed as graphical output
  to a printer or file.
- Use the units shown
  in the Units drop-down list
  or select other units to be used on this form.
- Use the Reset
  Defaults button to restore all values or suggested text to
  the program defaults.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Set Axis Labels Ranges form as follows:  Method 1 - This method can be used to specify parameters for displaying a pushover curve before a static nonlinear analysis has been run.   1. Click    the Define    menu > Pushover Parameters Sets command to display    a submenu of commands:  Force    vs Displacement, ATC    40 Capacity Spectrum, FEMA    356 Coefficient Method, FEMA    440 Equivalent Linearization, ASCE    41-13 NSP. Select one of the subcommands to display    the Define Pushover Parameters for    {Parameter} form; the name of the form depends on the    command used. 2. Click    the Add New    Parameters button, or highlight a previously defined    pushover parameter and click the  Add    Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show    Parameters button, to display the [Parameters for Base Shear vs Monitored Displ    form](Parameters_for_Base_Shear_vs_Monitored_Displ_Form.md), the [Parameters for ATC 40 Capacity Spectrum    form](Parameters_for_ATC_40_Capacity_Spectrum_Form.md), the [Parameters for FEMA 356 Coefficient Method    form](Parameters_for_FEMA_356_Coefficient_Method_Form.md), the [Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization    form](Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Equivalent_Linearization_Form.md), or the  [Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form](Parameters_for_FEMA_440_Displacement_Modification_Form.md),    depending on the command selected in Step 1. 3. # Spectra Comparison for Soil-Structure Interaction Effects Form

Use the Spectra Comparison for Soil-Structure Interaction Effects form to generate demand spectrum plots of free field motion, free field motion reduced for soil-structure interaction kinematic effects, and free field motion reduced for soil-structure interaction kinematic effects and foundation damping. The demand spectrum curves can be plotted as spectral displacement vs. spectral acceleration, period vs. spectral acceleration, or period vs. spectral displacement.

- Plot Type options. Choose the axes for the plot:  Sa-Sd (spectral acceleration vs spectral displacement), Sa-T (spectral acceleration vs period) or Sd-T (spectral displacement vs period). Spectral acceleration vs spectral displacement is the default.
- Items Visible On Plot area. Choose the items to be displayed on the plot. In some cases (e.g., when the items to be displayed occupy the same location on the plot),  it may be necessary to deselect an option so that other options become visible.

- Show Free Field Motion option and color box. The default color for the free field motion is red. Click the color box to display the Color form and select another color if desired.
- Show Kinematic Effects option and color box. The default color for the kinematic effects only is green. Click the color box to display the Color form and select another color if desired.
- Show Kinematic and Fnd Damping Effects option and color box. The default color for display kinematic effects and foundation damping is yellow. Click the color box to display the Color form and select another color if desired.

- Display area. The display area will show the plot using the selected axes. The Horiz and Vert display boxes will show the mouse pointer location if the mouse is moved over the plot.
- Units drop-down list. Use the units displayed or select another from the list; the units displayed will be used on the plot of the soil-structure interaction effects curve.
- Reset Defaults button. Clicking this button will return all options on the form to program defaults.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Spectra Comparison for Soil-Structure Interaction Effects form as follows:   1. Define a [nonlinear static analysis](../../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) case whose Load Application type is Displacement Control and whose Results Saved type is Multiple States; [run an analysis](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md). 2. Choose Method a, b, or c to specify the display for a pushover curve, define parameters for it, or save the options as a Named Set, respectively:     1. Click the Display menu > Show Pushover Curve command to display the Pushover Curve form. Select ASCE 41-13 NSP or FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization for the Plot Type, and click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing curve and click the  Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form or the Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization form.    2. Click the Define menu > Pushover Parameter Sets > ASCE 41-13 NSP command or the Define menu > Pushover Parameter Sets > FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization command to display the Define Pushover Parameters for FEMA 440 Displ Mod or the Define Pushover Parameters for FEMA 400 Eq Linear form; then click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing parameter set definition and click the Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form or the Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization form, respectively.    3. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Pushover Named Sets command to display the Define Pushover Named Sets form. Then click the Add New Named Set button, or highlight a previously defined Named Set and click the Add Copy of Named Set or Modify/Show Named Set button, to display the Pushover Named Set Data form. On that form select ASCE 41-13 NSP or FEMA 440 Linearization for the Plot Type, and click the Add New Parameters button, or select an existing named set and click the Add Copy of Parameters or Modify/Show Parameters button, to display the Parameters for ASCE 41-13 NSP form or the Parameters for FEMA 440 Equivalent Linearization form.  3. Check the Include Soil-Structure Interaction Effects check box and then click the Modify/Show SSI button to display the FEMA 440 Soil-Structure Interaction form. 4. Click the Show Spectra Comparison For SSI Effects button. |

# Undeformed Shape

Clicking the Display menu > Show Undeformed Shape command, the Show Undeformed Shape button, ![](../../assets/images/Images/Undeformed%20Shape%20Button.GIF), or the F4 function key does the following:

- If a model is being created, it clears the display of any assignments that are showing on the model. It essentially functions the same as the [Assign menu > Clear Display of Assigns command](../Assign/Clear_Display_of_Assigns.md) in such cases.

- If the on-screen display shows any type of results plotted on a model (e.g., a [Deformed Shape](Show_Deformed_Shape.md)),  it clears the display of the results and returns the view to an undeformed shape view.

Note that this command only affects the active window.

<!-- source: Menus/Display/Show_Virtual_Work_Diagram.htm | Show Virtual Work Diagram -->

# Virtual Work Diagram

Virtual work diagrams display the percentage of virtual work of an element relative to the balance of the structural members. It can be used to reduce structural deflection by indicating which elements have the highest percentage of energy and thus will most affect the deflection if their stiffnesses were to be modified.

1. Run an analysis.
2. Click the Display menu > Show Virtual Work Diagram command to access the [Virtual Work Diagram form](Virtual_Work_Diagram_Form.md).
3. On that form, select the Forces  and Displacements load cases, and the Value Type to be displayed.
4. Click the OK button to display the percentage of energy the element is experiencing relative to the other elements in the structure.

Example:  If the user is interested in reducing the roof story drift resulting from a wind load, a [wind load pattern](../Define/Load_Pattern/Wind_Load_Pattern_Form.md) is selected for the Force. For Displacement, a [load pattern](../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) is used that has lateral forces only at the roof level even though the real displacement is caused by a distributed wind load. The structure is then displayed with the percentage of virtual work energy that the element is experiencing from the stresses induced by the Force load pattern and the displacement from the Displacement load pattern. Essentially, this means that when the stiffness of an element with a higher percentage is modified, the deflection of the structure is more affected than if the stiffness of a lower percentage element is modified.

## Show Values

When this check box is checked, the display of the virtual work diagram will be include numerical values for the virtual work of the structure.

## Saved Named Set

Use this button to save the settings specified on this form as a Named Set.

- 1. Click the Saved Named Set button to access the Virtual Work Named Set form.
  2. Type a name in the Virtual Work Set edit box.
  3. Click the Add New VW Set button to save a [Virtual Work Named Set](../Define/Named_Sets.md) that can be recalled and applied to display a virtual work diagram.

Use the Change VW Set Name button to change the name of a Named Set.

1. Highlight the name of the Named Set to be changed.
2. Type a new name in the edit box
3. Click the Change VW Set Name button to change the name.

Use the Delete VW Set button to delete a Named Set.

1. Highlight the name of the Named Set to be deleted.
2. Click the Delete VW Set button to delete the selected Named Set.

## Show Named Set

Use the Show Named Set button to apply a previously defined Named Set to display a virtual work diagram.

- 1. Click the Show Named Set button to access the Select Virtual Work Named Set form.
  2. Highlight the name of the Named Set in the Select display area.
  3. Click the OK button to apply the Named Set to the display of the virtual work diagram.

# Step-by-Step Hinge Formation

Review the pushover hinge formation on a step-by-step basis as follows:

1. Click the Display menu > Show Deformed Shape command to display the [Deformed Shape form](Show_Deformed_Shape.md).
2. Select a [pushover case (i.e., static nonlinear)](../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) from the Case/Combo Name drop-down list.
3. Click the arrow keys in the status bar at the bottom of the SAP2000 window to step through the sequence of hinge formations.

# Step-by-Step Pushover Forces

Review the pushover forces on a step-by-step basis as follows

1. Click the Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Frame/Cable/Tendon command to access the [Member Force Diagrams for Frames form](Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Frames_Cables_Tendons.md).
2. Select a [pushover case (i.e., static nonlinear)](../Define/Load_Cases/Static/Nonlinear/Nonlinear_Static_Form.md) from the Case/Combo Name drop-down list.

5. Click the arrow keys in the status bar at the bottom of the SAP2000 window to step through the sequence of member forces.

# Virtual Work Diagram Form

Additional Forms:  Virtual Work Named Sets, Select Virtual Work Named Set

Use the options on the Virtual Work Diagram form to select the force, the displacement and the values for displaying the percentage of virtual work of an element relative to the balance of the structural members.

- Forces drop-down list. Select the load pattern for the force to be displayed.
- Displacements drop-down list. Select the load pattern for the displacement to be displayed. This is usually a load pattern that has forces at the location and in the direction of the displacement of interest.
- Value Type options. Select to display values as Relative or Absolute.
- Show Value check box. When this check box is checked, the display will include a numerical value for the element’s percentage of relative energy shown as well as color-coding for the element.
- Save Named Set button. With the Forces, Displacements, and Value Type set as required, click this button to access the Virtual Work Named Sets form and save the settings as a Named Set.
- - Save Named Set button. Type a name in the Virtual Work Set edit box to name the set of values specified and then click this button to save the Named Set.
  - Change VW Set Name button. If the name of a previously Named Set needs to be modified, select the Named Set in the Virtual Work Set display area; type a new named in the Virtual Work Set edit box and click the Change VW Set Name button.
  - Delete VW Set button. If a previously specified Named Set needs to be deleted, select the Named Set in the Virtual Work Set display area and click the Delete VW Set button.
- Show Named Set button. The Show Named Set button will be available only if a Named Set has been saved. Click this button to access the Select Virtual Work Named Set form. Highlight the Named Set to be displayed. Click the OK button. The value settings stored in the Named Set will be applied to the active display window.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Virtual Work Diagram form as follows:    Method 1:   1. Click the Define menu > Named Sets > Virtual Work command.   Method 2:   1. Define a [load case](../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) (or use the default DEAD or MODAL case) and [run an analysis](../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) 2. Click the Display menu > Show Virtual Work Diagram command. |

# Walking Vibration Analysis Form

The Walking Vibration Analysis Form enables the visualization of the floor vibration analysis results, specifically for the Excitation Sets marked with analysis type: walking.

The **Design Method** denotes thedesign code or methodology implemented.

## Method: **AISC Design Guide 11**

1. **Floor Occupancy Type** denotes the occupancy usage of the floor being analyzed. The available categories include: residences, offices, and shopping malls.
2. For the **Pedestrian Bodyweight,** a value of 168 lb is recommended.
3. **Equivalent Viscous Damping.** To ensure consistency, this damping value is taken from the modal damping used in the Excitation Set's steady-state load case. To convert from modal damping to viscous damping ratio, the following equivalence is used:

*d*
*k*
*(
ω
) =2
ζ*

where 

![](../../assets/images/image3.png) is the value specified as the stiffness proportional coefficient in the modal damping, and *ζ* is the equivalent viscous damping ratio.

- The **Analysis Summary** Table provides a summary of the calculations. Each Excitation Set may have two associated rows in the table: one to display the results related to the low frequencies, and another for the higher frequencies.

- - **Max FRF and Dominant Frequency:**The maximum value of the FRF plot, and the frequency at which such value is measured.
  - **DCR:** The design/capacity ratio, a comparison of the predicted peak sinusoidal acceleration and how it compares to the recommended limits for human comfort.
- The **Additional Details** panel provides the user with more information related to the calculations. The details are updated according to the selected row in the **Analysis Summary** Table.

- - **Modal Data:** The natural frequencies and periods of the current model, and the modal displacements of the Excitation and Response Joints in Z-GLOBAL direction.
  - **Frequency Response Function (FRF):** A plot of the acceleration measured at the Response Joint due to the loads applied (through the steady-state load case) at the Excitation Joint.
  - **Comfort Limit Plot:** A plot that displays predicted acceleration values alongside recommended human comfort limits. In this plot, the predicted acceleration is represented by a point, and the comfort limit by a line. If all the points fall below the comfort line, the predicted accelerations are unlikely to cause human discomfort.

For more information on Floor Vibration Analysis in Steel-Framed Structures, refer to the the Technical Note on*Floor Vibration Analysis*.

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Curved_Frames_and_Cables/Cable_Geometry_Form.htm | Cable Geometry Form -->

# Cable Geometry Form

Use the Cable Geometry form to refine the parabolic alignment of a cable.

- Line Object Type drop-down list. This drop-down list displays that the currently selected line object is a cable.

- Cable Type drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to select the type of cable (minimum tension at End I or at End J, tension at I-End, tension at J-End, horizontal tension component, maximum vertical sag, low-point vertical sag, undeformed length).
- Section Property drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to choose a [section property](../../Define/Section_Properties/Cable_Sections/Cable_Section_Data_Form.md) for the cable.
- Start X, Y, Z and End X, Y, Z  display boxes. These display boxes show the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the beginning and end of the cable.
- Number of Linear Segments edit box. Use this edit box to specify the number of segments used to define the cable.
- Added Weight Per Unit Length edit box. Use this edit box to specify additional weight for each length of the segment.
- Projected Uniform Gravity Load edit box. Use this edit box to specify the projected uniform gravity load for the cable.
- Tension at I-End edit/display box. When Tension at I-End is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box.  When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Tension at J-End edit/display box. When Tension at J-End is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box. When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Horizontal Tension Component edit/display box. When Horizontal Tension Component is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box. When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Maximum Vertical Sag edit/display box. When Maximum Vertical Sag is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box. When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Low-Point Vertical Sag edit/display box. When Low-Point Vertical Sag is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box. When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Length edit/display box. When the Cable - Length option is selected for the Curve/Cable Type, the default value can be changed by typing a new value in this edit box. When other curve/cable types are chosen, the value in this display box cannot be edited.
- Keep as Single Object option. Use this option to treat the cable as a single line object during analysis.
- Break into Multiple Equal Length Line Objects option Use this option to treat the cable as being comprised of multiple line objects during analysis.
- Break into Multiple Line Objects with Equal Projected Length on Chord option Use this option to treat the cable as being comprised of multiple line objects of equal length as projected on the chord during analysis.
- Coordinate System drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select a coordinate system other than global if one has been defined (see [Define Coordinate Systems/Grids](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Coordinate_Systems_Grid.md) for more information about defining a coordinate system).
- Units drop-down list. Use the existing units or use the drop-down list to select revised units for working with the data on the form.
- Refresh button and the Computed Point Coordinates for Linear Segments (Undeformed/Deformed Cable Geometry) spreadsheet. Click the Refresh button to update the Computed Point Coordinate for Linear Segments (Undeformed/Deformed Cable Geometry) spreadsheet area after making selections or changes in the other areas of the form. The cells in this spreadsheet cannot be edited directly.
- Use Undeformed Geometry for Cable Object and the Use Deformed Geometry for Cable Object options. Use these options to change the display in the spreadsheet to show the undeformed or deformed values for coordinates, sag, distance and relative distribution of the points defining the cable.

## See Also

[Curved Frame Geometry](Curved_Frame_Geometry_Form.md)

| --- |
| Access the  Cable Geometry form as follows:  Method 1:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon Element button  to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Cable from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click on a grid intersection in the active view to specify the beginning point of the cable. Click on a second grid intersection to specify the end point of the cable. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Cable Geometry form.   Method 2:   1. Select a frame object that has been drawn as a cable object. 2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Edit Cable Geometry command.   Method 3:   1. # Curved Frame Geometry Form

Use the  Curved Frame Geometry form to refine the parabolic alignment of a curved frame.

Curved Frame

- Line Object Type drop-down list. This drop-down list displays the currently selected line object type. The drop-down list can be used to change line object from a curved frame to a straight frame.

- Curve Type drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to select the type of curved frame (circular or parabolic), and how the curve is to be defined, by specifying a 3rd point ID, by specifying the coordinates of a 3rd point, or by defining a planar point and radius.
- Section Property drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to choose a [section property](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md) for the curved frame.
- Start X, Y, Z  and End X, Y, Z  display boxes. These display boxes show the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the beginning  and end of the curved frame.
- 3rd Point ID drop-down list. This option is available when a 3rd Point ID option has been selected in the Curve/Cable Type drop-down list. Select the ID of the third point used to define the curved frame.
- 3rd Point X, Y, Z edit box. These edit boxes are available when a 3rd Point Coords option has been selected in the Curve/Cable Type drop-down list. Use these edit boxes to specify the coordinates of the third point used to define the curved frame.
- Number of Linear Segments edit box. Use this edit box to specify the number of segments used to define the curved frame.
- Radius edit box. This edit box is available when a Planar Point & Radius option has been selected in the Curve/Cable Type drop-down list. Use the edit box to specify the radius for the curved frame.
- Curve length display box. This display box shows the length of the curved frame as specified  when the beginning and ending of the curved frame was defined, as described in Step 3 of Method 1 above.
- Refresh button and Computed Point Coordinates for Linear Segments spreadsheet. Click the Refresh button to update the Computed Point Coordinate for Linear Segments spreadsheet area after making selections or changes in the other areas of the form. The cells in this spreadsheet cannot be edited directly if Method 1 or 2 above was used to access the form. To use this spreadsheet to directly change the linear segments, use Method 3 to access the Curved Frame Geometry form.
- T/C Limits button. Click this button to display the [Frame T/C Limits form](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Tension_Compression_Limits.md). Use the form to specify tension and compression limits.
- Units drop-down list. Use the existing units or use the drop-down list to select revised units for working with the data on the form.
- Coordinate System drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select a coordinate system other than global if one has been defined (see [Define Coordinate Systems/Grids](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Coordinate_Systems_Grid.md) for more information about defining a coordinate system).
- Keep as Single Line Object option. Use this option to treat the curved frame as a single line object during analysis.
- Break into Multiple Line Objects option Use this option to treat the curved frame as being comprised of multiple line objects during analysis.

# Draw 1 Joint Link

Use the following method to add a joint link when the model is displayed in a 2-D View:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 2-D View command](../View/Set_2-D_View.md) to set the active window to select the plane in which the joint link is to be added.
3. Click the Draw menu > Draw 1 Joint Link command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to specify the [Link Property](../Define/Section_Properties/Link_Support_Properties/Define_Link_Support_Properties.md) and any offsets (X, Y, or Z).
4. Click on a grid intersection or any other point in that plane to add a joint link.

Use the following method to add a joint link when the model is displayed in a 3-D View:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Click the Draw menu > Draw 1 Joint Link command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to specify the [Link Property](../Define/Section_Properties/Link_Support_Properties/Define_Link_Support_Properties.md) and any offsets (X, Y, or Z).
3. In the 3-D view, click on a grid intersection to add a joint link.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem O](../../Example_Problems/Problem_O.md) and [Problem Q](../../Example_Problems/Problem_Q.md).

# Draw 2 Joint Link

Use the following method to draw a 2 joint link when the model is displayed in a 2-D View:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 2-D View](../View/Set_2-D_View.md) command to set the active window to select the plane in which the joint is to be added.
3. Click the Draw menu > Draw 2 Joint Link Element command to display the Properties of Object form and to switch to drawing a frame object between 2 points. Use the form to specify the [Link Property](../Define/Section_Properties/Link_Support_Properties/Define_Link_Support_Properties.md), plane offset, and drawing controls.
4. Click on a grid intersection, a previously defined joint or any point in the plane. Click again on another point to add a single link object. Every subsequent click will add another link object unless a double click on the same joint is performed or the Enter key is pressed. Pressing the ESC key will also terminate the sequential drawing mode and enable Select mode.

Use the following method to draw a 2 joint link when the model is displayed in a 3-D View:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Click the Draw menu > Draw 2 Joint Link Element command to display the Properties of Object form and to switch to drawing a link object between 2 points. Use the form to specify the [Link Property](../Define/Section_Properties/Link_Support_Properties/Define_Link_Support_Properties.md), plane offset, and drawing controls.
3. In the 3-D view, click on a grid intersection or a previously defined joint (a small red ball appears to confirm that the joint has been selected).
4. Click on another grid intersection or a joint to add a link object. Every subsequent click on a selected point will add another link object unless a double click on the same joint is performed or the Enter key is pressed. Pressing the ESC key will also terminate the sequential drawing mode and enable Select mode.

Note: It is not possible to draw a frame object between any two arbitrary points in space in the 3-D view.

## See Also

# Draw Developed Elevation Definition

Form:  Named Displays and Views

Use the Draw menu > Draw Developed Elevation Definition command to define a developed elevation graphically.

1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Developed Elevation Definition to initiate the definition. This will change the active window into an X-Y plane view.
2. Click the left mouse button at a point representing the beginning point for the developed elevation. Continue selecting points to define the location of the developed elevation.
3. Double left mouse click on the last point to end drawing of the developed elevation.
4. Type a name for the developed elevation into the Named Displays edit box.
5. Click the Add New Named Display button. The name typed in the edit box will appear in the list.

   - Change Named Display Name button. Highlight the name of the named display to be changed. Type a new name in the edit box and then click this button to change the name.
   - Delete Named Display button. Highlight the name of the named display to be deleted. Then click this button to delete the named display.
6. Click the OK button. The active window will show the newly defined named display.

Use the [Display menu > Show Named Display command](../Display/Show_Named_Display.md) to display the developed elevation.

## See Also

[Show Named View](../Display/Show_Named_View.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Draw_Edit_General_Reference_Line.htm | Draw Edit General Reference Line -->

# Draw/Edit General Reference Line

Form:
 General Reference Lines, Draw General Reference
Line Plan Projection, Edit General Reference Line, Define Curve at Gen
Ref Line Point

Use the Draw menu > Draw/Edit
General Reference Line command to display the General
Reference Lines form and add, change or delete a general reference
line. Objects can be [extruded](../Edit/Extrude.md) relative
to a general reference line.

1. Click
   the Draw menu > Draw/Edit General Reference
   Line command to display the General
   Reference Lines form.
2. Use
   the following buttons to complete the appropriate action:

- Add
  New Gen Ref Line Name button.
- 1. Type a name for
     a general reference line in the Gen
     Ref Lines edit box at the top of the display list.
  2. Click the Add New Gen Ref Line Name button. The newly
     specified name will appear in the display list.
  3. If it is not already
     highlighted, highlight the newly specified general reference line
     name by clicking on it in the display list.
  4. Click the Draw Selected Gen Ref Line button to display
     the Draw General Reference Line Plan Projection
     form and draw the general reference line.

Note:
 Similar to the Properties of Object
forms that appear when other objects are drawn in SAP2000, the Draw
General Reference Line Plan Projection and Edit
General Reference Line forms "float" over the display
in the active window. As necessary, move the forms out of the drawing
area by clicking on the blue title of the form and dragging the form to
the desired location.

The items on the Draw General Reference Line Plan Projection
include the following:

1. 1. - Gen
        Ref Line Name display box. The name of the general
        reference line as specified on the General
        Reference Lines form appears in this display box.
      - Ref
        Line Coord Sys display box.
        The general reference line coordinate system is the coordinate
        system that was active when the general reference line was
        first defined (i.e., the first time the Draw
        menu > Draw/Edit General Reference Line command
        was used to define the general reference line). This coordinate
        system cannot be changed by the user.
      - Color
        display box. The color shown in this display box will be used
        to display the general reference line as it is being drawn.
        Click on this box to display the Color
        form and change the display color.
      - Maximum
        Segment Length edit box. Use this edit box to specify
        the maximum length of the segments used to define any curves
        in the general reference line. The shorter the segment lengths,
        the smoother the curve.
      - Maximum
        Subtended Angle edit box. This edit box can be used
        to specify a maximum angle in degrees when a circular alignment
        for the general reference line is required. The length of
        the segments used to define the general reference line will
        be based on this angle. The smaller the angle, the smoother
        the curve.
      - Visible
        Plan check box. When this check box is checked, the
        general reference line will be visible in any windows displaying
        the model. When the check box is unchecked, the general reference
        line will not be shown in any windows displaying the model.
   5. After setting the
      above parameters, draw the reference line as follows:

      1. Click the mouse
         button anywhere in the active window to specify the beginning
         of the general reference line.
      2. Move the mouse
         pointer to the next point along the general reference line
         and again click the mouse button. Continue this process until
         the general reference line has the desired alignment. Note
         that the general reference line cannot intersect/cross itself.
      3. Double click
         on the last point or click the OK
         button to exit the drawing mode. The window will refresh and
         the Edit General Reference Line
         form will automatically appear. The
         options available on the Edit
         General Reference Line form
         are the same as those on the Draw
         General Reference Line Plan Projection form,
         with the following additions:

1. 1. 1. - Display
           Control
         - - Show Plan check
             box. When this check box is checked, the program will
             display the general reference line on a plan view
             of the model.
           - Show Developed Elevation
             check box. When this check box is checked, the program
             will display the general reference line on a developed
             elevation view of the model.
   1. 4. With the Edit
         General Reference Line form displayed,

         1. Click
            on a point along the general reference line (not
            the line itself) to display a drop-down menu of commands,
            including the following:

Note:
As necessary, use the other options described in this topic  (see
below) to add points to the general reference line before using these
commands.

1. 1. 5. 1. - Define
              Curve at Point option. Use this option to display
              the Define Curve at Gen Ref
              Line Point form. Use the form to select a Curve Type (select
              an option from the drop-down list) and specify the
              associated curve parameters, which vary depending
              on the type of curve selected.
            - Move
              Point option. Use this option to display the
              Move form. Specify a
              Move Option:
            - - Move by Specified Distance
                option. When this option is selected, specify
                the distance to move the selected point by entering
                a distance value, as measured from the start of
                the general reference line, in the Delta
                X/S and Delta
                Y/Z edit boxes.
              - Move to Specified Coords
                option. When this option is selected, specify
                the values to Change
                Coordinates To in the X/S
                and Y/Z
                edit boxes.

Note:
 The [Reshape mode](Set_Reshape_Element_Mode.md) also
can be used to move points on the general reference line.

- 1. 5. 1. - Add
             Adjacent Points. Both
             of the following options will display the Divide Selected Segments form. Use the form to
             specify the number of objects into which the segment
             of the general reference line is to be divided. Type
             in the ratio of the last object to the first, if the
             division is not to be in equal lengths. Dividing a
             segment into sub-segments will add a point or points
             to the general reference line.
           - - Add to Segment Before
               Point option. When this option is chosen,
               the additional object(s), and thus the point(s),
               will be added to the segment of the general reference
               line preceding the point. If no segment precedes
               the point, this option will not be available.
             - Add to Segment After
               Point option. When this option is chosen,
               the additional object(s), and thus the point(s),
               will be added to the segment of the general reference
               line after the point. If no segment follows the
               point, this option will not be available.
           - Delete
             Point option. Use this option to delete the
             selected point.
        2. Click
           on the general reference line (not on a point)
           to display a drop-down menu of commands to divide or combine
           segments of the general reference line, including the
           following:

           - Divide Segment option.
             This option will display the Divide
             Selected Segments form. Use the form to specify
             the number of objects into which the segment of the
             general reference line is to be divided. Type in the
             ratio of the last object to the first, if the division
             is not to be in equal lengths. Dividing a segment
             into sub-segments will add a point or points to the
             general reference line.
           - Combine
             Segments (and remove
             points)
           - - Combine with Preceding
               Segment option. When this option is used,
               the selected segment will be combined with the
               segment that precedes it, thereby removing points
               from the general reference line.
             - Combine with Following
               Segment option. When this option is used,
               the selected segment will be combined with the
               segment that follows it, thereby removing points
               from the general reference line.
- Change
  Gen Ref Line Name button.
- 1. Highlight a general
     reference line name in the display list by clicking on it. Note
     that the selected name will appear in the Gen
     Ref Lines edit box.
  2. Type a new name
     in the Gen Ref Lines
     edit box.
  3. Click the Change Gen Ref Line Name button to change
     the name of the general reference line.
  4. If appropriate,
     click the Edit Selected Gen Ref Line
     button to display the Edit General Reference
     Line form and edit the selected general reference line
     as described above.

- Delete
  Gen Ref Line button.
- 1. Highlight a general
     reference line name in the display list by clicking on it. Note
     that the selected name will appear in the Gen
     Ref Lines edit box.
  2. Click the Delete Gen Ref Line button to delete the
     general reference line.

When a general reference
line is displayed in the active window, it is also possible to select
the line and use the Delete key on the keyboard to delete the general
reference line.

# Draw - Frame/Cable/Tendon

Form:  Properties of Object

Use the Draw menu > Frame/Cable/Tendon command or  Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button ![](../../assets/images/Images/FRAMED_shg.gif) to draw a straight or curved frame object, a cable, or a tendon.

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Click the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button ![](../../assets/images/Images/FRAMED_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Frame/Cable/Tendon command to display the floating Properties of Object form and switch to drawing a line object between two points.
3. Click the Type of Line drop-down list to display the available options for the object:  Straight Frame, Curved Frame, Cable, or Tendon. Choose the appropriate option. Use the other drop-down lists and edit box to select additional parameters, such as the Section ([frame](../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md), [cable](../Define/Section_Properties/Cable_Sections/Cable_Sections.md), [tendon](../Define/Section_Properties/Tendon_Sections/Tendon_Sections.md)), Moment Releases, XY Plane Offset Normal, and [Drawing Control Type](Drawing_Controls.md).

   - Straight Frame option.
   - 1. Click on a grid intersection, a previously defined joint or any point in the plane.
     2. Click again on another point to add a single straight frame object. Every subsequent click will add another straight frame object unless a double click on the same joint is performed or the Enter key is pressed. Pressing the ESC key will also terminate the sequential drawing mode and enable Select mode.
   - Curved Frame option.
   - 1. Click on the grid intersection that defines the beginning point for the curved frame.
     2. Click on the grid intersection to define the end of the curved frame. When the mouse button is released, the [Curved Frame Geometry form](Curved_Frames_and_Cables/Curved_Frame_Geometry_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.
   - Cable option.
   - 1. Click on the grid intersection that defines the beginning point for the cable.
     2. Click on the grid intersection to define the end of the cable. When the mouse button is released, the [Cable Geometry form](Curved_Frames_and_Cables/Cable_Geometry_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, cable unit weight, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.
   - Tendon option.
   - 1. Click on a grid intersection, a previously defined joint or any point in the plane to specify the beginning point for the tendon.
     2. Click again on another point to specify the end point for the tendon. When the mouse button is released, the [Tendon Data for Line Object {Number} form](Tendon/Tendon_Data_for_Line_Object_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, cable unit weight, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.

Note: It is not possible to draw a frame object between any two arbitrary points in space in the 3-D view.

Example:   Drawing a straight frame is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md) and [Problem E](../../Example_Problems/Problem_E.md).

# Draw Isolated Foundation

Use the Draw > Draw Isolated Foundation command to draw an Isolated Footing, Pile Group, Pile Pier, or Pile Shaft Foundation property.

Note: Combined footings or wall / strip footings are drawn by using the Draw > Draw Strip Foundation command to draw a Combined Footing Foundation property.  

## Drawing an Isolated Foundation

1. Draw > Draw Isolated Foundation command to bring up the Properties of Object form below.
2. From the Property drop down menu choose from the various isolated foundations that have already been defined.  Refer to the See Also topics below for information about defining the various Isolated Foundation Properties.
3. Specify the Rotation about Global Z entry to rotate the local axis of the pile or foundation about the global Z axis.  For pile pier or pile shaft, this merely rotates the element that defines the pile.  For a isolated footing or pile group foundation, this will rotate the entire foundation (including plate elements that make up the footing or pile cap) about the global Z axis.
4. Click on a single joint.  This single joint will define the center of an Isolated Footing or Pile Group, or the top point of a Pile Pier or Pile Shaft.

## 

Important Note: Refer to the See Also topics below for information about how these various isolated foundations are modeled (soils springs, line objects, area objects, etc).

# Draw Mode

SAP2000 has two modes of mouse-cursor operation in the active window: Draw mode and [Select mode](Set_Select_Mode.md). The program can only be in one mode at a time. In Draw mode, the mouse cursor is usually used to draw (create) or modify objects in the model. Many types of Draw modes are available, depending on the type of action to be performed. In Draw mode, actions are performed directly on the objects using the mouse. Draw mode can also be used to create nonstructural items, such as [developed elevations](Draw_Developed_Elevation_Definition.md) and [reference points](Draw_Reference_Point.md). When the model is [locked](../Options/Locking_and_Unlocking_the_Model.md), the Draw mode is not available.

Draw mode is the default mode when a [new model is started](../File/New_Model.md). The Draw mode allows for drawing new members and editing one object or a joint at a time. Set Draw mode by choosing one of the drawing commands from the Draw menu, or the corresponding toolbar button.

Note 3D solid objects are not created using any of the Draw menu commands. They are created by [extruding area objects](../Edit/Extrude.md).

- [Set Reshape Element Mode](Set_Reshape_Element_Mode.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHAPEM_shg.gif)
- [Draw Special Joint](Draw_Special_Joint.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/JOINTAD_shg.gif)
- [Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon](Draw_Frame_Cable_Tendon.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/FRAMED_shg.gif)

- [Quick Draw Braces](Quick_Draw_Braces.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/Quick%20Draw%20Braces%20button.GIF)
- [Quick Draw Secondary Beams](Quick_Draw_Secondary_Beams.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/Quick%20Draw%20Secondary%20Beams.GIF)
- [Draw Poly Area](Draw_Poly_Area.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLD_shg.gif)
- [Draw Rectangular Area](Draw_Rectangular_Area.md) ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLR_shg.gif)
- [Quick Draw Area](Quick_Draw_Area.md)  ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLDQ_shg.gif)

# Draw Poly Area

Draw the area object in a 2-D View as follows:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on if they are not already turned on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 2-D View](../View/Set_2-D_View.md) command to set the active window to select the plane in which the area object is to be added.
3. Click the Draw Poly Area Element button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLD_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Draw Poly Area command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to specify the [area section](../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md) and any drawing controls.
4. Click on a grid intersection, a previously defined joint or any point in that plane.
5. Click again on any number of other points either clockwise or counterclockwise, colinear or not, to draw the area object. Note that the [Edit menu > Edit Areas > Remove Points from Area command](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Remove_Points_from_Area.md) can be used to remove points from the edges of area object, and the [Edit menu > Edit Areas > Add Point to Area Edge](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Add_Point_to_Area_Edge.md) command can be used to add points to the edges of area objects.
6. Return to the first point and double click on it to complete the poly area. Click the Select button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_994924187.gif) or the Esc key on the keyboard to exit Draw mode.

![](../../assets/images/Images/SCRNCAP8_shg.gif)

### Draw the area object in a 3-D View as follows:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on if they are not already on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 3-D View](../View/Set_3-D_View.md) command to set the active window to select the plane in which the area object is to be added.
3. Click the Draw Poly Area Element button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLD_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Draw Poly Area command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to specify the area property and any [Drawing Controls](Drawing_Controls.md).
4. In the 3-D view, click on a grid intersection, a line/edge or a previously defined joint (a small red ball appears to confirm that the point has been selected).
5. Click on any other similar points either clockwise or counterclockwise, colinear or not, to draw the area object.
6. Return to the first point and double click on it to complete the poly area. Click the Select button ![](../../assets/images/EBX_994924187.GIF) or the Esc key on the keyboard to exit Draw mode.

Note: It is not possible to draw an area object between arbitrary locations in space in the 3-D view. When drawing in 3-D, you must snap to points, lines/edges, or grids.

![](../../assets/images/Images/SCRNCAP9_shg.gif)

Note:  For best results, all points of a poly area should be essentially in the same plane.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem U](../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

## See Also

[Quick Draw Area](Quick_Draw_Area.md)

[New Labels](New_Labels.md)

[Change Labels](../Edit/Change_Labels.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Draw_Rectangular_Area.htm | Draw Rectangular Area -->

# Draw Rectangular Area

A rectangular-shaped area can be drawn in a 2-D View only, as follows:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on if they are not already on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 2-D View command](../View/Set_2-D_View.md) to set the active window to select the plane in which the area object is to be added.
3. Click the Draw Rectangular Element button  ![](../../assets/images/Images/SHELLR_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Draw Rectangular Area command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to select the [area section](../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md).
4. Click on a grid intersection, a previously defined joint or any point in that plane.
5. Click again on the opposite corner of the shape to draw an area object by defining the two opposite corners of the rectangular shape.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem M](../../Example_Problems/Problem_M.md), [Problem S](../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md), and [Problem Z](../../Example_Problems/Problem_Z.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Draw_Reference_Point.htm | Draw Reference Point -->

# Draw Reference Point

Use the Draw menu > Draw Reference Point command to draw individual reference points in a plan view for facilitating the placement of other objects.

1. Set the active window to a plan view.
2. Click the Draw menu > Draw Reference Point command to display the Properties of Object form. Use the form to specify any X or Y offset.

Note:  Right clicking in the background (not on an object) of a display window displays a menu of selected commands, including the Create Reference Lines on Plan command. This method can be used instead of Step 2.

3. Click in the active window to locate the reference point and then use the reference point to place other objects in the model.

Note:  Right clicking on the reference point will display a drop-down menu of options, including the Edit Reference Lines command. Click that command to display the [Edit Reference Line form](Edit_Reference_Line_Form.md). Use that form to modify the location of the vertical reference line defined by the reference point.

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Draw_Section_Cuts.htm | Draw Section Cuts -->

# Draw Section Cuts

Form:  Section Cut Stresses and Forces

Use the Draw menu > Draw Section Cuts command to display integrated forces along a specified section cut.

Note:  Use this command after an analysis has been run ([Analyze menu > Run Analysis](../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md)) and with a deformed shape (with or without results) displayed in the active window  
(e.g., [Display menu > Show Deformed Shape](../Display/Show_Deformed_Shape.md),  
[Display menu > Forces/Stresses > Frames/Cable/Tendons,](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Frames_Cables_Tendons.md)     
[Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Shells](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Shells.md),  
[Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Asolids](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Asolids.md),  
[Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Planes](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Planes.md),  
[Display menu > Show Forces/Stresses > Solids](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Forces_Stresses_Solids.md),  
[Display menu > Show Forces/ Stresses > Links](../Display/Show_Forces_Stresses/Show_Force_Stresses_Links.md))

1. Use the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis.
2. SAP2000 will automatically display a deformed shape after the analysis has been run, which can be used in Step 3. Alternatively, select an option from the Display menu to display results on the model. See the Display topics for more information about the results that can be generated and the forms and options used in generating various result displays.
3. With the deformed shape displayed, click the Draw menu > Draw Section Cuts command.
4. Move the mouse pointer/cursor to the starting point of the section cut to be drawn on the deformed shape and click the left mouse button. Drag the mouse to the ending point for the section cut. SAP2000 will display the Section Cut Stresses & Forces form. The form has the following areas:

   - Section Cutting Line Projected Coordinates, Start Point and End Point The X, Y and Z values displayed in this area of the form are the coordinates of the starting point and ending point of the section cut. Type directly in these edit boxes to adjust the location of the section, if necessary. Click the Refresh button to complete relocation of the section cut and to update the display of the integrated forces.
   - Resultant Force Location and Angle  The X, Y, Z values displayed in this area of the form are the coordinates of a point along the section cut. The initial values are the mid-point between the Start Point and End Point. Type revised values in the edit box to display forces at another location along the section cut.  The angle value is the angle measured counterclockwise from the positive Global X axis to the positive X axis of the local coordinate system in which the integrated forces are reported. The initial X direction is parallel to the section cut from the Start Point toward the End Point.  Use the check boxes in this area of the form to select the forces to be included in the calculation (that is, the forces associated with frames, shells, asolids, planes, solids, links). If a check box is unavailable, that object is not included in the model.
   - Integrated Forces  The values displayed in these edit boxes are the forces and moments along the right and left sides of the section cut at the point/coordinates defined by the coordinates listed in the Resultant Force Location edit boxes.
   - Save Cut button. Click the Save Cut button to save the specified cut for the Right Side or the Left Side, or click both buttons to save both sides of the section cut.
   - Refresh Button If changes are made to the Start Point or End Point, the Resultant Force Location coordinates, or the objects to be included (frames, shells, asolids, planes, solids, links), click the Refresh button to view the recalculated Integrated Forces.

See Also

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Draw_Special_Joint.htm | Draw Special Joint -->

# Draw Special Joint

In building a model in SAP2000, it is not necessary to pre-define joints. The joints are automatically added to the ends or corners of objects. Special Joints are those joints added by the user. Adding joints may be necessary in rare cases, such as at one end of an NLLink Element - an end where there is no other object present and hence no automatically generated joint.

Add a special joint in a 2-D View as follows:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on if they are not already on.
2. Use the [View menu > Set 2-D View command](../View/Set_2-D_View.md) to set the active window to select the plane in which the joint is to be added.
3. Click the Draw Special Joint button ![](../../assets/images/Images/JOINTAD_shg.gif)  or the Draw menu > Draw Special Joint command to display the Properties of Object form and switch to Add Special Joint mode. Use the form to specify any offset (X, Y, or Z).
4. Click on a grid intersection or any other point in that plane to add a joint.

Add a special joint in a 3-D View as follows:

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on if they are not already on.
2. Click the Draw Special Joint button ![](../../assets/images/Images/JOINTAD_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Draw Special Joint command to display the Properties of Object form and to switch to Add Special Joint mode. Use the form to specify any offset (X, Y, or Z).
3. In the 3-D view, click on a grid intersection to add a joint.

Note:  The joints may be added only at grid intersections in 3-D view.  
  
Right click on a joint to open the [Point Information form](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Information_Forms/Point_Information_Location_Tab.md). Use the form to edit the joint location to place it precisely in the desired location. Also, double left clicking in the white cell associated with the Special Joint item accesses a message form that can be used to specify that the joint be flagged as a Special Joint (selected the Yes button), or not (select the No button).  
  
Also, unlike program-generated joints, a special joint is not deleted if the other objects connected to the joint are deleted. That is, it is possible for a special joint to be located "in mid air" if the surrounding objects are deleted without also deleting the special joint.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem E](../../Example_Problems/Problem_E.md) and [Problem Y](../../Example_Problems/Problem_Y.md).

## See Also

[New Labels](New_Labels.md)

[Change Labels](../Edit/Change_Labels.md)

# Draw Strip Foundation

Use the Draw > Draw Strip Foundation command to draw a [Combined Footing Foundation](../Define/Combined_Footing_Foundation_Property.md) property.

Note: Isolated foundations (footings, pile piers, pile shafts, pile groups) are drawn by using the Draw > Draw Isolated Foundation command to draw an Isolated Footing Foundation property.  

## Drawing a Strip Foundation

1. Draw > Draw Strip Foundation command to bring up the Properties of Object form below.
2. From the Property drop down menu choose from the various strip foundations or combined footing that have already been defined.  Refer to the See Also topic below for information about defining the various Strip Foundation Properties.
3. Specify the Intermediate Points.  "Yes" indicates that connectivity to specify that any points that occur between the twp main points that defined the foundation will automatically be connected to the foundation.  "No" would indicate that intermediate points will not be directly supported by the foundation.
4. Click on two joints that define the line of the main load points for the combined footing / strip footing.

## 

Important Note: Refer to the See Also topic below for information about how combined footing foundations are modeled (soils springs, line objects, area objects, etc).

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Drawing_Controls.htm | Drawing Controls -->

# Drawing Controls

Drawing Controls provide the capability to constrain one of the axes when drawing or reshaping an object. For example, using a constraint, the user can quickly draw a frame object parallel to one of the global axes. The keyboard key/drawing controls and their associated actions include the following:

- H - Locks the horizontal component of the next point to that of the previous one.
- V - Locks the vertical component of the next point to that of the previous one.
- A - Locks the parallel angle component of the next angle to that of the previous angle.
- L - Locks the length component of the next segment to that of the previous segment.
- S - Locks the length and angle components of the next point to that of the previous point.
- D - Locks the change in the horizontal and vertical components of the next point to that of the previous one.
- Press the space bar or select None from the Drawing Controls menu if you want to remove the drawing control option.

There are three steps to using the constraint tools:

1. Locate the first point.
2. Press one of the constraint keys or select an option in the Properties of Object form that appears following use of the Draw menu > Set Reshape Element Mode command, the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command, or the Draw menu > Poly Area command.
3. Locate the next point. SAP2000 picks up only the unconstrained component of the selected point.

Note: Snaps can be used in conjunction with drawing controls, but are not required. Only the unconstrained component of the selected snap point is used when a control has been selected. [Snap tools](Snap_To.md) can also be used when [reshaping an object](Set_Reshape_Element_Mode.md).

## See Also

[Nudge Feature](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Nudge_Feature.md)

[Right Mouse Button](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Right_Mouse_Button.md)

[Selection List](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Selection_List.md)

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Drawing Controls as follows:   - Click he Draw menu > Set Reshape Element Mode, Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon or Draw menu > Poly Area command to display a Properties of Object form with the Drawing Controls options. - While in Draw or Reshaper mode, depress the  H, V, A, L, S, D keys on your keyboard while drawing or reshaping an object. |

# Edit Reference Line Form

The Edit Reference Line form is used to add a reference line, modify its location, or delete a reference line.

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Import_User_Mesh_as_Area_Object.htm | Import User Mesh as Area Object -->

# Import User Mesh as Area Object

Form:  Import User Mesh as Area Object

The Import User Mesh as Area Object command allows for the import of a .DXF file containing ACAD 3DFACE data that defines an internal element mesh – this mesh should be restricted to 3 or 4 node elements only, and all elements must be in the same plane and the mesh must be one contiguous region. SAP2000 allows this mesh to be positioned at any location in the model, and to be assigned any existing SAP2000 area property. This feature allows for the creation of arbitrary user-defined internal element meshes, in an external application, for use with area objects in SAP2000. When the mesh is imported, SAP2000 automatically generates an area object that is used for selections and assignments, the boundary of which is defined by the extent of the mesh. The imported user mesh is automatically stored with the area object.

Typically, it is recommended that the general meshing option found on the [Area Object Dividing or Meshing](../Assign/Area_Object_Dividing_or_Meshing.md) form be used when meshing areas as it provides accurate and computationally efficient results, with the benefit that it will automatically re-mesh if the model is altered. However, on occasion the sophisticated user may wish to set their own mesh using the Import User Mesh as Area Object command, perhaps to capture unique behavior where the general mesh is not appropriate. Unlike the general mesh though, the user mesh will not adjust to changes made to the model - it is in essence "locked." The program will not allow changes to the geometry of objects with a user mesh. To change the geometry, the user mesh must first be removed.

Note: It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that the imported mesh aligns with the structural objects in the SAP2000 model. There must be nodes in the mesh that will align with the columns, beams and other area elements in SAP2000 – SAP2000 will not perform any adjustment of the imported mesh to provide connectivity and stability.

Click the Draw menu > Import User Mesh as area Object command to access the Import DXF File form. Use the form to locate the filename/path of the .DXF file to be imported. Highlight the filename and click the Open button to access the Import User Mesh as Area Object form. The form displays the mesh in the active window (3D or Plan).

The toolbar options can be used to change the view of the imported mesh.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  | 3D button - Click this button to display the object in a 3D view. |
|  | Zoom buttons - Click these buttons to Restore Full View, Zoom In One Step, Zoom Out One Step, and Rubber Band Zoom, respectively. |
|  | Rotate 3D View button - Click this button when a 3D view is displayed and use the mouse to adjust the view direction. |

## Location

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z coordinate locations where the origin of the imported mesh (.DXF file) should be located in the SAP2000 model.

Note: If the imported mesh is positioned in the same plane as an existing area object and is identical in size and shape, the existing object will be replaced by the imported object. If the size and shape is not identical and there is overlap with an existing object, there may be multiple objects at the same location.

## Scaling

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z scaling factors to adjust the size of the imported object. A factor of 1 in an edit box indicates that there will be no scaling, while a value other than one means that object will be scaled in that direction by the specified value.

## Rotation

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z rotation angles in degrees. Non-zero values will result in the imported object being rotated about the axis the specified angle.

Holding the cursor on a node of the imported object mesh will display the coordinates along the bottom of the window.

The user mesh may be viewed by going to the View menu > Set Display Options command and checking the User Mesh checkbox under Areas region on the **Object Options**tab.

Note:  Once the user mesh and its associated area object have been imported into SAP2000, the user mesh **cannot** be directly modified, although it may be moved and replicated using the Edit commands.

Changes to the user mesh can be done either by using an external application and then re-importing into SAP2000, or by the following procedure:

1. Select the area object with the user mesh to be edited.
2. Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Explode User Mesh to Areas  command to convert the user mesh elements into area objects.
3. Edit the geometry of the area objects to match the desired internal user mesh layout using the Edit commands.
4. Select all of the area objects created previously using the Explode User Mesh to Areas command, including those with modified geometry.
5. Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Merge Areas to Create User Mesh command to combine the selected area objects into a single object with a new internal user mesh.

## See Also

[Automatic Mesh Options (for Areas)](../Analyze/Automatic_Mesh_Settings_for_Areas.md)

[Explode User Mesh to Areas](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Explode_User_Mesh_to_Shells.md)

[Merge Areas to Create User Mesh](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Merge_Shells_to_Create_User_Mesh.md)

[Remove User Mesh From Area Object](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Remove_User_Mesh_from_Area_Object.md)

[Convert Current Mesh to User Mesh](../Edit/Edit_Areas/Convert_Current_Mesh_to_User_Mesh.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Import_User_Mesh_as_Solid_Object.htm | Import User Mesh as Solid Object -->

# Import User Mesh as Solid Object

Form:  Import User Mesh as Solid Object

The Import User Mesh as Solid Object command allows for the import of a .DXF file containing ACAD line or acDbLine data that denote the edges of solid elements which form an internal element mesh - the mesh must be one contiguous region. SAP2000 allows this mesh to be positioned at any location in the model, and to be assigned any existing SAP2000 solid property. This allows for the creation, in an external application, of arbitrary user-defined internal element meshes for use with solid objects. When the mesh is imported, SAP2000 automatically generates a solid object that is used for selections and assignments, the boundary of which is defined by the extent of the mesh. The imported user mesh is automatically stored with the solid object.

This feature allows a user to set their own mesh using the Import User Mesh as solid Object command. Unlike automatic meshing, the user mesh will not adjust to changes made to the model - it is in essence "locked." The program will not allow changes to the geometry of objects with a user mesh. To change the geometry, the user mesh must first be removed.

Note: It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that the imported mesh aligns with the structural objects in the SAP2000 model. There must be nodes in the mesh that will align with the columns, beams and other elements in SAP2000 – SAP2000 will not perform any adjustment of the imported mesh to provide connectivity and stability.

Click the Draw menu > Import User Mesh as Solid Object command to access the Import DXF File form. Use the form to locate the filename/path of the .DXF file to be imported. Highlight the filename and click the Open button to access the Import User Mesh as Solid Object form. The form displays the mesh in the active window (3D or Plan).

The toolbar options can be used to change the view of the imported mesh.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  | 3D button - Click this button to display the object in a 3D view. |
|  | Zoom buttons - Click these buttons to Restore Full View, Zoom In One Step, Zoom Out One Step, and Rubber Band Zoom, respectively. |
|  | Rotate 3D View button - Click this button when a 3D view is displayed and use the mouse to adjust the view direction. |

## Location

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z coordinate locations where the origin of the imported mesh (.DXF file) should be located in the SAP2000 model.

Note: If the imported mesh is positioned exactly overlapping an existing solid object and is identical in size and shape, the existing object will be replaced by the imported object. If the size and shape is not identical and there is overlap with an existing object, there may be multiple objects at the same location.

## Scaling

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z scaling factors to adjust the size of the imported object. A factor of 1 in an edit box indicates that there will be no scaling, while a value other than one means that object will be scaled in that direction by the specified value.

## Rotation

- X, Y, and Z edit boxes. Input the X, Y, & Z rotation angles in degrees. Non-zero values will result in the imported object being rotated about the axis the specified angle.

Holding the cursor on a node of the imported object mesh will display the coordinates along the bottom of the window.

The user mesh may be viewed by going to the View menu > Set Display Options command and checking the User Mesh checkbox under ***Solids***region on the **Object Options**tab.

Note: Once the user mesh and its associated solid objects have been imported into SAP2000, the user mesh **cannot** be directly modified, although it may be moved and replicated using the Edit commands.

**Tip:** Changes to the user mesh can be done either by using an external application and then re-importing into SAP2000, or by the following procedure:

1. Select the solid object with the user mesh to be edited.
2. Use the Edit menu > Edit Solids > Explode User Mesh to Solids command to convert the user mesh elements into solid objects.
3. Edit the geometry of the solid objects to match the desired internal user mesh layout using the Edit commands.

**Caution:** Once a solid with a user mesh has been exploded into individual solids, it CANNOT be converted back into a User Mesh. They remain individual solids.  

## See Also

[Solid Automatic Solid Mesh](../Assign/Solid/Solid_Automatic_Solid_Mesh.md)

[Explode User Mesh to Solids](../Edit/Edit_Solids/Explode_User_Mesh_to_Solids.md)

[Remove User Mesh from Solid Object](../Edit/Edit_Solids/Remove_User_Mesh_from_Solid_Object.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/New_Labels.htm | New Labels -->

# New Labels

Form:  New Labels

The labels in SAP2000 are alphanumeric. By default the program automatically assigns a numeric numbering scheme to the joints and objects. However, it is possible to assign an alphanumeric labeling scheme by giving an alpha prefix and a starting numeric sequence. All objects added after the scheme is initialized will be affected by the scheme.

Initialize a new labeling scheme as follows:

1. Click the Draw menu > New Labels command to display the New Labels form.

   - Prefix edit box. Enter a prefix for the labeling scheme for the joints, frames, areas, solids, and links.
   - Next Number edit box. Enter a starting number for the scheme. This number will be added to the prefix.
   - Increment edit box. Specify an increment for the numeric sequence
2. Use the appropriate [Draw menu command](Draw_Mode.md) to add joints, frames, cables, tendons, areas, and solids. The new labeling scheme will be applied to those objects added to the model following use of the Draw menu > New Labels command.

## See Also

[Change Labels](../Edit/Change_Labels.md)

[Set Display Options](../View/Set_Display_Options.md)

# Quick Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon

Use the Draw menu > Quick Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Quick Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button ![](../../assets/images/Images/FRAMEDQ_shg.gif)  to draw a straight or curved frame object, a cable, or a tendon.

1. Click the [View menu > Show Grids command](../View/Show_Grid.md) to turn the grids on.
2. Click the  Quick Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button ![](../../assets/images/Images/FRAMEDQ_shg.gif) or the Draw menu > Quick Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command to display the floating Properties of Object form and switch to drawing a frame object on the grid lines between grid intersections.
3. Click the Line Object Type drop-down list to display the available options for the object:  Straight Frame, Curved Frame, Cable, or Tendon. Choose the appropriate option. Use the other drop-down lists and edit box to select additional parameters, such as the Section ([frame](../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md), [cable](../Define/Section_Properties/Cable_Sections/Cable_Sections.md), [tendon](../Define/Section_Properties/Tendon_Sections/Tendon_Sections.md)), Moment Releases, XY Plane Offset Normal, and Drawing Control Type.

   - Straight Frame option.
   - 1. Click on a grid line to quickly draw a straight frame section along the grid line between the grid intersections. Every subsequent click will add another straight frame object unless a double click on the same grid line is performed or the Enter key is pressed. Pressing the ESC key will also terminate the sequential drawing mode and enable Select mode.
   - Curved Frame option.
   - 1. Click on the grid line to locate the beginning and ending points for the curved frame. When the mouse button is released, the [Curved Frame Geometry form](Curved_Frames_and_Cables/Curved_Frame_Geometry_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.
   - Cable option.
   - 1. Click on the grid line to quickly draw a cable along the grid line between grid intersections. When the mouse button is released, the [Cable Geometry form](Curved_Frames_and_Cables/Cable_Geometry_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, cable unit weight, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.
   - Tendon option.
   - 1. Click on a grid line to quickly draw a tendon along the grid line between grid intersections. When the mouse button is released, the [Tendon Data for Line Object {Number} form](Tendon/Tendon_Data_for_Line_Object_Form.md) displays. Use the form to review/change the section property, cable unit weight, number of linear segments, computed coordinates of the linear segments and so on.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem Q](../../Example_Problems/Problem_Q.md).
