<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Set_Reshape_Element_Mode.htm | Set Reshape Element Mode -->

# Set Reshape Element Mode

Activate the Reshaper tool and enter "reshape mode" using one of the following methods:

- Click the Reshaper button,  ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif).
- Select the  Draw menu > Reshape Object command.

In reshape mode, click on an area, line or point object and modify it in one of several ways. If you have difficulties using any of the methods, try using the method in a different view. A [Properties of Object form](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Properties_of_Object_Forms.md) will display with a number of Drawing Control options. The controls are assumed to be self-explanatory. Choose an option to assist in completing the object reshape operations described below.

- [Reshaping Area Objects](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  - Move an Area Object by Dragging.
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on the area object; a series of selection handles (squares that are the opposite color from the background color) appear at all corners of the area object.
  3. While holding down the left mouse button, drag the area object to a new location.

  The area object retains its original shape; it is simply relocated.

  Note: When an area object is moved by dragging, the corner points of the area object are disconnected from any other objects to which they might have been connected. Thus reshaping the area object in this manner affects only the area object, not any surrounding elements to which it may be connected.

  - Reshape an Area Object by Dragging a Corner.
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on one of the corner points of the area object.
  3. While holding down the left mouse button drag the corner point to a new location.

  The other corner points remain in their original locations; the area object takes on a different shape.

  Note: When the corner point of an area object is moved by dragging, the corner point is disconnected from any other objects to which it might have been connected. Thus reshaping the area object in this manner affects only the area object, not any surrounding elements to which it may be connected.

  - Reshape an Area Object by Specifying Coordinates. Right click on one of the corner points of the area object. This accesses a form that can be used to modify the global X, Y and Z coordinates of the corner point. The other corner points remain in their original locations; the area object takes on a different shape.

  Note: When the corner point of an area object is moved by specifying coordinates, the corner point is disconnected from any other objects to which it might have been connected. Thus, reshaping the area object in this manner affects only  the area object, not any surrounding elements to which it may be connected.
- [Reshaping Line Objects](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  - Move a Line Object by Dragging.
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on the line object. Selection handles (squares that are the opposite color from the background color) appear at the ends of the line object.
  3. While holding down the left mouse button, drag the line to a new location.

  The line object retains its original length; it is simply relocated.

  Note: When a line object is moved by dragging, the end points of the line object are disconnected from any other objects to which they may have been connected. Thus reshaping the line object in this manner only affects the line object, not any of the surrounding elements to which it may be connected.

  - Reshape a Line Object by Dragging.
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on the line object. Selection handles (squares that are the opposite color from the background color) appear at the ends of the line object.
  3. Left click on one of selection handles on the end points of the line object.
  4. While holding down the left mouse button, drag the end point to a new location.

  The other end point remains in its original location; the length or orientation of the line object changes.

  Note: When the end point of a line object is moved by dragging, the end point is disconnected from any other objects to which it may have been connected. Thus reshaping the line object in this manner only affects the line object not any surrounding elements to which it may be connected.

  - Reshape a Line Object by Specifying Coordinates.
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on the line object. Selection handles (squares that are the opposite color from the background color) appear at the ends of the line object.
  3. Right click on one of the end points of the line object (not the line object itself) to access the Move Coordinates form
  4. On the Move Coordinates form, modify the global X,  Y and Z coordinates of the end point.

  The other end point remains in its original location; the length of the line object changes.

  Note: When the end point of a line object is moved by specifying coordinates, the end point is disconnected from any other objects to which it may have been connected. Thus reshaping the line object in this manner only affects the line object, not any surrounding elements to which it may be connected.
- [Reshaping Point Objects](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  - Move a Point Object by Dragging
  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Left click on the point object. A selection handle (square that is the opposite color from the background color) appears on the point object.
  3. While holding down the left mouse button, drag the point to a new location.

  When a point object is moved by dragging, all of the objects connected to the point also move; they are either reoriented or resized, or both. Unlike area and line objects, the point object does not disconnect from the objects to which it is attached when it is reshaped/moved.

  - Move a Point Object by Specifying Coordinates
  1. Right click on the point object to access the [Point Information form](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Information_Forms/Point_Information_Location_Tab.md).
  2. On the Location Tab of the Point Information form, modify the global X or Y coordinates of the point.

  When a point object is moved by specifying coordinates, all of the objects connected to the point also move; they are either reoriented or resized, or both. Unlike area and line objects, the point object does not disconnect from the objects to which it is attached when it is reshaped/moved.
- [Reshaping Dimension Lines](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  Use the reshaper tool to move a dimension line to a new location. A dimension line can not be lengthen or shorten, even using the reshaper tool.

  Relocate a dimension line as follows:

  1. Set the Reshape Element Mode by clicking the Reshaper button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_34974760.gif) or the Draw menu > Reshape Object command.
  2. Click on the line so that the selection handles (squares that are the opposite color from the background color) appear at the ends of the dimension line.
  3. Left click on the dimension line.
  4. While holding down the left mouse button, drag it to a new location.

  The dimension line retains its original length; it is simply relocated. The leader lines are automatically adjusted as needed.

Deactivate the Reshaper tool and exit reshape mode using one of the following methods:

- Click the Pointer button,  ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_994924187.gif).

- Press the Esc key on your keyboard.

- Choose one of the drawing options from the Draw menu or the toolbar.

- Click on one of the select items in the Select menu.

- Run an analysis.

# Set Select Mode

The program has two modes of mouse-cursor operation in a display window: Draw mode and Select mode. The program can be in one mode at a time only. After a new model has been started, by default, the program is in Select mode. The mouse cursor is used to select objects before performing certain editing, assignment, display, and output operations. When the model is [locked](../Options/Locking_and_Unlocking_the_Model.md), the program is always in Select mode.

Use the Draw menu > Set Select Mode command or Set Select Mode button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_994924187.gif) to set the Select mode. The Select mode is also enabled if the Esc key is used while the program is in Draw mode.

The various commands on the Select menu can be used to specify selection criteria.

To exit Select mode, use any of the button or commands described in the [Draw Mode](Draw_Mode.md) topic of this Help.

## See Also

[Drawing Controls](Drawing_Controls.md)

[Pointer/Window](../Select/Select/Pointer_Window.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Snap_To.htm | Snap To -->

# Snap To

The snap tools can be used to increase accuracy and speed when drawing and editing objects. The snap tools can be turned on and off as objects are drawn, so that different locations can be specified for every point. More than one snap tool also can be set at the same time, providing for a choice of snap locations. The closest snap location is indicated by a red dot and a text field that identifies which snap location was found. Set the "search radius" for a snap to command using the [Options menu > Preferences> Dimensions/Tolerances command](../Options/Dimensions_Tolerances.md#Screen_Snap_to_Tolerance) and the Screen Snap to Tolerance edit box; the value in that edit box defines the distance in pixels that the program will search to locate the specified "snap to" object (e.g., points and grids, midpoints and ends and so forth).

Note:  Snap tools can also be used when [reshaping an object](Set_Reshape_Element_Mode.md).

1. Select the appropriate snap tool.

   - Points and Grid Intersections button ![](../../assets/images/SnpJG.gif) or the Draw menu > Snap To > Points and Grid Intersections command.  The Snap to Joints and Grid Points tool finds and snaps to the joint or intersection of grid lines closest to the mouse pointer.
   - Ends and Midpoints button ![](../../assets/images/Images/Snp_me.gif)  or the Draw menu > Snap To > Ends and Midpoints command. The Snap to Ends and Midpoints tool finds and snaps to the closest midpoint or end of frames and shells. It will also snap to the end points of NLLink elements.
   - Intersections button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SNP_INT.GIF) or the Draw menu > Snap To > Intersections command. The Snap To Intersections tool finds and snaps to the intersection of two frame objects and a frame object with an area object, regardless of whether there is a joint at the intersection location.
   - Perpendicular Projections button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SNP_PRP.GIF) or the Draw menu > Snap To > Snap to Perpendicular Projections command. The Snap To Perpendicular Projections tool finds and snaps to the intersection point of a line drawn from the last entered point perpendicular to the frame objects or area edge closest to the mouse pointer. This is a helpful way to make sure that lines are perpendicular to each other.
   - Lines and Edges button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SNP_LIN.GIF) or the Draw menu > Snap To > Snap to Lines and Edges command.  The Snap to Lines and Edges tool finds and snaps or “hugs” the closest frame object, grid line or edge of the closest area object. Even though this does not provide the same level of accuracy as the other snap options, it is a good way to make sure that the object being drawn is located on the object being “hugged.”
   - Find Grids button ![](../../assets/images/Images/IMG00030.GIF) or  the Draw menu > Snap to > Fine Grid command. The Snap to Fine Grid tool finds and snaps to the intersections of the fine grids in a planar view.  The Fine Grid spacing may be controlled using the Options menu > Preferences > Dimensions/Tolerances command.

Note:  The snap options are evaluated in the above order. For example, if a location has both an end point and an intersection, the end point will be found first because it is evaluated first.

2. Move the pointer in the graphics window.
3. When a snap location is found close to the pointer, a red dot and a text field describing the snap location is displayed.
4. When the desired snap location is found, click the left mouse button to accept it.
5. Modify the Snap options as required and continue entering elements.

It is sometimes helpful to use the snap tools to quickly draw an object then use the commands on the Edit menu to modify the object.

## See Also

[Drawing Controls](Drawing_Controls.md)

# Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} Form

Use the  Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form to refine the parabolic alignment of the tendon.

- Plane drop-down list. Choose the tendon line local plane for this tendon definition.
- Modify Axes button and Angle display box. Click the Modify Axes button to display the Tendon Local Axis form. Use that form to rotate the tendon axis, as needed. This is an angle by which local axis 2 of the object will be rotated around the local axis 1. Local axis 1 is along the length of the object. By default the local axis 2 is always in the 1-Z plane, except if the object is vertical and then it is parallel to the global X axis.
- Number of Points edit box. Specify the number of points to be used to define the parabolic shape of the tendon using this edit box.
- Tendon Layout Data spreadsheet area. As described above, this form can be accessed using the Quick Start button or the Parabolic Calculator button on the [Tendon Data for Line Object form](Tendon_Data_for_Line_Object_Form.md).
- - If the form is accessed using the Quick Start button, this area will be "pre-loaded" with the coordinate and slope data for the template parabolic tendon chosen on the Tendon Quick Start Templates form. Review the data, and as necessary, make changes using the Number of Points edit box, the Quick Start button (lower left corner of the form), and the spreadsheet cells, as described below.
  - If the form is accessed using the Parabolic Calculator button, this area of the form will be loaded with the data for the beginning and ending of the tendon. Use the Number of Points edit box, the Quick Start button (lower left corner of the form), and the spreadsheet cells to change the data as follows:
  - - Number of Control Points area and Number of Points edit box. Typing a new number in this edit box will add blank rows to the spreadsheet area. Click in those cells to type in new data for the coordinates and slope, or to display a drop-down list for the Slope Type and if necessary, specify the slope ratio.

When changes are made using the Quick Start button in the lower left corner of the form (see next bullet), this edit box will change automatically.

- 1. - Template (Num Spans) area and Quick Start button (lower left corner of the form). Use the drop-down list associated with this button to specify the number of spans to be used in defining the parabolic shape of the tendon. After selecting a number, click the Quick Start button to automatically fill the Tendon Layout Data spreadsheet area with program-calculated coordinate and slope data for the parabolic tendon. Those data then can be edited by clicking in the cells and typing new data for the coordinates and slope, or by selecting from the Slope Type drop-down list and if necessary, specifying the slope ratio.
     - Coord 1, Coord 2 Type, Coord 2, Slope Type, and Slope edit boxes and drop-down lists. Use the cells in these columns to specify that coordinate 2 be user-specified or program calculated, and if user-specified, to specify the value for coordinate 2 in the Coord 2 edit box; to specify that the slope be user specified or program calculated, and if user-specified, to specify the slope ratio in the Slope edit box.
- Display Area. This area of the form will display a graphic of the data in the Tendon Layout Data spreadsheet area. Use the various options associated with it to evaluate the graphic and locate and control the mouse pointer.
- - Units drop-down list. Use the existing units or use the drop-down list to select revised units for working with the data on the form.
  - Distance display/edit box. This display box shows the location of the mouse pointer on the graphic as measured from the start of the tendon. Typing a distance value in the edit box will move the mouse pointer to that location.
  - Coord 1, Coord 2, and Slope display boxes. These display boxes show the coordinate and slope data for the mouse pointer as it passes over the graphical display. The values cannot be edited.
  - No Snap option. When this option is chosen, no snaps are enabled and, as the mouse pointer is moved over any portion of the display, the location of the mouse pointer will display, as appropriate, in the Coord 1, Coord 2 and Slope display boxes.
  - Snap to Local 1 Axis option. When this option is chosen, SAP2000 displays a small red dot that snaps to the Local 1 Axis and, as the mouse is moved, displays the coordinate data for that point along the Local 1 Axis in the Coord 1 display box.
  - Snap to Tendon option. When this option is chosen, SAP2000 displays a small red dot that snaps to the tendon and displays the coordinate data for that point along the tendon in the Coord 1, Coord 2 and Slope display boxes.
  - Snap to Points option. When this option is chosen, SAP2000 displays a small red dot that snaps to the points along the tendon and displays the coordinate data for the point that define the tendon in the  the Coord 1, Coord 2 and Slope display boxes.
- Calculated Results
- - Clear button. Clicking this button will remove any program-calculated results from the spreadsheet area and will remove the graphical display from the display area.
  - Refresh button. Click this button to ensure that the graphic display reflects any changes made to the data in the spreadsheet area of the form.
- Use Calculated Results for this Tendon check box and Done button. If this check box is checked when the Done button is clicked, the data in the spreadsheet area will be transferred automatically to the Tendon Layout Data area of the Tendon Data for Line Object form. If the check box is not checked, the data will be ignored.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form as follows:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable Element button to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Tendon from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click in the active view to specify the beginning point of the tendon. Click a second time to specify the end point of the tendon. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Tendon Data for Line Object form. 5. Click either of the following buttons     - Quick Start button.    - 1. Click the Quick Start button to display the Tendon Quick Start Templates form.      2. Choose a "Parabolic Tendon" option and click the OK button to display the Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form.    - Parabolic Calculator button. Click this button to display the Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form.   Note:  After a tendon has been drawn as described above (Steps 1 through 3), right clicking on the tendon will display the Tendon Data for Line Object form (replaces Steps 1 through 4). |

# Draw - Move Tendon Form

Use the Move Tendon form to move the tendon a specified distance or to specified coordinates.

- Coordinate System drop-down list. Select the [coordinate system](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) in which the move is being defined.
- - Object Type drop-down list. Depending on the selection made in the Coordinate System drop-down list,  this drop-down list will appear. Select the object type and the coordinate system for the specified object.
  - Object drop-down list. Depending on the selection made in the Object Type drop-down list, this drop-down list will appear, listing the IDs for the target object type. Select an ID and the coordinate system for the specified object.
- Move by Specified Distance option. When this option is chosen, use the Delta 1, Delta 2, and Delta 3 edit boxes to specify in the current units the change in the position of the tendon relative to its current locations (e.g., entering 100 inches in the Delta 1 edit box moves the tendon 100 inches to the right).
- Move Start to Specified Coords option. When this option is chosen, use the Coord 1, Coord 2, and Coord 3 edit boxes to specify the new coordinates for the starting location of the tendon.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Move Tendon form as follows:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon Element button to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Tendon from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click in the active view to specify the beginning point of the tendon. Click a second time to specify the end point of the tendon. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Tendon Data for Line Object form. 5. Click the Move Tendon button to display the Move Tendon form.   Note:  After a tendon has been drawn as described above, right clicking on the tendon also will display the Tendon Data for Line Object form (i.e., skip to Step 5—click the  Move Tendon button to display the Move Tendon form). |

# Tendon Data for Line Object Form

Additional forms: Tabulated Tendon Profile for Line Object {Number}, Tendon Layout Display for Line Object, Tendon Load Assignment for Line Object

Use the Tendon Data for Line Object form to specify tendon segment type, property, load, discretization and other parameters.

Tendon Layout Data

- Point ID display cell. The number shown in this display cell is assigned by the program to identify the tendon.
- Segment Type drop-down list and 1 Coord, 2 Coord, 3 Coord edit boxes.  The necessary data can be specified using the following alternative approaches:
- - Select a segment type from the drop-down list and where appropriate specify the 1, 2 and 3 coordinates in the spreadsheet cells, and then use the Insert Above, Insert Below, Modify, or Delete buttons to specify a segment or to modify or delete a previously specified segment. The two defaults cannot be modified or deleted because they define the beginning and the end of the tendon. Adding segments to the tendon definition allows changes to the alignment of the tendon. Click the Delete All button to delete all segment entries except the defaults; SAP2000 will display a message box asking for confirmation that all entries are to be deleted.
  - Quick Start button. Click the Quick Start button to display the [Tendon Quick Start Templates form](Tendon_Quick_Start_Templates_Form.md), which has a number of options for the tendon alignment. Select an option by clicking on it and then click the OK button.
  - - If a "Straight Tendon" option has been selected, the Tendon Data for Line Object form will redisplay with data for the selected option transferred automatically to it.
    - If a "Parabolic Tendon" option has been selected, the [Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form](Define_Parabolic_Tendon_Layout_for_Line_Object_Number_Form.md) will display with the data for the selected option transferred automatically to the spreadsheet area of that form. Use that form to refine the tendon alignment as needed.
  - Parabolic Calculator button. Click the Parabolic Calculator button to display the [Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form](Define_Parabolic_Tendon_Layout_for_Line_Object_Number_Form.md). Use that form to define a parabolic tendon alignment.
- Tendon Layout Display area.
- - Double click the graphic in the display area to display the Tendon Layout Display for Line Object form; use that form to review the tendon layout relative to the 1-2, 1-3, and 2-3 axes. When the mouse pointer is moved over any of the graphics, the coordinate location and distance of the pointer from the start of the segment will display in the associated display boxes (1,2 or 1, 3, or 2, 3).  
      
    The Coordinate System, Object Type, and Object drop-down lists can be used to specify that any coordinate system be used for the displays shown on the 1-2, 1-3, or 2-3 display areas. Note that the presence or absence of the Object drop-down list depends on the selection made in the Object Type drop-down list. The Snap To options function similarly to those on the  Tendon Data for Line Object form (see Snap Option description below). Click the Done button to close the form and return to the Tendon Data for Line Object form.
  - Refresh Plot button. Click this button to ensure that changes made on the Tendon Data for Line Object form are reflected in the display area.
  - Show Table button. Click this button to display the Tabulated Tendon Profile for Line Object {Number} form. The spreadsheet area of that form displays the tendon data in tabular format. The cells cannot be edited and are provided for informational purposes as well as to provide an opportunity to copy the data or send the data to Excel.
  - Mouse Pointer Location edit/display box. When the mouse pointer is moved over the graphic, the distance of the pointer from the beginning of the segment and the coordinate location relative to the 1-2, 1-3 and 2-3 axes will display in the associated display boxes. It is possible to type a value in the Distance edit box to display the 1-2, 1-3, and 2-3 coordinates for that specific location on the segment.
- Tendon Layout Display Options area.
- - Show 1-2 Axes option. When this option is selected, the 1-2 Axes view of the specified segment is shown in the Tendon Layout Display area of the form.
  - Show 1-3 Axes option. When this option is selected, the 1-3 Axes view of the specified segment is shown in the Tendon Layout Display area of the form.
  - Show 2-3 Axes option. When this option is selected, the 2-3 Axes view of the specified span is shown in the Tendon Layout Display area of the form.
- Snap Option
- - No Snap option. When this option is chosen, no snaps are enabled and, as the mouse pointer is moved over any of the display, the location of the mouse pointer will display, as appropriate, in the 1, 2, and 3 display boxes in the Mouse Pointer Location area in the lower left of the form.
  - Snap To Tendon option. When this option is chosen, SAP2000 displays a small red dot that snaps to the tendon or tendon segment and displays the coordinate data for that point along the tendon in the Mouse Pointer Location area in the lower left of the form.
- Units drop-down list. Use the displayed units or select new units from the drop-down list.
- Move Tendon button. Click the Move Tendon button to display the [Move Tendon form](Draw_Move_Tendon_Form.md).
- Tendon End Point Objects
- - I End display box. Displays the numerical ID for the joint at the beginning of the tendon.
  - J End display box.  Displays the numerical ID for the joint at the end of the tendon.
- Tendon Section drop-down list and Add and Show buttons. This drop-down list displays the [tendon sections](../../Define/Section_Properties/Tendon_Sections/Tendon_Sections.md) that have been defined for the model. As necessary, change the tendon section by selecting another section from that list. Clicking the Add and Show button displays the [Tendon Section Data form](../../Define/Section_Properties/Tendon_Sections/Tendon_Section_Data_Form.md).
- Tendon Loads display box and the Add and Show buttons. This drop-down list displays the load pattern to which the tendon definition has been added. As necessary, change the load pattern by selecting another pattern from that list. Clicking the Add button displays the [Tendon Load form](Tendon_Load_Form.md); use the form to specify a new load for the tendon.  When the Show button is used, the Tendon Load Assignment for Line Object form displays. That form displays the load data for review purposes and the data cannot be edited.

Note:  When tendons are modeled as elements, the Elastic Shortening Stress, Creep Stress, Shrinkage Stress, and Steel Relaxation Stress specified using the Tendon Load form apply in addition to the losses computed by the analysis dues to dependent behavior defined in the material properties. Elastic Shortening Stress generally should be set to zero.

- Tendon Local Axes Angle display box and the Modify button. The angle of the tendon relative to the X axis is shown in this display box. Click the Modify button to display the Tendon Local Axis form. To change the angle of the tendon, enter a value in the Angle in Degrees edit box.
- Max. Tendon Discretization and Length edit box. Use this edit box to specify frequency of discretization of the tendon by specifying a Length in the edit box.
- Group Loaded by Tendon drop-down list. Use this drop-down list to select the group of objects to which the tendon load is being applied. The [Group](../../Define/Groups.md) would be expected to consist of, for example, point, line, area, or solid objects comprising slabs, beams and the like.
- Coordinate System drop-down list. Use the drop-down list to select a coordinate system other than global if one has been defined (see [Define Coordinate Systems/Grids](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Coordinate_Systems_Grid.md) for more information about defining a coordinate system).
- - Object Type drop-down list. Depending on the selection made in the Coordinate System drop-down list,  this drop-down list will display. Select an object type and the coordinate system for the specified object type.
  - - Object drop-down list. Depending on the selection made in the Object Type drop-down list, this drop-down list will display, listing the IDs for the target object type. Select an ID and the coordinate system for the specific object.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Tendon Data for Line Object form as follows:  Method 1:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button , to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Tendon from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click in the active view to specify the beginning point of the tendon and then click a second time to specify the end point of the tendon. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Tendon Data for Line Object form.   Method 2:   1. Select an object that has been drawn as a tendon (see Method 1); only one object may be selected at a time. 2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Edit Tendon Profile command to access the Tendon Data for Line Object form.   Note:  After a tendon has been drawn as described in Method 1, right clicking on the tendon also will display the Tendon Data for Line Object form. |

# Tendon Load Form

Use the Tendon Load form to define the tension on the tendon.

- Load Pattern Name drop-down list. Choose the load pattern to which the tendon load definition is to be added. Alternatively, click the + (plus symbol) beside the drop-down list to access the [Define Load Patterns form](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md); use the form to define a load pattern that will then be available in the drop-down list.
- Units drop-down list. Use the displayed units or select new units from the drop-down list.
- Jack From This Location options. Choose the option to specify the location for applying the stress or force on the tendon.
- - I-End (Start) of Tendon option. Specify that the force or stress is to be applied at the start of the tendon.
  - J-End (End) of Tendon option. Specify that the force or stress is to be applied at the end of the tendon.
  - Both Ends Simultaneously option. Specify that the force or stress is to be applied to both the start and end of the tendon.
- Load Type options and Tendon Load edit box. Choose to apply tension to the tendon as a Force or Stress. Then use the default Force or Stress shown in the edit box, or type a revised value in the edit box.
- Friction and Anchorage Losses options.
- - Curvature Coefficient edit box. Use the default or specify the curvature coefficient for the prestress loss.
  - Wobble Coefficient edit box. Use the default or specify a revised wobble coefficient in this edit box.
  - Anchorage Set Slip edit box. Use the default or specify a revised distance for the anchor slip.
- Other Loss Parameters edit boxes.  When tendons are modeled as elements, the parameters in this area of the form (Elastic Shortening Stress, Creep Stress, Shrinkage Stress, Steel Relaxation Stress) apply in addition to the losses computed by the analysis due to time dependent behavior defined in the material properties. Elastic Shortening Stress generally should be set to zero.

- Options. Specify how the load is to be applied.

- Replace Existing Loads option. Replaces the currently specified tendon load, if any, with the new load. If no assignment exists, the new assignment is still made. This is the default option.
- Delete Existing Loads option. Deletes any and all tendon load assignments made to the tendon.

## See Also

[Tendon Data For Line Object](Tendon_Data_for_Line_Object_Form.md)

| Access the Tendon Load form as follows:    Method 1:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon button , to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Tendon from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click in the active view to specify the beginning point of the tendon and then click a second time to specify the end point of the tendon. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Tendon Data for Line Object {Number} form.   Note:  After a tendon has been drawn as described above, right clicking on the tendon also will display the Tendon Data for Line Object {Number} form.   5. Click the Tendon Loads Add button to display the Tendon Load form.   Method 2:   1. Select an existing tendon type line object(s). 2. Click the Assign menu > Tendon Loads > Tendon Force/Stress command to display the Tendon Load form. |

# Tendon Quick Start Templates Form

Use the Tendon Quick Start Templates form to specify the tendon layout using template alignments.

1. Plane drop-down list. Choose the tendon line local plane for this tendon definition.
2. Modify Axes button and Angle display box. Click the Modify Axes button to display the Tendon Local Axis form. Use that form to rotate the tendon axis, as needed.  This is an angle by which the local axis 2 of the element will be rotated around the local axis 1. The local axis 1 is along the length of the element.  By default the local axis 2 is always in the 1-Z plane, except if the element is vertical and then it is parallel to the global X axis.
3. Number of Spans drop-down list. Choose the number of spans for the tendon from this drop-down list. Ten is the maximum.
4. Select a Quick Start Option. Select an option by clicking on it.
5. Click the OK button.

   - If a "Straight Tendon" or "Circular Tendon" option has been selected, the Tendon Data for Line Object form will redisplay with the selected option transferred automatically to it.
   - If a "Parabolic Tendon" option has been selected, the [Define Parabolic Tendon Layout for Line Object {Number} form](Define_Parabolic_Tendon_Layout_for_Line_Object_Number_Form.md) will display with the data for the selected option transferred automatically to the spreadsheet area of the form. Use that form to refine the tendon alignment as needed.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Tendon Quick Start Templates form as follows:   1. Click the Draw menu > Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon command or the Draw Frame/Cable/Tendon Element button to display the floating Properties of Object form. 2. Select Tendon from the Line Object Type drop-down list. 3. Click in the active view to specify the beginning point of the tendon. Click a second time to specify the end point of the tendon. 4. Release the mouse button to display the Tendon Data for Line Object form. 5. Click the Quick Start button to display the Tendon Quick Start Templates form.   Note:  After a tendon has been drawn as described herein, right clicking on the tendon also will display the Tendon Data for Line Object form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Draw/Tendon/Tendon_Response_Form.htm | Tendon Response Form -->

# Tendon Response Form

Form: Tendon Response

The Tendon Response Form can be accessed three ways:

1. Right-click on a tendon object when displaying the undeformed shape. This will show the form Tendon Data For Line Object. Click the “Show” button for the Tendon Loads to bring up the form Tendon Load Assignment Data, then click “Show Prestress Losses”.
2. From the Bridge Tendon Data form, click the “Loss Params” button to open the Prestress Loss Parameters form. Then click “Show Prestress Losses”.
3. After an analysis has been run, right-click on a tendon object when displaying frame/cable/tendon force diagrams.

In the first two cases, the Tendon Response form will plot the specified tendon force or stress for a given load pattern (a) Prior to Seating, (b) After Seating and (c) After Other Losses. These are plotted along the length of the tendon to show the effect of the specified losses. For case (3), the actual tendon force computed by analysis for a given load case or load combination will be shown in addition to these three prestress loss curves.

Use the following parameters to control the plot:

- **Tendon Line Object** drop-down list. Choose to display the tendon response. This option is only available when displaying frame/cable/tendon forces, case (3) above.
- **Result Type** option. Select either the force or stress response for which the tendon response plot is to be displayed.
- **Units** drop-down list. Use the displayed units or use this drop-down list to change the units for the form. The selected units will be used to display the response plot.
- **Export to Excel** button. When this button is clicked, the program exports the specified force or stress data to an Excel workbook and automatically launches Excel to display the downloaded data.
- **Done** button. Click to exit the form.
- **Load Pattern** drop-down list. Choose a load pattern for which the specified tendon losses are to be plotted.
- **Load Case/Combo** drop-down list. Select a [load case](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) or [load combination](../../Define/Load_Combination/Load_Combination.md) for which the tendon forces or stresses from analysis are to be plotted. This option is only available when displaying frame/cable/tendon forces, case (3) above.
- **Multivalued Options.** The availability of these options depends on the load case chosen in the *Case/Combo* drop-down list.
- - **Envelope Max/Min** option. Choose this option to display the maximum and minimum results over all time steps.
  - **Envelope Max** option. Choose this option to display the maximum results over all time steps.
  - **Envelope Min** option. Choose this option to display the minimum results over all time steps.
  - **Step** selection box. Use this selection box to choose the number of steps to be included in the plot.
- **Tendon Response Plot** display area. The plot is displayed in this area of the form. Use the horizontal scroll bar at the bottom of the display or hold the left mouse button to move the mouse pointer along the plot to review data for specific points along the plot line. The data will be shown in the text boxes on the right hand side of the form.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Add_to_Model_from_Template.htm | Add to Model from Template -->

# Add to Model from Template

Use the Edit menu > Add to Model from Template command to add objects to a model using a template.

1. Click the Edit menu > Add to Model From Template command to display the same [New Model form](../File/New_Model.md) as is displayed when the File menu > New Model command is used.
2. Click on the template to be added to the model.
3. Type in the parameters in the edit boxes to specify the number, height, width and so forth of the objects being added to the model.
4. Depending on the template selected, check the Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin and click the Edit Grid button or click on the Locate Origin button to access the [Define Grid Data](../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md)  or [Coordinate System](../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) forms, respectively. Use those forms to define the origin and orientation of the templates being added. Those forms allow the added templates to be shifted and rotated relative to the global coordinate system. By default, the template models are added at the origin of the global coordinate system.
5. Click OK.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem T](../../Example_Problems/Problem_T.md) and [Problem U](../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Change_Labels.htm | Change Labels -->

# Change Labels

Form:  Interactive Name Change

By default, the names (labels) of the objects and all defined entities (loads, properties, and the like) in the model are sequentially designated by the program using alphanumeric characters. Use the Edit menu > Change Labels command to access the Interactive Name Change form and change the name of any of the named items.

1. Choose the object or defined entity to be relabeled from the Item Type drop-down list (e.g., Analysis Cases, Combination Definitions, Element Labels-Area, Element Labels-Frame, and so forth).
2. Change the labels for the selected Item Type using auto relabeling or by direct entry.

Note: The current labeling scheme is shown in the Current Name column of the table displayed in the Name List for {Item Type} area of the form.

1. - Auto Relabeling.
   - 1. Specify a labeling scheme using the options available in the Auto Relabel Controls area of the form
     1. - Prefix edit box. If desired, specify numbers or letters as a prefix for the numbering sequence. For example, to specify an automatic numbering sequence of A2, A3, A4 and so forth, type A in this edit box.
        - Next Number edit box. Use this edit box to specify the starting number for the new numbering sequence.  
            
          For example, if the numbering currently starts with 1 and you want it to start with 10, type 10 in this edit box. Depending on the selections made for the Increment, First Relabel Order and Second Relabel Order options (see Note below), after the sub-command chosen in Step b (below) has been executed, the cell in the New Number column opposite from the Current Number of 1 will change to 10, Current Number 2 will change to 11, the Current Number 3 will change to 12 and so on.
        - Increment edit box. Use this edit box to specify an increment for the numbering sequence. For example, type 2 in this edit box if you want the sequence to be 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and so forth, assuming a starting number (i.e., Next Number) of 1, or 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 assuming a starting number of 2, and so on.
        - First Relabel Order drop-down list. Select the "direction" for starting the relabeling sequence by selecting the X, Y, or Z coordinate.
        - Second Relabel Order drop-down list. Select the next direction for continuing the relabeling sequence.

Note:  By default, objects are numbered first in the X direction, then the Y direction, then the Z direction. If the New Name column presents you with a surprising sequence after executing Step b (below), verify that the labeling order is as it should be.

1. 1. 1. - Minimum Number Digits edit box. Type a value in this edit box to specify the formatting for the numbering scheme. For example, if 3 is entered into this edit box, the numeric portion of the labeling scheme will use three digits, such that if the Current Name is 1, the relabeled number will be written as 001. Relabeling in this manner can be helpful for sorting.

1. - 2. Click the Edit menu > Auto Relabel command on the Interactive Name Change form and choose the All in List sub command, or select items in the table displayed in the Name List for {Item Type} area of the form, then click the Edit menu > Auto Relabel > Highlighted in List command.

        - The All in List command will change all labeling.
        - The Highlighted in List command will change only those items you have selected.
   - Direct Entry. Type the new name in the New Name column in the table shown in the Name List for {Item Type} area of the form.

3. Click the OK button to complete the renaming and close the form.

Note:  Objects may be selected before using the Edit menu > Change Labels command to reduce the number of items listed in the table shown in the Name List for {Item Type} display area on the Interactive Name Change form.

- List Names of Selected Elements Only check box. If objects were selected before the Edit menu > Change Labels command was used, this check box will be checked and the Name List for {Item Type} area of the form will display a table showing the labels associated with the selected objects when that type of object has been selected in the Item Type drop-down list. Unchecking this check box will display, for the selected Item Type, the labels for all objects, not just the selected objects.

The Interactive Name Change form has the following menu commands:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Command | Action |
| Edit |  |
| Cut | Allows an item in the New Name column to be cut and copied to the Windows Clipboard for subsequent pasting using the Paste command. |
| Copy | Allows an item in the New Name column to be copied to the Windows Clipboard for subsequent pasting using the Paste command. |
| Paste | Allows an item in the New Name column that has been cut or copied to the Windows Clipboard to be pasted into a location you specify in the New Name column. |
| Delete | Deletes the items selected in the New Name column. |
| Copy All in Data Grid | Copies the entire table in the Name List for {Item Type} area of the form to the Windows Clipboard for subsequent pasting into another program, such as Microsoft Excel. |
| Find | Accesses the [Find and Replace form](Find_and_Replace.md). |
| Replace | Accesses the [Find and Replace form](Find_and_Replace.md). |
| Reset to Current Names | Resets the entries in the New Name column to match the entries in the Current Name column. |
| Auto Relabel |  |
| All in List | Updates the labeling for all of the named objects or defined entities as specified by changes made in the New Name column. |
| Highlighted in List | Updates the labeling for the selected named objects or defined entities as specified by changes made in the New Name column. |
| View |  |
| Hide Selected Rows | Hides the selected rows in the table. |
| Show All Rows | Unhides any hidden rows to display all rows in the table. |

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem S](../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Cut_Copy_and_Paste.htm | Cut Copy and Paste -->

# Cut, Copy, and Paste

The Edit menu > Cut, Edit menu > Copy and Edit menu > Paste commands work similar to the standard cut, copy and paste Windows commands. An object(s) must be selected before the command is used.

The entire structure or any selected part of the structure may be cut or copied and then pasted back into the model at any user-specified location.

Note: The Cut and Copy commands cut and copy only the geometry and connectivity of the selected object to the Windows clipboard. Other assignments made to the selected object are not copied using these commands; copying assignments can be accomplishing using the [Assign menu > Copy Assigns and Assign menu > Paste Assigns commands](../Assign/Copy_Assigns.md).

TIP:  The [Edit menu > Replicate](Replicate.md) command can be used to quickly replicate objects in the model using linear, radial or mirror options.  Also the File menu > Export and File menu > Import commands can be used to export model data to a spreadsheet where the data can be modified quickly using a spreadsheet program before the data is imported back into the model.

Members of the model can be deleted by selecting them and pressing the Delete button on the keyboard or using the Edit menu > Delete command or its associated toolbar button.

# Divide Solids

Form:  Divide Selected Solids

Use the Edit menu > Divide Solids command to divide solid objects on all faces.

1. Select one or more solid objects that need to be divided.
2. Click the Edit menu > Divide Solids command to access the Divide Selected Solids form.
3. Specify the number of solid objects between [faces 1 and 3, 2 and 4, and 5 and 6](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Sign_Convention.md) into which the object should be divided using the Num. Solids Between 1 and 3, Num. Solids Between 2 and 4, and Num. Solids Between 5 and 6 edit boxes.
4. Click the OK button.

Note: The number of solid objects between faces 1 and 3, 2 and 4, and 5 and 6 should be similar.

# Add Point to Area Edge

Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Add Point to Area Edges command to add colinear points to the edges of area objects.

1. Click the Set Display Options button ![](../../../assets/images/Images/Set%20Display%20Options%20button.jpg) and uncheck the Invisible check box in the Joints area of the Display Options for Active Window form to turn on the display of the points in the active window. This step is optional but recommended to facilitate use of this feature.
2. Select the area objects to which points are to be added to the edges.
3. Click the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Add Point to Area Edges command. The program will automatically add points to the edges at the midpoint between the existing points of the selected object. Repeat Steps 2 and 3 to add as many points as needed. The [Edit menu > Edit Areas > Remove Points from Area command](Remove_Points_from_Area.md) can be used to remove the added points.

![](../../../assets/images/Images/Add%20Points%20to%20Area%20Edges.JPG)

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Convert_Current_Mesh_to_User_Mesh.htm | Convert Current Mesh to User Mesh -->

# Convert Current Mesh to User Mesh

Select a mesh of area object(s) and use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Convert Current Mesh to User Mesh command to convert the SAP2000 generated mesh into a user mesh. When converted to a user mesh the mesh will be locked, i.e., no changes can be made to the mesh. If a revision to the mesh is required, the user mesh must first be removed by using the Edit menu > Edit Areas > [Remove User Mesh From Area Object](Remove_User_Mesh_from_Area_Object.md) command before a new mesh can be assigned.

The conversion to a user mesh may be verified by right clicking on the area objects and reviewing the Area Meshing Options on the Assignments tab of the Area Information form.

Note: The Edit menu > Edit Areas> Convert Current Mesh to User Mesh command will only be available for a selected area object if the current mesh is displayed. The user mesh may be displayed by going to the View menu > Set Display Options command and checking the User Mesh checkbox under Areas region on the **Object Options**tab.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Divide_Areas.htm | Divide Areas -->

# Divide Areas

Form:  Divide Selected Areas

SAP2000 allows area objects to be divided into smaller objects in the object-based model, and meshed into elements in the analysis model. Dividing the object is accomplished using the Edit menu > Edit Areas> Divide Areas command. Meshing an area object is accomplished using the [Assign menu > Area > Automatic Area Mesh command](../../Assign/Area/Area_Automatic_Area_Mesh.md).

This topic addresses dividing area objects for use in the object-based model.

1. Select the area objects to be divided.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Areas> Divide Areas command to access the Divide Selected Areas form.
3. Choose the option to specify how the object is to be divided. The [Area Object Dividing or Meshing](../../Assign/Area_Object_Dividing_or_Meshing.md) topic explains how the program works and uses illustrations to show the effects of the various options.

Note:  Dividing an area object is performed on one object at a time.

1. - Divide Area Into This Number of Objects (Quads and Triangles Only) options and Along Edge from Point 1 to 2 and Along Edge from Point 1 to 3 edit boxes. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided into the number of objects specified using the edit box for each edge. The program adds points to the adjacent edges, at equally spaced intervals, and then automatically adds the same number of points along the opposite edges so that dividing lines can be drawn between the opposing points on the edges to create the specified number of objects.
   - Divide Area Into Objects of This Maximum Size (Quads and Triangles Only) and Along Edge from Point 1 to 2 and Along Edge from Point 1 to 3 edit boxes. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided into n number of objects of the maximum length specified in the edit box for each of the adjacent edges. The program adds points along each edge at equally spaced intervals such that the length of any of the resulting divided objects does not exceed the length specified in the edit boxes. The length specified determines the number of objects to be created and thus the number of points added to each edge.
   - Divide Area Based On Points On Area Edges (Quads and Triangles Only), Points Determined From options. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided based on specified lines and points. The specified lines and points must lie in the plane of the area object. The program will not extend the selected line to make it intersect an edge; the selected line must already intersect an edge of the selected object. These options may be used in combination.
   1. - Intersection of Visible Straight Grid Lines With Area Edges check box. Check this check box to specify that points be added, and thus the object divided, at the intersection of the visible straight grid lines with the edges of the selected area object. Use the [View menu > Show Grid command](../../View/Show_Grid.md) to display grid lines.
      - Intersection of Selected Straight Line Objects With Area Edges check box. Check this check box to specify that points be added, and thus the object divided, at the intersection of the edge of the selected area object with a selected straight line object that has been drawn or defined to cross the selected object's edge.
      - Selected Point Objects On Area Edges check box. Check this check box to specify that the object be divided based on the point drawn or defined on the object's edge.  Note that the point object and the area object must both be selected and lie in the same plane.

Note:  If a point is being drawn on the edge of the object before using point-related options, the [Draw menu > Snap To > Lines and Edges command](../../Draw/Snap_To.md) may be helpful in placing the point accurately on the object's edge.

1. - Divide Area Using Cookie Cut Based On Selected Straight Line Objects option. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided based on a selected straight line object. For this option, the selected line object does not need to intersect with the edge of the selected area object. If the selected line object does not intersect with the selected object's edge or fully transect the selected area object, the program places a point on the object's edge along the projected path of the selected line object. Note that the selected line object and selected area object must lie in the same plane.
   - Divide Area Using Cookie Cut Based On Selected Points Objects option and Rotation of Cut Lines From Area Local Axes (Deg) edit box. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided based on a selected point object. For this option, the selected point object does not need to lie on the edge of the selected area object. The program "draws dividing lines" that pass through the selected point to proportionately placed points on the area object's opposing edge or edges. Use the edit box to specify the rotation in degrees of the "dividing line" from the original local 1 and 2 axes of the selected area object. Positive rotations appear counterclockwise when the local 3 axis is pointing toward you.
   - Divide Area Using General Divide Tool Based On Selected Points and Lines option, Maximum Size of Divided Object edit box. Use this option to specify that the selected object be divided based on selected point or line objects and the maximum length for the resulting divided object, as entered in the edit box. For this option, the selected point or line object must lie within the same plane as the selected area object and lie within the selected object (i.e., the point can not lie on the edge of the object and the line can not cross the edge of the area object or have its end points on the edge of the area object). The program divides the selected object into n number of objects based on the maximum size specified in the edit box and the locations of the selected points and lines within the area object.  See the [Area Object Dividing or Meshing](../../Assign/Area_Object_Dividing_or_Meshing.md) topic for more clarification.

4. Choose an option to specify the Local Axes for Added Points:

   - Make same on Edge if adjacent corners have same local axes definition check box. Use this check box to specify that the local axes definitions for new points added along the edges of an area object are the same as an adjacent area object corner point if the local axes definition for the adjacent corners are identical.
   - Make same on Face if all corners have same local axes definition check box. Use this check box to specify that the local axes definition for the new points on the face of the area object are set the same as a corner point of the area object if the local axes definitions for all of the corner points of the area object are identical.
5. Choose an option to specify Restraints and Constraints For Added Points:

   - Add on Edge when restraints/constraints exist at adjacent corner points (Applies if added edge point and adjacent corner points have same local axes definition) check box. Use this check box to specify that a restraint degree of freedom (or constraint) is added to new points on the edges of the area object if both adjacent corners have that degree of freedom restrained (constrained) and the local axes definitions for the adjacent corners and the new point are identical.
   - Add on Faces when restraints/constraints exist at all corner points (Applies if added face point and all corner points have same local axes definition) check box. Use this check box to specify that a restraint degree of freedom (or constraint) is added to new points on the face of the area object if all area object corners have that degree of freedom restrained (constrained) and the local axes definitions of all corners and the new points are identical.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem M](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_M.md), [Problem S](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md), [Problem U](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md) and [Problem Z](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Z.md).

## See Also

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Expand_Shrink_Areas.htm | Expand_Shrink Areas -->

# Expand/Shrink Areas

Form:  Expand/Shrink Areas

Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Expand/Shrink Areas command to access the Expand/Shrink Areas form. Use that form to specify offsets for area edges to make areas larger or smaller.

1. Select the object(s) to be made larger or smaller by (a) clicking on the object (which selects all edges of the object), (b) clicking on the edge(s) of the object(s), or (c) clicking on both the object(s) and a point(s) that defines the object(s). Both the object and a point must be selected because a point may be used to define more than one object.
2. Click the  Edit menu > Edit Areas > Expand/Shrink Areas command to access the Expand/Shrink Areas form.
3. In the Offset area of the form, specify the distance that the selected edge(s) or point(s) is to be offset in the Offset Distance edit box. A positive value expands the area and a negative value shrinks the area. The offset distance is measured perpendicular to the area edge.
4. In the Expand/Shrink Options area, select the appropriate option:

   - Offset All Area Edges option. Use this option to offset all edges of the area object the distance specified in the Offset Distance edit box. Note that for this command, an object is considered selected if any single point or edge of the object has been selected.
   - Offset Selected Area Edges Only option. With an edge(s) selected, use this option  to offset the selected edge(s) of the area object the distance specified in the Offset Distance edit box.
   - Offset Selected Points of Selected Areas Only option. With a point(s) selected, use  this option to offset the selected point(s) of the area object the distance specified in the Offset Distance edit box.  The offset for points is measured along a bisector angle formed by the area edges adjacent to the selected point(s).

# Explode User Mesh to Shells

Select an area object(s) containing a user mesh and use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Explode User Mesh to Areas command to replace each internal element in the user mesh with a new area object of equivalent shape and size. The new area objects will have the same assignments as the original area object selected for explosion.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Merge_Areas.htm | Merge Areas -->

# Merge Areas

Form:  Merge Two Polys

Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Merge Areas command to access the Merge Two Polys form. Use that form to specify how the assignments for the individual areas will be treated.

1. Select the areas to be merged. Note that selected areas essentially in the same plane and sharing a common edge or with overlapping area edges will be merged. Areas that lie one on top of the other or that share no common or overlapping edges will not be merged, and an error message will display indicating that no objects to be merged have been selected.

![](../../../assets/images/Images/Merge%20Areas.JPG)

2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Merge Areas command to access the Merge Two Polys form.
3. In the Keep Assignments for Selected Area portion of the form, choose an area that has assignments suitable for the merged area. That is, the assignments of the chosen area will apply to the merged area. For example, assume overlapping areas 1 and 2 have been selected, and area 1 has an [area section assignment](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md) of ASEC1 and area 2 has an area section assignment of ASEC 2. If 1 (area 1) is selected on the Merge Two Polys form, the merged area will have a section assignment of ASEC1. If 2 (area 2) is selected, the merged area will have a section assignment of ASEC2. Use the Show Area button associated with each area object to access the Area Information form for that object. With that form displayed, click on the Assignments tab to view any assignments made to the object.

Remove Colinear Points Along Merged Area Edges check box. When objects with overlapping edges are merged, the program adds points where the edges intersect. If this check box is unchecked, those additional points remain as part of the object. When the check box is check, the program removes those additional points when the merge is complete.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Merge_Shells_to_Create_User_Mesh.htm | Merge Shells to Create User Mesh -->

# Merge Areas to Create User Mesh

Select two or more area objects and use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Merge Areas to Create User Mesh command to combine multiple area objects into a single area object with an internal user mesh. User mesh denotes a mesh based on user specified geometry. Assignments for the new object will be the same as the assignments of the area object that was first created. The assignments for the merged area object should be verified by right clicking on the object and reviewing information on the Area Information form.

Note: Only area objects with 3 or 4 nodes may be merged due to the reason that the mesh is based on the boundaries of the selected area objects, and meshing uses 3 and 4 node elements.

The area objects selected should lie in the same plane to ensure an appropriate merge. Changing the area object geometry will not alter the user mesh, resulting in a mesh that may no longer be appropriate.

The user mesh may be viewed by going to the View menu > Set Display Options command and checking the User Mesh checkbox under Areas region on the **Object Options**tab.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Areas/Remove_Points_from_Area.htm | Remove Points from Area -->

# Remove Points from Area

Use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Remove Point from Area command to remove selected points from the edges of area objects.

1. Click the Set Display Options button ![](../../../assets/images/Images/Set%20Display%20Options%20button.jpg) and uncheck the Invisible check box in the Joints area of the Display Options for Active Window form to turn on the display of the points in the active window.
2. Click on the area object from which points are to be removed from the edges.
3. Click on the point(s) to be removed.
4. Click the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Remove Point from Area command. The program will remove the selected point (s). If a point was not colinear with the remaining (unselected) points, the area object will be reshaped.

![](../../../assets/images/Images/Remove%20Points%20from%20Areas.JPG)


---

# Remove User Mesh from Area Object

Select an area object(s) containing a user mesh and use the Edit menu > Edit Areas > Remove User Mesh from Area Object command to remove the internal element user mesh that was previously stored as part of the area object.

The user mesh may be viewed by going to the View menu > Set Display Options command and checking the User Mesh checkbox under Areas region on the **Object Options**tab.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Lines/Divide_Frames.htm | Divide Frames -->

# Divide Frames

Form:  Divide Selected Frames

Use the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Divide Frames command to access the Divide Selected Frames form. The form has options to divide a frame into user-specified segments of user-defined size, or break a frame at intersections with selected frames and joints.

Divide the selected frame into user specified segments of user defined sizes as follows:

1. Select the frame objects to be divided.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Divide Frames command to access the Divide Selected Frames form.
3. Select the "Divide into" option.
4. Type in the number of objects the frame object is to be divided into.
5. Type in the ratio of the last object to the first, if the division is not to be in equal lengths.
6. Click the OK button.

Break a frame that intersects with selected frames and joints as follows:

1. Select the frame objects to be broken into the multiple objects and also select the intersecting objects or joints.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Divide Frames command to access the Divide Selected Frames form.
3. Select the Break at intersections with selected Joints, Frames, Area Edges and Solid Edges option.
4. Click the OK button.

EXAMPLE

![](../../../assets/images/Images/BREAK_shg.gif)

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem J](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_J.md), and  [Problem W](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_W.md).

## See Also

[Frame - Automatic Frame Mesh](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Automatic_Frame_Mesh.md)

Form:  Tendon Data for Line Object

Use the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Edit Tendon Profile command to edit a line object drawn as a tendon.

# Join Frames

1. Select the frame objects to be joined.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Join Frames command. This will immediately join the selected frame objects into a single object and remove unused joints remaining after the joining process.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Lines/Trim_Extend_Frames.htm | Trim Extend Frames -->

# Trim/Extend Frames

Form: Trim/Extend Selected Frames

The Edit menu > Edit Lines > Trim/Extend Frames command can be used to lengthen frame elements that are too short, or shorten frame element that are too long.

1. Select the frame to be extended or trimmed along with its end points.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Lines > Trim/Extend Frames command to access the Trim/Extend Selected Frames form.
3. Choose the appropriate option:  Trim Frames or Extend Frames.
4. Click the OK button.

SAP2000 will lengthen or shorten the frame element to the nearest joint/grid intersection.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Points/Add_Grid_at_Selected_Points.htm | Add Grid at Selected Points -->

# Add Grid at Selected Points

Form:  Add Grid Lines at Selected Point

After selecting one or more point objects in the model, use the Edit menu > Edit Points > Add Grid at Selected Points command to access the Add Grid Lines at Selected Point form and add grid lines in the current coordinate/grid system.

Use the options on the form to specify that the new grid line(s) be parallel to the X, Y, or Z axis in the current coordinate system. A new grid line will be added at each selected point.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Points/Align_Points.htm | Align Points -->

# Align Points

Form:  Align Selected
Points

Selected points may be aligned with the specified X, Y or Z coordinate
or to the nearest line using the Edit menu >
Edit Points > Align Points command. Select the axis and specify
the coordinates of that axis where the selected points are to be aligned.

1. Select the points to be aligned.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit
   Points > Align Points command to access the Align
   Selected Points form.
3. Choose the appropriate alignment option. Only one
   option can be selected (i.e., the options are mutually exclusive):

   - Align Points
     to X-Ordinate, Align Points
     to Y-Ordinate, Align Points
     to Z-Ordinate will align
     points relative to the X, Y, and Z coordinates, respectively.
   - Align Points
     to Nearest Line will align the selected points along the
     nearest line (not a selected line).
4. Click the OK button.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Points/Connect.htm | Connect -->

# Connect

The Edit menu > Edit Points > Connect command can be used to connect all selected objects that have been [Disconnected](Disconnect.md) from each other or that were connected to independent joints. When objects are reconnected, the independent joints are collapsed into a common joint that is shared by all the combined objects.

1. Select the objects to be connected to each other.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Points > Connect command.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Points/Disconnect.htm | Disconnect -->

# Disconnect

All objects connected to each other normally share a common joint. The Edit menu > Edit Points > Disconnect command will break off the objects from the joint and will add duplicate joints to each of those objects.

1. Select the joints to be disconnected from the objects.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Points > Disconnect command.

Tip: This is a very useful command for some special modeling conditions. This feature adds separate joints to objects sharing common joints. After the joint is disconnected, special constraints may be added to those joints. For example, use this feature to add separate joints and then (a) specify [moment release constraints](../../Assign/Joint/Joint_Constraints.md) between two adjacent edges of shell objects, or (b) add a zero length non-linear [link](../../Assign/Link_Support/Link_Support_Properties.md) using separate joints at the same location.

## See Also

[Connect](Connect.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Edit_Points/Merge_Joints.htm | Merge Joints -->

# Merge Joints

Form:  Merge Selected Points

Joints within the default [Auto Merge Tolerance](../../Options/Dimensions_Tolerances.md) are automatically merged. Those Joints that lie outside this tolerance may be merged as follows:

1. Select the joints to be merged.
2. Click the Edit menu > Edit Points > Merge Joints command to display the Merge Selected Joints form.
3. Accept or change the Merge Tolerance.
4. Click the OK button.

Hints:  
This is a very useful command for merging two models.  
  
If elements are drawn with [Snaps](../../Draw/Snap_To.md) turned off, there may be extraneous joints at common locations. Those extraneous joints may be easily eliminated using this command.  
  
Models developed in CAD programs may have beam joints drawn 6 inches or so away from column joints. This is a powerful option to merge beam joints to column joints in such models imported from CAD.

# Explode User Mesh to Solids

Select a solid object(s) containing a user mesh and use the Edit menu > Edit solids > Explode User Mesh to Solids command to replace each internal element in the user mesh with a new solid object of equivalent shape and size. The new solid objects will have the same assignments as the original solid object selected for explosion.
