<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Extrude.htm | Extrude -->

# Extrude

Form:  Extrude Points to Frames/Cables, Extrude Lines to Areas, Extrude Areas to Solids, Shell to Shell Extrusion, Line to Line Extrusion, Define Extrusion Path

Use the Edit menu > Extrude command to sweep selected objects through space to create new objects of higher dimension or to convert lines to areas and areas to solids with the same thickness as the original line or area object. The process of extrusion increases the dimensional space of an existing object by one. In other words, line objects are of one dimension that can be generated from a dimensionless object, the point object. In a similar manner, a two-dimensional object, area or plate/shell can be generated from a one-dimensional object, the line object. This feature is especially suited to creating solid objects from plate/shells, plate/shell objects from beams and beams/columns from points/nodes.

1. Select the object to be extruded.
2. Click the Edit menu > Extrude command and select the appropriate sub-command

1. - Extrude Points to Frames/Cables. This command accesses the Extrude Points to Lines form (see Item 3).
   - Extrude Lines to Areas. This command accesses the Extrude Lines to Areas form (see Item 3).
   - Convert Lines to Areas. The command immediately converts line objects into area objects of the same thickness (this is not extrusion in the sense of sweeping the object through space).
   - Convert Lines to Solids. The command immediately converts line objects into solid objects of the same thickness (this is not extrusion in the sense of sweeping the object through space).
   - Extrude Areas to Solids. This command accesses the Extrude Lines to Areas form (see Item 3).
   - Convert Areas to Solids. The command immediately converts area objects into solid objects of the same thickness (this is not extrusion in the sense of sweeping the object through space). When converting area objects into solid objects, two solid objects are created for each area object, each with half the thickness from the section property of the area object.
   - Add Solids Between Areas. This command accesses the Shell to Shell Extrusion form. Use the form to specify the number of divisions in the solid along the 1, 2, and 3 axis.
   - Add Areas between Lines. This command accesses the Line to Line Extrusion form.  When multiple lines have been selected before this command is used, the program must determine between which two lines the areas will be added. The program sorts the lines based on the sorting direction, and then draws the areas between adjacent lines in the direction specified.

3. If the Extrude Points to Lines form, Extrude Lines to Areas form or Extrude Areas to Solids form is displayed, choose the Linear, Radial, or Advanced tab and specify the appropriate parameters. The parameters will extrude the object linearly, radially, or along any defined path. Specify the number of new objects to be created during the extrusion process, and specify if the original object of lower dimension should be retained or deleted.

Linear Extrusion Tab

1. - Increment Data. For linear extrusion, specify the increment distance along the X-axis (dx), the increment distance along the Y-axis (dy), the increment along the Z-axis (dz), and the number of times the object is to be extruded. The object is then extruded the specified number of times, each time incrementing the global X, Y and Z coordinates by the specified dx, dy and dz.
   - Delete Source check box. A Delete Source check box is provided on the Extrude Lines to Areas and Extrude Areas to Solids form. Checking this check box will delete the lines or areas used to create the extrusion. Leaving the check box unchecked will keep the source.

Example:

![](../../assets/images/Images/Extrude%20Linear.bmp)

Radial Extrusion Tab

A typical use of this type of extrusion is to generate a cylindrical surface from radial extrusion of a single line about the central axis of the cylinder.

1. - Rotate about Axis. Choose the axis about which the radial extrusion will occur.
   - Rotate about Point. Specify the coordinates of the point about which the radial rotation is desired.
   - Increment Data. Specify the Incremental Data in the form of an Angle of rotation, Number of extrusions and the Total Rise along the axis of rotation. The rotation angle is input in degrees. Angles are measured from the positive global X-axis. Positive angles appear counterclockwise when viewed from above.

The object is then extruded the specified number of times, each time incrementing the location of the objects by the specified rotation angle.

1. - Delete Source check box. A Delete Source check box is provided on the Extrude Lines to Areas and Extrude Areas to Solids form. Checking this check box will delete the points, lines or areas used to create the extrusion. Leaving the check box unchecked will keep the source.

Example:

![](../../assets/images/Images/Extrude%20Radial.bmp)

Advanced Extrusion Tab

Points, lines and areas can be extruded along any defined curve. The extrusion path may be defined by specifying the Global X, Y and Z coordinates. Twist, skew and scaling may also be applied to the extruding entities.

- - Absolute Coordinates option. Choose this option to use the global coordinates.
  - Relative Coordinates option. Choose this option to specify starting coordinates for X, Y, and Z.
  - Define/Modify Path button. Click the Define/Modify Path button to access the Define Extrusion Path form. Use the Define Extrusion Path form to specify the twist, skew and scaling for the curves along which the entity will be extruded.

- Extrusion Path spreadsheet. The path for the extrusion can be specified by typing values directly into the appropriate cells.
- Quick Paths area.

- Type of Quick Path drop-down list. This drop-down list displays a number of typical curves that may be used to define the extrusion path without specifying the actual coordinates. Depending on the type of curve chosen, specify the additional necessary data, such as Start and End X, Y, and Z coordinates, Center coordinates, Third Point coordinates, Number of Divisions (i.e., smoothness constant) and the like.

Important:  After making a selection from the drop-down list be sure to click the Insert button to "insert" the data for the selected curve type into the Extrusion Path spreadsheet.

- From General Ref Line option. This option is included in the drop-down list if a [General Reference Line](../Draw/Draw_Edit_General_Reference_Line.md) has been drawn in the model. When this option is selected, the replication will occur relative to the General Reference Line, and the X, Y, and Z coordinates will be automatically specified on the Extrude {Object Type} to {Object Type} form when the OK button is clicked to close the Define Extrusion Path form.

Note:  If after closing the Define Extrusion Path form the OK button is not available on the Extrude {Object Type} to {Object Type} form, try changing to another view (XY, XZ, YZ).  
  
Also, the From General Ref Line option can only be used with the Relative Coordinates options. If the Absolute Coordinates Option is chosen, the program will ignore the General Reference Line.

1. - Delete Source check box. A Delete Source check box is provided on the Extrude Lines to Areas and Extrude Areas to Solids form. Checking this check box will delete the lines or areas used to create the extrusion. Leaving the check box unchecked will keep the source.

# Find and Replace

- Find. Type the text or data to be found and click the Find Next button. Click the Done button to close the form. Use the Match entire cell only and Match case check boxes as necessary to establish elementary search criteria. Use the drop-down list to specify that the search proceed down or up the table.
- Replace. Type the text or data to be found. Type the text or data to replace the found text. Click the Find Next button. Click the Done button to close the form. Use the Match entire cell only and Match case check boxes as necessary to establish elementary search criteria. Use the drop-down list to specify that the search proceed down or up the table.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Interactive_Database_Editing.htm | Interactive Database Editing -->

# Interactive Database Editing

Form: Choose Tables for Interactive Editing

Use the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command to create or edit model definition data in tabular format rather than in graphical mode or using the Draw and Assign menu forms. Only model definition data (not analysis results or design data) can be edited this way. The model must be [unlocked](../Options/Locking_and_Unlocking_the_Model.md) to use this feature.

1. Click the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command to access the Choose Tables for Interactive Editing form.
2. Check the check boxes associated with the data type (structure, geometry, properties, loads, load cases, joint assigns, frame/cable assigns) that is to be edited. The types of data selected determine the tables available for editing. If objects are selected before the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command, only the selected objects will be available in tables that contain object-specific data.
3. Click the OK button to access the [Interactive Database Editing](Interactive_Database_Editing_Form.md) form that is used to complete the editing operation.

Important: Do not use interactive table editing to rename objects or other defined entities! Instead, use the [Edit menu > Change Labels command](Change_Labels.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Interactive_Database_Editing_Form.htm | Interactive Database Editing Form -->

# Interactive Database Editing - {Table Name} Form

Use the Interactive Database Editing form to make any additions, deletions, or modifications to the tables selected using  the Choose Tables for Interactive Editing form. The changes can then be applied to the model and shown in the display area of the SAP2000 window. The Interactive Database Editing form has a display area and various menu options and buttons that can be used to add records to or delete records from the table shown in the display area, copy records, move records, and find or find and replace user-specified data.

- {Table Name} drop-down list. Use the drop-down list near the top of the form to select the table to be edited. If the alternative method of displaying the form is used (see above), only one table name will be listed in this drop-down list.
- Spreadsheet area. Modify records in the table by typing directly in the cells, including using numerical formulas (e.g., 2+3/4). Right-click within any field (column) and a menu of pertinent operations will appear. The menu includes the Field Description option, which when clicked displays a form that shows a description for the item. If the field expects numeric input, the menu includes the [Calculator](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Calculator.md) option, which can be used to speed data entry when formulae are involved. If the field expects text input, use the View menu > Drop-Down List command to display a drop-down list of all acceptable values for the selected cell.

Important: Objects and other defined entities are identified by their names in the tables. If you change any names, those items will be considered as new when the tables are brought back into the model. Do not use interactive table editing to rename objects or other defined entities! Instead, use the Edit menu > Change Labels command.

The units used for a given field can be changed by clicking on the cell just below the column heading. Select the new units from the drop-down list that appears. Changing the units for one field will change the units for other related fields. The units chosen while interactively editing tables are temporary. All values will be converted back to the current model units when the editing is applied to the model.

- Apply to Model button. Click the Apply to Model button or the File menu > Apply to Model command to accept the changes. Or click the Done button or the File menu > Done (Close DB and Return to Model) command and respond No when prompted to cancel the changes.

The Interactive Database Editing form has the following commands and buttons to help edit the selected table. Some of these commands can also be accessed by right clicking in a display cell.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command | Button | Action |
| File menu |  |  |
| Apply to Model | Apply to Model | Applies the changes made in the table to the model and closes the Interactive Database Editing form. |
| Done (Close DB and Return to Model) | Done | Closes the Interactive Database Editing form without changing the model, unless No is selected in response to the prompt to cancel the changes. |
| Excel menu |  |  |
| Send Database Table to Excel | To Excel | Sends the table to Microsoft Excel, which launches automatically and displays the table. Excel's spreadsheet functionality can then be used to edit the table. After editing the data using Excel, do not close Excel. Instead, return to SAP2000 and select the From Excel button to save the changes or the Cancel Excel button to discard them; Excel will close automatically. |
| Receive Database Table from Excel | From Excel | With Excel open, return to SAP2000 and click the From Excel button to bring a table into SAP2000 that had been sent to Excel from SAP2000 using the To Excel button. Excel will close automatically. |
| Cancel Database Table in Excel | Cancel Excel | With Excel open, return to SAP2000 and click the Cancel Excel button to discard changes made to a table that had been sent to Excel from SAP2000 using the To Excel button. Excel will automatically be closed. |
| Edit menu |  |  |
| Undo and Redo |  | Undo will undo the last action. Redo will redo the last action. |
| Cut, Copy, Paste | Copy, Paste | Select a cell(s) to be cut, copied, or pasted using standard Windows operations. |
| Paste Insert | Paste Insert | Use with cut or copy to paste the cut or copied cell(s) to the row in the table above the selected cell(s). |
| Paste Append | Paste Append | Use with cut or copy to paste the cut or copied cell(s) to the end of the table. |
| Delete |  | Deletes the contents of the selected cell, but not the cell. |
| Delete Record | Delete Record | Deletes the selected record/row. |
| Insert Blank Records |  | Inserts a blank record/row above the selected record/row in the table. |
| Append Blank Records | Append Blank Rows | Adds a blank record/row to the end of the table. |
| Move Record Up | Up Arrow | Moves the selected record/row up in the table. |
| Move Record Down | Down Arrow | Moves the selected record/row down in the table. |
| Find | Find | Displays the [Find and Replace form](Find_and_Replace.md). |
| Replace | Replace | Displays the [Find and Replace form](Find_and_Replace.md). |
| Align (General Left, Center, Right) | None | Use the Align options to align text in the selected cell(s). |
| View menu |  |  |
| Maximize | None | Toggles the Interactive Database Editing form from the default size to fill the entire computer screen. Functions similar to the Windows minimize/maximize feature. |
| Hide Selected Column | None | Hides the selected columns. |
| Show All Columns | None | Shows any columns that have been hidden using the Hide Selected Column command. |
| Autofit Column | None | Changes the column width to accommodate the cell with the most characters, which may result in the column being narrowed. |
| Field Description | None | Displays a form that describes the selected item in the table. |
| Element Information | None | Displays an information form when an object is selected. |
| Calculator | None | Accesses the [Calculator](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Calculator.md) form to speed data entry when formulae are required. The cursor must be in a cell that accepts such entry for this command to be available. |
| Drop-Down List | None | Displays a drop-down list of all acceptable values for the selected cell when the expected data type is text. |
| Options menu |  |  |
| Overwrite Mode | None | Toggles the overwrite mode on and off. When the overwrite mode is on, text typed in the cell will replace the existing text. When the overwrite mode is off, text typed into the cell will be inserted where the cursor is located. |
| Show/Hide | None | Toggles the display of the buttons on the right-hand side of the form on and off. Hiding the buttons, expands the display area for the table. |
| Highlight Table Changes | None | Toggles the highlighting of changes off and on. |
| Advanced Import Options | Advanced Options | Accesses the [Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing](Interactive_Editing_Tabular_Database_Import_Options_Form.md) form. Use the form to specify how the data should be integrated back into the database after editing the individual tables. |
| Always Display Log After Import | None | Toggles the display of the [Interactive Database Import Log form](Interactive_Database_Import_Log_Form.md) on or off after the edited table has been reintroduced to the model database. |

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Interactive Database Editing - {Table Name} form as follows:   1. Click the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command to display the Choose Tables for Interactive Editing form. 2. Select the table to be edited by clicking the associated check box. 3. Click the OK button to display the Interactive Database Editing form.   Alternatively, after Step 2, expand the tree associated with a table type by clicking on the plus (+) symbol preceding the table type name. Continue expanding the tree until the table appears (Table: {Name}. Right click on the table name and select Interactively Edit Table from the resulting drop-down list. This method can be used to display one table at a time. |

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Interactive_Database_Import_Log_Form.htm | Interactive Database Import Log Form -->

# Interactive Database Import Log Form

The Interactive Database Import Log form has a large area that provides a summary of the import data, including the source file, the import type and options, the types of tables/data to be imported, and any error messages, warnings, or information used to help resolve conflicts between the imported data and the elements, objects and other items present in an existing model or data that has previously been imported into a model.

Note:  In the Database Import Summary Data area, the first entry likely will refer to the "Program Control Table." This table lists the name and version number of the program used to create the data being imported, the building codes used and the like. This table must be included with the data to be imported into SAP2000 or an error will occur.

- Error button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the Error shown in the display area. An error should be investigated. It is likely that during the import SAP2000 will have skipped the record/data associated with the error because an error could cause the program to crash or introduce an critical error in the model geometry.
- Warning button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the first Warning item shown in the display area. A Warning item advises you of situations that should be noted for further consideration.
- Information button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the first Information item shown in the display area. An Information item indicates what actions SAP2000 took to resolve conflicts between the imported data and any existing or previously imported data.
- Revert to Backup button.  When data is being imported into an existing model, SAP2000 creates a backup file of the model before the data is imported. Click the Revert to Backup button if after reviewing the any error messages, warnings, or information you decide not to complete the import. After this button is clicked, SAP2000 will display the model was it was before the most recent import process was initiated.
- Write to Text File button. Click this button to generate a text file containing the text from the import log (i.e., the text shown in the display area of the form).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Interactive Database Import Log form as follows:   1. Click the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command to display the Choose Tables for Interactive Editing form. 2. Choose the data to be displayed and click the OK button to display the table for the selected data type. 3. On the displayed table, click the  Options menu > Always Display Log After Import  command so that the Interactive Database Import Log form will display when data is imported into the table for the selected data type. |

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Interactive_Editing_Tabular_Database_Import_Options_Form.htm | Interactive Editing Tabular Database Import Options Form -->

# Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing Form

The Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing form has options for specifying how changes made to database tables are integrated back into the model database. The Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing form has four tabs.

Note:  The name of the tab appears in all capital letters when that tab has been selected for display.

- Items with Same Name tab. When items in the edited table have the same names, an option is available to specify that the last item with the duplicated name overwrite any previous items with that name (Overwrite previous item). Alternatively, the first item in the table with a duplicated name can be used, with any subsequent items with the same name being ignored (Ignore subsequent items). When items in the edited table have the same names as items in the model database, options are available to specify that the edited table items (a) replace the items in the model, (b) are ignored, or (c) are added to the model with a new name
- Items in Same Location tab. When items in the edited table are in the same location as items in the model database, options are available to specify if the items in the edited table should be allowed to duplicate items in the same location, replace items in the same location, be ignored, or be ignored with specified exceptions.
- Items Deleted from Database tab. This tab has an option to delete items from the model and an option to not delete items from the model. The default is to delete items from the model when the edited table contains records that duplicate records in the model database. With the "do not delete" option selected, records can be removed from the table without removing the associated object from the model. This is a convenient way of removing the records that are not being edited without adversely affecting the model. Limiting the amount of data displayed in the tables also can be accomplished by selecting objects before accessing the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command.
- Message Control tab. Options are available to specify if error messages, warnings, or other information should be displayed. Options also are available to specify if the frequency of the display of error messages or warnings should cause the reintroduction of the edited table into the model database to abort.
- - An error should be investigated. It is likely that during the reintroduction of the edited table SAP2000 will have skipped the record/data associated with the error because an error could cause the program to crash or introduce a critical error in the model geometry.
  - A Warning item advises you of situations that should be noted for further consideration.
  - An Information item indicates what actions SAP2000 took to resolve conflicts between the edited table data and the model database.
- Reset Tab Defaults and Reset All Default buttons. Use these buttons to restore default selections to the Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing form on a tab-by-tab basis or for the entire form, respectively.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing form as follows:   1. Click the Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing command to display the Choose Tables for Interactive Editing form. 2. Choose the data to be displayed and click the OK button to display the table for the selected data type. 3. On the displayed table, click the Advanced Options button to display the Tabular Database Import Options - Interactive Editing form. |

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Merge_Duplicates.htm | Merge Duplicates -->

# Merge Duplicates

Form:  Merge Duplicates

Use the Edit menu > Merge Duplicates command to access the Merge Duplicates form and combine duplicate objects into one object. Use the Edit menu > Show Duplicates command to verify that duplicates are included in the model and, if so, where they are located.

1. Select the objects to be merged. The duplicate objects must be of the same type (joints merge with joints, frames merge with frames, and so forth) and must have the same coordinates in the model.
2. Click the Edit > Merge Duplicates command to access the Merge Duplicates form.
3. Select the appropriate options to specify how the loads, masses, and other assignments belonging to the individual objects are to be combined for the merged object.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Move.htm | Move -->

# Move

Form:  Move Selected Objects

The move feature is a way to select parts of the structure and relocate them in the model.

1. Select the members and joints to be moved.
2. Click the Edit menu > Move command to access the Move Selected Objects form.
3. Enter the relative movement of the selected members in the Delta X, Y and Z direction edit boxes. Alternatively, click the **Pick Two Points on Model** button and then interactively click two points on the model to define the delta values.
4. Click the **Apply** button to move the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to move the selected object(s) and close the form.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem E](../../Example_Problems/Problem_E.md), and [Problem U](../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

## See Also

[Nudge Feature](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Nudge_Feature.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Replicate.htm | Replicate -->

# Replicate

Form: Replicate

Replicate is another very powerful way of generating a large model from a small model when the objects and/or joints form a linear or radial pattern or are symmetrical about a plane. When joints or objects are replicated, the assignments on those joints and objects are also replicated (for example, member section assignments, member loads, joint loads and joint restraints). This is a major benefit of using Replicate rather than the Cut, Copy and Paste commands, which can be used to cut, copy, or paste lines, areas and joints but not their assignments or loads.

1. Select the objects to be replicated.
2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command and choose the Linear, Radial, or Mirror tab to complete the following types of replication.

[Replicate in a Linear Array](javascript:TextPopup(this))

1. 1. Select the members and joints to be replicated.
   2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to access the Replicate form.
   3. Click on the Linear tab.
   4. Fill in the dx, dy and dz offset distances in the Increments edit boxes. Alternatively, click the **Pick Two Points on Model** button and then interactively click two points on the model to define the increment values.
   5. Type the number of times the selected entities are to be replicated in the Number edit box.
   6. Click the Apply button to replicate the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to replicate the selected object(s) and close the form.

EXAMPLE:

![](../../assets/images/Images/REPLICA1_shg.gif)

[Replicate in a Radial Array](javascript:TextPopup(this))

1. 1. Select the members and joints to be replicated.
   2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to access the Replicate form.
   3. Click on the Radial tab.
   4. Check the axis about which the selected entities are to be rotated, i.e. Parallel to X, Parallel to Y, or Parallel to Z in the Rotate About Line area of the form. The 3D Line option is used for replicating along a specified line (see the Replicate in a Radial Array and Specify Replication Placement description in this topic).
   5. Type the ordinates to shift the radial replication in the edit boxes in the Intersection of Plane with {XY, YZ, XZ} Plane area of the form. Alternatively, click the **Pick One Point on Model** button and then interactively click a point on the model to define the ordinate values.
   6. Type the increment angle and the number of times the selected entities is to be replicated in the Increment Data edit boxes.
   7. Click the Apply button to replicate the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to replicate the selected object(s) and close the form.

Example

![](../../assets/images/Images/REPLICA2_shg.gif)

[Replicate in a Radial Array and Specify Replication Placement](javascript:TextPopup(this))

1. 1. Select the members and joints to be replicated.
   2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to display the Replicate form.
   3. Click on the Radial tab.
   4. Select the 3D Line option in the Rotate About Line area of the form.
   5. Define the coordinates of the line about which the replication will occur using the x1, y1, z1 and x2, y2, and y3 edit boxes in the Coordinates of 2 Points Defining Line area of the form. Alternatively, click the **Pick Two Points on Model** button and then interactively click two points on the model to define the coordinates of the line.
   6. Type in the increment angle and the number of times the selected entities are to be replicated in the Increment Data edit boxes.
   7. Click the Apply button to replicate the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to replicate the selected object(s) and close the form.

EXAMPLE:

![](../../assets/images/Images/REPLICA3_shg.gif)

[Replicate Using the Mirroring Option](javascript:TextPopup(this))

1. 1. Select the members and joints you want to replicate.
   2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to access the Replicate form.
   3. Click on the Mirror tab.
   4. Check the plane about which the selected entities are to be rotated, i.e., Parallel to Z, Parallel to X, or Parallel to Y in the Rotate About Line area of the form.
   5. Type the ordinates to shift the mirrored replication in the edit boxes in the Intersection of Plane with {XY, YZ, XZ} Plane area of the form. Alternatively, click the **Pick Two Points on Model** button and then interactively click two points on the model to define the increment values.
   6. Click the Apply button to replicate the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to replicate the selected object(s) and close the form.

EXAMPLE:

![](../../assets/images/Images/REPLICA4_shg.gif)

[Replicate Using the Mirroring Option and Specify Replication Placement](javascript:TextPopup(this))

1. 1. Select the members and joints to be replicated.
   2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to access the Replicate form.
   3. Click on the Mirror tab.
   4. Select the 3D Plane  option in the Mirror About Plane area of the form.
   5. Define the coordinates of the plane about which the replication will occur using the x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, y3 and x3, y3, z3 edit boxes in the Coordinates of 3 Points Defining Plane area of the form. Alternatively, click the **Pick Two Points on Model** button and then interactively click two points on the model to define the coordinates of the line.
   6. Click the Apply button to replicate the selected object(s) and keep the form open, or click the **OK** button to replicate the selected object(s) and close the form.

EXAMPLE:

![](../../assets/images/Images/Replicate%20Mirror%20SP%202.GIF)![](../../assets/images/Images/Replicate%20Mirror%20SP%201.GIF)

- Modify/Show Replicate Options button. Each of the tabs has a Modify/Show Replicate Options button. Click that button to access the [Replicate Options form](Replicate_Options_Form.md) and select the assignments on the original objects to be transferred to the newly created objects.  
    
  After the options have been selected and the OK button has been clicked to return to the Replicate form, the number of options selected and the total options available on the Replicate Options form are shown immediately below the Modify/Show Replicate Options button.
- Delete Original Objects check box. When this check box is checked, the selected objects being replicated will be deleted after the replication operation has been completed.

Example: Linear replication is demonstrated in [Problem B](../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md), [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem O](../../Example_Problems/Problem_O.md), [Problem S](../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md), and [Problem Z](../../Example_Problems/Problem_Z.md).

Mirror replication is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md) and [Problem U](../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

Radial replication is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md) and [Problem D](../../Example_Problems/Problem_D.md).

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Replicate_Options_Form.htm | Replicate Options Form -->

# Replicate Options Form

Use the options on the Replicate Options form to select which assignments on the original objects are to be transferred to the newly created objects. Check the boxes next to all assignments to be copied. For load assignments, choose which load patterns are to be considered.

- Assignments tab. The Assignments tab contains check boxes for all properties that have been assigned to the objects in the model. Check the check box associated with an assignment to specify that the assignment be replicated. If an option is not available, that type of assignment has not been included in the model or is not assigned to the selected object.
- Loads and Design tab. The Loads and Design tab contains check boxes for all loads and the design overwrites included in the model. Check the check box associated with a load or design overwrite to specify that they be replicated. If an option is not available, that type of load or overwrite has not been included in the model or is not assigned to the selected object.
- - Select Load Patterns button. Click the Select Load Patterns button to access the Select Load Patterns form and select the load patterns to be considered by clicking on them in the Select display area of the form. Use the Shift key and Ctrl button to make multiple selections.

- Check/Uncheck All button. The Check/Uncheck All button allows all options to be selected or deselected  using a single click. A Check/Uncheck All button is available for each of the assignment or load and design options as well as a Check/Uncheck All button for the entire form, which checks or unchecks all check boxes on the form.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Replicate Options form as follows:   1. Select objects to be replicated. 2. Click the Edit menu > Replicate command to display the Replicate form. 3. Click the Modify/Show Replicate Options button. |

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Show_Duplicates.htm | Show Duplicates -->

# Show Duplicates

Use the Edit menu > Show Duplicates command to verify that duplicates are included in the model and, if so, where they are located. Duplicate objects can be defined as objects of the same type (joints, frames, shells, Asolids, solids and so forth) that have the same coordinates in the model. If duplicate objects are unnecessary, the Edit menu > Show Duplicates command can be very useful in locating them so that they can be [deleted](Delete.md) or [merged](Merge_Duplicates.md). Duplicates can not be drawn or created; they can result when data is imported from other programs, such as AutoCAD, CIS/2 Step and the like.

1. Click the Edit menu > Show Duplicates command. Any duplicate objects will be shown in different colors.

<!-- source: Menus/Edit/Undo_and_Redo.htm | Undo and Redo -->

# Undo and Redo

Use the Edit menu > Undo command or the Undo button ![](../../assets/images/Images/UNDO_shg.gif) to reverse an action performed during  the modeling process back to the last time the model was saved. If the Undo command is used for too many steps, the steps will begin to be "redone."

Use the Edit menu > Redo command or the Redo button ![](../../assets/images/Images/REDO_shg.gif) to restore an action performed during the modeling process.

The Undo and Redo commands work sequentially. In other words, if you have just finished the sixteenth operation since your last save, you can use the Undo feature to undo the sixteenth operation,  then the fifteenth operation, and so on. You could not, however, decide that you wanted to undo only the seventh operation, for example.

The Undo and Redo commands can be used for the actions performed using the Edit, Draw, and Assign menu commands.

# Advanced Report Writer

Form:  Create Custom Report

Use the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to access the Create Custom Report form and create a report that contains an existing Access database(s), an Excel spreadsheet(s), or plain text (.s2k format) exported from SAP2000, or use the Create Custom Report form to create a new table(s) in Access database format.

Use the Create Custom Report form to specify that the resulting report be accessible using Microsoft Word, a text editor, or Internet Explorer. The report created using the Create Custom Report form can pull together tables from one or more database files that can be from the same or different models.

The report can contain section headings, arbitrary text between the tables, and pictures using many different file formats. The Create Custom Report form has options that control the format of the tables, page setup, and fonts.

The Create Custom Report form has the following buttons, options, and display areas:

- Select the Current Database File: Use one of the following buttons to initiate the report creation process:
- - [Find Existing DB File button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    Click the Find Existing
    DB File button to access the Microsoft
    Access Database form and select the MS Access file
    (\*.mdb) to be included in the report.
  - [Convert Excel File button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    Use this button to locate an Excel file
    that will be converted to a DB file.

    Click the Convert
    Excel File button to access the Select
    Microsoft Excel Workbook to Convert form and select
    the MS Excel file (\*.xls) to be used to initiate the report
    creation process.
  - [Convert Text File button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    Use this button to locate a text file
    that will be converted to a DB file.

    Click the Convert
    Text File button to access the Save
    Text File to Convert form and select the SAP2000 text
    file (\*.s2k; \*.$2k) to be used to initiate the report creation
    process.
  - [Create New DB File button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

    Click the Create
    New DB File button to access the [Choose
    Tables to Export for Access](../../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md) form and select the
    data tables to be used in creating a new Access database file
    and initiate the report creation process.

File display box. This box will display the path and filename of the file selected or created using the above button.

Note:  The Access, Excel or Text file accessed using the Create Custom Report form must have been created by exporting it from SAP2000 using the appropriate File menu > Export command. See [Export SAP2000 MS Access Database mdb File](../Export/Export_SAP2000_MS_Access_Database_mdb_file.md), [Export SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet xls File](../Export/Export_SAP2000_MS_Excel_Spreadsheet_xls_file.md) and [Export SAP2000 .s2k Text File](../Export/Export_SAP2000_s2k_Text_File.md) for information about creating export files.

- Report File Type
- - [RTF](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    When this option is selected, SAP2000
    will create the report with an RTF (rich text format) extension
    using the path and filename you specify after clicking the
    Create Report button.

    - Open
      report in Microsoft Word check box. If the Open report in Microsoft Word
      check box is checked, Word will automatically open and
      display the report after the report has been set up and
      the Create Report button has
      been clicked.
  - [TXT](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    When this option is selected, SAP2000
    will create the report with a TXT extension using the path
    and filename you specify after clicking the Create
    Report button.

    - Open
      report in default text editor check box. If the
      Open report in default
      editor check box is checked, the default text editor
      will automatically open and display the report after the
      report has been set up and the Create
      Report button has been clicked.
    - Send
      data directly to printer check box. If the Send date directly to printer
      check box is checked, SAP2000 will automatically send
      the report to the default printer after the report has
      been set up and the Create Report
      button has been clicked.
  - [HTML](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    When this option is selected, SAP2000
    will create the report with an HTML (hype-text markup language)
    extension using the path and filename you specify after clicking
    the Create Report button.

    - Open
      Report in Internet Explorer check box.  If
      the Open Report in Internet
      Explorer  check box is checked, Internet Explorer
      will automatically display the report after the report
      has been set up and the Create Report
      button has been clicked.

Note:  The .RTF, .TXT, and .HTML files are saved when the Create Report button is clicked; those files can then be edited using the appropriate program. The settings selected in creating the report are not saved until the Save Named Report button has been clicked. Saving the settings makes it possible to use the Create Custom Report form to edit the report after it has been generated (e.g., add additional files to the report from other models). Use the Save Named Report button and the Open Named Report button to save the settings specified on the form and then open/use the saved settings to generate reports, allowing multiple reports to have consistent layouts/formats.

- Report Setup

- [List of Tables in Current Database File.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  When an existing
  Access database, Excel spreadsheet, or text file is selected for
  inclusion in the report, the various tables in the file are listed
  in this area of the Create Custom Report
  form.

  1. Highlight
     the name of a table in the list. Use standard Windows selection
     methods (i.e., hold down the Shift key or the Ctrl key while
     clicking the left mouse button) to make multiple selections.
  2. Click
     the Add Selected DB Table(s) to Report
     button to specify that the table be included in the report.
     The name of the selected table(s) will appear in the Items Included in Report
     display area of the form.
- Add Additional Items to Report

- 1. - [Section button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Section
       button to access the [Report Item - Section form](Report_Item_Section_Form.md).
     - [Text button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Text
       button to access the [Report Item - Text form](Report_Item_Text_Form.md).
     - [Picture button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

       Click the Picture
       button to access the [Report Picture form](Report_Picture_Form.md).
     - [Page Break button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Use the Page
       Break button to insert a page break at any point
       in the report. A notation identifying the location of
       the page break relative to the other items in the report
       will appear in the Items
       Included in Report display area of the form.
     - [Blank Line(s) button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

       Click the Blank
       Line(s) button to access the [Report Item - Blank Lines form](Report_Item_Blank_Lines_Form.md).

- Insertion Point for Items Added to Report

- 1. - [After Selected Item option](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Use this option to add items to a
       report at a location other then the end of the report.

       1. Highlight the heading, text,
          picture, page break, or blank line(s) that is to precede
          the item(s) to be added.
       2. Click the appropriate button
          in the Add Additional
          Items to Report area of the form.
     - [At End of List option.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

       The At
       End of List option is the default. When this option
       is used, any items added to the report using the buttons
       in the Add Additional
       Items to Report area of the form will be added
       to the end of the report.

- Apply to Entire Report

- 1. - [Report Setup button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Report
       Setup button to access the [Report Setup form](Report_Setup_Form.md) and specify
       various setup options.
     - [Apply Formats button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Apply
       Formats button to select a previously defined style
       sheet file (\*.fmt) and apply it to all tables in the report.
       After clicking the Apply Formats
       button, select the .fmt file from the Database
       Table Formats File form.

       See the
       description for the Save Formats
       button with respect to saving style sheet files.
     - [Save Formats button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Save
       Formats button to specify a filename and save the
       table format specified using the options on the Modify/Show Database Table Format
       form.  Use the Modify/Show
       Database Table Format form as follows:

       1. Highlight
          a table name in the Items
          Included in Report area of the Create
          Custom Report form.
       2. Click
          the Modify/Show button
          to display a database table
          form.
       3. On the
          table form, click the Format
          command to display the Modify/Show
          Database Table Format form.
       4. Set
          the options on the [Modify/Show Database Table Format
          form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md) and then click the Save
          Table Format to File button.
       5. Specify
          a name for the file and click the OK
          button to return  to the Create
          Custom Report form.
       6. Repeat
          the process as necessary for additional tables.

       On the Create
       Custom Report form, click the Save
       Formats button to save any or all of the formats
       specified for the tables in the report in a single style
       sheet.
     - [Default Formats button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

       Click the Default
       Formats button to apply program default style sheets
       to the tables included in the report.
     - [Clear Filters Only button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

       Click the Clear
       Filters Only button to remove any field filtering
       criteria established using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format
       form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).

       See the description for the Save Formats button with respect
       to saving style sheet files.
     - [Clear Sorts Only button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

       Click the Clear
       Sorts Only button to remove any table sorting criteria
       established using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format
       form](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md).

       See the description for the Save Formats button with respect
       to saving style sheet files.

- Items Included in Report (Table Formats File for Added Tables:  Program Default)
- - [Modify/Show button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

    Use the Modify/Show
    button to modify a previously added item.

    1. Highlight the item to be modified.
    2. Depending on the type of item highlighted
       (table, section heading, text, picture, blank lines),
       a form will appear that can be used to modify the selected
       item.

       - The
         [Modify/Show
         Database Table Format](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md) form will appear
         when a table has been selected.
       - [Report Item - Section form](Report_Item_Section_Form.md).
       - [Report Item - Text form](Report_Item_Text_Form.md).
       - [Report Picture form](Report_Picture_Form.md).
       - [Report Item - Blank Lines
         form](Report_Item_Blank_Lines_Form.md).
  - [Remove button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

    Use the Remove
    button to delete previously added items form the report.

    1. Highlight the item to be removed.
    2. Click the Remove
       button to delete the item from the report.
  - [Arrow buttons](javascript:TextPopup(this))

    Use the Arrow
    buttons to move the items listed in the Items
    Included in Report display area of the form up or down
    to rearrange the order of the presentation of the data in
    the report.

    1. Highlight the item to be moved.
    2. Click the Up arrow to move the
       item up in the list (present the data earlier in the report).
       Click the Down arrow to move the item down in the list
       (present the data later in the report).
- [Save Named Report button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

  Click the Save Named Report button
  to access the [Named
  Report form](Named_Report_Form.md).
- [Open Named Report button](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

  Click the Open Named
  Report button to access the Select
  Named Report form.

  1. Highlight
     the name of a previously named report.
  2. Click
     the OK button to open the previously
     saved named report template.
- [Change Source DB button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  Click the Change Source
  DB button to display the Report
  Item - Filenames form. Use the form to change the source
  for the data being used in the report.
- [Create Report button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  After the items to be included in the report
  have been selected, and the format for the report has been established,
  click the Create Report button to
  generate the report in the specified .RTF, .TXT, or .HTML format.
  The report file will be available in the specified subdirectory

- [Done button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  Click the Done
  button to close the Create Custom Report
  form.

# Named Report Form

Use the Named Report form to save, modify or delete a named report, which is the settings specified using the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md). After the settings have been saved in a Named Report, those settings can be easily recalled and applied to create a report by clicking the Open Named Report button on the Create Custom Report form.

 The Named Report form has three button:

- Add New Report button.
- 1. Type a name for the report template in the Report edit box.
  2. Click the Add New Report button to save the settings specified on the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md).
- Change Report Name button.
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously named report.
  2. Type a new name in the Report edit box.
  3. Click the Change Report Name button to change the name of the report template.
- Delete Named Report button.
- 1. Highlight the name of a previously named report.
  2. Click the Delete Named Report button to delete the previously named report.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Named Report form as follows:   1. Click the  File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Save Named Report button. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Item_Blank_Lines_Form.htm | Report Item Blank Lines Form -->

# Report Item - Blank Lines Form

Use the Report Item - Blank Lines form to add blank lines to a report. Type the number of lines to be added to the report in the Number of Blank Lines edit box.

The "size" of the blank lines depends on the font size applied to the text immediately preceding the blank lines. For example, if the blank lines immediately follow a Section heading with a 20 point font, the blank lines will use the 20 point font size.

A notation identifying the location of the blank line(s) relative to the other items in the report will appear in the Items Included in Report display area of the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Blank Lines form as follows:   1. Click the  File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Blank Line(s) button in the Add Additional Items to Report area of the form. |

# Report Item - Cover Page Form

Use the Report Item - Cover Page form to specify that a cover page be included or not included when the report is printed or displayed electronically (e.g., as an .HTML file).

- Print Cover Page option. When this option is selected, the check boxes in the Cover Page Options area of the Report Item - Cover Page form become available. Choose the appropriate check boxes to include the current date and any information recorded using the [File menu > Modify/Show Project Information](../Modify-Show_Project_Information.md) command and the Project Information form. Assuming that the data was recorded on the Project Information form, the selected items will appear on the cover page when the report is generated. If nothing has been entered on the Project Information form, nothing will print on the cover page even if the check boxes have been checked.
- Do Not Print Cover Page option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will not include a cover page when the report is generated.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Cover Page form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the  Report Setup button to display the Report Setup form. 3. Click the Cover Page Layout button to display the Report Item - Cover Page form. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Item_Filename.htm | Report Item Filename -->

# Report Item - Filename Form

Use the Report Item - Filename form to change the source database from which the data tables are extracted for use in the report. This button is intended to be used after a report format has been saved by clicking the Save Named Report button. Thus, after a report format has been specified, the report can be recreated  quickly and easily using data from other data sources.

1. Use the various options on the [Custom Report Writer form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md) to define a report format.
2. Save that format using the [Save Named Report button](Named_Report_Form.md).
3. Click the Change Source DB button to display the Report Item - Filename form.
4. Click the Change Selected Database Filename button to display a form that can be used to specify the path and filename to select another database from which the data will be extracted and reported using the saved format.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Filename form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to access the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Change Source DB button. |

# Report Item - Font Form

The Report Item - Font
form has separate tabs to be used to specify the font name, size, and
special formatting (bold, italic, underline, strike through) for the items
added to the report.

- Click the Modify
  Font Setup button, which appears on all tabs, to access the
  Font form and modify the font.
- Section
  Headings tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the
  text added using the [Report Item - Section form](Report_Item_Section_Form.md).
- Text
  Headings tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the
  text added using the [Report
  Item - Text form](Report_Item_Text_Form.md) and the Heading
  edit box.
- Text
  tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the text added using
  the [Report
  Item - Text form](Report_Item_Text_Form.md).
- Table
  Titles tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the titles
  of the tables included in the report.
- Field
  Headings tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the
  [column
  headings (i.e., field names)](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md) in the tables included in the report.
- Table
  Data tab. Controls the font, size and appearance of the data
  shown in the tables included in the report.
- Reset
  Defaults. Use the Selected Tab
  button or the All Tabs button to reset
  the options on one or all tabs to default settings.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Font form as follows:   1. Click    the File    menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display    the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click    the Report    Setup button to access the Report    Setup form. 3. Click    the Font    Setup button to display the Report    Item - Font form. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Item_Page_Setup_Form.htm | Report Item Page Setup Form -->

# Report Item - Page Setup Form

Use the Report Item - Page Setup form to specify options for the pages of the report.

- Units Used for Page Setup Distances options. Choose to specify the dimensions for the page in inches or millimeters (i.e., paper width, margins, and so forth).
- Print Orientation options. Specify that the report be printed using a Portrait (height dimension larger than width dimension) or Landscape (width dimension larger than height dimension) orientation.
- Printer. This display box shows the printer "connected" to the computer being used to create the custom report.
- Paper Width (from printer) and Paper Height (from printer). The dimensions shown in these edit boxes correspond to the dimensions of the paper tray of the Printer identified in the Printer display box. That is, if the paper tray contains 8 1/2 x 11 inch paper and the print orientation is Portrait, the dimensions will be Paper Width 8.5 and Paper Height 11.
- Top Margin, Bottom Margin, Left Margin, Right Margin edit boxes. Use these edit boxes to specify the distances from the printed materials to the edge of the paper.
- Header and Footer Edge Distance edit boxes. Use these edit boxes to specify the distances from any Header or Footer text and the edge of the paper.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Page Setup form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Report Setup button to access the Report Setup form. 3. Click the Page Setup button to display the Report Item - Page Setup form. |

# Report Item - Section Form

Use the Report Item - Section
form to add a section heading to a report. SAP2000 will sequentially number
sections in the report each time the Section
button is clicked. Use the Section name as provided in the Heading
edit box, add to it by typing in the edit box, or highlight it and type
over it to replace it. The heading text will appear in the Items
Included in Report display area of the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md) relative to
the location of the other items in the report.

- Include
  a Page Break before the Section Heading. When this check box
  is checked, SAP2000 will put the heading/text in the Heading
  edit box at the top of a new page when the Report
  File Type is RTF (Microsoft
  Word). That is, the page break will precede the text in the Heading edit box. This option has
  no effect when the TXT or HTML option is selected.
- Include
  a Page Break after the Section Heading. When this check box
  is checked, SAP2000 will include a page break after the heading/text
  in the Heading edit box when
  the Report File Type is RTF (Microsoft Word). This option
  has no effect when the TXT or HTML option is selected.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Section form as follows:   1. Click    the  File    menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display    the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click    the Section    button in the Add    Additional Items to Report area    of the form. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Item_Text_Form.htm | Report Item Text Form -->

# Report Item - Text Form

Use the Report Item - Text form to add headings and text to the report.

Type text in the Heading edit box on this form and SAP2000 will add a sub-heading, or Level 2 heading, to the report. Type summary explanations or other text in the Text edit box; if no heading is included in the Heading edit box, this text will follow the Heading text added to the report using the [Section button](Report_Item_Section_Form.md). If no Heading text is included, the text will appear where placed in the order of items shown in the Items Included in Report display area of the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md).

When typing in the Text display area of the form, hold down the Ctrl key while pressing the Enter key to add a paragraph break (i.e., end a paragraph and add a blank line between paragraphs).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Item - Text form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Text button in the Add Additional Items to Report area. |

# Report Item - Picture Form

Use the Report Item - Picture form to add a .bmp, .emf, .gif, .jpg, or .wmf file to the report.

Use the Browse button to specify the path and filename of the picture file to be included in the report.

Type the figure caption in the Caption edit box. Locate both the caption (above or below the picture) and the picture itself (left, right, center) by choosing the appropriate option(s).

Options are available to include a page break before or after the picture.

A notation identifying the picture path and filename and the location of the picture relative to the other items in the report will appear in the Items Included in Report display area of the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md).

<!-- source: Menus/File/Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Setup_Form.htm | Report Setup Form -->

# Report Setup Form

Use the Report Setup form to specify setup options for a report to be created using the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md). The Report Setup form has the following options:

- Current Database Table Formats File for Tables Added to the Report.
- - Use Program Default Table Formats option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will apply default program formats for the table(s) included in the report.
  - Use Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option. When this option is selected, the Select button becomes enabled. Click the Select button to access the Database Files Format File form, which can be used to locate style sheet files (\*.fmt) and apply a style sheet to a table when the table is added to the report.  
      
    Thus, when this option is used, be sure to click the Report Setup button to select a style sheet file before selecting any tables to be included in the report (i.e., before highlighting a table name in the List of Tables in Current Database File area on the Create Custom Report form; see the [Create Custom Report form](Advanced_Report_Writer.md) topic for more information regarding the report creation process, including the steps to create a style sheet).

- Report Setup
- - Page Setup button. Click the Page Setup button to access the [Report Item - Page Setup form](Report_Item_Page_Setup_Form.md).
  - Font Setup button. Click the Font Setup button to access the [Report Item - Font form](Report_Item_Font_Form.md).
  - Cover Page Layout button. Click the Cover Page Layout button to access the [Report Item - Cover Page form](Report_Item_Cover_Page_Form.md).
- Report Options
- - Include Database File Names with Table Titles option. When this option is selected, the report will contain the name of the table as well as the filename of the database from which the table was taken.
  - Include Filter Criteria String Beneath Table Titles option. When this option is selected, the report will show the filter criteria, if any, used in generating the table(s). The information will be presented beneath the table title(s).
  - Include Hyperlinked Contents List option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create a table of contents for the report and present it at the beginning of the report. The items listed in the contents will be hyperlinked to the appropriate section of the report, allowing quick access to the various sections of the report when the Report File Type is .RTF or .HTML. This option has no effect when the Report File Type is TXT.
- Apply Formats to All Tables
- - Apply from File button. Similar to the Use Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option (see above), the Apply from File button can be used to specify and apply a style sheet file (\*.fmt) to the tables included in a report. However, unlike the Use Formats from User Defined Table Formats File option, the Apply from File button can be used to apply a style sheet to all tables in the report after the tables have been added to the report.
  - Apply Program Default button. Click the Apply Program Default button to apply the program default style sheet to all tables in the report.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Report Setup form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Advanced Report Writer command to display the Create Custom Report form. 2. Click the Report Setup button in the Apply to Entire Report area. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Batch_File_Control.htm | Batch File Control -->

# Batch File Control

Form:  Batch File Control

A batch file is a list of SAP2000 model files. When a batch file is run, SAP will open the listed model files in succession, run their analyses, and manage the analysis files (save all, save some files, or delete all files) with no action required by the user. Thus, the File menu > Batch File Control command is useful for running multiple models when the computer is unattended (e.g., overnight).

Note:  Use the [Analyze menu > Set Analysis Options command](../Analyze/Set_Analysis_Options.md) to specify that model definition and analysis results tables be automatically saved after an analysis has been run for a model.  With that option set, use the File menu > Batch File Control command to generate the analysis results of multiple model files (i.e., output tables) as well as the analysis files for those models (i.e., binary files).

Click the File menu > Batch File Control command to access the Batch File Control form. Use the form to complete any of the following:

- [Define a New Batch File](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  1. Access the Batch File Control form using the File menu > Batch File Control command.
  2. Click the Specify New Batch File Name button. A Windows form for specifying the path and batch file name will appear. Select the path and type the batch file name into the File name edit box. Click the Save button and the batch file name will appear in the Text Batch File Name edit box near the top of the Batch File Control form.
  3. Type the path and name of the model file to be included in the batch file in the SAP2000 Filename (Full Path) edit box near the middle of the form. Alternatively click the Browse For SAP2000 Files button to locate the files. When a file has been located, click on it and the path and filename will appear in the SAP2000 Filename (Full Path) edit box.
  4. Click the Add button in the lower right area of the form to add the file to the list. The path and filename will appear in the display area in the middle of the form.
  5. Click the "Load Cases to Run" drop-down list and choose to have SAP run All load cases, or only Selected cases. The cases are selected when the analysis is run. See [Run Analysis](../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) for more information about selecting cases.
  6. Click the "Options for Analysis Files" drop-down list and choose from the following:

     - Save All. SAP2000 will save all of the analysis files generated when the analyses are run. Depending on the size of the model files, this option may require substantial file storage space.
     - Save Recovery Only. SAP2000 will save the minimum number of files needed to generate results. Use this option when file storage space is limited.
     - Delete All. SAP2000 will delete all of the analysis files generated when the analyses are run. Use this option when the [Analyze menu > Set Analysis Options command](../Analyze/Set_Analysis_Options.md) has been used to specify that model definition and analysis results tables be automatically saved after the analysis has been run. Use of the option will limit the space required for file storage.
- [Save a Batch File Definition to a Text File](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  Save the batch file definition so that it can be recalled and run without redefining the list.

  1. Define a new batch file as described above.
  2. Click the Save Current Batch File List to Text File button.
- [Open an Existing Batch Text File](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  1. Access the Batch File Control form using the File menu > Batch File Control command.
  2. Click the Browse For Existing Batch Files button. A Windows form for specifying the path and batch file name will appear. Select the path and the batch file name, which will appear in the File name edit box. Click the Open button and the batch file name will appear in the Text Batch File Name edit box near the top of the Batch File Control form.
  3. As necessary use the following buttons to make changes to the list of model files:
  1. - Add button. Follow Steps 3 and 4 of the Define a New Batch File explanation above to add a model file to the batch file definition.
     - Modify button. Highlight the model file name to be modified in the list in the display area in the middle of the form. Follow Steps 5 and 6 of the Define a New Batch File explanation above to change the analysis cases to be run and the management of the analysis files, respectively. Click the Modify button to complete the change(s).
     - Delete button. Highlight the model file name to be deleted in the list in the display area in the middle of the form. Click the Delete button.
     - Change Filename Path button. Click the Change Filename Path button to access the [Batch File Path form](Batch_File_Path_Form.md).
- [Run a Batch File](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  1. Define a batch file or open an existing batch text file as described above.
  2. Use the Add, Modify, Delete and Change Filename Path buttons to make any necessary changes to the batch definition before running the batch file (see the Open an Existing Batch Text File explanation for more information about using these buttons).
  3. Click the Run Models in Current Batch File List button to begin the batch run. That particular session of SAP2000 cannot be used while the batch file is running.
  4. If the batch file has not been saved to a text file, SAP will prompt you to save it.
  5. When the batch files are complete, the Status of Batch File Analyses form will appear, displaying a summary of the runs in the batch.
- Done button. Click the Done button to close the form.

Note: The [Advanced Command Line Switches (/R and /D only)](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Starting_SAP2000_from_the_Command_Line.md) apply to all files listed in the batch file.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Batch_File_Path_Form.htm | Batch File Path Form -->

# Batch File Path Form

Form:  Batch File Path

Use the Batch File Path form to specify the location of the model files to be used during a batch file analysis run.

1. Type the new path in the New Path to Program Files display box or use the Select Path button to access the Select a Path form. The Select a Path form has a drop-down list to help select the drive and a display area to help select the subdirectory for the model files.
2. Choose from the following options to specify the files to which the new path should be applied:

1. - Only Change the Path of the Selected File on the Batch File Control Form. Use this option if the path is to be changed for a single file.
   - 1. If necessary, return to the Batch File Control form by clicking the Cancel button on the Batch File Path form.
     2. Select the file for which the path is to be changed by highlighting it in the display area in the middle of the Batch File Control form.
     3. Click the Change Filename Path button to access the Batch File Path form.
     4. Identify the new path as described in Step 1 above.
     5. Select the Only Change the Path of the Selected File on the Batch File Control option.
     6. Click the OK button.
   - Change the Path of All Files with the Same Path as the Selected Path Shown Above. Use this option to change the path of multiple specified files. All files with the same path as that shown in the Selected Path display box will be changed to the path specified in the New Path to Program Files display box.
   - Change the Path of All Files. Use this option to change the path of all files to the path specified in the New Path to Program Files display box. This is the default option.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Batch File Path form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > Batch File Control command to display the Batch File Control form. 2. Define a batch file or open an existing batch file as described in [Batch File Control](Batch_File_Control.md). 3. Highlight a filename in the table and click the Change Filename Path button . |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Capture_Enhanced_Metafile.htm | Capture Enhanced Metafile -->

# Capture Enhanced Metafile

The Enhanced Metafile is a vector file format that can be read by many graphics programs as well as some office tools such as word processors.

1. Click the File menu > Capture Enhanced Metafile command.
2. Choose Current Window or User Region in Window, which will display the Open File for Saving Enhanced Metafile form.

   - The Current Window option captures the entire graphic displayed in the active window.
   - The User Region in Current Window option is used in conjunction with windowing to capture a user-specified portion of the active window.
3. Select the path and type the file name in the File name edit box.
4. Click the Save button to save the text input file with an .EMF extension.

Note: When using the User Region in Current Window command, after Step 3, drag the mouse across the image to select the region of the model that you want to capture. Then click the OK button in the pop-up box.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Capture_Picture.htm | Capture Picture -->

# Capture Picture

Form:  Open File for Saving Picture

Use the File menu > Capture Picture command to create a .bmp, .gif, .jpeg, .png, or .tif file format of any of the following:

- [Entire Screen](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  The File menu > Capture Picture > Entire Screen command captures all of the Windows screen, including Windows Start and Windows title bar.

  ![](../../assets/images/Images/Test1.jpg)
- [SAP2000 Main Window](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  The File menu > Capture Picture > SAP2000 Main Window command captures all of the SAP window, including toolbars and status bars.

  ![](../../assets/images/Images/Test1-2.jpg)
- [Current Window w/ Titlebar](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  The File menu > Capture Picture > Current Window w/Titlebar command captures the current window with the title bar:

  ![](../../assets/images/Images/Test1-3.jpg)
- [Current Window w/o Titlebar](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  The File menu > Capture Picture > Current Window w/o Titlebar command captures the current window without the title bar:

  ![](../../assets/images/Images/Test1-4.jpg)
- [User Region in Current Window](javascript:TextPopup(this))

  The File menu > Capture Picture > User Region in Window command option is used in conjunction with windowing to capture a user-specified portion of the active window.

  ![](../../assets/images/Images/Test1-5.jpg)

1. Display the desired 2D or 3D View in the active window.
2. Click the File menu > Capture Picture > {Option} command.
3. When the Open File for saving picture form appears, enter a name in the Filename edit box and, if necessary, change the path using the Save In drop-down list.
4. Locate the desired file format in the Save as Type drop-down list (e.g., .bmp, .gif, .jpeg, .png, or .tif); highlight the desired format to select.

Note: When using the User Region in Current Window command, after Step 4, drag the mouse across the image to select the region of the model that you want to capture. Then click the OK button in the pop-up box.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Create_Report.htm | Create Report -->

# Create Report

Use the File menu > Create Report command  to generate a report for the open file.

1. Create a model, and as necessary, complete analysis and design.
2. Click the [File menu > Report Setup command](Report_Setup.md) to access the Report Setup Data form. Use that form to specify the filename and storage path, the report format (.rtf, .htm, .txt), the orientation (portrait or landscape), and the various items to be included (e.g., cover page, hyperlinked TOC, load patterns, load cases/combinations, and so forth).

Note:  For larger or more complex models, the program may display the Statics for Large Report form, which indicates, among other information, the number of lines of data to be included in the report. The form provides the option to continue with report generation (Yes) or not (No). When larger quantities of data are to be included, it will take longer to generate the report. It may take considerable time and available memory to generate reports for larger/complex models. It may be necessary to reduce the number of items to be included in the report using the Report Setup Data form.

3. Click the  File menu > Create Report command. When this command is clicked, a file storage form displays with the storage path identified based on the selection made on the Report Setup Data form.

Note:  This command generates output for the open file only. Use the [File menu > Advanced Report Writer](Advanced_Report_Writer/Advanced_Report_Writer.md) command to  further refine the report layout, including combining data from multiple model files into a single report.
