<!-- source: Menus/File/Create_Video/Create_Cyclic_Animation_Video.htm | Create Cyclic Animation Video -->

# Create Cyclic Animation Video

Form:  Video File, Animation Video File

Use the File menu > Create Video > Cyclic Animation command to create videos of animated mode shapes and other deformed shape plots of the structure. A mode shape or deformed shape must be displayed in the active window for this command to be available (i.e., an analysis must have been run). The videos are saved as .avi files. They can be played back using the media player that comes with Windows.

1. Run an analysis to display in the active window the deformed shape to be animated cyclically.
2. Select the File menu > Create Video > Cyclic Animation command to access the Video File form. Specify the storage location and file name for the video file in the Save In drop-down list and File name edit box, respectively.
3. Click the Save button to access the Animation Video File Creation form.

1. - AVI Filename edit box:  Displays the name of the .avi file. Click the Browse button to change the path and filename for saving the video file.
   - AVI Options:
   - - Required duration (seconds): Use the default or specify a duration. For a slower display, increase the number of seconds and decrease the number of cycles in duration. For a faster display, decrease the duration and increase the number of cycles.
     - Number of cycles in duration: Use the default or specify your own number of cycles.
     - Frame Size (pixels): Use the default or define the frame size in pixels. Note that the more pixels, the larger the resulting .avi file. Also, the output device used to display the .avi helps to determine the quality of the video (i.e., regardless of the pixel count, the display can not be better than the output device allows).

4. Click the OK button and the [Video Compression form](Video_Compression_Form.md) will display. Choose the method for compressing the video file, or use the default uncompressed option. Click the OK button on the form to create the \*.avi file.


---
<!-- source: Menus/File/Create_Video/Create_Multi_Step_Animation_Video.htm | Create Multi Step Animation Video -->

# Create Multi-Step Animation Video

Form:  Video File, Time History Video File Creation

Use the File menu > Create Video > Create Multi-Step Animation Video command to create videos in SAP2000 showing the movement of the structure after a time history analysis has been run. The videos are saved as .avi files. They can be played back using the media player that comes with Windows.

Note: For best results make sure that all SAP2000 windows are showing undeformed views before attempting to create a time history video.

Be sure to define any [load patterns](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) or  [time history functions](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) needed and [define](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and [run](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) a time history load case before completing the following steps.

1. Click the File menu > Create Video > Create Multi-step Animation Video command to access the Video File form. Specify the storage location and file name for the video file in the Save In drop-down list and File name edit box, respectively.
2. Click the Save button to access the Multi-step Video File Creation form.

1. - AVI File Name edit box:  Displays the name of the .avi file. Click the Browse button to change the path and filename for saving the video file.
   - Plot Type:  Choose to plot the time history Analysis Results or the Multi-Step Load. The availability of the Multi-Step Load option depends on the program version and the load patterns specified in the model (e.g., wave).
   - Load Case Data:
   - - Case Name:  Select the named Time History case for which the video is being create.
     - Start Time, End Time, Time Increment: Use the default or define start and end times and time increments. The time increment controls how many different pictures (frames) of the deformed shape of the structure are created. For example, a time increment of 0.1 means a picture (frame) of the deformed shape is created for every one-tenth second of the time history.
   - Display Options:
   - - Wire Frame:  Choose this option to display the undeformed shape as a reference.
     - Cubic Curve:  Choose this option if frame objects are to be drawn using cubic curves between joints. Uncheck this check box if frame objects are to be drawn as straight lines between joints.
     - Absolute Displacements: Choose this option to add the ground displacements to the structure’s relative displacements when using ground acceleration
     - Magnification Factor:  This option controls the scaling of the vector components. The default factor is 10.
   - AVI Options:
   - - Frames per Second: The Frames per Second item controls how fast the time history is played back. To record the time history file in real time animation, make sure that the number of frames per second is equal to one over the time increment. The default for Frame Speed is 10.

Note: To view the animation in real time, the value for frames per second should be the same as 1/Time Increment. A larger value will speed up the animation and a smaller value will slow it down.

1. 1. - Frame Size (pixel): Use the default or define the frame size in pixels. Note that the more pixels the larger the resulting .avi file. Also, the output device used to display the .avi helps to determine the quality of the video (i.e., regardless of the pixel count, the display can not be better than the output device allows). The default for Frame Size is 640x480.

3. Click the OK button and the [Video Compression form](Video_Compression_Form.md) will display. Choose the method for compressing the video file, or use the default uncompressed option. Click the OK button on the form to create the \*.avi file.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem Q](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Q.md).

<!-- source: Menus/File/Create_Video/Create_Video.htm | Create Video -->

# Create Video

SAP can create videos showing the following:

- Animations of mode shapes and other deformed shape plots of the structure ([Cyclic Animation](Create_Cyclic_Animation_Video.md)).
- Movement of the structure during any time history analysis that has been run ([Multi Step Animation](Create_Multi_Step_Animation_Video.md)).

# Video Compression Form

Use the Video Compression form to choose a compressor to reduce the size of the final \*.avi file.

1. Choose the compression method by selecting an option from the Compressor drop-down list. By default, the Full Frames (Uncompressed) option is selected; as the name suggests, the file will uncompressed.
2. If available and as necessary, use the Key Frame Every and Data Rate check boxes and edit boxes and the Configure button to specify parameters for the different compressors; the options available are specific to the type of compressor and are assumed to be self-explanatory.
3. Click the OK button on the Video Compression form to create the \*.avi file.

| Access the Video Compression form as follows:  Method 1: Use this method when creating a Cyclic Animation Video   1. Run an analysis 2. Click the File menu > Create Video > Create Cyclic Animation Video to access the Animation Video File Creation form. 3. Specify a name and path for saving the video and then define the duration, number of cycles, and frame size. 4. Click the OK button to display the Video Compression form.   Method 2: Use this method when creating a Multi-Step Animation Video   1. Define any [load patterns](../../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) or  [time history functions](../../Define/Functions/Time_History/Define_Time_History_Function.md) needed and [define](../../Define/Load_Cases/Load_Case_Data_Form.md) and [run](../../Analyze/Set_Load_Cases_to_Run_and_Run_Analysis.md) a time history load case. 2. Click the File menu > Create Video > Create Multi Step Animation Video to access the Multi-Step Video File Creation form. 3. Specify a name and path for saving the video and then specify the load case, the start and end times and time increment, the display options and the file size. 4. Click the OK button to display the Video Compression form. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Export/Export_AutoCAD_dxf_dwg_File.htm | Export AutoCAD dxf dwg File -->

# Export - AutoCAD .dxf/.dwg File

Form:  Save AutoCAD .DXF File As, DXF File Export Option, DXF Export

A DXF file is a file with a .dxf extension containing graphic data saved in the AutoCAD Drawing Exchange Format. This type file of file can be read by many graphics programs and is commonly used to exchange data between graphics programs. The DXF export feature can export geometry data to all versions of AutoCAD up to AutoCAD 2020, and to most other programs capable of reading DXF files.

To generate a DXF file depicting your SAP2000 model, do the following:

- If you only want to show only a limited number of objects, select these objects. You can skip this step if you want to export the entire model.
- Select the File menu > Export > AutoCAD .dxf File command.

The Save AutoCAD. DXF File As form is displayed.

- Navigate to the folder of your choice, type the name of a new file or select an existing file to overwrite, and click the Save button. A form asking you whether or not to retrieve layer names from an existing DXF file is displayed.
- Select Yes to specify a DXF file from which to retrieve layer names, or No.

If you select Yes, the Select Template DXF File form is displayed and you can navigate to the folder of your choice and select a file.

The .DXF Export form is displayed. It features five drop-down lists that let you select the layers on which to create the various types of exported objects, and a text box in which you can type layer names to add to the drop-down lists. The NONE option in each of the drop-down lists is not a layer name; instead you can select it to leave out the corresponding type of object from the DXF file. Also, a given layer name can be used for only one object type and SAP2000 will issue a warning message if you attempt to assign the same layer name to more than one object type.

- Once you are satisfied with your layer assignments, click the OK button. The DXF file is written out.

The SAP2000 object types are written out as the following types of DXF objects:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| SAP2000 Objects | DXF Elements |
| Joints | Points |
| Frames | Lines |
| NLLinks | Points |
| Shells | 3Dfaces |
| Solids | Meshed Polylines |

The exported geometry is a 3D representation of the model unless the active window in SAP2000 is a 2D view. In that case, a 2D view is exported, with all text displayed in the SAP2000 active window also exported.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Export/Export_CIS_2_Step_File.htm | Export CIS/2 Step File -->

# Export - CIS/2 Step File

Form:  Create CIS/2 Step File, Save CIS/2 Step File As, Standards, Material Property Standards Assignments, Frame Section Standards Assignments

Use the File menu > Export > CIS/2 Step File command to export a file using the CIMSteel Integration Standards (CIS). CIS is a set of formal computing specifications used in the steel industry to make software applications mutually compatible. This file type is often used by steel fabricators outside the United States.

1. Use the File menu > Export > CIS/2 Step File command to access the Create CIS/2 Step File form.
2. Click the Browse button on the Create CIS/2 Step File form to access the Save CIS/2 Step File As form and set the path and filename (with a .STP extension) for the file to be exported. Click the Save button to return to the Create CIS/2 Step File form, and as necessary, use the buttons and options on that form to set the standards for the materials and frame sections in the exported CIS/2 Step file.

   - [Modify/Show Standards button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

     Click the Modify/Show Standards button to access the Standards form and verify/specify the standard being applied to the materials and frame sections in the exported CIS/2 Step file.

     - Standards (Name and Year) display area. The default and previously defined standards are listed in this display area.
     - Add New Standard button. Click the Add New Standard button to access the Standard Data form. Use the form to define a new standard. Type the appropriate information into the available edit boxes. Use the Type drop-down list to specify if the information is an industry Standard, a Proprietary standard, or a library standard. Click the OK button to close the form and return to the Create CIS/2 Step File form.
     - Modify/Show Standard button. Highlight an existing standard in the Standards (Name and Year) display area. Click the Modify/Show Standard button to access the Standard Data form. Use the form to modify the selected standard. Type the appropriate revisions in the available edit boxes. Click the OK button to close the form and return to the Create CIS/2 Step File form.
     - Delete Standard button. Highlight a Standard in the Standards (Name and Year) display area. Click the Delete Standard button. SAP2000 will issue a message asking you to confirm that you want to delete the selected standard.

     Note:  If an analysis has been run before the File menu > Export > CIS/2 Step File command is used, the model may be locked. If the model is located, the Add New Standard button and the Delete Standard button will not be available.
   - [Modify/Show Material Property Standards button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

     Click the Modify/Show Material Property Standards button to access the Material Property Standards Assignments form. Use the form to apply previously defined standards to the material properties in the model.

     1. Highlight a property in the Material Property List display area in the upper right portion of the form.
     2. Select a previously defined standard from the Standard drop-down list to apply to the highlighted property. If necessary, click the Modify/Show Standards button to access the Standard Data form and modify the previously defined standard to be more applicable to the selected material property.
     3. As appropriate, enter text in the Reference Number and Description edit boxes to help identify the standard being applied in the CIS/2 Step file.
     4. Click the Apply Standard to Selected Properties button to complete the assignment of the standard to the selected material property.
   - [Modify/Show Frame Section Property button.](javascript:TextPopup(this))

     Click the Modify/Show Frame Section Property button to access the Frame Section Standards Assignments form. Use the form to apply previously defined standards to the frame sections in the model.

     1. Highlight a section in the Frame Section Property List display area.
     2. Select a previously defined standard from the Standard drop-down list to apply to the highlighted frame section. If necessary, click the Modify/Show Standards button to access the Standard Data form and modify the previously defined standard to be more applicable to the selected frame section.
     3. As appropriate, enter text in the Reference Number and Description edit boxes to help identify the standard being applied in the CIS/2 Step file. Use the 'Ref Name' Same as Section Name check box to speed data entry; when the check box is checked, the Ref Name will be the same as the section name as it appears in the Frame Section Property List display area.
     4. Click the Apply Standard to Selected Properties button to complete the assignment of the standard to the selected material property.
   - Applied Loads Export Options. These options (Do Not Export Applied Loads, Export Member Loads Only, Export Element Loads Only)  are assumed to be self-explanatory.
   - Other Export Option check boxes. When these check boxes are checked, the analysis results will be exported with the CIS/2 Step file, and the beam end length offsets will be exported as joint offsets.

Note:  The Select Load Cases and Select Load Combinations button are only effective if an analysis was run before the File menu > Export > CIS/2 Step File command was used.

1. - Select Load Cases button. Click the Select Load Cases button to access the Select Load Cases form, which will display the load cases used in the model analysis. Choose the load cases to be included in the CIS/2 Step export, or use the Clear All button to exclude the load cases from the export.
   - Select Load Combinations button. Click the Select Load Combinations button to access the Select Combination Definitions form. Choose the load combination to be included in the CIS/2 Step export, or use the Clear All button to exclude the combinations from the export.
   - Export Selected Object Only check box. If objects are selected before the File menu > Export > Export CIS/2 Step File command is used, this check box will be checked. Only the selected items will be included in the export. Uncheck the check box to include all items in the export.

3. Click the OK button. SAP2000 will display a message when the CIS/2 Step file export is completed.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Export/Export_IFC_File.htm | Export IFC File -->

# Export IFC File

Form:  Create IFC
File

Use the File menu > Export
> IFC File command to export IFC File command to export IFC
files.

1. Open a SAP2000 model.
2. To export only selected
   objects from the model, make a selection. This option is helpful when
   a model has been previously exported to another application and you
   wish to update it. You can then export only those objects that need
   updating.
3. Click the File
   menu > Export > Export IFC File command to display the
   Create IFC File
   form.
4. To save the file under
   a different name or in a different folder location, click the Browse button, and specify these
   in the Save As
   form which is displayed.
5. Make
   relevant file format selections:  IFC2x3
   or IFC4, Architectural Coordination view or Structural view, and the
   length and force units.

IFC
files are repositories of Building Information Modeling BIM data. Most
of this data is not relevant to structural analysis and accordingly not
exported by SAP2000. Various types of IFC data are organized into subsets
named “views” which gather data types relevant to various aspects of building
design, construction, and maintenance. There are several such views, but
only two views are relevant to SAP2000: the “structural analysis view”,
and the “architectural coordination view”.

The
structural analysis view describes a building structure in terms of nodes,
elements, and loads. Files containing a structural analysis view are suitable
for export to other structural software, such as steel and concrete detailing
applications.

The architectural coordination
view describes the components of a building in architectural terms. Architectural
coordination view files are suitable for export to most building design
software as they are generally well imported.

Force units only apply
if you are writing a Structural
View file.

6. Choose
   specific model contents to export by checking or unchecking the corresponding
   buttons and boxes. The button letting you choose between Entire Model
   and Model Selection is only active if there are selected objects.
   Loads can only be exported to a Structural
   View file.
7. Click
   OK. SAP2000 writes the file.
   If there are warnings, a message box will be displayed to that effect.
   You should review the log file. Its name and folder location are the
   same as those of the model you exported, with the extension changed
   to .ifcexp.log.

# Export - SAP2000 Access Database .mdb File

Form:  Choose Tables to Export to Access File

Use the File menu > Export > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File command to export the model definition, analysis results, and design results as a SAP2000 tabular database to a Microsoft Access database file, usually with an .mdb extension.

Note:  If objects were selected before the File menu > Export > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File command is used, the data for only the selected objects will be exported.

1. Click the File menu > Export > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File command to access the [Choose Tables to Export to Access form](../../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md).
2. Check the check box(es) associated with the item(s) to be included in the export.
3. Click the OK button on the Choose Tables to Export to Access form to complete the export.

As many files as necessary can be exported from a given SAP2000 model. Each file may contain different tables or may apply to different parts of the model. The files may be used for processing by other programs, for modification before re-importing into SAP2000, or for any other purpose. However, if the exported file is to contain a complete description of the model, be sure to export all importable model-definition data for the entire structure.

# Export - SAP2000 .s2k Text File

Form:  Choose Tables to Export as Text File

Use the File menu > Export > SAP2000 .s2k Text File command to export the model definition, analysis results, and design results as a text file with a .$2k extension.

Note:  If objects were selected before the File > Export > SAP2000 .s2k Text File command is used, the data for only the selected objects will be exported.

1. Click the File menu > Export > SAP2000 .s2k Text File command to access the [Choose Tables to Export to Text File form](../../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md).
2. Use the form to select the data to be included in the export.
3. Click the OK button on the Choose Tables to Export to Text File form to complete the export.

As many files as necessary can be exported from a given SAP2000 model. Each file may contain different tables and may apply to different parts of the model. The files may be used for processing by other programs, for modification before re-importing into SAP2000, or for any other purpose. However, if the exported file is to contain a complete description of the model, be sure to export all importable mode definition data for the entire structure.

Note: A text file with a .$2k extension is saved at the same time that the model database is saved with an .SDB extension. The .$2k text file is for analysis purposes only or for recovering the model in emergency crash situations and is not a substitute for the database file. It does not contain all of the information about the model.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Access_Database_Import_Log_Form.htm | Access Database Import Log Form -->

# Access Database Import Log Form

The Access Database Import Log form has a large area that provides a summary of the import data, including the source file, the import type and options, the types of tables/data imported, and any error messages, warnings, or information used to help resolve conflicts between the imported data and the objects and other items present in an existing model or data that previously has been imported into a model.

Note:  In the Database Import Summary Log area, the first entry likely will refer to the "Program Control Table." That table lists the name and version number of the program used to create the data being imported, the building codes used and the like. This table must be included with the data to be imported into SAP2000 or an error will occur.

- Error button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the Error shown in the display area. An error should be investigated. It is likely that during the import SAP2000 will have skipped the record/data associated with the error because an error could cause the program to crash or introduce a critical error in the model geometry.
- Warning button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the first Warning item shown in the display area. A Warning item advises you of situations that should be noted for further consideration.
- Information button. When this button is clicked, SAP2000 will jump to the first Information item shown in the display area. An Information item indicates what actions SAP2000 took to resolve conflicts between the imported data and any existing or previously imported data.
- Revert to Backup button. When data is being imported into an existing model, SAP2000 creates a backup file of the model before the data is imported. Click the Revert to Backup button if after reviewing any error messages, warnings, or information you decide not to complete the import. After this button is clicked, SAP2000 will display the model as it was before the most recent import process was initiated.

Note:  The Revert to Backup  button appears only when an error or warning has been identified in the import.

- Write to Text File button. Click this button to generate a text file containing the text from the import log (i.e., the text shown in the display area of the form).

TIP:  Use the [Import Tabular Database Import Options form](Import_Tabular_Database_Import_Options_Form.md) to adjust the import options. For example, use that form to change the number of errors allowed before the program aborts the import.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Access Database Import Log form as follows:   1. Click one of the following commands to display the Import Tabular Database form.     - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File    - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File    - File menu > Import > SAP2000 V8 to V11 .s2k Text File 2. Click the OK button on the [Import Tabular Database form](Import_Tabular_Database_Form.md) to access an Import {Microsoft Access, Excel Spreadsheet, or SAP2000 Text} form. 3. Select the folder containing the file to be imported (.mdb, .xls, txt), and click on the desired file. 4. Click the Open button and SAP2000 will display the Access Database Import Log form. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_AutoCAD_dxf_dwg_File.htm | Import AutoCAD dxf dwg File -->

# Import - AutoCAD DXF File

Form:  Import DXF File, Import Information, DXF Import

A DXF file is a file with a .dxf extension containing graphics data saved in the AutoCAD Drawing Exchange Format. This type of file can be read by many graphics programs and is commonly used to exchange data between graphics programs. The DXF file import feature can import model geometry from all versions of AutoCAD up to AutoCAD 2020, and from most other programs capable of writing DXF files.

To import a DXF file into SAP2000, do the following:

- Select the File menu > Import > AutoCAD .dxf File command.

The Import DXF File form is displayed.

- Navigate to the folder of your choice, select a file, and click the Open button.

The Import Information form is displayed.

- Choose the axis corresponding to the Global Up Direction in the DXF file, specify the units the DXF file is written in , and click the OK button.

The DXF Import form is displayed. It features five instances of the list of the layers defined in the DXF file with check boxes next to each of the different layers. Above each list is a label describing the corresponding type of SAP2000 objects to import.

- Select the layer or layers on which the AutoCAD objects occur for each type of SAP2000 object to import, and click the OK button.

The following types of DXF objects are imported as the following SAP2000 types of objects:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| DXF Objects | SAP2000 Objects |
| Points | Special Points |
| Lines, Polylines, Arcs, Circles | Frames |
| Points, Lines | NLLinks |
| 3Dfaces | Shells |
| Polylines, Solids | Solids |

If you select the same layers to import for both SAP2000 Frames and NLLinks, the AutoCAD lines on that layer will all be imported as frame objects. If you select the same layer for both SAP2000 Frames and Solids, the polylines on that layer will be imported as series of frames objects.

## See Also

[Merge Joints](../../Edit/Edit_Points/Merge_Joints.md)

[Merge Duplicates](../../Edit/Merge_Duplicates.md)

[Merge Points](../../Assign/Joint/Merge_Numbers.md)

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_IFC_File.htm | Import IFC File -->

# Import IFC File

Form:  Import IFC File

Use the File menu > Import > Import IFC File command to import IFC files.

1. Click the  File menu > Import > Import IFC File command to display the Import IFC File form.
2. Use the top Browse button and the adjacent edit/display box to specify the path and filename of the IFC file to be imported.

SAP2000 reads the IFC file you selected and displays an account of its relevant content.

IFC files are repositories of Building Information Modeling BIM data. Most of this data is not relevant to structural analysis and accordingly not imported by SAP2000. Various types of IFC data are organized into subsets named “views” which gather data types relevant to various aspects of building design, construction, and maintenance. There are several such views, but only two views are relevant to SAP2000: the “structural analysis view”, and the “architectural coordination view”.

The structural analysis view describes a building structure in terms of nodes, elements, and loads. Files containing a structural analysis view are the most suitable for import into SAP2000, but are written by very few if any 3D building modeling programs.

The architectural coordination view describes the components of a building in architectural terms. Files containing an architectural coordination view are quite prevalent. Only some of the entities in these files are relevant to SAP2000, and whether these entities can be imported or not depends on how their geometry is described. For example, if the external faces of a beam or column are specified in the IFC file but its centerline is not, the beam or column cannot be imported. Furthermore, because the geometric extents of framing elements stop at the external faces of their supports, you will need to systematically adjust end points after import.

SAP2000 tabulates the number of “Structural Analysis Entities” on the left side of the form, and the number of “Architectural Coordination Entities” on the right side of the form.

3. Use the lower Browse button and the edit/display box next to it to specify the path and filename of a section catalog other than AISC16.XML. SAP2000 imports most IFC profiles that are subtypes of *IfcParameterizedProfileDef*, with a few exceptions such as *IfcEllipseProfileDef*. However, many 3D building modeling programs do not export section profiles this way, and instead export them as *IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef* entities which are defined by their outlines. Such profile entities are not directly usable for analysis and design. However, if their *ProfileName* attribute matches one of the section names in the section catalog you selected, these profile entities are imported as the corresponding SAP2000 section.
4. Next to the count of each type of entity is a check box. These check boxes let you control which types of IFC entities to import. If the file includes both Structural Analysis view and Architectural Coordination view entities, you should choose one type or the other. If you import both, you may get duplicate frame and shell objects.
5. Click the OK button to complete the import.

After a few moments, SAP2000 displays the imported model. If there are errors or warnings, a message box will be displayed to that effect. You should then review the log file. Its name and folder location are the same as those of the .IFC file you imported, with the extension changed to .ifcimp.log

# Import - IGES File

Form:  IGES Import

Use the File menu > Import > IGES File command to import an .igs file.

1. Click the File menu > Import > IGES File command to access the IGES Import form.
2. Click the Browse button to access the IGES File form.

   - Use the Look in drop-down list to set the path and the File name edit box to identify the .igs file to be imported.
3. Click the OK button to return to the IGES Import form.

   - The All entities present in file display area lists all entities in the file. The Entities to import display area provides the list of entities that can be chosen for import. To import an entity, check the associated check box.
   - Click the Import button to complete the import.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_NASTRAN_dat_file.htm | Import NASTRAN dat file -->

# Import - NASTRAN .dat file

Form:  NASTRAN Input File

Use the File menu > Import > NASTRAN .dat file command to import structural analysis models created using NASTRAN into SAP2000. The command imports geometry, connectivity, material and section properties, loads and constraint conditions. The import assumes that the NASTRAN files are compatible with MSC/NASTRAN Version 68.

Because NASTRAN and SAP2000 have different FEM libraries and different analytical capabilities, not all NASTRAN data can be imported; for example, curved shells cannot be imported.

1. Click the File menu > Import > NASTRAN .dat file command to display the NASTRAN Input File form.
2. Click the Read File button to display the Open NASTRAN Input File form. Use the form to locate the NASTRAN file to be imported, and click the Open button.
3. SAP2000 will redisplay the NASTRAN Input File form, read the NASTRAN file, and provide a status messages of which items were imported from the NASTRAN model and which items were ignored. The message displays in the large display area of the form.
4. If acceptable data has been identified, the Convert Data button will enable. Click that button to convert the file to a usable SAP2000 file.
5. Click the OK button to complete the import.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_OBJ_FIle.htm | Import OBJ FIle -->

# Import - OBJ File

Use the File menu > Import > OBJ File command to import a Wavefront OBJ (\*.obj) file enabling seamless integration of this type of 3D model into your workflow.

1. Click the File menu > Import > OBJ \*.obj File command to access a generic file selection form.
2. Use the Look in drop-down list to set the path and the File name edit box to identify the .obj file to be imported.
3. Click the OK button.
4. This will bring up the Import Information form.

## Import Information

- Global Up Direction: This setting identifies the orientation set in the OBJ file.
- Units: This setting identifies the units that are set in the OBJ file.
- Length Tolerance: This setting will discard elements whose lengths are less than the this tolerance.
- Max Arc Segment Length: This setting is used to discretize an arc into a series of straight lines.

## Supported Features

- Vertices, faces, normal vectors, and texture coordinates
- Triangular and quadrilateral meshes
- Group names
- Material names

## Limitations

Curves and curved surfaces (e.g. NURBS and Bézier patches) are not currently supported. These elements will be skipped during import and may result in incomplete geometry if the source model relies heavily on them.

**Important Notes**

- Ensure your OBJ files are triangular or quad-based BEFORE import.
- Use external tools to convert curved geometry into mesh approximations if needed.

**Note**: Future enhancements may include Object Names, and UV Mapping &  Shading Attributes. 

##

# Import - ProSteel Exchange Database File

Form:  ProSteel Database Import

Use the File menu > Import > ProSteel Exchange Database File command to import geometry and material property data from specified ProSteel 3D databases. ProSteel 3D is an object-oriented steel construction application based on AutoCAD. Its use and application are especially beneficial for various sectors in the steel construction industry such as structural engineering and steel-framed building construction, as well as all shape-based construction tasks.

1. Click the File menu > Import > ProSteel Exchange Database File command.
2. The ProSteel Database Import form will appear with Browse buttons that can be used to locate the exchange, material, and shape database files produced in ProSteel 3D that are to be imported.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_SAP2000_MS_Access_Database_mdb_File.htm | Import SAP2000 MS Access Database mdb File -->

# Import - SAP2000 MS Access Database mdb File

Form:  Import Tabular Database

The File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File command can be used to import model definition data that is stored in Microsoft Access database format into SAP2000 as a tabular database, usually in a file with an .mdb extension. Data can be imported into a [new model](../New_Model.md) or added to an existing model. The data could have been exported from the SAP2000 graphical user interface. For example, certain features can be [exported](../Export/Export_SAP2000_MS_Access_Database_mdb_file.md) from one model and imported into another model. In addition, exporting a model, modifying it, and then re-importing the data is useful for parameter studies and for iterative shape-finding problems.

1. Use the File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File command to access the [Import Tabular Database form](Import_Tabular_Database_Form.md) and import SAP2000 model definition data from an Access file.
2. Use the options available on the Import Tabular Database form to import the data into an existing model or to create a new model.

## See Also

[Merge Joints](../../Edit/Edit_Points/Merge_Joints.md)

[Merge Duplicates](../../Edit/Merge_Duplicates.md)

[Merge Points](../../Assign/Joint/Merge_Numbers.md)

# Import - SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File

Form:  Import Tabular Database

The File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File command can be used to import into SAP2000 model definition data that has been stored in Microsoft Excel spreadsheet format as a tabular database, usually in a file with an .xls extension. Data can be imported into a [new model](../New_Model.md) or added to an existing model. The data could have been exported from the SAP2000 graphical user interface. For example, certain features can be [exported](../Export/Export_SAP2000_MS_Excel_Spreadsheet_xls_file.md) from one model and imported into another model. In addition, exporting a model, modifying it, and then re-importing the data is useful for parameter studies and for iterative shape-finding problems.

1. Use the File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File command to access the [Import Tabular Database form](Import_Tabular_Database_Form.md) and import SAP2000 model definition data from an Excel spreadsheet file.
2. Use the options available on the Import Tabular Database form to specify the import of data into an existing model or to use the data to create a new model.

# Import - SAP2000 V6 or V7 Text Input (.s2k) File

Form:  Import Older Version Files

Model files created using  SAP2000 Version 6 or 7 can be imported into SAP2000. Older version files must first be converted to version 8 format.

1. Click the File menu > Import > SAP2000 V6 or V7 .s2k File command to access the Import Older Version Files form.
2. Click the Start Translator button to begin the process of converting an older file to a version 8 file. The Translator is a separate program that will launch and run with SAP2000 open.

   1. Click the File menu command within the Translator program and choose an option to import the appropriate file format:
   1. - Open SAP2000 V6/V7 (.SDB) File
      - Import SAP2000 V6/V7 Text (.s2k, .$sk) file. This text input file contains model definition data.

1. 2. The Open File form will appear. Use the form to select the folder containing the file to be imported, and click on the file name.
   3. After the model has been read into the Translator, use the File menu > Save as SAP2000 V8 (.sdb) File command on the Translator to save the model in the proper format for SAP2000 Version 8. It is a good idea to use a different file name for the version 8 file so as not to overwrite the previous file.
   4. Click the File menu > Exit command to close the Translator and return to SAP2000.

3. Click the File menu > Open command in SAP2000 to access the Open File form. Use the form to select the folder containing the newly saved Version 8 .SDB file.

## See Also

[Import SAP90 Text Input File](Import_SAP90_Text_Input_File.md)

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_SAP2000_V8_to_11_s2k_Text_File.htm | Import SAP2000 V8 to 11 s2k Text File -->

# Import - SAP2000 .s2k Text File

Form:  Import Tabular Database

Use the File menu > Import > SAP2000 .s2k Text File command to import SAP2000 model definition data that is stored in plain (ASCII) text format, usually in a file with an .s2k extension. Data can be imported into a [new model](../New_Model.md) or added to an existing model. The data could have been exported from the SAP2000 graphical user interface. For example, certain features can be [exported](../Export/Export_SAP2000_s2k_Text_File.md) from one model and imported into another model. In addition, exporting a model, modifying it, and then re-importing the data is useful for parameter studies and for iterative shape-finding problems.

1. Use the File menu > Import > SAP2000 .s2k Text File command to access the [Import Tabular Database form](Import_Tabular_Database_Form.md) and import SAP2000 model definition data from a plain (ASCII) text file.
2. Use the options available on the Import Tabular Database form to import the data into an existing model or to create a new model.

Tip: The complete model definition is automatically written out as a SAP2000 tabular database in a text file with extension .$2K whenever a model is saved. This file is intended for recovering the model in emergency crash situations. If for some reason you cannot open a SAP2000 model file (.SDB), try importing the corresponding .$2K file.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_SAP90_Text_Input_File.htm | Import SAP90 Text Input File -->

# Import - SAP90 Text File

Form:  Import Older Version Files

Model definition data that was saved as a text input file under SAP90 can be imported into SAP2000. The text file must be fully valid for versions 5.4 or 5.5 of SAP90 to import successfully.

Note: Some data may be interpreted differently between SAP90 and SAP2000. Be sure to check the imported model carefully.

1. Click the File menu > Import > SAP90 Text File command to access the Import Older Version Files form.
2. Click the Start Translator button. The Translator is a separate program that will launch and run with SAP2000 open and will translate the SAP90 file to a SAP2000 Version 8 file that can then be read by SAP2000.

   1. Click the File menu > Import SAP90 File command within the Translator program.
   2. The Open File form will appear. Use the form to select the folder containing the file to be imported, and click on the desired file.
   3. After the model has been read into the Translator, use the File menu > Save as SAP2000 V8 (.sdb) File command to save the model in the proper format for SAP2000 Version 8. It is a good idea to use a different file name for the version 8 file so as not to overwrite the previous file.
   4. Click the File menu > Exit command to close the Translator and return to SAP2000.

3. Click the File menu > Open command in SAP2000 to access the Open File form. Use the form to select the folder containing the newly saved Version 8 .SDB file.

See Also

[Import SAP2000 V6 or V7 s2k File](Import_SAP2000_V6_or_V7_s2k_File.md)

# Import Tabular Database Form

Use the Import Tabular Database form to specify if the imported data should be used to create a model or be added to an existing model. The form also has a button that can be used to access a form for specifying how potential data conflicts should be resolved.

1. Choose where the data is to be imported:

1. - New Model option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create a new model from the imported data. If an existing model is displayed on screen when this option is used, SAP2000 will prompt you to save it before importing the data to create a new model.
   - Add to Existing Model option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will import the data into the model displayed on screen.
   - - Click the Advanced Options button to control how SAP2000 resolves conflicts between imported data and data that is already present in the model. See [Import - Tabular Database Import Options](Import_Tabular_Database_Import_Options_Form.md) form for more information.

2. Click the OK button on the Import Tabular Database form to access an Import {Microsoft Access, Excel Spreadsheet, or SAP2000 Text} form.
3. Select the folder containing the file to be imported (.mdb, .xls, txt), and click on the desired file.
4. Click the Open button and SAP2000 will display the [Access Database Import Log](Access_Database_Import_Log_Form.md) form. Review that form before completing the import.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Import Tabular Database form as follows:  Click any of the following commands:   - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File - File menu > Import > SAP2000 V8 to V11 .s2k Text File |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Import/Import_Tabular_Database_Import_Options_Form.htm | Import Tabular Database Import Options Form -->

# Import - Tabular Database Import Options Form

Use the Tabular Database Import Options form to control the message log that is created during the import of model definition data, and to resolve conflicts between imported data and data present in an existing model. The form has the following four tabs:

TIP:  The name of the tab appears in all capital letters when that tab has been selected.

- Message Control. Use the data on the Message Control tab to control the types of messages to display, and what to do if an excessive number of errors or warnings is encountered.
- Coordinate Transformation Use the options on the Coordinate Transformation tab to control the location and orientation of objects that are imported.
- Items with Same Name  Use the options on the Items with Same Name tab to resolve conflicts between items having the same names. If items within the imported table duplicate data in the model, choose to have the imported data overwrite the model data, or have the program ignore the data in the imported table.
- Items in Same Location  Use the options on this tab to specify what to do with imported objects that have the same location as objects already in an existing model or that were previously imported. The options are assumed to be self explanatory.

Reset Tab to Defaults button. Click this button to reset the values on the displayed tab to the program defaults.

Reset All Defaults button. Click this button to reset the values on all of the tabs, including those not currently displayed, to the program defaults.

## See Also

[Merge Joints](../../Edit/Edit_Points/Merge_Joints.md)

[Merge Duplicates](../../Edit/Merge_Duplicates.md)

[Merge Points](../../Assign/Joint/Merge_Numbers.md)

Click one of the following commands to display the Import Tabular Database form.     - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Access Database .mdb File    - File menu > Import > SAP2000 MS Excel Spreadsheet .xls File    - File menu > Import > SAP2000 V8 to V11 .s2k Text File 2. Click the Advanced Options button. |

# Template - 2D Frames

The template structures available on the 2D Frames form include portal, concentric braced or eccentric braced frames.

Choose the type of frame by clicking on it in the 2D Frames Type drop-down list in the upper left corner of the form. A drawing of the selected frame type will be shown in the small display box.

[Portal Frames](javascript:TextPopup(this))

- Portal Frame Dimensions
- - Number of Stories edit box. Specify the number of stories in this edit box.
  - Story Height edit box. Specify the story height in this edit box. This height applies to all stories in the model.
  - Number of Bays edit box. Specify the number of bays in this edit box. This number applies to all stories in the model.
  - Bay Width edit box. Specify the width of the bays in this edit box. This width applies to all bays in the model.
  - Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin check box and Edit Grid button. When this check box is checked and the Edit Grid button is clicked, the [Define Grid System Data](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) form displays. Use the form to specify the grid spacing and to locate the origin as needed.
- Section Properties
- - Beams and Columns drop-down lists. SAP2000 will suggest section properties for the beams and columns in these drop-down lists. The section properties will apply to the entire length of the beams and columns.

TIP: Click the + (plus) symbol next to the drop-down lists to access the [Frame Properties form](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md); use that form to add, modify or delete a frame section definition. The [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) can be used to change the section property later, if needed.

- Restraints check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign default restraints to each point at the base of the model.

[Braced (Concentric) Frames](javascript:TextPopup(this))

- Braced Frame (Concentric) Dimensions
- - Number of Stories edit box. Specify the number of stories in this edit box.
  - Story Height edit box. Specify the story height in this edit box. This height applies to all stories in the model.
  - Number of Bays edit box. Specify the number of bays in this edit box. This number applies to all stories in the model.
  - Bay Width edit box. Specify the width of the bays in this edit box. This width applies to all bays in the model.
  - Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin check box and Edit Grid button. When this check box is checked and the Edit Grid button is clicked, the [Define Grid System Data](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) form displays. Use the form to specify the grid spacing and to locate the origin as needed.
- Section Properties
- - Beams, Columns, and Braces drop-down lists. SAP2000 will suggest section properties for the beams, columns, and braces in these drop-down lists. The section properties will apply to the entire length of the beams, columns and braces.

TIP: Click the + (plus) symbol next to the drop-down lists to access the [Frame Properties form](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md); use that form to add, modify or delete a frame section definition. The [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) or the [Assign menu > Tendon > Tendon Properties command](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) can be used to change the section property later, if needed.

- Restraints check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign default restraints to each point at the base of the model.

[Braced (Eccentric ) Frames](javascript:TextPopup(this))

- Braced Frame (Eccentric) Dimensions
- - Number of Stories edit box. Specify the number of stories in this edit box.
  - Story Height edit box. Specify the story height in this edit box. This height applies to all stories in the model.
  - Number of Bays edit box. Specify the number of bays in this edit box. This number applies to all stories in the model.
  - Bay Width edit box. Specify the width of the bays in this edit box. This width applies to all bays in the model.
  - Gap Width edit box. Specify the width of the gaps in the eccentrically braced frame.
  - Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin check box and Edit Grid button. When this check box is checked and the Edit Grid button is clicked, the [Define Grid System Data](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) form displays. Use the form to specify the grid spacing and to locate the origin as needed.
- Section Properties
- - Beams, Columns, and Braces drop-down lists. SAP2000 will suggest section properties for the beams, columns, and braces in these drop-down lists. The section properties will apply to the entire length of the beams, columns and braces.

TIP: Click the + (plus) symbol next to the drop-down lists to access the [Frame Properties form](../../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md); use that form to add, modify or delete a frame section definition. The [Assign menu > Frame > Frame Sections command](../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md) or the [Assign menu > Tendon > Tendon Properties command](../../Assign/Tendon/Tendon_Properties.md) can be used to change the section property later, if needed.

- Restraints check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign default restraints to each point at the base of the model.

Example:  Use of the portal frame template is demonstrated in [Problem A](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_A.md), [Problem G](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_G.md), [Problem K](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_K.md), [Problem L](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_L.md), [Problem N](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_N.md), [Problem Q](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_Q.md),  and [Problem V](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_V.md).

Set the Units to Metric or English using the Initialize Model from Defaults with Units drop-down list or the Initialize from Existing Model option. 3. Click the 2D Frames button. |

# Template - 3D Frames

The template structures available using the 3D Frame form include an open frame building, perimeter frame building, beam-slab building, or flat plate building.

Choose the type of frame by clicking on it in the 3D Frames Type drop-down list in the upper left corner of the form. A drawing of the selected frame type will be shown in the small display box.

[Open Frame Building or Perimeter Frame Building](javascript:TextPopup(this))

- Open Frame/Perimeter Frame Building Dimensions
- - Number of Stories edit box. Specify the number of stories for the structure in this edit box.
  - Story Height edit box.  Specify the story height in this edit box. This height applies to all stories in the structure.
  - Number of Bays, X edit box. Specify the number of bays along the X axis in this edit box. This number of bays applies to all stories in the structure.
  - Bay Width, X edit box. Specify the bay width along the X axis. This width applies to all bays along the X axes in the structure.
  - Number of Bays, Y edit box. Specify the number of bays along the Y axis in this edit box. This number of bays apples to all stories in the structure.
  - Bay Width, Y edit box. Specify the bay width along the Y axis. This width applies to all bays along the Y axes in the structure.
  - Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin check box and Edit Grid button. When this check box is checked and the Edit Grid button is clicked, the [Define Grid System Data](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) form displays. Use the form to specify the grid spacing and to locate the origin as needed.
- Section Properties
- - Beams and Columns drop-down lists. SAP2000 will suggest section properties for the beams and columns in these drop-down lists. The section properties will apply to the entire length of the beams and columns.

- Restraints check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign default restraints to each point at the base of the model.

# Template - Blank

Clicking the File menu > New Model command and selecting the Blank button will display a blank SAP2000 main screen.  Use this option to "start a model from scratch" or as the starting point for importing a model from an earlier version or from another program, such as AutoCAD or ProSteel 3D. See the File menu > Import command options for more information.

Example:  Use of this template is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md).

# Template - Grid Only

Form:  New Coord/Grid System

<!-- source: Menus/File/Model_Templates/Template_Plates_and_Pipes.htm | Template Plates and Pipes -->

# Template - Plates and Pipes Templates

The Plates and Pipes Templates form has the following areas:

- Select Object area. The available templates are listed by categories in this area (e.g., Plates, Pipes, Tubes, Pipe Supports, and so on). Click on a listed item to select it.
- Object/Model View area. When a template is clicked in the Select Object area, SAP2000 display a drawing of the selected object in the Object/Model View area of the form. The type of view can be changed by clicking the Parametric View button, the Object View button, or the Model View button. The toolbar type buttons in this area of the form can be used to Restore a full view, change the "camera angle"/perspective on the view, Pan the view, and zoom in or out on the view.
- Definitions spreadsheet area. When a template is clicked in the Select Object area, SAP2000 fills this spreadsheet with parameters that define the object and default values for those parameters for the selected object. Click in the Dimensions cell to type a revised dimension value.
- Parameters and Options area. The options available in this area depend on the selection made in the Select Object area.
- - Max Mesh Size edit box. Use this edit box to specify the maximum size for meshing of the area objects used to define the selected object.
  - Close Hole check box. Check this check box to close the hole in an object that has a hole.
  - Close End check box. Check this check box to add a closure to objects that have ends.
- Add To Current Model area. Use the edit boxes in this area to specify the Scale for the selected object in the X, Y and Z directions, or to Rotate the orientation of the object by a specified rotation angle, or to Move the placement of the object relative to the global X, Y, and Z.
- Add Current Object button. Click this button to add the selected object to the model.
- Remove Last Object button. Click this button to remove the last object added to the model. This button must be used before the OK button is clicked for it to be effective.
- Clear Current Model button. Click this button to remove all objects added to the current model. This button must be used before the OK button is clicked for it to be effective.

When the OK button is clicked, SAP2000 initializes the new model using the specified parametric and model definition values.

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Plates and Pipes Templates form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > New Model command to display the New Model form. 2. Set the Units to Metric or English using the Initialize Model from Defaults with Units drop-down list or the Initialize from Existing Model option. 3. Click the Pipes and Plates button to display the Plates and Pipes Templates form. |

# Template - Staircases

The template structures available using the Staircases form consist of three types of
staircase: Staircase Type 1 (one flight of steps per story), Staircase
Type 2 (two flights of steps per story) or Spiral Staircase.

Choose the type of staircase by clicking on it in
the Staircase Type drop-down
list in the upper left corner of the form. A drawing of the selected staircase
type will be shown in the small display box.

[Staircase
Type 1](javascript:TextPopup(this))

- Staircase Type 1 Dimensions  This type of staircase consists of
  one flight of steps per story.

Note:
 Click the Parametric Definition
button to display a drawing illustrating the following parameters.

- - Number
    of Stories edit box. Specify the number of stories
    that the staircase spans.
  - Story
    Height, +/- edit box. Specify the height of the stories.
  - Left
    Level Width, -X edit box. Specify the width of the
    staircase on its left level.
  - Stair
    Projected Length edit box. Specify the projected length
    of the staircase.
  - Right
    Level Width, +X edit box. Specify the width of the
    staircase on its right level.
  - Opening
    Btw. Stairs edit box. Specify the length of the opening
    between the flights of the staircase.
  - Width
    1, -Y edit box. Specify the width of the floor level
    in the minus Y direction.
  - Stair
    Width 2, +Y edit box. Specify the width of the staircase
    in the plus Y direction.
  - Max
    Mesh Spacing edit box. Specify the maximum mesh spacing.
  - Locate
    Origin button. Click this button to display the [Coord
    System Location and Orientation](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) [form](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md).
    Use the form to specify the location of the origin for the
    model.

    drop-down list. SAP2000 will suggest a section property for
    the areas in this drop-down list. The section property will
    apply to all of the areas.

# Template - Storage Structures

The template structures available using the Storage Structures form consist of three types
of storage structures:  Water Tower Type 1, Water Tower Type 2 or
Circular Silo.

Choose the type of storage structures by clicking
on it in the Storage Structure Type
drop-down list in the upper left corner of the form. A drawing of the
selected staircase type will be shown in the small display box.

[Water Tower Type 1 and Water
Tower Type 2](javascript:TextPopup(this)).

These template structures are essentially the
same, except Water Tower Type 2 is defined with a wide base.

Note:
 Click the Parametric Definition
button to display a drawing illustrating the following parameters.

- Dimensions
- - Num
    of Divisions, Angular edit box. Specify the number
    of angular divisions comprising the tower.
  - Max
    Spacing, Surface Z edit box. Specify the maximum spacing
    for the divisions in the Z direction. The smaller the number,
    the more divisions and more complex the structure.
  - Elevation/Diameter
    spreadsheet area. The cells in this spreadsheet specify the

    model.
- Section Properties

    drop-down list. SAP2000 will suggest a section property for

    apply to all of the areas.

TIP:
Click the + (plus) symbol next to the drop-down list to access the

modify or delete an area section definition. The [Assign menu > Areas > Area Sections command](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md)

# Template - Underground Concrete

The template underground structures available using
the Underground Concrete Structures form
include top slabs, bottom slabs, risers, top sections, bottom sections,
and 3-sided bridges for subgrade construction. Use the Underground
Concrete Structures form to specify the geometry and load for each
type of structure.

1. Click the button for
   the structural element of the underground structure to be defined:
   Top Slab, Bottom
   Slab, Riser, Top
   Section, Bottom Section or 3-Sided Bridge.
2. Click the {Structure
   Type} Properties tab and use the options to specify the geometry
   of the structural element, including specifying any holes in the structure
   or restraints, and to orient the origin of the structural element
   relative to the global coordinate system. The specific options available
   depend on the type of structure.
3. Click the Loading
   Data tab and use the options to load the structural element.
   The options available depend on the type of structure.
4. When the Top
   Slab, Top Section, or 3-Sided
   Bridge button has been clicked in Step 1, the options on the
   Truck Load tab can be used
   to specify loading resulting from a specified number of trucks on
   the structure.

1. - Restraints
     check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign
     default restraints to each point at the base of the model.
   - Gridlines check box. When this check
     box is checked, the model will display with grid lines when the
     OK button is clicked. Uncheck this
     check box to turn off the grid lines. The View
     menu > Show Grids command also can be used to turn the
     grid lines on or off after the model has been initiated.
   - Locate
     Origin button. Click this button to display the [Coord
     System Location and Orientation](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md) [form](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Coord_System_Location_and_Orientation_Form.md).
     Use the form to specify the location of the origin for the model
     relative to the global coordinate system.
   - Units
     drop-down list. Use the units displayed in this drop-down list
     or choose revised units from the drop-down list.

1. - {Structure
     Type} Properties tab
   - - Structure Properties. The
       options in this area of the forms are used to specify the
       geometry for the structure and are assumed to be self explanatory.
     - Hole Data
     - - Number
         of Holes edit box. Specify the number of holes
         using this edit box. Clicking the Update
         button will add the specified number of holes/rows to
         the spreadsheet.
       - Spreadsheet
         area. Use this area of the form to specify shape
         (rectangular or circular) and coordinates for any holes/openings
         in the Top or Bottom Slab and Top or Bottom section. Click
         the Type cells
         to select the appropriate shape (i.e., Rectangular or
         Circular). Type coordinate values in the appropriate cells
         of the spreadsheet (e.g., specify the location for the
         center of the hole relative to X and Y coordinates; specify
         the size of the hole by specifying the length in the x
         and y directions). Click the cell in the Active
         column to add or exclude the hole as defined using the
         other columns.
   - Loading
     Data tab
   - - Unit
       Weight of Soil and Depth
       of Overburden edit boxes. Use the defaults or specify
       values for the unit weight of soil on the underground structure
       and the depth of the overburden.
     - Consider
       Water Table check box and Unit
       Weight of Water and Distance
       Below Grade edit boxes. When this check box is checked,
       the loading effects of groundwater on the underground structure
       will be considered. Use the default value for the unit weight
       of the water or use the edit box to specify another value.
       Also indicate the depth of groundwater below grade.
     - Include
       Traffic Loading check box and Equivalent
       Surcharge, q edit box. When this check box is checked,
       traffic loading on the structure will be considered. Use the
       default value for equivalent surcharge or specify another
       value in the edit box.
     - LL
       Surcharge Pressure (Lateral) check box and Surcharge
       Pressure, p edit box. When this check box is checked,
       live load surcharge pressure will be considered. Use the default
       or use the edit box to specify another surcharge pressure
       value.
     - Include
       Top Structure Loading and Equivalent
       Distributed Load, w edit box. When the structure is
       a Bottom Slab, check this check box and use the edit box to
       specify an equivalent distributed load to represent the top
       structure loading on the bottom slab.
     - Include
       Lateral Earth Pressure check box. For all structure
       types except Top and Bottom Slab, check this check box to
       include lateral earth pressures on the structure.
     - Include
       Cover Soil Loading check box. For all structure types
       except Riser, check this check box to include cover soil in
       the load calculation.
   - Truck
     Load tab. Use the spreadsheet on this tab to specify truck
     loading data. First use the Number
     of Trucks edit box to specify the number of trucks for
     which loading data will be provided. Then click the Update
     button to add or remove rows from the spreadsheet area. Use the
     cells in the spreadsheet to locate the load (X Center and Y Center),
     specify the size (X Size and Y Size), specify the Total Load per
     vehicle, assign the load to a Load Case, and specify if the load
     is active (Yes) or not (No).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Underground Concrete Structures form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > New Model    command to display the    New Model form. 2. Set    the Units to Metric or English using the Initialize    Model from Defaults with Units drop-down    list or the Initialize from Existing Model option. 3. Click    the Underground    Concrete button. |

# Template - Wall

Use the Shear Wall form to specify the following items by typing directly in the edit boxes or checking or unchecking the check boxes.

Shear Wall Dimensions

- Number of Divisions, X edit box. Specify the number of divisions along the X axis.
- Division Width, X edit box. Specify the width of the divisions along the X axis.
- Number of Divisions,  Z edit box Specify the number of divisions along the Z axis.
- Division Width, Z edit box. Specify the width of the divisions along the Z axis.
- Use Custom Grid Spacing and Locate Origin check box and Edit Grid button. When this check box is checked and the Edit Grid button is clicked, the [Define Grid](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) [System Data](../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Grid_System_Data_Form.md) form displays. Use the form to specify the grid spacing and to locate the origin as needed.

Section Properties

- Areas drop-down lists. Choose the section property for the areas from this drop-down list. The section property chosen will apply to all of the areas in the wall.

TIP: Click the + (plus) symbol next to the drop-down list to access the [Area Sections form](../../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md); use that form to add, modify or delete an area section definition. The [Assign menu > Areas > Area Sections command](../../Assign/Area/Area_Sections.md) can be used to change the section property later, if needed.

Restraints check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 will assign default restraints to each point at the base of the model.

Example:  Use of this template is demonstrated in [Problem B](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_B.md), [Problem F](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_F.md) and [Problem U](../../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

|  |
| --- |
| Access the Shear Wall form as follows:   1. Click the File menu > New Model command to display the New Model form. 2. Set the Units to Metric or English using the Initialize Model from Defaults with Units drop-down list or the Initialize from Existing Model option. 3. Click the Wall button. |

<!-- source: Menus/File/Modify-Show_Comments_and_Log.htm | Modify-Show Comments and Log -->

# Modify/Show Comments and Log

Form:  Log

Use the File menu > Modify/Show Comments and Log command to access the Log form. SAP2000 will automatically record in the Log when and where the file was stored. The Log can also be used to track the status of the model to date, to keep a "to-do" list for the model, and to retain key results that can be used to monitor the effects of changes to the model. Those notations can be deleted or modified and comments can be typed directly into the log at any time.

Click the Write to Text File button to generate a text file containing the text from the log.

Click the Done button to close the Log form.

## See Also

[Show Input-Output Text File](Show_Input-Output_Text_File.md)

# Modify/Show Project Information

Form: Project Information

The data entered on the Project Information
form can be added to printed output ([Print
Tables](Print_Tables.md) or [Custom
Report Writer](Advanced_Report_Writer/Advanced_Report_Writer.md)) and included in an exported file or an on-screen [display](../Display/Show_Tables.md) using the [Choose Tables For {Editing, Display, Printing, Export}
form](../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md) and selecting the Model Definition
area, Miscellaneous Data type,
Project Information table.

1. Click the File
   menu > Modify/Show Project Information command or click
   the Modify/Show Info button on the [New Model form](New_Model.md)
   to access the Project Information form.
2. Type directly in the
   edit boxes to enter project data in the Project
   Information List area of the form.

1. - Use the Edit
     menu on the form to Cut, Copy, Paste and Delete text in
     the Project Information List
     area of the form.
   - Click in a row and
     use the Clear Data button to clear
     the data in the row.
   - Click the Clear All button to clear all rows of data
   - Click the Add Row button to add a new Item
     and Data row after the
     Program Defined items (e.g., Company Name, Client Name, Project
     Name) in the Project Information
     List area of the form. Type directly in the resulting edit
     boxes.
   - Click on a row that
     you have entered and click the Insert Row
     button to insert a row above the selected row.
   - Click on a row that
     you have entered and click the Delete Row
     button to delete the selected row.

Note
that the Insert and Delete
buttons cannot be used on Program Defined items.

The project information can be edited using the [Edit menu > Interactive Database Editing
command](../Edit/Interactive_Database_Editing_Form.md) as well as using the Project Information
form, as described herein.

Portions of this information can also be used on a report cover using
the [Report Item - Cover Page form](Advanced_Report_Writer/Report_Item_Cover_Page_Form.md).

## See Also

[Show Input-Output
Text File](Show_Input-Output_Text_File.md)

# New Model

Form:  New Model

Click the File menu > New Model command to access the New Model form and start a new model. The form has options to initialize the model and to start the model from template files. Initializing the model determines the units to be used and the default definitions of all properties, loads, analysis cases,and the like—everything except the grids, objects, and assignments to the objects. The template files include a wide range of typical structures. The templates typically produce structures with uniform spacing, unless you choose to modify the spacing using the individual template forms (see below). After a model has been generated using a template, the model can be modified using the commands on the Edit, Draw, Define, and Assign menus.

- New Model Initialization. Select one of the following options:
- - Initialize the Model from Defaults with Units option and drop-down list. When this option is selected, SAP will use the default program definitions. The default definitions are typical for the choice made in the Select Template area of the form (see below). Where necessary, the default definitions can be modified using the commands on the Define and Assign menus. Use the drop-down list to specify the units to be used in the model.

Note: The units used to start a model become the base units for that model. If different units are used in the model, they are always converted to and from these base units. The model will always open in the base units, so choose the units carefully.

- - Initialize Model from an Existing File  option. When this option is selected, SAP will use the units and definitions from an existing model. This method is generally preferable if common sets of properties, analyses, and design definitions are to be used for projects of a certain type. If this option is selected, click one of the template buttons in the Select Template area of the form. Then, when the program displays the Open Model File form, specify the path and filename for a previously stored model file that is to be used for initializing the new model.
- Modify/Show Info button. Click the button to access the [Project Information form](Modify-Show_Project_Information.md). Use that form to add project specific information that will appear in the various forms of output, including [written reports](Create_Report.md).
- Select Template. This area of the form has several buttons with drawings of typical structures.
- 1. Click the button that most closely describes the structure to be modeled. The model can be modified using the commands on the Edit, Draw, Define, and Assign menus. However, choosing a template that closely resembles the structure to be analyzed and designed can greatly speed the overall modeling process.
  2. A form specific to the type of structure will appear. Choose or change the default values in the edit boxes on the form. Also, use the appropriate Section Properties drop-down list(s) to specify the [frame, chord, brace](../Define/Section_Properties/Frame_Sections/Frame_Section.md) or [area](../Define/Section_Properties/Area_Sections/Define_Area_Sections.md) section properties for the model. The drop-down list(s) provide access to additional forms that can be used to define the [material properties](../Define/Material/Define_Materials.md).
  3. Click the OK button to close the form. SAP will display the selected structure in the active window.

Note: Remember to save your model periodically. Click the Save button ![](../../assets/images/Images/SAVE_shg.gif) or use the File menu > Save command.

The [Edit menu > Add to Model from Template command](../Edit/Add_to_Model_from_Template.md) also will access these templates and add them to an existing model.

The following table identifies the structure templates available and the buttons to be clicked on the New Model form to access them.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Open.htm | Open -->

# Open

To open an existing SAP2000 model, click the File menu > Open command to access a standard Windows form for opening files. Select the folder where the SAP2000 file is located. Models are saved in a binary file with an .SDB extension.

If a file created using Version 6 or 7 of SAP2000 is selected, the file must first be translated into Version 8 before it can be used in this version. See [Import SAP2000 V6 or V7 s2k File](Import/Import_SAP2000_V6_or_V7_s2k_File.md)  for more information.

Quickly access the most recently opened SAP2000 models by clicking on the file name listed near the bottom of the File menu, above the File menu > Exit command.

Tip: The complete model definition is automatically written as a SAP2000 tabular database in a text file with a .$2K extension whenever the model is saved. If for some reason the model cannot be opened using the .SDB file, try importing the corresponding .$2K file. See [Import SAP2000 V8 to V11 .s2k Text File](Import/Import_SAP2000_V8_to_11_s2k_Text_File.md) for more information.

## See Also

[Starting SAP2000 from the Command Line](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Starting_SAP2000_from_the_Command_Line.md)
