<!-- source: Menus/File/Report_Setup.htm | Report Setup -->

# Report Setup

Form:  Report Setup Data

Click the File menu > Report Setup command to access the Report Setup Data form. Use the options on the form to specify the types of data and output format for generating a report for the model file open when the command is executed. Additional options that allow further refinement of the report layout, including combining data from multiple model files into a single report, are available using the [File menu > Advanced Report Writer](Advanced_Report_Writer/Advanced_Report_Writer.md) command.

After specifying the report layout using the  Report Setup Data form, click the [File menu > Create Report command](Create_Report.md) to identify the filename and path for saving the file and then to generate the report in the specified format (see Report Output Type below).

- Report Contents File. Use these options to specify the types of data and the general layout for the data to be included in the report as specified in a .xml file, including, for example, company logos and names on the cover page. Use the [Help menu > Documentation command](../Help/Documentation.md) to access  more information about the specific structure of the .xml file.
- - Default File option. As indicated on the form, when this option is selected, SAP2000 reads the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file located in the user settings folder. If the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file does not exist or is not in the settings directory, SAP2000 will prompt for a different name.
  - - ? If you are having difficulties locating the settings folder, click the "?" (question mark)  and a form showing the path to your settings folder will display. Note that this folder may be hidden.
  - User Specified option. When this option is selected, the Report Contents XML File form will display. Use that form to select the path and filename of a user-created .xml file. Click the Browse button to enable a search of your system for a filename and path. The documentation accessible using the Help menu > Documentation command provides an example to demonstrate how to create an alternate .xml file.
- Table Format File display box and Browse button. The format file (.fmt) to be used for specifying the layout of the tables to be included in the report is displayed in this display box. Format files can be created using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md) and edited using the [Table Format File Data form](../Options/Database/Edit_Format_File.md).
- Report Output Type options
- - RTF File (Microsoft Word). When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create the report with an RTF (rich text format) extension using the path and filename you specify after clicking the File menu > Create Report command. The format is compatible with Microsoft Word.
  - HTML File (Internet Explorer). When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create the report with an HTML (hype-text markup language) extension using the path and filename you specify after clicking the File menu > Create Report command. The format is compatible with Internet Explorer.
  - Text to Printer. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will send the report directly to the default printer.
  - Text File (No Pictures). When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create the report with a TXT extension using the path and filename you specify after clicking the  File menu > Create Report command. The format of the printout will be suitable for 8.5 x 11 inch paper, with either portrait or landscape orientation. Note that with this option, any graphics associated with the selected output will be excluded from the print.
  - Text File With No Splits (No Pictures). When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create the report with a TXT extension using the path and filename you specify after clicking the  File menu > Create Report command. The format of the printout will be suitable for continuous feed printers. Note that with this option, any graphics associated with the selected output will be excluded from the print.
- Report Group drop-down list. This drop-down list can be used to specify the [Group(s)](../Define/Groups.md) for which data will be included in the report. This option is helpful in focusing the report on key components in your model.
- Report Page Orientation options. Choose Portrait or Landscape orientation. Portrait output is longer than it is wide, and landscape output is wider than it is long.
- Report Items options.
- - Include Cover Page (Based on Project Information) check box. When this check box is checked, the information input using the File menu > Modify/Show Project Information command and [Project Information form](Modify-Show_Project_Information.md) will appear on the cover page of the report. If no information is provided on that form, the program will draw from the registration information used for the computer being used to create the report.
  - Include Hyperlinked Contents (RTF and HTML) check box. When this check box is checked, the contents of the report will include  hyperlinks to the various sections in the report. This option is compatible with the RTF File and HTML File Report Output Types only.
  - Include Filter Criteria String Beneath Table Titles check box. When this check box is checked, any filter criteria specified in the .fmt file will be printed beneath the table title(s). Note that filter criteria can be specified using the [Modify/Show Database Table Format form](../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md), which is used to create the Table Format File (.fmt) -- see above.
- Load Patterns Select Load Patterns button. Click this button to access the Select Load Patterns form. Highlight the [load pattern(s)](../Define/Load_Pattern/Define_Load_Patterns.md) to be included in the report. Click the Clear All button on that form to exclude data for all load patterns.
- Load Cases/Combos (Results) Select Load Cases/Combos button. Click this button to display the Select Load Cases form. Use that form to select the load cases to be included in the report.
- Output Options Modify/Show Output Options button. Click this button to display the Output Options form. Use that form to set output parameters for each load case type. Click on an option to select it. For time history load cases and other load cases with multi-valued responses, specify that the output be generated as envelopes or as step-by-step results.
- Output Selections drop-down list and Modify/Show Output Selection button. This drop-down list and button are available only if the model file includes one or more of the following:  [generalized displacement](../Define/Generalized_Displacements.md), [section cut](../Define/Section_Cuts.md), or [named sets](../Define/Named_Sets.md) (virtual work, pushover, joint time history response spectra, plot function traces). Use the drop-down list to indicate that data for one of the preceding items be included in the report. Select an item and then clicked the Modify/Show Output Selection button to display the Select {item} form. Use that form to specify the specific items to be included in the report.

<!-- source: Menus/File/Save_and_Save_As.htm | Save and Save As -->

# Save and Save As

Use the File menu > Save command to
save a SAP2000 model. SAP will prompt you to save the file on a periodic
basis if the Options menu > Auto Save File
command is used and the appropriate option is selected on the [Model Save Options form](../Options/Auto_Save_Model.md). It is still prudent,
however, to use the File menu > Save command
from time to time to perform a full save of model.

If the model has not been saved previously, SAP will prompt for a path
and filename. If the file has been previously saved, SAP will store the
file in the same location with the same filename, overwriting the previous
version. SAP will save the model in a binary file and append an .SDB extension.

Use the File menu > Save As command
to save a model file using a different name. When the command is used,
SAP will prompt for the new path and filename. If major changes are to
be made to a model, it may be prudent to save a version of the file under
a separate name before making the changes. In addition, saving the file
under different names as work progresses can be helpful.

SAP will prompt you to save the model before exiting the program if
any changes were made to it since the last time the file was saved.

Note:  SAP2000
automatically saves the model when the analysis is run.

Important:
 If any analyses have been run, SAP will save the analysis results
along with the file when the File menu > Save
command is used. However, SAP will not
save the analysis results along with the file when the File
menu > Save As command is used. Thus, use the File
menu > Save command before using the File
menu > Save As command.

# Show Input/Output Text File

Form:  Display Text File

The File menu > Show Input/Output Text Files command provides a convenient way to view input and output text files. The input text files might include those with the .$2k and .s2k extensions and perhaps any time history or response spectrum text files. The output files might include the output printed to a file rather than to a printer. Typically, those files have a .txt extension.

1. Click the File menu > Show Input/Output Text Files command to access the Display Text File form.
2. Select the path and filename for the file to be viewed. Click the Open button to display the file using Windows WordPad.
3. Use the menu commands in WordPad to print, save, edit, or format the file as necessary.

# Contents and Index

Use the Help menu > Contents and Help command to display this Help utility. SAP2000 has Contents, Search and Index tabs. Use any of those tabs to locate the information you need to use the program effectively.

- The Contents tab displays a listing of the various books and topics included in the Help.
- Use the edit box on the Search tab to initiate a keyword search.
- The edit box on the Index tab can also be used to initiate a search of the topics that have been indexed for the Help.

The Help utility also has Back, Forward, Home, and Print buttons. The Back and Forward buttons can be used to move from screen to screen within the utility. The Home button can be used to display the default Help screen. Use the Print button to print any of the displayed topics.

<!-- source: Menus/Help/Documentation.htm | Documentation -->

# Documentation

Form:  SAP2000 Documentation

Use the Help menu > Documentation command to display the  SAP2000 Documentation form and display documentation related to SAP2000. The form displays topics in a tree structure in a list box. Click the Display Selected Document button to open the document for the selected topic. The document files related to the topics must be stored in the appropriate directories. If they are not, new directory paths may be set using the [Set File Paths button.](Document_File_Path.md)

With the list of documents displayed, right click on a document title to display a description of the document contents.

# User Added Documentation

The listing of documents available using the Help menu > Documentation command can be modified by the user as follows.

1. Locate the Microsoft Access database file SapDocs.mdb in the Manuals subfolder where SAP is installed; that Access database file controls the Help menu> Documentation command and is used to determine the documents listed in the display area of the SAP2000 Documentation form.
2. Copy the SapDocs.mdb file and rename it to SapDocsn.mdb, where n can be any single digit from 0 to 9. If there are multiple files, the one with the highest digit n is used.
3. To add your own documents to the list of documents on the SAP2000 Documentation form, such as documents outlining company standards or documents translated into other languages, edit the SapDocsn.mdb file created in Step 2 using Microsoft Access.

Note:  Be sure to use the file created in Step 2 when editing as described in Step 3 because the original SapDocs.mdb (the file found in Step 1)  includes the default document title list provided with the program, and thus the original file (SapDocs.mdb) may be overwritten in future updates of the program.  Also note that the "Control" table in the SapDocsn.mdb file defines the table names that are used to organize the listing of individual document titles on the SAP2000 Documentation form; that is, the input provided on the Control table defines the tree-like structure used to display document titles on the SAP2000 Documentation form.

4. Use the Help menu > Documentation command to access the SAP2000 Documentation form. The document titles in the SapDocsn.mdb file after Step 3 should now appear in the display list of the SAP2000 Documentation form.

<!-- source: Menus/Help/Getting_Help.htm | Getting Help -->

# Getting Help

Support is available free of charge for 90 days following purchase and thereafter in accordance with the terms of your maintenance agreement. Please call CSI’s offices to inquire about the maintenance agreement. Standard phone and fax support is available from CSi support engineers in the United States via a toll call between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. Pacific time, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays.

If you are experiencing problems using the software:

- Consult the documentation and other printed information included with the software.
- Check the online Help for the command or form.
- Visit CSI’s web site at [www.csiamerica.com](https://www.csiamerica.com) to access the SAP "Watch &Learn Movies."

If you cannot find a solution:

- Contact CSI’s Offices via phone at (510) 845-2177.
- Send a fax with questions and a sketch of the model to CSi at (510) 845-4096.
- Send the input file via E-mail to [support@csiamerica.com](mailto:support@csiamerica.com).

If you call, be at your computer and have the appropriate documentation (e.g., User’s manual) at hand. Please have the following information:

- The version number of the program (access using the Help menu > About SAP2000 command--see below).
- The hardware configuration (computer make, operating system, hard disk size and RAM size).
- The exact wording of error messages that appeared on screen.
- A description of what happened and what operation was being performed  when the problem occurred.
- A description of any attempts to solve the problem.

If you send a Fax or E-mail, include the following information:

- Your name, Company name, and phone number.
- The version and version number of the program (access using the Help menu > About SAP2000 command--see below).
- The hardware configuration (computer make, operating system, hard disk size and RAM size).
- The exact wording of any error messages that appeared on screen.
- A description of what happened and what operation was being performed when the problem occurred.
- A description of any attempts to solve the problem.
- For E-mail only:  an attachment, including the model and any other pertinent data files.

## About SAP2000

The About SAP2000 form provides some useful and important information about SAP2000 and about your computer. When contacting us for technical support or for information on product upgrades, you should always tell us the version of the program that you are using. Find this version number by clicking the Help menu > About SAP2000 command and reading the first (top) line on the left-hand side of the form. It will say something like "SAP2000 Nonlinear Version x.xx" or "SAP2000 Plus Version x.xx."

In addition, when you have technical support questions that may be related to the physical memory in your computer, or to your computer's operating system, always tell us about your computer's memory and operating system. You can find this information in the bottom of the left-hand side of the About SAP2000 form.

# Auto Refresh

When the Options menu >
Auto Refresh command is active (preceded by a check mark), SAP2000
will automatically update the on-screen display each time changes are
made. When working with a very large or complex model, turning this feature
off may be helpful to reduce downtime associated with redrawing the model.
When the feature is turned off, use the Refresh Window
button ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-318063808.gif) or the View
menu > Refresh View command to update the on-screen display.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Auto_Save_Model.htm | Auto Save Model -->

# Auto Save Model

Form: Model Auto Save Options

The Options menu > Auto Save Model command toggles the auto save features on and off.

1. Click the Options menu > Auto Save Model command to display the Model Auto Save Options form.
2. Choose the appropriate option for automatically saving the model files.

   - Auto Save Model File at Specified Intervals option and Interval in Minutes edit box. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will automatically save the .SDB file. Specify how frequently the model is to be saved by entering a value in the Interval in Minutes edit box.  
       
     When the specified interval of minutes has passed, SAP2000 will display a prompt indicating it is time to save the model. Click the OK or Cancel button.
   - Always Save .$2k Text File option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will automatically save the text file associated with the model. The .$2k file contains the complete model definition as a SAP2000 tabular database. The file is intended for recovering the model in emergency crash situations. If for some reason the SAP2000 model file (.SDB) can not be opened, it may be possible to open the model by importing the corresponding .$2k file.

# Colors

Form:  Assign Display Colors, Assign Output Colors

Use the Options menu > Colors > Display command to specify colors used by the program for on-screen display; use the Options menu > Colors > Output command to specify colors for printing to a color or monochrome printer.

1. Click the Options menu > Colors > Display or the Options menu > Colors > Output command to display the Assign Display Colors form or the Assign Output Colors form.

- Use the options on the Assign Display Colors form to set colors for viewing the structural configuration, including joints, frames, shells, grids and the background.
- Use the options on the Assign Output Colors form to set the colors for the analysis and design results.

2. On either tab, choose to set the colors for the screen and the printer.

- Select screen or printer.
- Change the colors by clicking the appropriate button on the form or by double clicking on the appropriate color.
- Select a new color and click the OK button.

3. Click the Reset button to restore the SAP2000 defaults.
4. Click the OK button.

Note: The Default printer colors are set for a monochrome printer. Manually select the colors to print in color and check the Use Color Printer checkbox.

You may also use the Show Frame Section Thickness in Extruded Views check box to better view the thickness of various elements of a cross section. Extruded views can be set using the View menu > [Set Display Options](../View/Set_Display_Options.md) command.

Form:  Database Documentation to Word

Use the Options menu > Database > Documentation to Word command to create a file(s) in Microsoft Word format that identifies the types of data in the database, including a brief descriptions of the function of the data, the units, the format and the like.

Note:  Use the [Choose Tables For form](../../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md)  to access the data within the database and display, print, or export the data in  Microsoft Word or Excel format.

   - Document All Tables option. When this option is selected, SAP2000 will create the documentation for all tables included in the model file.

3. File Name and Set File Name button. Click the Set File Name button to display the Save Database Documentation As form and specify the file name for the document. After the file has been created, it can be opened as a document in the Microsoft Word program, version Word 97 or later.

Open Word File after Documentation is Created check box. When this check box is checked, Microsoft Word will launch automatically and open the newly created database file in Microsoft Word format.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Database/Set_Current_Format_File_Source.htm | Set Current Format File Source -->

# Set Current Format File Source

Form: Set Database Table Formats File

The database table format may be altered using the Options menu > Database > Set Current File Source command. Select from the options available on the Set Database Table Formats File form.

- Program Default option. This is the default. When this option is selected, SAP2000 uses the default table formats programmed into the software when generating table.
- Default File option. As indicated on the form, when this option is selected, SAP2000 uses the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file located in the same directory as the Sap2000.exe file. If the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file does not exist or is not in the same directory as the Sap2000.exe file, a prompt will appear indicating that one of the other options must be selected.
- User Specified File option and the Browse button. When this option is selected, the Database Table Formats File form will display. Use that form to specify the file name and path for a [previously defined table format](../../../Database_Tables/Modify_Show_Database_Table_Format_Form.md) to be used when generating tables. As necessary, click the Browse button to redisplay the form  and locate another .xml file.

[Edit Format File](Edit_Format_File.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Database/Set_Current_Table_Name_Source.htm | Set Current Table Name Source -->

# Set Current Table Name Source

Form: Set Table Name Source

The database table names may be altered using the Options menu > Database > Set Current Table Name Source command. Select from the options available on the Set Table Name Source form.

- Program Default option. This is the default. When this option is selected, SAP2000 uses the default table names programmed into the software when generating table.
- Default File option. As indicated on the form, when this option is selected, SAP2000 reads the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file located in the user settings folder. If the SapDefaultFormatFile.fmt file does not exist or is not in the settings directory, SAP2000 will prompt for a different name.
- - ? If you are having difficulties locating the settings folder, click the "?" (question mark)  and a form showing the path to your settings folder will display. Note that this folder may be hidden.
- User Specified File option and the Browse button. When this option is selected, the Table Name Source XML File form will display. Use that form to specify the file name and path for a previously defined .xml file to be used when generating tables. As necessary, click the Browse button to redisplay the form and locate another .xml file. For more information about .xml files, use the Help menu > Documentation command to access .xml topics.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Dimensions_Tolerances.htm | Dimensions Tolerances -->

# Dimensions/Tolerances

Click the Options menu > Dimensions/Tolerances command to access the Dimensions/Tolerances Preferences form. The following items can be specified:

- Auto Merge Tolerance. This item is used as a basic tolerance check in the model. It is entered in length units. The SAP2000 default for this item is 0.1 inch in English units and 1 mm in metric units. Following are some typical uses of the tolerance.
- - When a joint is drawn or generated within this distance from another joint, the drawn/generated joint is merged into the original joint.
  - If a joint is within this distance from a frame, the joint is assumed to be supported by the frame. When the analysis is run, the frame is broken up at the joint and connected to the joint. Note that this might put a small kink in the frame if the joint is not exactly on the frame.
  - If a joint is within this distance from being in a plane, it is assumed to be in the plane.
- 2D View Cutting Planes, +/-.   All objects within this specified distance from a 2D planar view will be included in the 2D view.
- Plan Fine Grid Spacing. This is the spacing of invisible grid points that are used by the [Draw menu > Snap to > Fine Grid command](../Draw/Snap_To.md) and the associated Snap to Invisible Grid button. This item is entered in length units. The SAP2000 default for this item is 12 inches in English units or 304.8 mm in metric units.

Note:  The Change Plan Fine Grid Spacing form is a shortcut that can be used to adjust the fine grid spacing. Choose to apply the change relative to the origin or the last click. Access the Change Plan Fine Grid Spacing form by right clicking on a grid line and selecting the Plan Fine Grid Spacing option from the resulting drop-down list.

- Plan Nudge Value. This is the distance that a [nudged object](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Nudge_Feature.md) moves after you have pressed the appropriate key on the keyboard. This item is entered in length units. The SAP2000 default for this item is 12 inches in English units or 304.8 mm in metric units.

Note:  The Change Plan Nudge Value form is a shortcut that can be used to adjust the nudge value. Access the Change Plan Nudge Value form by right clicking on a grid line and selecting the Plan Nudge Value option from the resulting drop-down list.

- Screen Selection Tolerance. When clicking on an object to select it, the mouse pointer must be within this distance of the object to select it. This item is entered in pixels. The screen selection tolerance has no effect on selection by windowing. The SAP2000 default for this item is 3 pixels.
- Screen Snap to Tolerance. When using the [snap features](../Draw/Snap_To.md) in SAP2000, the mouse pointer must be within this distance of a snap location to snap to it. This item is entered in pixels. The SAP2000 default for this item is 12 pixels.
- Screen Line Thickness. This parameter controls the thickness of lines on the screen. All lines are affected except for the bounding plane line. The thickness is entered in pixels. This item has no effect on text fonts. It also does not affect the aerial view. The SAP2000 default for this item is 1 pixel.
- Printer Line Thickness. This parameter controls the thickness of lines and fonts that are output to the printer. All lines are affected. The thickness is entered in pixels. The SAP2000 default for this item is 4 pixels.
- Maximum Graphic Font Size. When the [zoom in feature](../View/Zoom_Feature.md) is used, the font size becomes proportionately larger. However the font size is never made larger than the specified maximum graphic font size. The maximum graphic font size is entered in points. The SAP2000 default for this item is 8 points. This font size does not apply to the grid line identification labels whose size is determined by the specified size of the bubble.
- Minimum Graphic Font Size. When the [zoom out feature](../View/Zoom_Feature.md) is used, the font size becomes proportionately smaller. However the font size is never made smaller than the specified minimum graphic font size. The minimum graphic font size is entered in points. The SAP2000 default for this item is 3 points. Changing the minimum graphic font size can be helpful to increase the minimum font size to make it easier to read the on-screen display. This font size does not apply to the grid line identification labels whose size is determined by the specified size of the bubble.
- Auto Zoom Step. This is the size of the step used for the View menu > Zoom In One Step command and the View menu > Zoom Out One Step command as well as their associated toolbar buttons. This parameter is entered in percentage. The magnification of all objects in a view is increased or decreased by this percentage. The SAP2000 default for this item is 10%.
- Shrink Factor. When you shrink the objects in a view using the Shrink Object Toggle button, ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-489955461.gif), all line objects are shrunk by this specified percentage. The SAP2000 default for this item is 70%. Note that you can also shrink objects by selecting the [View menu > Set Display Options command](../View/Set_Display_Options.md), or its associated button ![](../../assets/images/Images/Set%20Display%20Options%20button.GIF), and checking the Object Shrink Objects check box in the General area of the Display Options for Active Window form. Typically area objects are not shrunk by this percentage. Instead they are shrunk by a set number of pixels that is built into the program. In the unusual case where shrinking the area object by the set number of pixels causes it to become an illegal object (because an edge has zero length), the area object reverts to using the percentage specified here.
- Max Line Length in Text File. This factor is the number of characters SAP2000 will use in a line of text before wrapping the text to another line when a .S2k or .$2k file is created.

Use the Reset to Default button to restore all items on the form to default values.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem C](../../Example_Problems/Problem_C.md), [Problem G](../../Example_Problems/Problem_G.md), [Problem J](../../Example_Problems/Problem_J.md), and [Problem N](../../Example_Problems/Problem_N.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Options/Graphic_Mode_Settings_Form.htm | Graphic Mode Settings Form -->

# Graphic Mode Settings Form

Click the Options menu > Graphics Mode > Graphic Mode Settings command to display the Graphic Mode Settings form,  which offers controls for the graphical effects used to display the model.

Note:  Each time the program is launched, the program "remembers" which graphical mode was set the last time the program was used.

 Use the tabs on the form to set display parameters when the graphics mode has been set to GDI Plus or DirectX. Where applicable, use these options in conjunction with the options available on the [Display Options for Active Window form](../View/Set_Display_Options.md) to enhance the display and make the effects more noticeable and thus easier to interpret. The potential effects of using these display controls on the speed of the program depends on the graphics card and computer configuration.

- GDI Plus tab - GDI Plus makes two-dimensional drawing easier.
- - Text check box and drop-down list. Check this check box and then select a font from the drop-down list to change the font used to display text on the model.
  - Anti Aliasing of Lines check box. Anti-aliasing is the technique of minimizing aliasing (jagged or blocky patterns) when representing an image. This option is enabled/applied when the check box is checked.
  - Transparency check box. Check this check box to allow line and area objects to be displayed as transparent, rather then solid, objects. The amount or intensity of the transparency is specified using the Options menu > Colors > Display command.
- DirectX tab - Direct X is better suited for displaying full color graphics and 3D animation.
- - Text check box and drop-down list. Check this check box and then select a font from the drop-down list to change the font used to display text on the model.
  - Anti Aliasing of Lines check box. Anti-aliasing is the technique of minimizing aliasing (jagged or blocky patterns) when representing an image. This option is enabled/applied when the check box is checked.
  - Transparency check box. Check this check box to allow line and area objects to be displayed as transparent, rather then solid, objects. The amount or intensity of the transparency is specified using the Options menu > Colors > Display command.
  - N-Patch Tessellation check box. N-path tessellation is an advanced DirectX rendering option that tessallates the frame object mesh (only in [extrude view](../View/Set_Display_Options.md)) using the N-path tessellation scheme. For patch tessellation, SAP2000 uses five extra points to create smooth edges. Check this box to enable this feature.
  - Line Vertical Offset edit box. This offset provides a small distance between parallel lines and surfaces that represent different faces of an object when rendering certain graphical results, such as contour plots. Typically, the default value should be used.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Graphics_Card_Information.htm | Graphics Card Information -->

# Video Care Information

Use the Options menu > Graphics Mode > Graphics Card(s) Information command to open the Video Care Information window. This window shows the ID, Memory, Description, and Compatibility for the various graphics cards for your system. SAP2000 will which generally determine which graphics card to use for rendering based on the one with the most GPU memory.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Options/Graphics_Mode.htm | Graphics Mode -->

# Graphics Mode

Use the Options menu > Graphics Mode command to specify GDI Plus or ActiveX display mode. Then the Options menu > Graphics Mode > Graphics Mode Settings command can be used to display the [Graphics Mode Settings form](Graphic_Mode_Settings_Form.md); use that for to  refine the model display.  When some of the options are used in conjunction with the options available on the [Display Options for Active Window form](../View/Set_Display_Options.md), the display of various objects in the model is more noticeable and thus easier to interpret. The potential effects of using these commands on the speed of the program depends on the graphics card and computer configuration.

- GDI Plus (Standard) command  -- GDI Plus makes two-dimensional drawing easier.
- DirectX command -- Direct X is better suited for displaying full color graphics and 3D animation..

Note:  Each time the program is launched, the program "remembers" which graphical mode was set the last time the program was used.

Note:  For each of the commands, the  [Options menu > Colors > Display command](Colors.md) can be used to specify a color scheme. When the SAP2000 query asks if you want to switch to the default background color, select No to use the color scheme specified using the .Options menu > Colors > Display command.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Options/Locking_and_Unlocking_the_Model.htm | Locking and Unlocking the Model -->

# Locking and Unlocking the Model

Use the  Options menu > Lock Model
command or the corresponding toolbar button![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-192273012.gif) to lock
or unlock the model. This command functions as a toggle, alternately locking
and unlocking the model.

Locking the model prevents changes to it. SAP2000 automatically locks
the model after running an analysis to prevent any changes that would
invalidate the analysis results. When the model is locked, most Edit,
Draw, Define and Assign commands that directly affect the objects are
not available. One exception is the Define menu
> Load Cases commands, which can be used to define or modify
a load  case when the model is locked. If the definition of a load
case that has already been run is changed, SAP2000 will display a warning
that the analysis results will be deleted for that case and for all cases
that depend on it.

Design operations can be performed on a locked model — in fact, they must be performed
on a locked model because the analysis results must be present.

Commands that affect groups, views, and display items are not locked.

When a model for which analysis results are available is unlocked, SAP2000
will display a warning that unlocking the model will cause all analysis
results to be deleted.

SAP2000 has an option for plotting moment diagrams for frame elements with positive values on the tension side of the member or on the compression side of the member. Click the Options menu > Moment Diagrams on Tension Side command to toggle this option on the tension side or on the compression side

.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Reset_Toolbars.htm | Reset Toolbars -->

# Reset Toolbars

Toolbars can be [customized](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Customize_Toolbars.md) to suit specific working preferences. Reset toolbars to the original alignment at any time using the Options menu > Reset Toolbars command.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Set_Calculator_Memory.htm | Set Calculator Memory -->

# Set Calculator Memory

Form:  Set Calculator Memory

SAP2000 offers a Calculator feature to assist with mathematic operations in forms that accept generic entry. That is, various commands access forms where values are added using edit boxes. The Calculator form can be used to calculate the values to be entered.

One of the Calculator options is a Memory function. This function allows a value or formula to be specified that can be recalled during calculation of a result for subsequent use in a form edit box.

Set Calculator Memory as follows:

1. Click the Options menu > Set Calculator Memory command.
2. Type a value or formula into the edit box.
3. Click the OK button.

Store two different memory items using the Memory 1 (m1) and Memory 2 (m2) edit boxes. See [Calculator](../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Calculator.md) for more information about the calculator feature, including how to apply the value(s) or formula(s) stored using the Options menu > Set Calculator Memory command.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Set_Program_Default_Display_Units.htm | Set Program Default Display Units -->

# Set Program Default Display Units

Form:  Program Default Database Number Formatting Options, Database Named Formats

The number formatting specified using the Options menu > Set Program Default Display Units command will be followed in any databases generated by the program.

1. Click the Options menu > Set Program Default Display Units command to access the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form.

1. - Always Use Current Units check box. When this check box is checked, SAP2000 applies the defaults displayed on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form.

When this check box is unchecked, changes can be made to the various cells/edit boxes on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form. Click in a cell to access a drop-down list of available values (Units, Always Use E Format) or to type a new value to change the default (Decimal Places, Minimum Significant Figures, Zero Tolerance).

1. - Override Auto E Format check box. When this check box is checked, the program prints very small numbers that have been automatically converted by the program to E format (e.g., 1.3704 E-13) as zero.

The  Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form has a Format menu with the following sub-commands. Note that the Always Use Current Units check box must be unchecked for the options on this format menu to be available:

1. - Save Named Format command. Click this command to access the Database Named Formats form and save the selections made on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form to a named file that can then be easily reused. The Database Named Formats form has the following buttons

Note:  If the commands on this menu are not available, uncheck the Always Use Current Units check box and try the commands again.

1. 1. 1. Add New Format Name

         1. Type a name in the edit box in the Format area of the Database Named Formats form.
         2. Click the Add New Format Name button.
      2. Change Format Name

         1. Highlight the Format Name in the Format display area. The Format Name will display in the edit box above the list of named formats.
         2. Type a new name in the edit box.
         3. Click the Change Format Name button.
      3. Delete Format

         1. Highlight the Format Name in the Format display area.
         2. Click the Delete Format button.

1. - Set to English Defaults command. Using this command will display all values on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form, and thus in the program, in English units.
   - Set to Metric Defaults command. Using this command will display all values on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form, and thus in the program, in Metric units.
   - Set to Current Consistent Units command. By default, the values on the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form are consistent with the base units specified when the model was [initialized](../File/New_Model.md). If the units have been changed using the Set to English Defaults or the Set to Metric Defaults command, this command will restore the values to be consistent with the specified base units.
   - Set to Named Format command. This command can be used to access the named format file created using the Save Named Format command. Click the Set to Named Format command to access the Select Format form. Highlight the named format to be used and click the OK button. The previously saved settings will be applied to the Program Default Database Number Formatting Options form.

See Also

[Set Current Format File Source](Database/Set_Current_Format_File_Source.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Show_Bounding_Plane.htm | Show Bounding Plane -->

# Show Bounding Plane

Use the Options menu > Show Bounding Plane command to toggle the bounding plane feature on and off.

When this feature is active, a cyan line appears in some views showing you the location of the active plan or elevation view. For example, if a plan view is active and a three-dimensional view is also showing, the cyan bounding plane appears in the three-dimensional view around the story level associated with the plan view. As a second example, if an elevation (or developed elevation) view is active and a plan view is also showing, the cyan line appears in the plan view showing the location of the elevation.

The table below lists the circumstances where the bounding plane (line) appears.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active Window | Other Visible Window | Bounding Plane or Line Visible? |
| Plan | Plan | No |
| Elevation | No |
| 3D | No |
| Elevation | Plan | Yes |
| Elevation | Yes |
| 3D | Yes |
| 3D | Plan | No |
| Elevation | No |
| 3D | No |

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Show_Tips_at_Startup.htm | Show Tips at Startup -->

# Show Tips at Startup

When SAP2000 launches, Startup Tips may appear. Toggle these tips on or off using the Options menu > Show Tips at Startup command.

Note that the option chosen is saved in the SAP2000.ini file in the Windows or WinNT directory. If this file is deleted or moved, the selected option is lost and the program defaults to showing the tips.

Note: It is not necessary to click the OK button associated with the tip or click the "X" button in the upper right-hand corner of the tip window to continue. Simply left click anywhere in the entire SAP2000 window to close the Tip of the Day window. For example, as soon as the SAP2000 graphical interface starts,  immediately click the File menu and the Startup Tips window closes and the File menu displays.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Options/Show_Tool_Tips_in_Forms.htm | Show Tool Tips in Forms -->

# Show Tool Tips in Forms

Tool Tips may appear when the cursor is allowed to
rest on an option name, an edit box, a drop-down list and so forth when
a form is displayed. Toggle these tips on or off using the Options
menu > Show Tips at Startup command. Generally, the tool tips
provide information similar to that provided in the Help topics, but in
brief format.

The feature is on (i.e., tool tips, where available,
will display) when a check mark precedes the option.

<!-- source: Menus/Options/Sound.htm | Sound -->

# Sound

Click the Options menu > Sound command to toggle on or off the sound produced by SAP2000 when it is displaying animation of [deformed shapes and mode shapes](../Display/Show_Deformed_Shape.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Options/Windows.htm | Windows -->

# Windows

A model can be displayed in up to four windows simultaneously. When two windows are displayed, they can be displayed tiled horizontally or vertically. A different view can be displayed in each window. Use the Options menu > Windows command at any time to specify the number of windows to be used.

As a shortcut to close a window, click on the X in the upper right-hand corner of the window. The remaining windows will automatically resize. This method cannot be used to close the last window. Click the down arrow to display a drop-down list that includes an "Add New Window" command.

A window is the "Active Window" when its tab  is highlighted. Only one window at a time can be active. Click in a window to make it active.

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Clear_Selection.htm | Clear Selection -->

# Clear Selection

Use the Select menu > Clear Selection command or the Clear Selection button ![](../../assets/images/Images/CLR_shg.gif)  to clear the selection of all currently selected objects. It is an all or nothing command. The command can not be used to selectively clear a portion of a selection. To selectively clear a selection, left click on the selected objects one at a time or use the [Select menu > Deselect commands](Deselect.md).


---
<!-- source: Menus/Select/Deselect.htm | Deselect -->

# Deselect

Objects can be deselected one at a time by left clicking on the selected objects. A more powerful way to deselect items is to use the Select menu > Deselect command. This gives you access to most of the selection methods available on the Select menu ([Pointer/Window](Select/Pointer_Window.md), [Intersecting Line](Select/Intersecting_Line.md), [3D Box](Select/Coordinate_Specification/Select_3D_Box.md), [XY Plane](Select/Coordinate_Specification/Select_XY_Plane.md), [XZ Plane](Select/Coordinate_Specification/Select_XZ_Plane.md), [YZ Plane](Select/Coordinate_Specification/Select_YZ_Plane.md), [Groups](Select/Select_Groups.md), [Frame Sections](Select/Properties/Select_Frame_Sections.md), [Cable Properties](Select/Properties/Select_Cable_Properties.md), [Tendon Properties](Select/Properties/Select_Tendon_Properties.md), [Area Sections](Select/Properties/Select_Area_Sections.md), [Solid Properties](Select/Properties/Select_Solid_Properties.md), [Link Properties](Select/Properties/Select_Link_Properties.md), [Joint Constraints](Select/Assignments/Select_Joint_Constraints.md), [Labels](Select/Select_Labels.md), [All](Select/Select_All.md)), except that now they are used to deselect rather than to select.

For example, assume that you want to select all of the objects in your model except for those in a particular XZ plane. Do this by first using the Select menu > Select > All command and then using the Select menu > Deselect > Coordinate Specification > Click Joint in XZ Plane command.


---
<!-- source: Menus/Select/Get_Previous_Selection.htm | Get Previous Selection -->

# Get Previous Selection

Use the Select menu > Get Previous Selection command or the Restore Previous Selection button,![](../../assets/images/Images/PS_shg.gif) to select whatever objects were last previously selected.

For example, assume that some line objects have been selected and that frame section properties were assigned to them. Immediately after this operation, use this command to select the line objects again and assign something else to them, such as member end releases.

# Joint Supports

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Assignments > Joint Constraints command to display the Select Supported Joints form.
2. Select the Supported Degrees of Freedom and the type of Support (Restraints, Joint Springs, Line Spring Support Joints, Area Spring Support Joints and so on) by checking the appropriate check box.
3. Click the OK button. All support joints matching the specified criteria will be selected.

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Assignments > Joint Constraints command to display the Select Constraints form.
2. Click to select one or more of the previously defined constraints. Use the Shift and Ctrl keys to make multiple selections.

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Coordinate_Specification/Select_3D_Box.htm | Select 3D Box -->

# Select - 3D Box

The Select menu > Select > Coordinate Specification > 3D Box command works in a [3D View](../../../View/Set_3-D_View.md). Unlike some of the other selection commands that select objects  without regard to their connection to other objects, the Select menu > Select > Coordinate Specification > 3D Box command selects points, frames, cables, tendons, areas or solids, giving full consideration to connections among the objects.

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Coordinate Specification > 3D Box command to enable the 3D Box Selection mode.
2. Left click in the active window and hold down the left mouse button; then drag the mouse diagonally over the target area, to the opposite diagonal corner of the "3D selection box." Note that the specified corner points of the selection box must occur at point objects or at the intersection of grid lines. Also note that when dragging the mouse, the diagonal must be through the interior of the selection box, not along the face of the selection box.
3. Release the mouse button and any objects within the 3D Box will be selected.

## See Also

[Specified Coordinate Range](Specified_Coordinate_Range.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Coordinate_Specification/Specified_Coordinate_Range.htm | Specified Coordinate Range -->

# Specified Coordinate Range

Form:  Select By Specified Coordinate Range

Use the Select menu > Select > Coordinate Specification > Specified Coordinate Range command to access the Select By Specified Coordinate Range form. Use that form to select objects on the basis of X, Y, and Z coordinate limits.

- Coordinate System drop-down list. Choose the coordinate system in which the coordinate limits are applied.
- Units drop-down list. Use the displayed units or select new ones from this drop-down list for the values specified on this form.
- Select All Objects That Are options
- - Entirely Inside the Specified Selection Volume option. Use this option when the objects to be selected are fully within the specified coordinate range.
  - Entirely or Partially Inside the Specified Selection Volume option. Use this option when the objects to be selected are fully or partially within the specified coordinate range. Using this option, objects that cross the boundary limits will be selected.
- Select These Object Types options. Choose the type of objects to be selected by clicking the appropriate check boxes:  Point, Line, Area, Solid and Link. By default, all object types are selected.

The X Coordinate Limits, Y Coordinate Limits, and Z Coordinate Limits options can be used in any combination to define the coordinate limits on which the selection is based.

## See Also

[Select 3D Box](Select_3D_Box.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Intersecting_Line.htm | Intersecting Line -->

# Select - Intersecting Line

The intersecting line selection features draws a line through one or more objects to select them. Use this feature as follows:

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Intersecting Line command or the Select Using Intersecting Line button, ![](../../../assets/images/Images/SELECTIL_shg.gif).
2. Draw the intersecting line as follows.

   1. Position the mouse pointer to one side of the object(s) to be selected.
   2. Depress and hold down the left button on the mouse.
   3. While keeping the left button depressed, drag the mouse across the object(s) to be selected.
   4. Release the left mouse button.

Note the following about the intersecting line selection method:

- As you drag your mouse, a "rubber band line" appears. The rubber band line is a dashed line that changes length and orientation as you drag the mouse. It extends from the point where you first depressed the left mouse button to the current mouse pointer position. Any visible object that is intersected (crossed) by the rubber band line when you release the left mouse button is selected.

- When you make a selection using the intersecting line method, you do not then remain in an intersecting line mode such that you could immediately make another intersecting line selection. Instead, you default back to a window selection mode. You must click the Select menu > Select > Intersecting Line command or the Select Using Intersecting Line button, ![](../../../assets/images/Images/SELECTIL_shg.gif) every time you use the selection method even if you are doing several intersecting line selections in succession.

## See Also

[Pointer/Window](Intersecting_Line.md)


---
<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Intersecting_Poly.htm | Intersecting Poly -->

# Intersecting Poly

Use the Select menu > Select > Intersecting Poly command to select objects by clicking the left mouse button in the active window to delineate a poly shape. Objects are selected when the lines of the poly shape enclose them as well as when the lines defining the poly shape intersect with them. Note that the lines defining the poly shape cannot cross or intersect with each other.

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Intersecting Poly command to enable the Intersecting Poly Select mode.
2. Click in the active window to begin selecting the target objects.
3. Move the mouse to the next location and click the left mouse button to draw the first side of the poly shape. Continue clicking in the active window at any number of points to enclose the object(s) to be selected within the lines defining  the poly shape or to intersect the lines defining the poly shape with the object(s) to be selected. As noted above, the lines defining the poly shape cannot cross or intersect with each other.
4. Exit the Intersecting Poly Select mode by double clicking the left mouse button. Any objects fully within the poly-shaped area or that intersect with the lines defining the poly shape will be selected. Note that using the Esc key will cancel the selection, rather than exit the Intersecting Poly Select mode.

## See Also


---
<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Pointer_Window.htm | Pointer Window -->

# Select - Pointer/Window

With the program in [Select mode](../../Draw/Set_Select_Mode.md), objects can be selected graphically in the active display window using the mouse cursor. Selected objects are indicated by dashed lines. A window is active when the blue title bar at the top of the window is highlighted.

Note: Only objects that are present in the active display window can be selected. For example, if the display of Frame/Cable/Tendon objects has been turned off in the active window (see [Set Display Options](../../View/Set_Display_Options.md)), windowing around a portion of the structure that contains those objects will NOT select them. Other, non-graphical selection methods are not restricted by the visibility of the objects (see options on the Select menu).

- By Pointer  Each mouse click on an object selects or deselects the object. Only a single object at a time can be selected/deselected using selection By Pointer. When in Select mode, selection/deselection By Pointer is always available. Use the [Selection List](../../../Keyboard_Commands_and_Special_Features/Selection_List.md) when multiple objects are present within the [screen selection tolerance](../../Options/Dimensions_Tolerances.md) of the mouse click.

Tip: It is sometimes easier to select a single point object by drawing a window around it rather than trying to click on it.

- By Window  Draw a window around one or more objects to select them. Draw a window around an object as follows:

1. 1. Position the mouse pointer above and to the left  (or below and to the right) of the object(s) to be selected by windowing.
   2. Depress and hold down the left button on the mouse.
   3. While keeping the left button depressed, drag the mouse to a position below and to the right  (or above and to the left) of the object(s) to be selected.
   4. Release the left mouse button.

Tip: If the mouse moves from left to right while dragging, only objects completely inside the window are selected. If  the mouse moves from right to left while dragging, objects fully or partially inside the rectangle will be selected. Dragging from top to bottom or bottom to top does not affect selection.

Note: Window selections are additive. Objects in the selection window that were previously selected will stay selected.

Objects can also be deselected by window. To deselect by window, click the Select > Deselect > Pointer/Window, command and then draw the selection window as described above. The command must be used each time an object or set of objects is to be deselected.

After performing a single selection or deselection using any of the selection/deselection methods on the Select menu, the program automatically returns to selection By Window.

## See Also

[Intersecting Line](Intersecting_Line.md)

[Get Previous Selection](../Get_Previous_Selection.md)

[Deselect](../Deselect.md)

[Clear Selection](../Clear_Selection.md)

[Select 3D Box](Coordinate_Specification/Select_3D_Box.md)

[Show Tips at Startup](../../Options/Show_Tips_at_Startup.md)

# Poly

2. Click in the active window to begin selecting the target objects.
3. Move the mouse to the next location and click the left mouse button to draw the first side of the poly shape. Continue clicking in the active window at any number of points to enclose the object(s) to be selected within the lines defining  the poly shape. As noted above, the lines defining the poly shape cannot cross or intersect.
4. Exit the Poly Select mode by double clicking the left mouse button. Any objects fully within the poly-shaped area will be selected. Note that using the Esc key will cancel the selection, rather than exit the Poly Select mode.

# Select - Frame Sections

Use the Select menu > Select > Properties > Frame Sections command to select line objects based on their [section definitions](../../../Assign/Frame/Frame_Sections.md).

1. Click the Select menu >Select > Properties > Frame Sections command to display the Select Sections form.
2. Click to select one or more of the previously defined sections. Use the Shift and Ctrl keys to make multiple selections.
3. Click the OK button. All frame objects assigned the selected section type(s) will be selected.

[Select - Area Sections](Select_Area_Sections.md)

[Select - Cable Properties](Select_Cable_Properties.md)

[Select - Solid Properties](Select_Solid_Properties.md)

[Select - Labels](../Select_Labels.md)

# Select - Link Properties

# Select - Tendon Properties

Use the Select menu > Select > Properties > Tendon Properties command to select line objects that have been [drawn as tendons](../../../Draw/Tendon/Tendon_Data_for_Line_Object_Form.md) and assigned tendon properties.

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Select_All.htm | Select All -->

# Select - All

Click the Select All button  ![](../../../assets/images/Images/Select%20All.jpg)  or the Select menu > Select > All command to select all of the objects in the model. The total number of objects selected is displayed on the status bar. Be careful using this command. The command does not select only the objects shown in a particular window, but rather it literally selects all objects in the model.

TIP:  This command is a useful technique to determine the total number of objects in a model.

# Select - Groups

Use the Select menu > Select > Groups command to select objects based on their [group assignments](../../Assign/Assign_to_Groups.md).

1. Click the Select menu > Select >  Groups  command to display the Select Groups form. The names listed in this list box are those defined using the [Define menu > Groups](../../Define/Groups.md) or [Assign menu > Assign to Groups command](../../Assign/Assign_to_Groups.md).
2. Click to select one or more of the previously defined groups. Use the Shift and Ctrl keys to make multiple selections.
3. Click the OK button. All elements belonging to those groups will be selected.

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Select_Labels.htm | Select Labels -->

# Select - Labels

Form:  Select by Labels

Use the Select menu > Select > Labels command to select objects on the basis of their labels. This command can be used to select a single object, multiple objects as defined by specifying a labeling increment, or multiple objects by selecting them from a list of object labels.

1. Click the Select menu > Select > Labels command to display the Select by Labels form. Choose the Selection Type:  Select Objects or Deselect Objects.
2. Choose the type of object to be selected from the Object Type drop-down list.
3. Choose one of the Select Options. The options available elsewhere on the form depend on the choice made here.

   - Select a Single Object option. With this option selected, choose the object label from the Object Label drop-down list.
   - Select Multiple Objects by Specifying Increment option. With this option selected, use the Start Label drop-down list and the End Label drop-down list  to specify the first and last objects to be selected. Use the Increment edit box to specify the interval at which objects are to be selected (e.g., entering 3 would result in every 3rd object being selected).
   - Select Multiple Objects from List option. With this option selected, choose one or more object labels from the display area using standard Windows operations for multiple selection. [Click here to learn about methods for selecting multiple sections](javascript:TextPopup(this))

     - Select and Drag Method. Select one object label by left clicking on it and then continue to hold down the left mouse button while dragging your mouse up or down to select additional adjacent object labels.
     - Select Shift Method. Select one object label by left clicking on it. Then hold down the Shift key on your keyboard and select another object label. The second object label is added to the selection as well as all object labels between the first and second object label.
     - Select Ctrl Method. Select one object label by left clicking on it. Then hold down the Ctrl key on your keyboard and select another adjacent or non-adjacent object label. That object is added to the selection. You can continue holding down the Ctrl key and clicking on other objects to add them to the selection.
4. After setting the various select options, click one of the following buttons.

   - Select Specified Items button. Click this button to select the object(s) without closing the Select by Labels form. The selected objects will be highlighted in the active window. If necessary, click on the Select by Labels form to drag it out of the way.
   - OK button. Click the button to select the objects and close the form. The selected objects will be highlighted in the active window.

Note: The total number of Objects selected is displayed on the status bar.

# Click Straight Line Object

Use the Select menu > Select Lines Parallel to > Click Straight Line Object command to select all line objects parallel to the line object selected after the command is used.

1. Click the Select menu > Select Lines Parallel to > Click Straight Line Object command to activate the Select Lines Parallel To mode.
2. Click on a line object in the active window.

When the mouse button is released, all line objects in the model parallel to the line selected in Step 2 will be selected.

## See Also

[Coordinate Axes or Plane](Coordinate_Axes_or_Plane.md)

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select/Select_Lines_Parallel_To/Coordinate_Axes_or_Plane.htm | Coordinate Axes or Plane -->

# Coordinate Axes or Plane

Use the Select menu > Select > Select Lines Parallel to > Coordinates Axes or Plane command to access the Select Lines form. Use the form to specify when line objects will be selected on the basis of their orientation relative to specified coordinate axes and planes, or line or area objects.

- Select Lines That Are options.
- - Parallel to Specified Items option. When this option is chosen, line objects will be selected when those line objects are parallel (within the tolerance angle) to the specified axes, plane, line object, or area object.
  - Not Parallel To Specified Items options. When this option is chosen, line objects will be selected when those line objects are not parallel (within the tolerance angle) to the specified axes, plane, line object, or area object.
- Compare Line Orientation To options.
- - Coordinate Axes and Planes option. When this option is selected, also choose the coordinate system and the axis or plane to which the line objects to be selected are parallel or are not parallel.
  - - Coordinate System drop-down list. Choose the coordinate system for the objects to be selected.
    - - Toggle Display Coordinate System button. This button is available if a [coordinate system](../../../Define/Coordinate_Grid_System/Define_Coordinate_Systems_Grid.md) other than Global has been defined for the model. Clicking the button toggles the display/visibility of the alternate coordinate system on or off.
    - X Axis, Y Axis, Z Axis, XY Plane, XZ Plane, and YZ Plane options. Choose the axis or plane to which the line objects to be selected are or are not parallel (within the tolerance angle), depending on the option selected in the Select Lines That Are area of the form.
  - Line Objects option and Select One or More Line Objects display list. When this option is selected, the display list is added to the form. Select one or more line objects to which the line objects to be selected are or are not parallel (within the tolerance angle), depending on the option selected in the Select Lines That Are area of the form.

1. - Area Objects option and Select One or More Area Objects display list. When this option is selected, the display list is added to the form. Select one or more area objects to which the line objects to be selected are or are not parallel (within the tolerance angle), depending on the option selected in the Select Lines That Are area of the form.
   - Clear button. When available, click this button to deselect all objects selected in the Select One or More Line Objects display list or the Select One or More Area Objects display list.

- Tolerance Angle in Degrees options.
- - Default (0.057 degrees) option. When this option is selected, the tolerance angle is 0.057 degrees. Thus, line objects that are parallel or are not parallel within 0.057 degree of the specified axes, plane, or line or area object will be selected, depending on the option selected in the Select Lines That Are area of the form.
  - User Angle option and edit box. Use this option and the edit box to specify another tolerance angle. Line objects that are or are not parallel within the specified tolerance of the specified axes, plane, or line or area object will be selected, depending on the option selected in the Select Lines That Are area of the form.

# Select - Invert Selection

The Select menu > Invert Selection command changes the selection such that the currently selected objects are no longer selected and all objects that are not currently selected are selected.

<!-- source: Menus/Select/Select_Using_Tables.htm | Select Using Tables -->

# Select Using Tables

Click the Select menu > Select Using Tables command to access the [Choose Tables for Display form](../../Database_Tables/Choose_Tables_For_Form.md). Use that form to specify which objects to select by selecting the data associated with the object(s). This selection method allows the application of a filter, thereby allowing the selection of a subset(s) of the original object selection.

When this selection method is applied, data tables will list the selected objects and the objects will be selected in the graphical display. The object associated with the "current record" will flash in the graphical display.

<!-- source: Menus/Tools/Add_Show_Plug_Ins.htm | Add Show Plug Ins -->

# Add/Show Plug Ins

Form:  External Plug In Data

A plug in is a software tool from an external source (i.e., not from
CSi) that works inside SAP2000 to provide additional features to the program.
For example, a plug in may add import/export capabilities, customized
model-building templates, customized design or other post-processing of
results, or it may perform parametric studies. Many other possibilities
can be envisioned.

Note: It is recommended
that you save your model, possibly under a new name, before using a plug
in until you gain confidence in the applicability and stability of the
plug in. Also, the plug in must be compatible with the current version
of SAP2000, and the plug in must be installed on your computer so that
SAP2000 can find it.

Click the Tools menu > Add/Show Plug Ins
command to access the External Plug In Data
form. Use that form to add a plug in from an external source. The plug
in is added through the SAP2000 API.  A maximum of nine plug ins
can be added at any one time.

- Plug
  In Name edit box. Use this edit box to specify the name of
  the plug in. This name should match exactly with the name used by
  the creator of the plug in from the external source.
- Menu
  Text edit box. When a valid plug in is added, the name of the
  plug in, as specified in this edit box, will be added to the Tools
  menu.
- **Plugin Path** edit
  box. Use this edit box to specify the path of a .NET plugin. The **Plugin
  Path** field should be left blank for COM plugins.
- Status
  display box. If the status show "OK," the plug in has been
  added successfully. If SAP2000 is unable to locate a plug or the plug
  in is not compatible, this display box will provide an error message.
  If the file cannot be found, be sure to check that the plug in is
  on your computer (i.e., has been registered). If the plug in is not
  compatible, please contact the developer of the plug in for assistance.
- - Add
    button. With the plug in name and menu text specified, click this
    button to add the plug in to the Tool menu.
  - Modify
    button.  Highlight an existing plug in, type in new menu
    text, and click this button to modify the plug in name on the
    Tool menu.
  - Delete
    button. Highlight an existing plug in and click this button to
    delete the plug in and remove its name from the Tool menu.
  - Up/Down
    Arrow buttons.  These arrow buttons are enabled if
    more plug ins have been specified than can be displayed in the
    large display area. Use the buttons to scroll up/down through
    the list of plug ins.
  - Info
    button.  Highlight an existing plug in the display list and
    click this button to display any information that the originator
    of the plug in specified in the plug in. If nothing displays,
    the originator of the plug in did not provide information for
    display.

After a plug in is added to SAP2000, use the Tools
menu > {Plug In Name} command to activate the plug in. The first
time a plug in is used in a given SAP2000 session, a warning will appear
concerning the following:

- the plug in is not part
  of SAP2000 and is not supplied by Computers and Structures, Inc.
- the plug in can change
  your model and affect analysis and design results
- the plug in may cause
  the program to crash or hang, causing loss of data.

Note:  If
you have any questions or problems with the use of a plug in, please contact
the developer of the plug in for assistance. Computers and Structures,
Inc., is unable to provide technical support for any plug in that is not
supplied by us.

## Information for Developers

Please refer to CSI\_OAPI\_Documentation.chm
for information on creating plugins. CSI\_OAPI\_Documentation.chm
can be found in the SAP2000 installation directory.

<!-- source: Menus/Tools/CSiLoadOptimizer.htm | CSiLoadOptimizer -->

# CSiLoadOptimizer

Use the  Tools menu > CSiLoadOptimizer
command to access the CSiLoadOptimizer feature. This tool can be used
in determining an optimal set of loads, including cable tensioning, to
achieve specific goals in a structural model. The loads to be optimized
can be applied in any static load case, which can be of type linear, nonlinear,
or staged construction. The goals are specified as the values to be attained
for response quantities such as joint displacements, generalized displacements,
joint reactions, and member forces or moments. The optimization operation
consists of determining the scale factors of variable loads in the static
load case linear to best meet these goals.

Click the Resources button on the CSiLoadOptimizer
form and then the Documentation button to display a Technical Note in
.pdf format and learn more about this feature.

<!-- source: Menus/Tools/Set_as_Active_Instance_for_API.htm | Set as Active Instance for API -->

# Set as Active Instance for API

Use the  Tools menu > Active API Instance command to make the
current instance of SAP2000 the "active instance" so that it
will then respond to subsequent calls to cHelper.GetObject()
API function. If the current instance is the active instance, then this
command is disabled. In either case, the process ID of the current instance
is displayed with the menu command for use with the API function cHelper.GetObjectProcess().

<!-- source: Menus/View/Pan.htm | Pan -->

# Pan

The pan feature allows a view to be "moved" within the window such that areas beyond the original edges of the view can be displayed.

1. Click the View menu > Pan command or the Pan button, ![](../../assets/images/Images/IMG00044.GIF) , to pan a view.
2. Hold down the left mouse button in the view and drag the mouse (while holding down the left mouse button) to pan the view.

The  command or toolbar button must be clicked every time the Pan feature is used.

Note:  Use the middle mouse button as a short cut to Pan the active view. Depress the middle mouse button and move the mouse in the active window to Pan the view.

Restore the view displayed immediately before the Pan command or button was used by clicking the View menu > Restore Full View command or Restore Full View button, ![](../../assets/images/Images/ebx_-661494151.gif).


---
<!-- source: Menus/View/Previous_Zoom.htm | Previous Zoom -->

# Previous Zoom

Switch between two previously zoomed views using the View menu > Restore Previous Zoom command or by clicking the Restore Previous Zoom button![](../../assets/images/Images/IMG00041.GIF).  Only the currently active screen is affected by this command.


---
<!-- source: Menus/View/Refresh_View.htm | Refresh View -->

# Refresh View

Redraw the current window in full view with an image that accounts for the drawing order of each member using the View menu > Refresh View command. Because this command verifies the drawing order of each element while redrawing, and redraws only in the full view mode, this command can be slower than the View menu > Refresh Window command.


---
<!-- source: Menus/View/Refresh_Window.htm | Refresh Window -->

# Refresh Window

Redraw the current window using the View menu > Refresh Window command. This command simply redraws the image as last viewed, and does not take into account the drawing order of the elements. As a result, this command is faster to execute than the View menu > Refresh View command, which redraws the current window in full view while verifying drawing order.


---
<!-- source: Menus/View/Remove_Selection_from_View.htm | Remove Selection from View -->

# Remove Selection from View

Use the View menu > Remove Selection from View command to remove selected objects from the active display window.

1. Select the objects to be removed from the active display window.
2. Click the View menu > Remove Selection from View command and the selected objects will no longer be included in the active display window, although the objects remain in the model. This command can be helpful when working on a complex model with many types of objects concentrated in the same area.

Use the [View menu > Restore Previous Selection](Restore_Previous_Selection.md) command to redisplay the selected objects.

Note:  Right clicking anywhere in an active window will display a drop-down menu of commands, including the Remove Selection from View command. Clicking that command is the same as using the View menu > Remove Selection from View command.  Thus, select objects before right clicking and selecting the Remove Selection from View command from the resulting drop-down menu.


---
<!-- source: Menus/View/Restore_Previous_Selection.htm | Restore Previous Selection -->

# Restore Previous Selection

The View menu > Restore Previous Selection command is used in conjunction with the View menu > Remove Selection from View command.  When the [View menu > Remove Selection from View command](Remove_Selection_from_View.md) is used, the selected portion of the model is removed from the current display window (not from the model). The View menu > Restore Previous Selection command is used to redisplay the selected objects in the current display window.

Note:  Right clicking anywhere in an active window will display a drop-down menu of commands, including the Restore Previous Selection command. Clicking that command is the same as using the View menu > Restore Previous Selection command.

<!-- source: Menus/View/Set_2-D_View.htm | Set 2-D View -->

# Set 2-D View

Form:  Set 2D View

It is sometimes easier to build a model while working in 2D elevation or plan views. Use the View menu > Set 2D View command to access the Set 2D View form and set the active window to a 2D View.

Note: It is also possible to choose a plane by clicking one of the 2D view buttons  ![](../../assets/images/Images/2DVIEW_shg.gif),  and then using the up or down arrow buttons  ![](../../assets/images/Images/UPDOWN_shg.gif)  to move to an appropriate plane.

1. Click the View menu > Set 2D View command to access the Set 2D View form.
2. Select the X-Y, X-Z or Y-Z plane. Fill in the edit box with the appropriate Z, Y or X coordinate.
3. Select the View Direction:  Front or Back Face.
4. Click OK.

Use rubber band zoom to zoom into a window. Clicking once anywhere in the window will restore the original view.

Example:  Use of this command is demonstrated in [Problem S](../../Example_Problems/Problem_S.md) and [Problem U](../../Example_Problems/Problem_U.md).

## See Also

[Select 3D View](Set_3-D_View.md)
